person:aaron_1.name: Aaron
person:aaron_1.title: Aaron
person:aaron_1.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator. He was born in Egypt three years before his brother Moses, and a number of years after his sister Miriam (2:1, 4; 7:7). He married Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab of the house of Judah (6:23; 1 Chr. 2:10), by whom he had four sons, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. When the time for the deliverance of Isarael out of Egypt drew nigh, he was sent by God (Ex. 4:14, 27-30) to meet his long-absent brother, that he might co-operate with him in all that they were required to do in bringing about the Exodus. …

person:abagtha_3.name: Abagtha
person:abagtha_3.title: Abagtha
person:abagtha_3.summary: One of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus’s court (Esther 1:10; 2:21).

person:abda_4.name: Abda
person:abda_4.title: Abda
person:abda_4.summary: The father of Adoniram, whom Solomon set over the tribute (1 Kings 4:6); i.e., the forced labour (R.V., “levy”).

person:abdeel_5.name: Abdeel
person:abdeel_5.title: Abdeel
person:abdeel_5.summary: Servant of God, (Jer. 36:26), the father of Shelemiah.

person:abdiel_9.name: Abdiel
person:abdiel_9.title: Abdiel
person:abdiel_9.summary: Servant of God, (1 Chr. 5:15), a Gadite chief.

person:abdon_10.name: Abdon
person:abdon_10.title: Abdon
person:abdon_10.summary: The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:13-15). He is probably the Bedan of 1 Sam. 12:11.

person:abdon_11.name: Abdon
person:abdon_11.title: Abdon
person:abdon_11.summary:
One of the “sons” of Shashak (1 Chr. 8:23).
This is the name also of a Levitical town of the Gershonites, in the tribe of Asher (Josh. 21:30; 1 Chr. 6:74). The ruins of Abdeh, some 8 miles north-east of Accho, probably mark its site.

person:abdon_12.name: Abdon
person:abdon_12.title: Abdon
person:abdon_12.summary: The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

person:abel_13.name: Abel
person:abel_13.title: Abel
person:abel_13.summary: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain (Gen. 4:1-16). Guided by the instruction of their father, the two brothers were trained in the duty of worshipping God. “And in process of time” (marg. “at the end of days”, i.e., on the Sabbath) each of them offered up to God of the first-fruits of his labours. Cain, as a husbandman, offered the fruits of the field; Abel, as a shepherd, of the firstlings of his flock. “The Lord had respect unto Abel and his offering; but unto Cain and his offering he had not respect” (Gen. 4:3-5). …

person:abiah_15.name: Abiah
person:abiah_15.title: Abiah
person:abiah_15.summary: The second son of Samuel (1 Sam. 8:2; 1 Chr. 6:28). His conduct, along with that of his brother, as a judge in Beer-sheba, to which office his father had appointed him, led to popular discontent, and ultimately provoked the people to demand a royal form of government.

person:abiah_17.name: Abiah
person:abiah_17.title: Abiah
person:abiah_17.summary: One of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8). “Abiah,” A.V.

person:abiathar_20.name: Abiathar
person:abiathar_20.title: Abiathar
person:abiathar_20.summary: Father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli. When his father was slain with the priests of Nob, he escaped, and bearing with him the ephod, he joined David, who was then in the cave of Adullam (1 Sam. 22:20-23; 23:6). He remained with David, and became priest of the party of which he was the leader (1 Sam. 30:7). When David ascended the throne of Judah, Abiathar was appointed high priest (1 Chr. 15:11; 1 Kings 2:26) and the “king’s companion” (1 Chr. 27:34). Meanwhile Zadok, of the house of Eleazar, had been made high priest. …

person:abida_21.name: Abida
person:abida_21.title: Abida
person:abida_21.summary: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

person:abidan_22.name: Abidan
person:abidan_22.title: Abidan
person:abidan_22.summary: Father of judgment; judge, head of the tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus (Num. 1:11; 2:22).

person:abiel_18.name: Abiel
person:abiel_18.title: Abiel (Arbathite)
person:abiel_18.summary: An Arbathite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:32); called also Abi-albon (2 Sam. 23:31).

person:abiel_23.name: Abiel
person:abiel_23.title: Abiel
person:abiel_23.summary: The son of Zeror and father of Ner, who was the grandfather of Saul (1 Sam. 14:51; 1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39). In 1 Sam. 9:1, he is called the “father,” probably meaning the grandfather, of Kish.

person:abiezer_24.name: Abiezer
person:abiezer_24.title: Abiezer
person:abiezer_24.summary: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:27; comp. 1 Chr. 27:12).

person:abiezer_763.name: Abiezer
person:abiezer_763.title: Abiezer
person:abiezer_763.summary: The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Josh. 17:2; comp. Judg. 6:34; 8:2). He was also called Jeezer (Num. 26:30).

person:abigail_26.name: Abigail
person:abigail_26.title: Abigail
person:abigail_26.summary: The wife of the churlish Nabal, who dwelt in the district of Carmel (1 Sam. 25:3). She showed great prudence and delicate management at a critical period of her husband’s life. She was “a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance.” After Nabal’s death she became the wife of David (1 Sam. 25:14-42), and was his companion in all his future fortunes (1 Sam. 27:3; 30:5; 2 Sam. 2:2). By her David had a son called Chileab (2 Sam. 3:3), elsewhere called Daniel (1 Chr. 3:1).

person:abigail_27.name: Abigail
person:abigail_27.title: Abigail
person:abigail_27.summary: The sister of David, and wife of Jether an Ishmaelite (1 Chr. 2:16, 17). She was the mother of Amasa (2 Sam. 17:25).

person:abihail_31.name: Abihail
person:abihail_31.title: Abihail
person:abihail_31.summary: The second wife of King Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:18), a descendant of Eliab, David’s eldest brother.

person:abihail_32.name: Abihail
person:abihail_32.title: Abihail
person:abihail_32.summary: The father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai (Esther 2:15).

person:abihu_33.name: Abihu
person:abihu_33.title: Abihu
person:abihu_33.summary: Father of Him; i.e., “worshipper of God”, the second of the sons of Aaron (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2; 26:60; 1 Chr. 6:3). Along with his three brothers he was consecrated to the priest’s office (Ex. 28:1). With his father and elder brother he accompanied the seventy elders part of the way up the mount with Moses (Ex. 24:1, 9). On one occasion he and Nadab his brother offered incense in their censers filled with “strange” (i.e., common) fire, i.e., not with fire taken from the great brazen altar (Lev. 6:9, etc.), and for this offence they were struck dead, and were taken out and buried without the camp (Lev. 10:1-11; comp. Num. 3:4; 26:61; 1 Chr. 24:2). …

person:abihud_34.name: Abihud
person:abihud_34.title: Abihud
person:abihud_34.summary: One of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:3); called also Ahihud (ver. 7).

person:abijah_14.name: Abijah
person:abijah_14.title: Abijah
person:abijah_14.summary: The daughter of Zechariah (2 Chr. 29:1; comp. Isa. 8:2), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz. She is also called Abi (2 Kings 18:2).

person:abijah_35.name: Abijah
person:abijah_35.title: Abijah
person:abijah_35.summary: A son of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel. On account of his severe illness when a youth, his father sent his wife to consult the prophet Ahijah regarding his recovery. The prophet, though blind with old age, knew the wife of Jeroboam as soon as she approached, and under a divine impulse he announced to her that inasmuch as in Abijah alone of all the house of Jeroboam there was found “some good thing toward the Lord,” he only would come to his grave in peace. As his mother crossed the threshold of the door on her return, the youth died, and “all Israel mourned for him” (1 Kings 14:1-18).

person:abijah_36.name: Abijah
person:abijah_36.title: Abijah
person:abijah_36.summary: A descendant of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, a chief of one of the twenty-four orders into which the priesthood was divided by David (1 Chr. 24:10). The order of Abijah was one of those which did not return from the Captivity (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42; 12:1).

person:abijah_38.name: Abijah
person:abijah_38.title: Abijah
person:abijah_38.summary: The son of Rehoboam, whom he succeeded on the throne of Judah (1 Chr. 3:10). He is also called Abijam (1 Kings 14:31; 15:1-8). He began his three years’ reign (2 Chr. 12:16; 13:1, 2) with a strenuous but unsuccessful effort to bring back the ten tribes to their allegiance. His address to “Jeroboam and all Israel,” before encountering them in battle, is worthy of being specially noticed (2 Chr. 13:5-12). It was a very bloody battle, no fewer than 500,000 of the army of Israel having perished on the field. He is described as having walked “in all the sins of his father” (1 Kings 15:3; 2 Chr. 11:20-22). …

person:abimael_39.name: Abimael
person:abimael_39.title: Abimael
person:abimael_39.summary: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

person:abimelech_40.name: Abimelech
person:abimelech_40.title: Abimelech (King of Gerar)
person:abimelech_40.summary: A king of Gerar in the time of Isaac, probably the son of the preceeding (Gen. 26:1-22). Isaac sought refuge in his territory during a famine, and there he acted a part with reference to his wife Rebekah similar to that of his father Abraham with reference to Sarah. Abimelech rebuked him for the deception, which he accidentally discovered. Isaac settled for a while here, and prospered. Abimelech desired him, however, to leave his territory, which Isaac did. Abimelech afterwards visited him when he was encamped at Beer-sheba, and expressed a desire to renew the covenant which had been entered into between their fathers (Gen. 26:26-31).

person:abimelech_41.name: Abimelech
person:abimelech_41.title: Abimelech
person:abimelech_41.summary: A son of Gideon (Judg. 9:1), who was proclaimed king after the death of his father (Judg. 8:33-9:6). One of his first acts was to murder his brothers, seventy in number, “on one stone,” at Ophrah. Only one named Jotham escaped. He was an unprincipled, ambitious ruler, often engaged in war with his own subjects. When engaged in reducing the town of Thebez, which had revolted, he was struck mortally on his head by a mill-stone, thrown by the hand of a woman from the wall above. Perceiving that the wound was mortal, he desired his armour-bearer to thrust him through with his sword, that it might not be said he had perished by the hand of a woman (Judg. 9:50-57).

person:abinadab_43.name: Abinadab
person:abinadab_43.title: Abinadab
person:abinadab_43.summary: A Levite of Kirjath-jearim, in whose house the ark of the covenant was deposited after having been brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1). It remained there twenty years, till it was at length removed by David (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; 1 Chr. 13:7).

person:abinadab_44.name: Abinadab
person:abinadab_44.title: Abinadab
person:abinadab_44.summary: The second of the eight sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:8). He was with Saul in the campaign against the Philistines in which Goliath was slain (1 Sam. 17:13).

person:abinadab_45.name: Abinadab
person:abinadab_45.title: Abinadab
person:abinadab_45.summary: One of Solomon’s officers, who “provided victuals for the king and his household.” He presided, for this purpose, over the district of Dor (1 Kings 4:11).

person:abinadab_641.name: Abinadab
person:abinadab_641.title: Abinadab
person:abinadab_641.summary: One of Saul’s sons, who peristed with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2; 1 Chr. 10:2).

person:abinoam_46.name: Abinoam
person:abinoam_46.title: Abinoam
person:abinoam_46.summary: Father of kindness, the father of Barak (Judg. 4:6; 5:1).

person:abiram_47.name: Abiram
person:abiram_47.title: Abiram (son of Eliab)
person:abiram_47.summary: One of the sons of Eliab, who joined Korah in the conspiracy against Moses and Aaron. He and all the conspirators, with their families and possessions (except the children of Korah), were swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1-27; 26:9; Ps. 106:17).

person:abiram_48.name: Abiram
person:abiram_48.title: Abiram
person:abiram_48.summary: The eldest son of Hiel the Bethelite, who perished prematurely in consequence of his father’s undertaking to rebuild Jericho (1 Kings 16:34), according to the words of Joshua (6:26).

person:abishag_49.name: Abishag
person:abishag_49.title: Abishag
person:abishag_49.summary: Father of (i.e., “given to”) error, a young woman of Shunem, distinguished for her beauty. She was chosen to minister to David in his old age. She became his wife (1 Kings 1:3, 4, 15). After David’s death Adonijah persuaded Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, to entreat the king to permit him to marry Abishag. Solomon suspected in this request an aspiration to the throne, and therefore caused him to be put to death (1 Kings 2:17-25).

person:abishai_50.name: Abishai
person:abishai_50.title: Abishai
person:abishai_50.summary: Father of (i.e., “desirous of”) a gift, the eldest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was the brother of Joab and Asahel (2 Sam. 2:18; 1 Chr. 2:16). Abishai was the only one who accompanied David when he went to the camp of Saul and took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster (1 Sam. 26:5-12). He had the command of one of the three divisions of David’s army at the battle with Absalom (2 Sam. 18:2, 5, 12). He slew the Philistine giant Ishbi-benob, who threatened David’s life (2 Sam. 21:15-17). He was the chief of the second rank of the three “mighties” (2 Sam. 23:18, 19; 1 Chr. 11:20, 21); and on one occasion withstood 300 men, and slew them with his own spear (2 Sam. 23:18). …

person:abishua_51.name: Abishua
person:abishua_51.title: Abishua
person:abishua_51.summary: The son of Phinehas the high priest (1 Chr. 6:4, 5, 50; Ezra 7:5).

person:abishur_53.name: Abishur
person:abishur_53.title: Abishur
person:abishur_53.summary: Father of the wall; i.e., “mason”, one of the two sons of Shammai of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 29).

person:abital_54.name: Abital
person:abital_54.title: Abital
person:abital_54.summary: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).

person:abitub_55.name: Abitub
person:abitub_55.title: Abitub
person:abitub_55.summary: Father of goodness, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:11).

person:abiud_56.name: Abiud
person:abiud_56.title: Abiud
person:abiud_56.summary: A descendant of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim (Matt. 1:13, “Abiud”); called also Juda (Luke 3:26), and Obadiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

person:abner_57.name: Abner
person:abner_57.title: Abner
person:abner_57.summary: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25). He first introduced David to the court of Saul after the victory over Goliath (1 Sam. 17:57). After the death of Saul, David was made king over Judah, and reigned in Hebron. Among the other tribes there was a feeling of hostility to Judah; and Abner, at the head of Ephraim, fostered this hostility in the interest of the house of Saul, whose son Ish-bosheth he caused to be proclaimed king (2 Sam. 2:8). A state of war existed between these two kings. …

person:abraham_58.name: Abraham
person:abraham_58.title: Abraham
person:abraham_58.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea. He then, with his father and his family and household, quitted the city of Ur, in which he had hitherto dwelt, and went some 300 miles north to Haran, where he abode fifteen years. The cause of his migration was a call from God (Acts 7:2-4). There is no mention of this first call in the Old Testament; it is implied, however, in Gen. 12. While they tarried at Haran, Terah died at the age of 205 years. …

person:absalom_59.name: Absalom
person:absalom_59.title: Absalom
person:absalom_59.summary: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26). The first public act of his life was the blood-revenge he executed against Amnon, David’s eldest son, who had basely wronged Absalom’s sister Tamar. This revenge was executed at the time of the festivities connected with a great sheep-shearing at Baal-hazor. David’s other sons fled from the place in horror, and brought the tidings of the death of Amnon to Jerusalem. Alarmed for the consequences of the act, Absalom fled to his grandfather at Geshur, and there abode for three years (2 Sam. …

person:achaicus_60.name: Achaicus
person:achaicus_60.title: Achaicus
person:achaicus_60.summary: (1 Cor. 16:17), one of the members of the church of Corinth who, with Fortunatus and Stephanas, visited Paul while he was at Ephesus, for the purpose of consulting him on the affairs of the church. These three probably were the bearers of the letter from Corinth to the apostle to which he alludes in 1 Cor. 7:1.

person:achan_61.name: Achan
person:achan_61.title: Achan
person:achan_61.summary: Called also Achar, i.e., one who troubles (1 Chr. 2:7), in commemoration of his crime, which brought upon him an awful destruction (Josh. 7:1). On the occasion of the fall of Jericho, he seized, contrary to the divine command, an ingot of gold, a quantity of silver, and a costly Babylonish garment, which he hid in his tent. Joshua was convinced that the defeat which the Israelites afterwards sustained before Ai was a proof of the divine displeasure on account of some crime, and he at once adopted means by the use of the lot for discovering the criminal. It was then found that Achan was guilty, and he was stoned to death in the valley of Achor. …

person:achbor_63.name: Achbor
person:achbor_63.title: Achbor
person:achbor_63.summary: The son of Micah, one of those whom Josiah sent to the prophetess Huldah to ascertain from her the meaning of the recently discovered book of the law (2 Chr. 34:20). He is called Achbor in 2 Kings 22:12.

person:achish_66.name: Achish
person:achish_66.title: Achish
person:achish_66.summary: The king with whom David sought refuge when he fled from Saul (1 Sam. 21:10-15). He is called Abimelech in the superscription of Ps. 34. It was probably this same king to whom David a second time repaired at the head of a band of 600 warriors, and who assigned him Ziklag, whence he carried on war against the surrounding tribes (1 Sam. 27:5-12). Achish had great confidence in the valour and fidelity of David (1 Sam. 28:1, 2), but at the instigation of his courtiers did not permit him to go up to battle along with the Philistine hosts (1 Sam. 29:2-11). David remained with Achish a year and four months.

person:achsah_68.name: Achsah
person:achsah_68.title: Achsah
person:achsah_68.summary: Anklet, Caleb’s only daughter (1 Chr. 2:49). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher. This was done by Othniel (q.v.), who accordingly obtained her as his wife (Josh. 15:16-19; Judg. 1:9-15).

person:adah_69.name: Adah
person:adah_69.title: Adah (wife of Lamech)
person:adah_69.summary: The first of Lamech’s two wives, and the mother of Jabal and Jubal (Gen. 4:19, 20, 23).

person:adah_414.name: Adah
person:adah_414.title: Adah
person:adah_414.summary: The first of Esau’s three wives, the daughter of Elon the Hittite (Gen. 36:2, 4), called also Bashemath (26:34).

person:adam_78.name: Adam
person:adam_78.title: Adam
person:adam_78.summary:
Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses (Gen. 1:27-ch. 5). “God created man [Heb., Adam] in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.”
Adam was absolutely the first man whom God created. He was formed out of the dust of the earth (and hence his name), and God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and gave him dominion over all the lower creatures (Gen. 1:26; 2:7). …

person:adbeel_79.name: Adbeel
person:adbeel_79.title: Adbeel
person:adbeel_79.summary: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).

person:addar_80.name: Addar
person:addar_80.title: Addar
person:addar_80.summary: Ample, splendid, son of Bela (1 Chr. 8:3); called also “Ard” (Gen. 46:21)

person:addi_81.name: Addi
person:addi_81.title: Addi
person:addi_81.summary: Ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

person:adiel_83.name: Adiel
person:adiel_83.title: Adiel
person:adiel_83.summary: A family head of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

person:adina_88.name: Adina
person:adina_88.title: Adina
person:adina_88.summary: Slender, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:42), a Reubenite.

person:adino_89.name: Adino
person:adino_89.title: Adino
person:adino_89.summary: The Eznite, one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:8).

person:adnah_94.name: Adnah
person:adnah_94.title: Adnah
person:adnah_94.summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

person:adnah_95.name: Adnah
person:adnah_95.title: Adnah
person:adnah_95.summary: A general under Jehoshaphat, chief over 300,000 men (2 Chr. 17:14).

person:adonijah_97.name: Adonijah
person:adonijah_97.title: Adonijah
person:adonijah_97.summary: The fourth son of David (2 Sam. 3:4). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne. But Solomon, a younger brother, was preferred to him. Adonijah, however, when his father was dying, caused himself to be proclaimed king. But Nathan and Bathsheba induced David to give orders that Solomon should at once be proclaimed and admitted to the throne. Adonijah fled and took refuge at the altar, and received pardon for his conduct from Solomon on the condition that he showed himself “a worthy man” (1 Kings 1:5-53). He afterwards made a second attempt to gain the throne, but was seized and put to death (1 Kings 2:13-25).

person:adonijah_98.name: Adonijah
person:adonijah_98.title: Adonijah
person:adonijah_98.summary: A Levite sent with the princes to teach the book of the law to the inhabitants of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:adonijah_99.name: Adonijah
person:adonijah_99.title: Adonijah
person:adonijah_99.summary: One of the “chiefs of the people” after the Captivity (Neh. 10:16).

person:adonikam_100.name: Adonikam
person:adonikam_100.title: Adonikam
person:adonikam_100.summary: Whom the Lord sets up, one of those “which came with Zerubbabel” (Ezra 2:13). His “children,” or retainers, to the number of 666, came up to Jerusalem (8:13).

person:adoniram_102.name: Adoniram
person:adoniram_102.title: Adoniram
person:adoniram_102.summary: One who was “over the tribute;” i.e., “over the levy.” He was stoned by the Israelites after they had revolted from Rehoboam (2 Chr. 10:18). Called also Adoram (2 Sam. 20:24) and Adoniram (1 Kings 4:6).

person:adrammelech_103.name: Adrammelech
person:adrammelech_103.title: Adrammelech
person:adrammelech_103.summary: An idol; a form of the sun-god worshipped by the inhabitants of Sepharvaim (2 Kings 17:31), and brought by the Sepharvite colonists into Samaria.

person:adrammelech_104.name: Adrammelech
person:adrammelech_104.title: Adrammelech
person:adrammelech_104.summary: A son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria (2 Kings 19:37; Isa. 37:38).

person:adriel_105.name: Adriel
person:adriel_105.title: Adriel
person:adriel_105.summary: Flock of God, the son of Barzillai, the Meholathite, to whom Saul gave in marriage his daughter Merab (1 Sam. 18:19). The five sons that sprang from this union were put to death by the Gibeonites (2 Sam. 21:8, 9. Here it is said that Michal “brought up” [R.V., “bare”] these five sons, either that she treated them as if she had been their own mother, or that for “Michal” we should read “Merab,” as in 1 Sam. 18:19).

person:agabus_107.name: Agabus
person:agabus_107.title: Agabus
person:agabus_107.summary: A “prophet,” probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He prophesied at Antioch of an approaching famine (Acts 11:27, 28). Many years afterwards he met Paul at Caesarea, and warned him of the bonds and affliction that awaited him at Jerusalem should he persist in going thither (Acts 21:10-12).

person:agag_108.name: Agag
person:agag_108.title: Agag
person:agag_108.summary: A king of the Amalekites referred to by Balaam (Num. 24:7). He lived at the time of the Exodus.

person:agag_109.name: Agag
person:agag_109.title: Agag
person:agag_109.summary: Another king of the Amalekites whom Saul spared unlawfully, but whom Samuel on his arrival in the camp of Saul ordered, in retributive justice (Judg. 1), to be brought out and cut in pieces (1 Sam. 15:8-33. Comp. Ex. 17:11; Num. 14:45).

person:agee_110.name: Agee
person:agee_110.title: Agee
person:agee_110.summary: Fugitive, the father of Shammah, who was one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11)

person:agrippa_111.name: Agrippa
person:agrippa_111.title: Agrippa
person:agrippa_111.summary: Son of the foregoing, was born at Rome, A.D. 27. He was the brother of Bernice and Drusilla. The Emperor Claudius (A.D. 48) invested him with the office of superintendent of the Temple of Jerusalem, and made him governor (A.D. 50) of Chalcis. He was afterwards raised to the rank of king, and made governor over the tetrarchy of Philip and Lysanias (Acts 25:13; 26:2, 7). It was before him that Paul delivered (A.D. 59) his speech recorded in Acts 26. His private life was very profligate. He died (the last of his race) at Rome, at the age of about seventy years, A.D. 100.

person:agur_112.name: Agur
person:agur_112.title: Agur
person:agur_112.summary: Gatherer; the collector, mentioned as author of the sayings in Prov. 30. Nothing is known of him beyond what is there recorded.

person:ahab_113.name: Ahab
person:ahab_113.title: Ahab
person:ahab_113.summary: The son of Omri, whom he succeeded as the seventh king of Israel. His history is recorded in 1 Kings 16-22. His wife was Jezebel (q.v.), who exercised a very evil influence over him. To the calf-worship introduced by Jeroboam he added the worship of Baal. He was severely admonished by Elijah (q.v.) for his wickedness. His anger was on this account kindled against the prophet, and he sought to kill him. He undertook three campaigns against Ben-hadad II., king of Damascus. …

person:ahab_114.name: Ahab
person:ahab_114.title: Ahab
person:ahab_114.summary: A false prophet referred to by Jeremiah (Jer. 29:21), of whom nothing further is known.

person:ahasuerus_117.name: Ahasuerus
person:ahasuerus_117.title: Ahasuerus
person:ahasuerus_117.summary: The son of Darius Hystaspes, the king named in the Book of Esther. He ruled over the kingdoms of Persia, Media, and Babylonia, “from India to Ethiopia.” This was in all probability the Xerxes of profane history, who succeeded his father Darius (B.C. 485). In the LXX. version of the Book of Esther the name Artaxerxes occurs for Ahasuerus. He reigned for twenty-one years (B.C. 486-465). He invaded Greece with an army, it is said, of more than 2,000,000 soldiers, only 5,000 of whom returned with him. Leonidas, with his famous 300, arrested his progress at the Pass of Thermopylae, and then he was defeated disastrously by Themistocles at Salamis. …

person:ahaz_118.name: Ahaz
person:ahaz_118.title: Ahaz
person:ahaz_118.summary: The son and successor of Jotham, king of Judah (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7-9; 2 Chr. 28). He gave himself up to a life of wickedness and idolatry. Notwithstanding the remonstrances and warnings of Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, he appealed for help against Rezin, king of Damascus, and Pekah, king of Israel, who threatened Jerusalem, to Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, to the great injury of his kingdom and his own humilating subjection to the Assyrians (2 Kings 16:7, 9; 15:29). He also introduced among his people many heathen and idolatrous customs (Isa. 8:19; 38:8; 2 Kings 23:12). He died at the age of thirty-five years, after reigning sixteen years (B.C. …

person:ahaziah_120.name: Ahaziah
person:ahaziah_120.title: Ahaziah
person:ahaziah_120.summary: The son and successor of Ahab. He followed the counsels of his mother Jezebel, and imitated in wickedness the ways of his father. In his reign the Moabites revolted from under his authority (2 Kings 3:5-7). He united with Jehoshaphat in an attempt to revive maritime trade by the Red Sea, which proved a failure (2 Chr. 20:35-37). His messengers, sent to consult the god of Ekron regarding his recovery from the effects of a fall from the roof-gallery of his palace, were met on the way by Elijah, who sent them back to tell the king that he would never rise from his bed (1 Kings 22:51; 2 Kings 1:18).

person:ahaziah_121.name: Ahaziah
person:ahaziah_121.title: Ahaziah
person:ahaziah_121.summary: The son of Joram, or Jehoram, and sixth king of Judah. Called Jehoahaz (2 Chr. 21:17; 25:23), and Azariah (2 Chr. 22:6). Guided by his idolatrous mother Athaliah, his reign was disastrous (2 Kings 8:24-29; 9:29). He joined his uncle Jehoram, king of Israel, in an expedition against Hazael, king of Damascus; but was wounded at the pass of Gur when attempting to escape, and had strength only to reach Megiddo, where he died (2 Kings 9:22-28). He reigned only one year.

person:ahiah_128.name: Ahiah
person:ahiah_128.title: Ahiah
person:ahiah_128.summary: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:7, R.V.). In A.V. called “Ahiah.”

person:ahiam_129.name: Ahiam
person:ahiam_129.title: Ahiam
person:ahiam_129.summary: Mother’s brother, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:33; 1 Chr. 11:35).

person:ahiezer_132.name: Ahiezer
person:ahiezer_132.title: Ahiezer
person:ahiezer_132.summary: The chief of the Benjamite slingers that repaired to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

person:ahihud_133.name: Ahihud
person:ahihud_133.title: Ahihud
person:ahihud_133.summary: Name different in Hebrew, meaning brother of Judah. Chief of the tribe of Asher; one of those appointed by Moses to superintend the division of Canaan among the tribe (Num. 34:27).

person:ahihud_134.name: Ahihud
person:ahihud_134.title: Ahihud
person:ahihud_134.summary: A son of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:7).

person:ahijah_135.name: Ahijah
person:ahijah_135.title: Ahijah
person:ahijah_135.summary: A prophet of Shiloh (1 Kings 11:29; 14:2), called the “Shilonite,” in the days of Rehoboam. We have on record two of his remarkable prophecies, 1 Kings 11:31-39, announcing the rending of the ten tribes from Solomon; and 1 Kings 14:6-16, delivered to Jeroboam’s wife, foretelling the death of Abijah the king’s son, the destruction of Jeroboam’s house, and the captivity of Israel “beyond the river.” Jeroboam bears testimony to the high esteem in which he was held as a prophet of God (1 Kings 14:2, 3).

person:ahijah_137.name: Ahijah
person:ahijah_137.title: Ahijah
person:ahijah_137.summary: One of the five sons of Jerahmeel, who was great-grandson of Judah (1 Chr. 2:25).

person:ahijah_138.name: Ahijah
person:ahijah_138.title: Ahijah
person:ahijah_138.summary: A Pelonite, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:36); called also Eliam (2 Sam. 23:34).

person:ahijah_139.name: Ahijah
person:ahijah_139.title: Ahijah
person:ahijah_139.summary: A Levite having charge of the sacred treasury in the temple (1 Chr. 26:20).

person:ahikam_141.name: Ahikam
person:ahikam_141.title: Ahikam
person:ahikam_141.summary: Brother of support = helper, one of the five whom Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah in connection with the discovery of the book of the law (2 Kings 22:12-14; 2 Chr. 34:20). He was the son of Shaphan, the royal secretary, and the father of Gedaliah, governor of Judea after the destruction of Jerusalem by the Babylonians (2 Kings 25:22; Jer. 40:5-16; 43:6). On one occasion he protected Jeremiah against the fury of Jehoiakim (Jer. 26:24). It was in the chamber of another son (Germariah) of Shaphan that Baruch read in the ears of all the people Jeremiah’s roll.

person:ahimaaz_143.name: Ahimaaz
person:ahimaaz_143.title: Ahimaaz
person:ahimaaz_143.summary: The father Ahinoam, the wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

person:ahimaaz_144.name: Ahimaaz
person:ahimaaz_144.title: Ahimaaz
person:ahimaaz_144.summary: The son and successor of Zadok in the office of high priest (1 Chr. 6:8, 53). On the occasion of the revolt of Absalom he remained faithful to David, and was of service to him in conveying to him tidings of the proceedings of Absalom in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 15:24-37; 17:15-21). He was swift of foot, and was the first to carry to David tidings of the defeat of Absalom, although he refrained, from delicacy of feeling, from telling him of his death (2 Sam. 18:19-33).

person:ahiman_146.name: Ahiman
person:ahiman_146.title: Ahiman
person:ahiman_146.summary: One of the three giant Anakim brothers whom Caleb and the spies saw in Mount Hebron (Num. 13:22) when they went in to explore the land. They were afterwards driven out and slain (Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

person:ahiman_147.name: Ahiman
person:ahiman_147.title: Ahiman
person:ahiman_147.summary: One of the guardians of the temple after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:17).

person:ahimelech_126.name: Ahimelech
person:ahimelech_126.title: Ahimelech
person:ahimelech_126.summary: Son of Ahitub (1 Sam. 14:3, 18), Ichabod’s brother; the same probably as Ahimelech, who was high priest at Nob in the reign of Saul (1 Sam. 22:11). Some, however, suppose that Ahimelech was the brother of Ahijah, and that they both officiated as high priests, Ahijah at Gibeah or Kirjath-jearim, and Ahimelech at Nob.

person:ahimelech_149.name: Ahimelech
person:ahimelech_149.title: Ahimelech
person:ahimelech_149.summary: The son of Abiathar, and high priest in the time of David (1 Chr. 18:16). In the parallel passage, 2 Sam. 8:17, we have the name Ahimelech, and Abiathar, the son of Ahimelech. This most authorities consider the more correct reading.

person:ahinadab_151.name: Ahinadab
person:ahinadab_151.title: Ahinadab
person:ahinadab_151.summary: Brother of liberality = liberal, one of the twelve commissariat officers appointed by Solomon in so many districts of his kingdom to raise supplies by monthly rotation for his household. He was appointed to the district of Mahanaim (1 Kings 4:14), east of Jordan.

person:ahinoam_152.name: Ahinoam
person:ahinoam_152.title: Ahinoam
person:ahinoam_152.summary: The daughter of Ahimaaz, and wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

person:ahinoam_153.name: Ahinoam
person:ahinoam_153.title: Ahinoam
person:ahinoam_153.summary: A Jezreelitess, the first wife of David (1 Sam. 25:43; 27:3). She was the mother of Amnon (2 Sam. 3:2). (See 1 Sam. 30:5, 18; 2 Sam. 2:2.)

person:ahio_154.name: Ahio
person:ahio_154.title: Ahio
person:ahio_154.summary: One of the sons of Abinadab the Levite. While Uzzah went by the side of the ark, he walked before it guiding the oxen which drew the cart on which it was carried, after having brought it from his father’s house in Gibeah (1 Chr. 13:7; 2 Sam. 6:3, 4).

person:ahio_155.name: Ahio
person:ahio_155.title: Ahio
person:ahio_155.summary: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:14).

person:ahio_156.name: Ahio
person:ahio_156.title: Ahio
person:ahio_156.summary: One of the sons of Jehiel the Gibeonite (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:37).

person:ahira_157.name: Ahira
person:ahira_157.title: Ahira
person:ahira_157.summary: Brother of evil = unlucky, or my brother is friend, chief of the tribe of Naphtali at the Exodus (Num. 1:15; 2:29).

person:ahishar_161.name: Ahishar
person:ahishar_161.title: Ahishar
person:ahishar_161.summary: Brother of song = singer, the officer who was “over the household” of Solomon (1 Kings 4:6).

person:ahithophel_162.name: Ahithophel
person:ahithophel_162.title: Ahithophel
person:ahithophel_162.summary: Brother of insipidity or impiety, a man greatly renowned for his sagacity among the Jews. At the time of Absalom’s revolt he deserted David (Ps. 41:9; 55:12-14) and espoused the cause of Absalom (2 Sam. 15:12). David sent his old friend Hushai back to Absalom, in order that he might counteract the counsel of Ahithophel (2 Sam. 15:31-37). This end was so far gained that Ahithophel saw he had no longer any influence, and accordingly he at once left the camp of Absalom and returned to Giloh, his native place, where, after arranging his wordly affairs, he hanged himself, and was buried in the sepulchre of his fathers (2 Sam. 17:1-23). He was the type of Judas (Ps. 41:9).

person:ahitub_163.name: Ahitub
person:ahitub_163.title: Ahitub
person:ahitub_163.summary: The son of Phinehas. On the death of his grandfather Eli he succeeded to the office of high priest, and was himself succeeded by his son Ahijah (1 Sam. 14:3; 22:9, 11, 12, 20).

person:ahitub_164.name: Ahitub
person:ahitub_164.title: Ahitub
person:ahitub_164.summary: The father of Zadok, who was made high priest by Saul after the extermination of the family of Ahimelech (1 Chr. 6:7, 8; 2 Sam. 8:17).

person:ahoah_168.name: Ahoah
person:ahoah_168.title: Ahoah
person:ahoah_168.summary: Brotherly, one of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4). He is also called Ahiah (ver. 7) and Iri (1 Chr. 7:7). His descendants were called Ahohites (2 Sam. 23:9, 28).

person:aholiab_170.name: Aholiab
person:aholiab_170.title: Aholiab
person:aholiab_170.summary: Tent of the father, an artist of the tribe of Dan, appointed to the work of preparing materials for the tabernacle (Ex. 31:6; 35:34; 36:1, 2; 38:23).

person:aholibah_171.name: Aholibah
person:aholibah_171.title: Aholibah
person:aholibah_171.summary: My tent is in her, the name of an imaginary harlot, applied symbolically to Jerusalem, because she had abandoned the worship of the true God and given herself up to the idolatries of foreign nations. (Ezek. 23:4, 11, 22, 36, 44).

person:aholibamah_1761.name: Aholibamah
person:aholibamah_1761.title: Aholibamah
person:aholibamah_1761.summary: Jewess, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 26:34), elsewhere called Aholibamah (36:2-14).

person:akan_179.name: Akan
person:akan_179.title: Akan
person:akan_179.summary: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

person:akkub_181.name: Akkub
person:akkub_181.title: Akkub
person:akkub_181.summary: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

person:akkub_182.name: Akkub
person:akkub_182.title: Akkub
person:akkub_182.summary: The head of one of the families of Nethinim (Ezra 2:45).

person:alameth_184.name: Alameth
person:alameth_184.title: Alameth
person:alameth_184.summary: One of the nine sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

person:alemeth_185.name: Alemeth
person:alemeth_185.title: Alemeth
person:alemeth_185.summary: One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz (1 Chr. 8:36).

person:alexander_186.name: Alexander
person:alexander_186.title: Alexander
person:alexander_186.summary: A man whose father, Simon the Cyrenian, bore the cross of Christ (Mark 15:21).

person:alexander_187.name: Alexander
person:alexander_187.title: Alexander (Son of Simon)
person:alexander_187.summary: A relative of Annas the high priest, present when Peter and John were examined before the Sanhedrim (Acts 4:6).

person:alexander_188.name: Alexander
person:alexander_188.title: Alexander (Jew of Ephesus)
person:alexander_188.summary: A Jew of Ephesus who took a prominent part in the uproar raised there by the preaching of Paul (Acts 19:33). The Jews put him forward to plead their cause before the mob. It was probably intended that he should show that he and the other Jews had no sympathy with Paul any more than the Ephesians had. It is possible that this man was the same as the following.

person:alexander_189.name: Alexander
person:alexander_189.title: Alexander
person:alexander_189.summary: A coppersmith who, with Hymenaeus and others, promulgated certain heresies regarding the resurrection (1 Tim. 1:19; 2 Tim. 4:14), and made shipwreck of faith and of a good conscience. Paul excommunicated him (1 Tim. 1:20; comp. 1 Cor. 5:5).

person:allon_190.name: Allon
person:allon_190.title: Allon
person:allon_190.summary: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

person:almodad_191.name: Almodad
person:almodad_191.title: Almodad
person:almodad_191.summary: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

person:alphaeus_192.name: Alphaeus
person:alphaeus_192.title: Alphaeus
person:alphaeus_192.summary: The father of James the Less, the apostle and writer of the epistle (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13), and the husband of Mary (John 19:25). The Hebrew form of this name is Cleopas, or Clopas (q.v.).

person:alphaeus_193.name: Alphaeus
person:alphaeus_193.title: Alphaeus
person:alphaeus_193.summary: The father of Levi, or Matthew (Mark 2:14).

person:amalek_197.name: Amalek
person:amalek_197.title: Amalek
person:amalek_197.summary: Dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau (Gen. 36:12; 1 Chr. 1:36); the chief of an Idumean tribe (Gen. 36:16). His mother was a Horite, a tribe whose territory the descendants of Esau had seized.

person:amariah_198.name: Amariah
person:amariah_198.title: Amariah
person:amariah_198.summary: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:7, 52). He was probably the last of the high priests of Eleazar’s line prior to the transfer of that office to Eli, of the line of Ithamar.

person:amariah_200.name: Amariah
person:amariah_200.title: Amariah
person:amariah_200.summary: A Levite, son of Hebron, of the lineage of Moses (1 Chr. 23:19; 24:23).

person:amariah_201.name: Amariah
person:amariah_201.title: Amariah
person:amariah_201.summary: A “chief priest” who took an active part in the reformation under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 19:11); probably the same as mentioned in 1 Chr. 6:9.

person:amariah_202.name: Amariah
person:amariah_202.title: Amariah
person:amariah_202.summary: One of the high priests in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:15).

person:amasa_207.name: Amasa
person:amasa_207.title: Amasa
person:amasa_207.summary: The son of Abigail, a sister of king David (1 Chr. 2:17; 2 Sam. 17:25). He was appointed by David to command the army in room of his cousin Joab (2 Sam. 19:13), who afterwards treacherously put him to death as a dangerous rival (2 Sam. 20:4-12).

person:amasa_208.name: Amasa
person:amasa_208.title: Amasa
person:amasa_208.summary: A son of Hadlai, and chief of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12) in the reign of Ahaz.

person:amasai_209.name: Amasai
person:amasai_209.title: Amasai
person:amasai_209.summary: A Levite, son of Elkanah, of the ancestry of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:25, 35).

person:amasai_210.name: Amasai
person:amasai_210.title: Amasai
person:amasai_210.summary: The leader of a body of men who joined David in the “stronghold,” probably of Adullam (1 Chr. 12:18).

person:amasai_211.name: Amasai
person:amasai_211.title: Amasai
person:amasai_211.summary: One of the priests appointed to precede the ark with blowing of trumpets on its removal from the house of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 15:24).

person:amasai_212.name: Amasai
person:amasai_212.title: Amasai
person:amasai_212.summary: The father of a Levite, one of the two Kohathites who took a prominent part at the instance of Hezekiah in the cleansing of the temple (2 Chr. 29:12).

person:amasiah_213.name: Amasiah
person:amasiah_213.title: Amasiah
person:amasiah_213.summary: Burden of (i.e., “sustained by”) Jehovah, the “son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the Lord,” a captain over thousands under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:16; comp. Judg. 5:9).

person:amaziah_214.name: Amaziah
person:amaziah_214.title: Amaziah
person:amaziah_214.summary: The son and successor of Joash, and eighth king of the separate kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 14:1-4). He began his reign by punishing the murderers of his father (5-7; 2 Chr. 25:3-5). He was the first to employ a mercenary army of 100,000 Israelite soldiers, which he did in his attempt to bring the Edomites again under the yoke of Judah (2 Chr. 25:5, 6). He was commanded by a prophet of the Lord to send back the mercenaries, which he did (2 Chr. 25:7-10, 13), much to their annoyance. His obedience to this command was followed by a decisive victory over the Edomites (2 Chr. 25:14-16). …

person:amaziah_215.name: Amaziah
person:amaziah_215.title: Amaziah
person:amaziah_215.summary: The father of Joshah, one of the Simeonite chiefs in the time of Hezekiah (1 Chr. 4:34).

person:amaziah_216.name: Amaziah
person:amaziah_216.title: Amaziah
person:amaziah_216.summary: A Levite, son of Hilkiah, of the descendants of Ethan the Merarite (1 Chr. 6:45).

person:amaziah_217.name: Amaziah
person:amaziah_217.title: Amaziah
person:amaziah_217.summary: A priest of the golden calves at Bethel (Amos 7:10-17).

person:amittai_219.name: Amittai
person:amittai_219.title: Amittai
person:amittai_219.summary: True, the father of Jonah the prophet, a native of Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25; Jonah 1:1).

person:ammiel_220.name: Ammiel
person:ammiel_220.title: Ammiel
person:ammiel_220.summary: One of the twelve spies sent by Moses to search the land of Canaan (Num. 13:12). He was one of the ten who perished by the plague for their unfavourable report (Num. 14:37).

person:ammiel_221.name: Ammiel
person:ammiel_221.title: Ammiel
person:ammiel_221.summary: The father of Machir of Lo-debar, in whose house Mephibosheth resided (2 Sam. 9:4, 5; 17:27).

person:ammiel_222.name: Ammiel
person:ammiel_222.title: Ammiel
person:ammiel_222.summary: One of the sons of Obed-edom the Levite (1 Chr. 26:5).

person:ammihud_223.name: Ammihud
person:ammihud_223.title: Ammihud
person:ammihud_223.summary: The father of the Ephraimite chief Elishama, at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53).

person:ammihud_226.name: Ammihud
person:ammihud_226.title: Ammihud
person:ammihud_226.summary: The father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after the murder of Amnon (2 Sam. 13:37).

person:ammihud_227.name: Ammihud
person:ammihud_227.title: Ammihud
person:ammihud_227.summary: The son of Omri, and the father of Uthai (1 Chr. 9:4).

person:amminadab_228.name: Amminadab
person:amminadab_228.title: Amminadab
person:amminadab_228.summary: The father of Nahshon, who was chief of the tribe of Judah (Num. 1:7; 2:3; 7:12, 17; 10:14). His daughter Elisheba was married to Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

person:amminadab_229.name: Amminadab
person:amminadab_229.title: Amminadab
person:amminadab_229.summary: Chief of the 112 descendants of Uzziel the Levite (1 Chr. 15:10, 11).

person:ammishaddai_230.name: Ammishaddai
person:ammishaddai_230.title: Ammishaddai
person:ammishaddai_230.summary: People of the Almighty, the father of Ahiezer, who was chief of the Danites at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:12; 2:25). This is one of the few names compounded with the name of God, Shaddai, “Almighty.”

person:ammizabad_231.name: Ammizabad
person:ammizabad_231.title: Ammizabad
person:ammizabad_231.summary: People of the giver, the son of Benaiah, who was the third and chief captain of the host under David (1 Chr. 27:6).

person:amnon_232.name: Amnon
person:amnon_232.title: Amnon
person:amnon_232.summary: The eldest son of David, by Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Chr. 3:1; 2 Sam. 3:2). Absalom caused him to be put to death for his great crime in the matter of Tamar (2 Sam. 13:28, 29).

person:amnon_233.name: Amnon
person:amnon_233.title: Amnon
person:amnon_233.summary: One of the sons of Shammai, of the children of Ezra (1 Chr. 4:20; comp. 17).

person:amon_235.name: Amon
person:amon_235.title: Amon
person:amon_235.summary: The governor of Samaria in the time of Ahab. The prophet Micaiah was committed to his custody (1 Kings 22:26; 2 Chr. 18:25).

person:amon_236.name: Amon
person:amon_236.title: Amon
person:amon_236.summary:
The son of Manasseh, and fourteenth king of Judah. He restored idolatry, and set up the images which his father had cast down. Zephaniah (1:4; 3:4, 11) refers to the moral depravity prevailing in this king’s reign.
He was assassinated (2 Kings 21:18-26: 2 Chr. 33:20-25) by his own servants, who conspired against him.55

person:amorite_237.name: Amorite
person:amorite_237.title: Amorite
person:amorite_237.summary: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan (Gen. 14:7), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions. On the early Babylonian monuments all Syria, including Palestine, is known as “the land of the Amorites.” The southern slopes of the mountains of Judea are called the “mount of the Amorites” (Deut. 1:7, 19, 20). They seem to have originally occupied the land stretching from the heights west of the Dead Sea (Gen. 14:7) to Hebron (13. Comp. 13:8; Deut. 3:8; 4:46-48), embracing “all Gilead and all Bashan” (Deut. …

person:amos_238.name: Amos
person:amos_238.title: Amos
person:amos_238.summary: Borne; a burden, one of the twelve minor prophets. He was a native of Tekota, the modern Tekua, a town about 12 miles south-east of Bethlehem. He was a man of humble birth, neither a “prophet nor a prophet’s son,” but “an herdman and a dresser of sycomore trees,” R.V. He prophesied in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and was contemporary with Isaiah and Hosea (Amos 1:1; 7:14, 15; Zech. 14:5), who survived him a few years. Under Jeroboam II. the kingdom of Israel rose to the zenith of its prosperity; but that was followed by the prevalence of luxury and vice and idolatry. …

person:amoz_240.name: Amoz
person:amoz_240.title: Amoz
person:amoz_240.summary: Strong, the father of the prophet Isaiah (2 Kings 19:2, 20; 20:1; Isa. 1:1; 2:1). As to his personal history little is positively known. He is supposed by some to have been the “man of God” spoken of in 2 Chr. 25:7, 8.

person:amplias_241.name: Amplias
person:amplias_241.title: Amplias
person:amplias_241.summary: A Roman Christian saluted by Paul (Rom. 16:8).

person:amram_242.name: Amram
person:amram_242.title: Amram
person:amram_242.summary: The son of Kohath, the son of Levi. He married Jochebed, “his father’s sister,” and was the father of Aaron, Miriam, and Moses (Ex. 6:18, 20; Num. 3:19). He died in Egypt at the age of 137 years (Ex. 6:20). His descendants were called Amramites (Num. 3:27; 1 Chr. 26:23).

person:amraphel_244.name: Amraphel
person:amraphel_244.title: Amraphel
person:amraphel_244.summary: King of Shinar, southern Chaldea, one of the confederates of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a war against Sodom and cities of the plain (Gen. 14:1, 4). It is now found that Amraphel (or Ammirapaltu) is the Khammu-rabi whose name appears on recently-discovered monuments. After defeating Arioch (q.v.) he united Babylonia under one rule, and made Babylon his capital.

person:anak_252.name: Anak
person:anak_252.title: Anak
person:anak_252.summary: Long-necked, the son of Arba, father of the Anakim (Josh. 15:13; 21:11, Heb. Anok).

person:anamim_253.name: Anamim
person:anamim_253.title: Anamim
person:anamim_253.summary: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

person:anammelech_254.name: Anammelech
person:anammelech_254.title: Anammelech
person:anammelech_254.summary: One of the gods worshipped by the people of Sepharvaim, who colonized Samaria (2 Kings 17:31). The name means “Anu is king.” It was a female deity representing the moon, as Adrammelech (q.v.) was the male representing the sun.

person:anan_255.name: Anan
person:anan_255.title: Anan
person:anan_255.summary: Cloud, one of the Israelites who sealed the covenant after the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:26).

person:ananias_258.name: Ananias
person:ananias_258.title: Ananias (Husband of Sapphira)
person:ananias_258.summary: One of the members of the church at Jerusalem, who conspired with his wife Sapphira to deceive the brethren, and who fell down and immediately expired after he had uttered the falsehood (Acts 5:5). By common agreement the members of the early Christian community devoted their property to the work of furthering the gospel and of assisting the poor and needy. The proceeds of the possessions they sold were placed at the disposal of the apostles (Acts 4:36, 37). Ananias might have kept his property had he so chosen; but he professed agreement with the brethren in the common purpose, and had of his own accord devoted it all, as he said, to these sacred ends. …

person:ananias_259.name: Ananias
person:ananias_259.title: Ananias (Disciple at Damascus)
person:ananias_259.summary: A Christian at Damascus (Acts 9:10). He became Paul’s instructor; but when or by what means he himself became a Christian we have no information. He was “a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt” at Damascus (22:12).

person:ananias_260.name: Ananias
person:ananias_260.title: Ananias (High Priest)
person:ananias_260.summary: The high priest before whom Paul was brought in the procuratorship of Felix (Acts 23:2, 5, 24). He was so enraged at Paul’s noble declaration, “I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day,” that he commanded one of his attendants to smite him on the mouth. Smarting under this unprovoked insult, Paul quickly replied, “God shall smite thee, thou whited wall.” Being reminded that Ananias was the high priest, to whose office all respect was to be paid, he answered, “I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest” (Acts 23:5). This expression has occasioned some difficulty, as it is scarcely probable that Paul should have been ignorant of so public a fact. …

person:anath_261.name: Anath
person:anath_261.title: Anath
person:anath_261.summary: An answer; i.e., to “prayer”, the father of Shamgar, who was one of the judges of Israel (Judg. 3:31).

person:andrew_264.name: Andrew
person:andrew_264.title: Andrew
person:andrew_264.summary: Manliness, a Greek name; one of the apostles of our Lord. He was of Bethsaida in Galilee (John 1:44), and was the brother of Simon Peter (Matt. 4:18; 10:2). On one occasion John the Baptist, whose disciple he then was, pointing to Jesus, said, “Behold the Lamb of God” (John 1:40); and Andrew, hearing him, immediately became a follower of Jesus, the first of his disciples. After he had been led to recognize Jesus as the Messiah, his first care was to bring also his brother Simon to Jesus. The two brothers seem to have after this pursued for a while their usual calling as fishermen, and did not become the stated attendants of the Lord till after John’s imprisonment (Matt. …

person:andronicus_265.name: Andronicus
person:andronicus_265.title: Andronicus
person:andronicus_265.summary: Man-conquering, a Jewish Christian, the kinsman and fellowprisoner of Paul (Rom. 16:7); “of note among the apostles.”

person:aner_266.name: Aner
person:aner_266.title: Aner
person:aner_266.summary: A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

person:anna_268.name: Anna
person:anna_268.title: Anna
person:anna_268.summary: Grace, an aged widow, the daughter of Phanuel. She was a “prophetess,” like Miriam, Deborah, and Huldah (2 Chr. 34:22). After seven years of married life her husband died, and during her long widowhood she daily attended the temple services. When she was eighty-four years old, she entered the temple at the moment when the aged Simeon uttered his memorable words of praise and thanks to God that he had fulfilled his ancient promise in sending his Son into the world (Luke 2:36, 37).

person:annas_269.name: Annas
person:annas_269.title: Annas
person:annas_269.summary: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas (John 18:13), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Caiaphas (Luke 3:2). By the Mosaic law the high-priesthood was held for life (Num. 3:10); and although Annas had been deposed by the Roman procurator, the Jews may still have regarded him as legally the high priest. Our Lord was first brought before Annas, and after a brief questioning of him (John 18:19-23) was sent to Caiaphas, when some members of the Sanhedrim had met, and the first trial of Jesus took place (Matt. …

person:antipas_270.name: Antipas
person:antipas_270.title: Antipas
person:antipas_270.summary: A “faithful martyr” (Rev. 2:13), of whom nothing more is certainly known.

person:apelles_273.name: Apelles
person:apelles_273.title: Apelles
person:apelles_273.summary: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:10), and styles “approved in Christ.”

person:apollos_276.name: Apollos
person:apollos_276.title: Apollos
person:apollos_276.summary: A Jew “born at Alexandria,” a man well versed in the Scriptures and eloquent (Acts 18:24; R.V., “learned”). He came to Ephesus (about A.D. 49), where he spake “boldly” in the synagogue (18:26), although he did not know as yet that Jesus of Nazareth was the Messiah. Aquila and Priscilla instructed him more perfectly in “the way of God”, i.e., in the knowledge of Christ. He then proceeded to Corinth, where he met Paul (Acts 18:27; 19:1). He was there very useful in watering the good seed Paul had sown (1 Cor. 1:12), and in gaining many to Christ. His disciples were much attached to him (1 Cor. 3:4-7, 22). …

person:apollyon_2.name: Apollyon
person:apollyon_2.title: Apollyon
person:apollyon_2.summary: Destruction, the Hebrew name (equivalent to the Greek Apollyon, i.e., destroyer) of “the angel of the bottomless pit” (Rev. 9:11). It is rendered “destruction” in Job 28:22; 31:12; 26:6; Prov. 15:11; 27:20. In the last three of these passages the Revised Version retains the word “Abaddon.” We may regard this word as a personification of the idea of destruction, or as sheol, the realm of the dead.

person:apphia_278.name: Apphia
person:apphia_278.title: Apphia
person:apphia_278.summary: Increasing, a female Christian at Colosse (Philemon 1:2), supposed by some to have been the wife of Philemon.

person:aquila_279.name: Aquila
person:aquila_279.title: Aquila
person:aquila_279.summary: Eagle, a native of Pontus, by occupation a tent-maker, whom Paul met on his first visit to Corinth (Acts 18:2). Along with his wife Priscilla he had fled from Rome in consequence of a decree (A.D. 50) by Claudius commanding all Jews to leave the city. Paul sojourned with him at Corinth, and they wrought together at their common trade, making Cilician hair-cloth for tents. On Paul’s departure from Corinth after eighteen months, Aquila and his wife accompanied him to Ephesus, where they remained, while he proceeded to Syria (Acts 18:18, 26). When they became Christians we are not informed, but in Ephesus they were (1 Cor. …

person:arad_281.name: Arad
person:arad_281.title: Arad
person:arad_281.summary: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

person:aram_285.name: Aram
person:aram_285.title: Aram (son of Shem)
person:aram_285.summary:
The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).
The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine to the Euphrates. It corresponded generally with the Syria and Mesopotamia of the Greeks and Romans. In Gen. 25:20; 31:20, 24; Deut. 26:5, the word “Syrian” is properly “Aramean” (R.V., marg.). Damascus became at length the capital of the several smaller kingdoms comprehended under the designation “Aram” or “Syria.”

person:aram_286.name: Aram
person:aram_286.title: Aram (son of Kemuel)
person:aram_286.summary:
The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).
The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine to the Euphrates. It corresponded generally with the Syria and Mesopotamia of the Greeks and Romans. In Gen. 25:20; 31:20, 24; Deut. 26:5, the word “Syrian” is properly “Aramean” (R.V., marg.). Damascus became at length the capital of the several smaller kingdoms comprehended under the designation “Aram” or “Syria.”

person:aran_288.name: Aran
person:aran_288.title: Aran
person:aran_288.summary: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

person:archelaus_291.name: Archelaus
person:archelaus_291.title: Archelaus
person:archelaus_291.summary: Ruler of the people, son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, a Samaritan woman. He was educated along with his brother Antipas at Rome. He inherited from his father a third part of his kingdom viz., Idumea, Judea, and Samaria, and hence is called “king” (Matt. 2:22). It was for fear of him that Joseph and Mary turned aside on their way back from Egypt. Till a few days before his death Herod had named Antipas as his successor, but in his last moments he named Archelaus.

person:archippus_292.name: Archippus
person:archippus_292.title: Archippus
person:archippus_292.summary: Master of the horse, a “fellow-soldier” of Paul’s (Philemon 1:2), whom he exhorts to renewed activity (Col. 4:17). He was a member of Philemon’s family, probably his son.

person:ard_294.name: Ard
person:ard_294.title: Ard
person:ard_294.summary: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin (Num. 26:38-40). In 1 Chr. 8:3 he is called Addar. His descendants are mentioned in Num. 26:40.

person:ardon_295.name: Ardon
person:ardon_295.title: Ardon
person:ardon_295.summary: Descendant, the last of the three sons of Caleb by his first wife Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

person:aretas_297.name: Aretas
person:aretas_297.title: Aretas
person:aretas_297.summary: The father-in-law of Herod Antipas, and king of Arabia Petraea. His daughter returned to him on the occasion of her husband’s entering into an adulterous alliance with Herodias, the wife of Herod-Philip, his half-brother (Luke 3:19, 20; Mark 6:17; Matt. 14:3). This led to a war between Aretas and Herod Antipas. Herod’s army was wholly destroyed (A.D. 36). Aretas, taking advantage of the complications of the times on account of the death of the Emperor Tiberius (A.D. 37), took possession of Damascus (2 Cor. 11:32; comp. Acts 9:25). At this time Paul returned to Damascus from Arabia.

person:arieh_301.name: Arieh
person:arieh_301.title: Arieh
person:arieh_301.summary: The lion, the name of one of the body-guard slain with Pekahiah at Samaria (2 Kings 15:25) by the conspirator Pekah.

person:ariel_302.name: Ariel
person:ariel_302.title: Ariel
person:ariel_302.summary: One of the chief men sent by Ezra to procure Levites for the sanctuary (Ezra 8:16).

person:arioch_303.name: Arioch
person:arioch_303.title: Arioch (king of Ellasar)
person:arioch_303.summary: A king of Ellasar who was confederate with Chedorlamer (Gen. 14:1, 9). The tablets recently discovered by Mr. Pinches (see CHALDEA) show the true reading is Eri-Aku of Larsa. This Elamite name meant “servant of the moon-god.” It was afterwards changed into Rimsin, “Have mercy, O moon-god.”

person:aristarchus_306.name: Aristarchus
person:aristarchus_306.title: Aristarchus
person:aristarchus_306.summary: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2). He was Paul’s “fellow-prisoner” at Rome (Col. 4:10; Philemon 1:24).

person:arkite_308.name: Arkite
person:arkite_308.title: Arkite
person:arkite_308.summary: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

person:armoni_309.name: Armoni
person:armoni_309.title: Armoni
person:armoni_309.summary: Inhabitant of a fortress, the first-named of the two sons of Saul and Rizpah. He was delivered up to the Gibeonites by David, and hanged by them (2 Sam. 21:8, 9).

person:arphaxad_312.name: Arphaxad
person:arphaxad_312.title: Arphaxad
person:arphaxad_312.summary: Son of Shem, born the year after the Deluge. He died at the age of 438 years (Gen. 11:10-13; 1 Chr. 1:17, 18; Luke 3:36). He dwelt in Mesopotamia, and became, according to the Jewish historian Josephus, the progenitor of the Chaldeans. The tendency is to recognize in the word the name of the country nearest the ancient domain of the Chaldeans. Some regard the word as an Egypticized form of the territorial name of Ur Kasdim, or Ur of the Chaldees.

person:artaxerxes_313.name: Artaxerxes
person:artaxerxes_313.title: Artaxerxes
person:artaxerxes_313.summary: The king who obstructed the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 4:7). He was probably the Smerdis of profane history.

person:artaxerxes_314.name: Artaxerxes
person:artaxerxes_314.title: Artaxerxes
person:artaxerxes_314.summary: The king mentioned in Ezra 7:1, in the seventh year (B.C. 458) of whose reign Ezra led a second colony of Jews back to Jerusalem, was probably Longimanus, who reigned for forty years (B.C. 464-425); the grandson of Darius, who, fourteen years later, permitted Nehemiah to return and rebuild Jerusalem.

person:asa_318.name: Asa
person:asa_318.title: Asa
person:asa_318.summary: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land (1 Kings 15:8-14). The Lord gave him and his land rest and prosperity. It is recorded of him, however, that in his old age, when afflicted, he “sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians” (comp. Jer. 17:5). He died in the forty-first year of his reign, greatly honoured by his people (2 Chr. 16:1-13), and was succeeded by his son Jehoshaphat.

person:asahel_320.name: Asahel
person:asahel_320.title: Asahel
person:asahel_320.summary: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle (2 Sam. 2:18, 19). He is mentioned among David’s thirty mighty men (2 Sam. 23:24; 1 Chr. 11:26). Others of the same name are mentioned (2 Chr. 17:8; 31:13; Ezra 10:15).

person:asahiah_324.name: Asahiah
person:asahiah_324.title: Asahiah
person:asahiah_324.summary:
The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1). He had two sons, who bore symbolical names.
He exercised the functions of his office during the reigns of Uzziah (or Azariah), Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah (1:1). Uzziah reigned fifty-two years (B.C. 810-759), and Isaiah must have begun his career a few years before Uzziah’s death, probably B.C. 762. He lived till the fourteenth year of Hezekiah, and in all likelihood outlived that monarch (who died B.C. …

person:asaph_329.name: Asaph
person:asaph_329.title: Asaph
person:asaph_329.summary: The “recorder” in the time of Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 37).

person:asaph_330.name: Asaph
person:asaph_330.title: Asaph (Levite)
person:asaph_330.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30). The “sons of Asaph,” mentioned in 1 Chr. 25:1, 2 Chr. 20:14, and Ezra 2:41, were his descendants, or more probably a class of poets or singers who recognized him as their master.

person:asaph_332.name: Asaph
person:asaph_332.title: Asaph
person:asaph_332.summary: The “keeper of the king’s forest,” to whom Nehemiah requested from Artaxerxes a “letter” that he might give him timber for the temple at Jerusalem (Neh. 2:8).

person:asenath_335.name: Asenath
person:asenath_335.title: Asenath
person:asenath_335.summary: An Egyptian name, meaning “gift of the sun-god”, daughter of Potipherah, priest of On or Heliopolis, wife of Joseph (Gen. 41:45). She was the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim (50-52; 46:20).

person:asher_337.name: Asher
person:asher_337.title: Asher
person:asher_337.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings. The place of this tribe during the march through the desert was between Dan and Naphtali (Num. 2:27). The boundaries of the inheritance given to it, which contained some of the richest soil in Palestine, and the names of its towns, are recorded in Josh. 19:24-31; Judg. 1:31, 32. Asher and Simeon were the only tribes west of the Jordan which furnished no hero or judge for the nation. …

person:ashkenaz_338.name: Ashkenaz
person:ashkenaz_338.title: Ashkenaz
person:ashkenaz_338.summary: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race. They are mentioned in connection with Minni and Ararat, and hence their original seat must have been in Armenia (Jer. 51:27), probably near the Black Sea, which, from their founder, was first called Axenus, and afterwards the Euxine.

person:ashpenaz_339.name: Ashpenaz
person:ashpenaz_339.title: Ashpenaz
person:ashpenaz_339.summary: The master of the eunuchs of Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:3), the “Rabsaris” of the court. His position was similar to that of the Kislar-aga of the modern Turkish sultans.

person:ashtoreth_341.name: Ashtoreth
person:ashtoreth_341.title: Ashtoreth
person:ashtoreth_341.summary: The moon goddess of the Phoenicians, representing the passive principle in nature, their principal female deity; frequently associated with the name of Baal, the sun-god, their chief male deity (Judg. 10:6; 1 Sam. 7:4; 12:10). These names often occur in the plural (Ashtaroth, Baalim), probably as indicating either different statues or different modifications of the deities. This deity is spoken of as Ashtoreth of the Zidonians. She was the Ishtar of the Accadians and the Astarte of the Greeks (Jer. 44:17; 1 Kings 11:5, 33; 2 Kings 23:13). There was a temple of this goddess among the Philistines in the time of Saul (1 Sam. 31:10). …

person:asnappar_346.name: Asnappar
person:asnappar_346.title: Asnappar
person:asnappar_346.summary:
Probably the same as Assur-bani-pal (Sardanapalos of the Greeks), styled the “great and noble” (Ezra 4:10), was the son and successor (B.C. 668) of Esar-haddon (q.v.). He was “luxurious, ambitious, and cruel, but a magnificent patron of literature.” He formed at Nineveh a library of clay tablets, numbering about 10,000. These are now mostly in the British Museum. They throw much light on the history and antiquities of Assyria.
Assur-bani-pal was a munificent patron of literature, and the conqueror of Elam. Towards the middle of his reign his empire was shaken by a great rebellion headed by his brother in Babylon. …

person:asshur_349.name: Asshur
person:asshur_349.title: Asshur
person:asshur_349.summary: Second son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Gen. 10:11, 12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Num. 24:22, 24; Ezek. 27:23, etc.). In Gen. 2:14 “Assyria” ought to be “Asshur,” which was the original capital of Assyria, a city represented by the mounds of Kalah Sherghat, on the west bank of the Tigris. This city was founded by Bel-kap-kapu about B.C. 1700. At a later date the capital was shifted to Ninua, or Nineveh, now Koyunjik, on the eastern bank of the river.

person:athaliah_359.name: Athaliah
person:athaliah_359.title: Athaliah
person:athaliah_359.summary: The daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, and the wife of Jehoram, king of Judah (2 Kings 8:18), who “walked in the ways of the house of Ahab” (2 Chr. 21:6), called “daughter” of Omri (2 Kings 8:26). On the death of her husband and of her son Ahaziah, she resolved to seat herself on the vacant throne. She slew all Ahaziah’s children except Joash, the youngest (2 Kings 11:1, 2). After a reign of six years she was put to death in an insurrection (2 Kings 11:20; 2 Chr. 21:6; 22:10-12; 23:15), stirred up among the people in connection with Josiah’s being crowned as king.

person:augustus_366.name: Augustus
person:augustus_366.title: Augustus
person:augustus_366.summary: The cognomen of the first Roman emperor, C. Julius Caesar Octavianus, during whose reign Christ was born (Luke 2:1). His decree that “all the world should be taxed” was the divinely ordered occasion of Jesus’ being born, according to prophecy (Micah 5:2), in Bethlehem. This name being simply a title meaning “majesty” or “venerable,” first given to him by the senate (B.C. 27), was borne by succeeding emperors. Before his death (A.D. 14) he associated Tiberius with him in the empire (Luke 3:1), by whom he was succeeded.

person:azariah_376.name: Azariah
person:azariah_376.title: Azariah
person:azariah_376.summary: Son of Ethan, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:8).

person:azariah_380.name: Azariah
person:azariah_380.title: Azariah
person:azariah_380.summary: The son of Oded, a remarkable prophet in the days of Asa (2 Chr. 15:1). He stirred up the king and the people to a great national reformation.

person:azariah_385.name: Azariah
person:azariah_385.title: Azariah
person:azariah_385.summary: High priest in the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:17-20). He was contemporary with the prophets Isaiah, Amos, and Joel.

person:azariah_545.name: Azariah
person:azariah_545.title: Azariah
person:azariah_545.summary: The original name of Abed-nego (Dan. 1:6, 7, 11, 16). He was of the royal family of Judah, and with his other two companions remarkable for his personal beauty and his intelligence as well as piety.

person:azaziah_547.name: Azaziah
person:azaziah_547.title: Azaziah
person:azaziah_547.summary: One of the Levitical harpers in the temple (1 Chr. 15:21).

person:azaziah_548.name: Azaziah
person:azaziah_548.title: Azaziah
person:azaziah_548.summary: The father of Hoshea, who was made ruler over the Ephraimites (1 Chr. 27:20).

person:azaziah_549.name: Azaziah
person:azaziah_549.title: Azaziah
person:azaziah_549.summary: One who had charge of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13).

person:azel_551.name: Azel
person:azel_551.title: Azel
person:azel_551.summary: Noble, a descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43, 44).

person:azmaveth_555.name: Azmaveth
person:azmaveth_555.title: Azmaveth
person:azmaveth_555.summary: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:31).

person:azmaveth_558.name: Azmaveth
person:azmaveth_558.title: Azmaveth
person:azmaveth_558.summary: An overseer over the royal treasury in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:25).

person:azubah_567.name: Azubah
person:azubah_567.title: Azubah
person:azubah_567.summary: The daughter of Shilhi, and mother of king Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42).

person:azur_569.name: Azur
person:azur_569.title: Azur
person:azur_569.summary: The father of Hananiah, a false prophet (Jer. 28:1).

person:azzur_572.name: Azzur
person:azzur_572.title: Azzur
person:azzur_572.summary: One of those who sealed the covenant with Jehovah on the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:17).

person:baal_573.name: Baal
person:baal_573.title: Baal
person:baal_573.summary: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17). Baal is identified with Molech (Jer. 19:5). It was known to the Israelites as Baal-peor (Num. 25:3; Deut. 4:3), was worshipped till the time of Samuel (1 Sam 7:4), and was afterwards the religion of the ten tribes in the time of Ahab (1 Kings 16:31-33; 18:19, 22). It prevailed also for a time in the kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 8:27; comp. 11:18; 16:3; 2 Chr. 28:2), till finally put an end to by the severe discipline of the Captivity (Zeph. 1:4-6). …

person:baal_575.name: Baal
person:baal_575.title: Baal
person:baal_575.summary: A Benjamite, son of Jehiel, the progenitor of the Gibeonites (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

person:baal-hanan_576.name: Baal-hanan
person:baal-hanan_576.title: Baalhanan
person:baal-hanan_576.summary: A king of Edom, son of Achbor (Gen. 36:38, 39; 1 Chr. 1:49, 50).

person:baal-hanan_577.name: Baal-hanan
person:baal-hanan_577.title: Baalhanan
person:baal-hanan_577.summary: An overseer of “the olive trees and sycomore trees in the low plains” (the Shephelah) under David (1 Chr. 27:28).

person:baal-zebub_579.name: Baal-zebub
person:baal-zebub_579.title: Baal-zebub
person:baal-zebub_579.summary: Fly-lord, the god of the Philistines at Ekron (2 Kings 1:2, 3, 16). This name was given to the god because he was supposed to be able to avert the plague of flies which in that region was to be feared. He was consulted by Ahaziah as to his recovery.

person:baalis_578.name: Baalis
person:baalis_578.title: Baalis
person:baalis_578.summary: King of the Ammonites at the time of the Babylonian captivity (Jer. 40:14). He hired Ishmael to slay Gedaliah who had been appointed governor over the cities of Judah.

person:baanah_582.name: Baanah
person:baanah_582.title: Baanah
person:baanah_582.summary: One of the two sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, a captain in Saul’s army. He and his brother Rechab assassinated Ishbosheth (2 Sam. 4:2), and were on this account slain by David, and their mutilated bodies suspended over the pool at Hebron (5, 6, 12).

person:baanah_583.name: Baanah
person:baanah_583.title: Baanah
person:baanah_583.summary: The father of Heled, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29; 1 Chr. 11:30).

person:baanah_584.name: Baanah
person:baanah_584.title: Baanah
person:baanah_584.summary: Son of Hushai, another of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:16).

person:baasha_589.name: Baasha
person:baasha_589.title: Baasha
person:baasha_589.summary: Bravery, the third king of the separate kingdom of Israel, and founder of its second dynasty (1 Kings 15; 16; 2 Chr. 16:1-6). He was the son of Ahijah of the tribe of Issachar. The city of Tirzah he made the capital of his kingdom, and there he was buried, after an eventful reign of twenty-four years (1 Kings 15:33). On account of his idolatries his family was exterminated, according to the word of the prophet Jehu (1 Kings 16:3, 4, 10-13).

person:balaam_593.name: Balaam
person:balaam_593.title: Balaam
person:balaam_593.summary: Lord of the people; foreigner or glutton, as interpreted by others, the son of Beor, was a man of some rank among the Midianites (Num. 31:8; comp. 16). He resided at Pethor (Deut. 23:4), in Mesopotamia (Num. 23:7).
