It is evident that though dwelling among idolaters he had some knowledge of the true God; and was held in such reputation that it was supposed that he whom he blessed was blessed, and he whom he cursed was cursed. …

person:baladan_594.name: Baladan
person:baladan_594.title: Baladan
person:baladan_594.summary: He has given a son, the father of the Babylonian king (2 Kings 20:12; Isa. 39:1) Merodach-baladan (q.v.).

person:balak_387.name: Balak
person:balak_387.title: Balak
person:balak_387.summary: Empty; spoiler, a son of Zippor, and king of the Moabites (Num. 22:2, 4). From fear of the Israelites, who were encamped near the confines of his territory, he applied to Balaam (q.v.) to curse them; but in vain (Josh. 24:9).

person:bani_388.name: Bani
person:bani_388.title: Bani
person:bani_388.summary: One of David’s thirty-seven warriors, a Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

person:barabbas_399.name: Barabbas
person:barabbas_399.title: Barabbas
person:barabbas_399.summary: I.e., son of Abba or of a father, a notorious robber whom Pilate proposed to condemn to death instead of Jesus, whom he wished to release, in accordance with the Roman custom (John 18:40; Mark 15:7; Luke 23:19). But the Jews were so bent on the death of Jesus that they demanded that Barabbas should be pardoned (Matt. 27:16-26; Acts 3:14). This Pilate did.

person:barachel_400.name: Barachel
person:barachel_400.title: Barachel
person:barachel_400.summary: Whom God has blessed, a Buzite, the father of Elihu, one of Job’s friends (Job 32:2, 6).

person:barak_401.name: Barak
person:barak_401.title: Barak
person:barak_401.summary: Lightning, the son of Abinoam (Judg. 4:6). At the summons of Deborah he made war against Jabin. She accompanied him into the battle, and gave the signal for the little army to make the attack; in which the host of Jabin was completely routed. The battle was fought (Judg. 4:16) in the plain of Jezreel (q.v.). This deliverance of Israel is commemorated in Judg. 5. Barak’s faith is commended (Heb. 11:32). “The character of Barak, though pious, does not seem to have been heroic. Like Gideon, and in a sense Samson, he is an illustration of the words in Heb. 11:34, ’Out of weakness were made strong.’”

person:bariah_402.name: Bariah
person:bariah_402.title: Bariah
person:bariah_402.summary: Fugitive, one of Shemaiah’s five sons. Their father is counted along with them in 1 Chr. 3:22.

person:barkos_404.name: Barkos
person:barkos_404.title: Barkos
person:barkos_404.summary: Painter, (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55). The father of some of the Nethinim.

person:barnabas_1722.name: Barnabas
person:barnabas_1722.title: Barnabas
person:barnabas_1722.summary: Son of consolation, the surname of Joses, a Levite (Acts 4:36). His name stands first on the list of prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (13:1). Luke speaks of him as a “good man” (11:24). He was born of Jewish parents of the tribe of Levi. He was a native of Cyprus, where he had a possession of land (Acts 4:36, 37), which he sold. His personal appearance is supposed to have been dignified and commanding (Acts 14:11, 12). When Paul returned to Jerusalem after his conversion, Barnabas took him and introduced him to the apostles (9:27). …

person:barsabas_1720.name: Barsabas
person:barsabas_1720.title: Barsabas Justus
person:barsabas_1720.summary: Surnamed Barsabas (Acts 1:23); also called Justus. He was one of those who “companied with the apostles all the time that the Lord Jesus went out and in among them” (Acts 1:21), and was one of the candidates for the place of Judas.

person:bartholomew_405.name: Bartholomew
person:bartholomew_405.title: Bartholomew
person:bartholomew_405.summary: Son of Tolmai, one of the twelve apostles (Matt. 10:3; Acts 1:13); generally supposed to have been the same as Nathanael. In the synoptic gospels Philip and Bartholomew are always mentioned together, while Nathanael is never mentioned; in the fourth gospel, on the other hand, Philip and Nathanael are similarly mentioned together, but nothing is said of Bartholomew. He was one of the disciples to whom our Lord appeared at the Sea of Tiberias after his resurrection (John 21:2). He was also a witness of the Ascension (Acts 1:4, 12, 13). He was an “Israelite indeed” (John 1:47).

person:bartimaeus_406.name: Bartimaeus
person:bartimaeus_406.title: Bartimaeus
person:bartimaeus_406.summary: Son of Timaeus, one of the two blind beggars of Jericho (Mark 10:46; Matt. 20:30). His blindness was miraculously cured on the ground of his faith.

person:baruch_410.name: Baruch
person:baruch_410.title: Baruch
person:baruch_410.summary: The secretary of the prophet Jeremiah (32:12; 36:4). He was of the tribe of Judah (51:59). To him Jeremiah dictated his prophecies regarding the invasion of the Babylonians and the Captivity. These he read to the people from a window in the temple in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 36). …

person:barzillai_411.name: Barzillai
person:barzillai_411.title: Barzillai
person:barzillai_411.summary: A Gileadite of Rogelim who was distinguished for his loyalty to David. He liberally provided for the king’s followers (2 Sam. 17:27). David on his death-bed, remembering his kindness, commended Barzillai’s children to the care of Solomon (1 Kings 2:7).

person:barzillai_412.name: Barzillai
person:barzillai_412.title: Barzillai
person:barzillai_412.summary: A Meholathite, the father of Adriel (2 Sam. 21:8).

person:barzillai_413.name: Barzillai
person:barzillai_413.title: Barzillai
person:barzillai_413.summary: A priest who married a daughter of the preceding (Ezra 2:61).

person:bashemath_1887.name: Bashemath
person:bashemath_1887.title: Bashemath
person:bashemath_1887.summary: The daughter of Ishmael, the last of Esau’s three wives (Gen. 36:3, 4, 13), from whose son Reuel four tribes of the Edomites sprung. She is also called Mahalath (Gen. 28:9). It is noticeable that Esau’s three wives receive different names in the genealogical table of the Edomites (Gen. 36) from those given to them in the history (Gen. 26:34; 28:9).

person:bathsheba_416.name: Bathsheba
person:bathsheba_416.title: Bathsheba
person:bathsheba_416.summary: Daughter of the oath, or of seven, called also Bath-shu’a (1 Chr. 3:5), was the daughter of Eliam (2 Sam. 11:3) or Ammiel (1 Chr. 3:5), and wife of Uriah the Hittite. David committed adultery with her (2 Sam. 11:4, 5; Ps. 51:1). The child born in adultery died (2 Sam. 12:15-19). After her husband was slain (11:15) she was married to David (11:27), and became the mother of Solomon (12:24; 1 Kings 1:11; 2:13). She took a prominent part in securing the succession of Solomon to the throne (1 Kings 1:11, 16-21).

person:bealiah_419.name: Bealiah
person:bealiah_419.title: Bealiah
person:bealiah_419.summary: Whose Lord is Jehovah, a Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes of the sling and bow (1 Chr. 12:5).

person:bedan_427.name: Bedan
person:bedan_427.title: Bedan
person:bedan_427.summary: One of the judges of Israel (1 Sam. 12:11). It is uncertain who he was. Some suppose that Barak is meant, others Samson, but most probably this is a contracted form of Abdon (Judg. 12:13).

person:beeri_432.name: Beeri
person:beeri_432.title: Beeri
person:beeri_432.summary: The father of Judith, one of the wives of Esau (Gen. 26:34), the same as Adah (Gen. 36:2).

person:bela_434.name: Bela
person:bela_434.title: Bela
person:bela_434.summary: The son of Beor, and a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32, 33; 1 Chr. 1:43).

person:bela_436.name: Bela
person:bela_436.title: Bela
person:bela_436.summary: The eldest son of Benjamin (Num. 26:38; “Belah,” Gen. 46:21).

person:belshazzar_437.name: Belshazzar
person:belshazzar_437.title: Belshazzar
person:belshazzar_437.summary: Bel protect the king!, the last of the kings of Babylon (Dan. 5:1). He was the son of Nabonidus by Nitocris, who was the daughter of Nebuchadnezzar and the widow of Nergal-sharezer. When still young he made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and when heated with wine sent for the sacred vessels his “father” (Dan. 5:2), or grandfather, Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from the temple in Jerusalem, and he and his princes drank out of them. In the midst of their mad revelry a hand was seen by the king tracing on the wall the announcement of God’s judgment, which that night fell upon him. At the instance of the queen (i.e., his mother) Daniel was brought in, and he interpreted the writing. …

person:ben-ammi_451.name: Ben-ammi
person:ben-ammi_451.title: Ben-ammi
person:ben-ammi_451.summary: Son of my kindred; i.e., “born of incest”, the son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).

person:ben-hadad_452.name: Ben-hadad
person:ben-hadad_452.title: Ben-hadad
person:ben-hadad_452.summary: The king of Syria whom Asa, king of Judah, employed to invade Israel (1 Kings 15:18).

person:ben-hadad_453.name: Ben-hadad
person:ben-hadad_453.title: Ben-hadad
person:ben-hadad_453.summary: Son of the preceding, also king of Syria. He was long engaged in war against Israel. He was murdered probably by Hazael, by whom he was succeeded (2 Kings 8:7-15), after a reign of some thirty years.

person:ben-hadad_454.name: Ben-hadad
person:ben-hadad_454.title: Ben-hadad
person:ben-hadad_454.summary: King of Damascus, and successor of his father Hazael on the throne of Syria (2 Kings 13:3, 4). His misfortunes in war are noticed by Amos (1:4).

person:benaiah_439.name: Benaiah
person:benaiah_439.title: Benaiah
person:benaiah_439.summary: The son of Jehoiada, chief priest (1 Chr. 27:5). He was set by David over his body-guard of Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Kings 1:32; 1 Chr. 18:17). His exploits are enumerated in 2 Sam. 23:20, 21, 22; 1 Chr. 11:22. He remained faithful to Solomon (1 Kings 1:8, 10, 26), by whom he was raised to the rank of commander-in-chief (1 Kings 2:25, 29, 30, 34, 35; 4:4).

person:benjamin_463.name: Benjamin
person:benjamin_463.title: Benjamin (patriarch)
person:benjamin_463.summary:
The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place. His mother died in giving him birth, and with her last breath named him Ben-oni, son of my pain, a name which was changed by his father into Benjamin. His posterity are called Benjamites (Gen. 49:27; Deut. 33:12; Josh. 18:21).
The tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus was the smallest but one (Num. 1:36, 37; Ps. 68:27). During the march its place was along with Manasseh and Ephraim on the west of the tabernacle. At the entrance into Canaan it counted 45,600 warriors. It has been inferred by some from the words of Jacob (Gen. …

person:beor_465.name: Beor
person:beor_465.title: Beor
person:beor_465.summary: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

person:beor_466.name: Beor
person:beor_466.title: Beor
person:beor_466.summary: The father of Balaam (Num. 22:5; 24:3, 15; 31:8). In 2 Pet. 2:15 he is called Bosor.

person:bera_467.name: Bera
person:bera_467.title: Bera
person:bera_467.summary: Gift, or son of evil, king of Sodom at the time of the invasion of the four kings under Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2, 8, 17, 21).

person:berachah_468.name: Berachah
person:berachah_468.title: Berachah
person:berachah_468.summary: One of the Benjamite warriors, Saul’s brethren, who joined David when at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

person:berechiah_469.name: Berechiah
person:berechiah_469.title: Berechiah
person:berechiah_469.summary: Son of Shimea, and father of Asaph the musician (1 Chr. 6:39; 15:17).

person:berechiah_471.name: Berechiah
person:berechiah_471.title: Berechiah
person:berechiah_471.summary: The fourth of the five sons of Zerubbabel, of the royal family of Judah (1 Chr. 3:20).

person:berechiah_473.name: Berechiah
person:berechiah_473.title: Berechiah
person:berechiah_473.summary: One of the seven Ephraimite chieftains, son of Meshillemoth (2 Chr. 28:12).

person:bered_476.name: Bered
person:bered_476.title: Bered
person:bered_476.summary: A son of Shuthelah, and grandson of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20).

person:beriah_478.name: Beriah
person:beriah_478.title: Beriah
person:beriah_478.summary: One of Asher’s four sons, and father of Heber (Gen. 46:17).

person:beriah_479.name: Beriah
person:beriah_479.title: Beriah
person:beriah_479.summary: A son of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20-23), born after the slaughter of his brothers, and so called by his father “because it went evil with his house” at that time.

person:beriah_480.name: Beriah
person:beriah_480.title: Beriah
person:beriah_480.summary: A Benjamite who with his brother Shema founded Ajalon and expelled the Gittites (1 Chr. 8:13).

person:bernice_482.name: Bernice
person:bernice_482.title: Bernice
person:bernice_482.summary: Bearer of victory, the eldest daughter of Agrippa I., the Herod Agrippa of Acts 12:20. After the early death of her first husband she was married to her uncle Herod, king of Chalcis. After his death (A.D. 40) she lived in incestuous connection with her brother Agrippa II. (Acts 25:13, 23; 26:30). They joined the Romans at the outbreak of the final war between them and the Jews, and lived afterwards at Rome.

person:bethuel_487.name: Bethuel
person:bethuel_487.title: Bethuel
person:bethuel_487.summary: The son of Nahor by Milcah; nephew of Abraham, and father of Rebekah (Gen. 22:22, 23; 24:15, 24, 47). He appears in person only once (24:50).

person:bezaleel_490.name: Bezaleel
person:bezaleel_490.title: Bezaleel
person:bezaleel_490.summary: In the shadow of God; i.e., “under his protection”, the artificer who executed the work of art in connection with the tabernacle in the wilderness (Ex. 31:2; 35:30). He was engaged principally in works of metal, wood, and stone; while Aholiab, who was associated with him and subordinate to him, had the charge of the textile fabrics (36:1, 2; 38:22). He was of the tribe of Judah, the son of Uri, and grandson of Hur (31:2). Mention is made in Ezra 10:30 of another of the same name.

person:bigtha_494.name: Bigtha
person:bigtha_494.title: Bigtha
person:bigtha_494.summary: Garden, or gift of fortune, one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains who had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10).

person:bigthana_495.name: Bigthana
person:bigthana_495.title: Bigthana
person:bigthana_495.summary: One of the eunuchs who “kept the door” in the court of Ahasuerus. With Teresh he conspired against the king’s life. Mordecai detected the conspiracy, and the culprits were hanged (Esther 2:21-23; 6:1-3).

person:bildad_499.name: Bildad
person:bildad_499.title: Bildad
person:bildad_499.summary: Son of contention, one of Job’s friends. He is called “the Shuhite,” probably as belonging to Shuah, a district in Arabia, in which Shuah, the sixth son of Abraham by Keturah, settled (Gen. 25:2). He took part in each of the three controversies into which Job’s friends entered with him (Job 8:1; 18:1; 25:1), and delivered three speeches, very severe and stern in their tone, although less violent than those of Zophar, but more so than those of Eliphaz.

person:bilgah_500.name: Bilgah
person:bilgah_500.title: Bilgah
person:bilgah_500.summary: The head of the fifteenth sacerdotal course for the temple service (1 Chr. 24:14).

person:bilgah_501.name: Bilgah
person:bilgah_501.title: Bilgah
person:bilgah_501.summary: A priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5, 18).

person:bilhah_502.name: Bilhah
person:bilhah_502.title: Bilhah
person:bilhah_502.summary: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob (Gen. 29:29). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen. 30:3-8). Reuben was cursed by his father for committing adultry with her (35:22; 49:4). He was deprived of the birth-right, which was given to the sons of Joseph.

person:bilshan_505.name: Bilshan
person:bilshan_505.title: Bilshan
person:bilshan_505.summary: Son of the tongue; i.e., “eloquent”, a man of some note who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7).

person:birsha_513.name: Birsha
person:birsha_513.title: Birsha
person:birsha_513.summary: Son of wickedness, a king of Gomorrah whom Abraham succoured in the invasion of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

person:blastus_518.name: Blastus
person:blastus_518.title: Blastus
person:blastus_518.summary: Chamberlain to king Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:20). Such persons generally had great influence with their masters.

person:boaz_519.name: Boaz
person:boaz_519.title: Boaz
person:boaz_519.summary: The husband of Ruth, a wealthy Bethlehemite. By the “levirate law” the duty devolved on him of marrying Ruth the Moabitess (Ruth 4:1-13). He was a kinsman of Mahlon, her first husband.

person:buz_529.name: Buz
person:buz_529.title: Buz
person:buz_529.summary: The second son of Nahor and Milcah, and brother of Huz (Gen. 22:21). Elihu was one of his descendants (Job 32:2).

person:buz_530.name: Buz
person:buz_530.title: Buz
person:buz_530.summary: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad (1 Chr. 5:14).

person:caiaphas_532.name: Caiaphas
person:caiaphas_532.title: Caiaphas
person:caiaphas_532.summary: The Jewish high priest (A.D. 27-36) at the beginning of our Lord’s public ministry, in the reign of Tiberius (Luke 3:2), and also at the time of his condemnation and crucifixion (Matt. 26:3, 57; John 11:49; 18:13, 14). He held this office during the whole of Pilate’s administration. His wife was the daughter of Annas, who had formerly been high priest, and was probably the vicar or deputy (Heb. sagan) of Caiaphas. He was of the sect of the Sadducees (Acts 5:17), and was a member of the council when he gave his opinion that Jesus should be put to death “for the people, and that the whole nation perish not” (John 11:50). In these words he unconsciously uttered a prophecy. …

person:cain_533.name: Cain
person:cain_533.title: Cain
person:cain_533.summary: The first-born son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4). He became a tiller of the ground, as his brother Abel followed the pursuits of pastoral life. He was “a sullen, self-willed, haughty, vindictive man; wanting the religious element in his character, and defiant even in his attitude towards God.” It came to pass “in process of time” (marg. “at the end of days”), i.e., probably on the Sabbath, that the two brothers presented their offerings to the Lord. Abel’s offering was of the “firstlings of his flock and of the fat,” while Cain’s was “of the fruit of the ground.” Abel’s sacrifice was “more excellent” (Heb. 11:4) than Cain’s, and was accepted by God. …

person:cainan_534.name: Cainan
person:cainan_534.title: Cainan (antediluvian patriarch)
person:cainan_534.summary: The fourth antediluvian patriarch, the eldest son of Enos. He was 70 years old at the birth of his eldest son Mahalaleel, after which he lived 840 years (Gen. 5:9-14), and was 910 years old when he died. He is also called Kenan (1 Chr. 1:2).

person:cainan_535.name: Cainan
person:cainan_535.title: Cainan (son of Arphaxad)
person:cainan_535.summary: The son of Arphaxad (Luke 3:36). He is nowhere named in the Old Testament. He is usually called the “second Cainan.”

person:calcol_536.name: Calcol
person:calcol_536.title: Calcol
person:calcol_536.summary: (1 Chr. 2:6), sustenance, the same probably as Chalcol (1 Kings 4:31), one of the four sages whom Solomon excelled in wisdom; for “he was wiser than all men.”

person:caleb_537.name: Caleb
person:caleb_537.title: Caleb
person:caleb_537.summary: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus. He was one of the family chiefs of the tribe of Judah. He and Joshua the son of Nun were the only two of the whole number who encouraged the people to go up and possess the land, and they alone were spared when a plague broke out in which the other ten spies perished (Num. 13; 14). All the people that had been numbered, from twenty years old and upward, perished in the wilderness except these two. …

person:caleb_538.name: Caleb
person:caleb_538.title: Caleb
person:caleb_538.summary: One of the three sons of Hezron of the tribe of Judah. He is also called Chelubai (1 Chr. 2:9). His descendants are enumerated (18-20, 42-49).

person:canaan_914.name: Canaan
person:canaan_914.title: Canaan
person:canaan_914.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians. He had eleven sons, who were the founders of as many tribes (10:15-18).

person:candace_916.name: Candace
person:candace_916.title: Candace
person:candace_916.summary:
The queen of the Ethiopians whose “eunuch” or chamberlain was converted to Christianity by the instrumentality of Philip the evangelist (Acts 8:27). The country which she ruled was called by the Greeks Meroe, in Upper Nubia. It was long the centre of commercial intercourse between Africa and the south of Asia, and hence became famous for its wealth (Isa. 45:14).
It is somewhat singular that female sovereignty seems to have prevailed in Ethiopia, the name Candace (compare “Pharaoh,” “Ptolemy,” “Caesar”) being a title common to several successive queens. …

person:carmi_920.name: Carmi
person:carmi_920.title: Carmi
person:carmi_920.summary: The last named of the four sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9).

person:carmi_921.name: Carmi
person:carmi_921.title: Carmi
person:carmi_921.summary: The son of Zimri, and the father of Achan (Josh. 7:1), “the troubler of Israel.”

person:casluhim_923.name: Casluhim
person:casluhim_923.title: Casluhim
person:casluhim_923.summary: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12). Their original seat was probably somewhere in Lower Egypt, along the sea-coast to the south border of Palestine.

person:chedorlaomer_926.name: Chedorlaomer
person:chedorlaomer_926.title: Chedorlaomer
person:chedorlaomer_926.summary: (= Khudur-Lagamar of the inscriptions), king of Elam. Many centuries before the age of Abraham, Canaan and even the Sinaitic peninsula had been conquered by Babylonian kings, and in the time of Abraham himself Babylonia was ruled by a dynasty which claimed sovereignity over Syria and Palestine. The kings of the dynasty bore names which were not Babylonian, but at once South Arabic and Hebrew. The most famous king of the dynasty was Khammu-rabi, who united Babylonia under one rule, and made Babylon its capital. …

person:chemosh_931.name: Chemosh
person:chemosh_931.title: Chemosh
person:chemosh_931.summary: The destroyer, subduer, or fish-god, the god of the Moabites (Num. 21:29; Jer. 48:7, 13, 46). The worship of this god, “the abomination of Moab,” was introduced at Jerusalem by Solomon (1 Kings 11:7), but was abolished by Josiah (2 Kings 23:13). On the “Moabite Stone” (q.v.), Mesha (2 Kings 3:5) ascribes his victories over the king of Israel to this god, “And Chemosh drove him before my sight.”

person:chenaniah_935.name: Chenaniah
person:chenaniah_935.title: Chenaniah
person:chenaniah_935.summary: Whom Jehovah hath made. “Chief of the Levites,” probably a Kohathite (1 Chr. 15:22), and therefore not the same as mentioned in 26:29.

person:chilion_940.name: Chilion
person:chilion_940.title: Chilion
person:chilion_940.summary: The pining one, the younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, and husband of Orpah, Ruth’s sister (Ruth 1:2; 4:9).

person:chloe_943.name: Chloe
person:chloe_943.title: Chloe
person:chloe_943.summary: Verdure, a female Christian (1 Cor. 1:11), some of whose household had informed Paul of the divided state of the Corinthian church. Nothing is known of her.

person:chushan-rishathaim_944.name: Chushan-rishathaim
person:chushan-rishathaim_944.title: Chushan-rishathaim
person:chushan-rishathaim_944.summary: Cush of double wickedness, or governor of two presidencies, the king of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel in the generation immediately following Joshua (Judg. 3:8). We learn from the Tell-el-Amarna tablets that Palestine had been invaded by the forces of Aram-naharaim (A.V., “Mesopotamia”) more than once, long before the Exodus, and that at the time they were written the king of Aram-naharaim was still intriguing in Canaan. It is mentioned among the countries which took part in the attack upon Egypt in the reign of Rameses III. (of the Twentieth Dynasty), but as its king is not one of the princes stated to have been conquered by the Pharaoh, it would seem that he did not actually enter Egypt. …

person:claudia_946.name: Claudia
person:claudia_946.title: Claudia
person:claudia_946.summary: A female Christian mentioned in 2 Tim. 4:21. It is a conjecture having some probability that she was a British maiden, the daughter of king Cogidunus, who was an ally of Rome, and assumed the name of the emperor, his patron, Tiberius Claudius, and that she was the wife of Pudens.

person:claudius_947.name: Claudius
person:claudius_947.title: Claudius (4th Roman Emperor)
person:claudius_947.summary:
The fourth Roman emperor. He succeeded Caligula (A.D. 41). Though in general he treated the Jews, especially those in Asia and Egypt, with great indulgence, yet about the middle of his reign (A.D. 49) he banished them all from Rome (Acts 18:2). In this edict the Christians were included, as being, as was supposed, a sect of Jews. The Jews, however soon again returned to Rome.
During the reign of this emperor, several persecutions of the Christians by the Jews took place in the dominions of Herod Agrippa, in one of which the apostle James was “killed” (12:2). He died A.D. 54.

person:claudius_948.name: Claudius
person:claudius_948.title: Claudius Lysias
person:claudius_948.summary: Claudius Lysias, a Greek who, having obtained by purchase the privilege of Roman citizenship, took the name of Claudius (Acts 21:31-40; 22:28; 23:26).

person:clement_949.name: Clement
person:clement_949.title: Clement
person:clement_949.summary: Mild, a Christian of Philippi, Paul’s “fellow-labourer,” whose name he mentions as “in the book of life” (Phil. 4:3). It was an opinion of ancient writers that he was the Clement of Rome whose name is well known in church history, and that he was the author of an Epistle to the Corinthians, the only known manuscript of which is appended to the Alexandrian Codex, now in the British Museum. It is of some historical interest, and has given rise to much discussion among critics. It makes distinct reference to Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians.

person:cleophas_950.name: Cleophas
person:cleophas_950.title: Cleophas
person:cleophas_950.summary: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18). We know nothing definitely regarding him. It is not certain that he was the Clopas of John 19:25, or the Alphaeus of Matt. 10:3, although he may have been so.

person:conaniah_953.name: Conaniah
person:conaniah_953.title: Conaniah
person:conaniah_953.summary: Whom Jehovah hath set, a Levite placed over the tithes brought into the temple (2 Chr. 35:9).

person:cornelius_956.name: Cornelius
person:cornelius_956.title: Cornelius
person:cornelius_956.summary: A centurion whose history is narrated in Acts 10. He was a “devout man,” and like the centurion of Capernaum, believed in the God of Israel. His residence at Caesrea probably brought him into contact with Jews who communicated to him their expectations regarding the Messiah; and thus he was prepared to welcome the message Peter brought him. He became the first fruit of the Gentile world to Christ. He and his family were baptized and admitted into the Christian church (Acts 10:1, 44-48).

person:coz_958.name: Coz
person:coz_958.title: Coz
person:coz_958.summary: A descendant of Judah. 1 Chr. 4:8, “Coz;” R.V., “Hakkoz.”

person:crescens_960.name: Crescens
person:crescens_960.title: Crescens
person:crescens_960.summary: Increasing, probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He was one of Paul’s assistants (2 Tim. 4:10), probably a Christian of Rome.

person:crispus_961.name: Crispus
person:crispus_961.title: Crispus
person:crispus_961.summary: Curled, the chief of the synagogue at Corinth (Acts 18:8). He was converted and, with his family, baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

person:cush_962.name: Cush
person:cush_962.title: Cush (son of Ham)
person:cush_962.summary: A son, probably the eldest, of Ham, and the father of Nimrod (Gen. 10:8; 1 Chr. 1:10). From him the land of Cush seems to have derived its name. The question of the precise locality of the land of Cush has given rise to not a little controversy. The second river of Paradise surrounded the whole land of Cush (Gen. 2:13, R.V.). The term Cush is in the Old Testament generally applied to the countries south of the Israelites. It was the southern limit of Egypt (Ezek. 29:10, A.V. “Ethiopia,” Heb. Cush), with which it is generally associated (Ps. 68:31; Isa. 18:1; Jer. 46:9, etc.). It stands also associated with Elam (Isa. 11:11), with Persia (Ezek. 38:5), and with the Sabeans (Isa. 45:14). …

person:cyrenius_967.name: Cyrenius
person:cyrenius_967.title: Cyrenius
person:cyrenius_967.summary: The Grecized form of Quirinus. His full name was Publius Sulpicius Quirinus. Recent historical investigation has proved that Quirinus was governor of Cilicia, which was annexed to Syria at the time of our Lord’s birth. Cilicia, which he ruled, being a province of Syria, he is called the governor, which he was de jure, of Syria. Some ten years afterwards he was appointed governor of Syria for the second time. During his tenure of office, at the time of our Lord’s birth (Luke 2:2), a “taxing” (R.V., “enrolment;” i.e., a registration) of the people was “first made;” i.e., was made for the first time under his government.

person:cyrus_968.name: Cyrus
person:cyrus_968.title: Cyrus
person:cyrus_968.summary:
(Heb. Ko’resh), the celebrated “King of Persia” (Elam) who was conqueror of Babylon, and issued the decree of liberation to the Jews (Ezra 1:1, 2). He was the son of Cambyses, the prince of Persia, and was born about B.C. 599. In the year B.C. 559 he became king of Persia, the kingdom of Media being added to it partly by conquest. Cyrus was a great military leader, bent on universal conquest. Babylon fell before his army (B.C. 538) on the night of Belshazzar’s feast (Dan. 5:30), and then the ancient dominion of Assyria was also added to his empire (cf., “Go up, O Elam”, Isa. 21:2).
Hitherto the great kings of the earth had only oppressed the Jews. Cyrus was to them as a “shepherd” (Isa. …

person:dagon_969.name: Dagon
person:dagon_969.title: Dagon
person:dagon_969.summary: Little fish; diminutive from dag = a fish, the fish-god; the national god of the Philistines (Judg. 16:23). This idol had the body of a fish with the head and hands of a man. It was an Assyrio-Babylonian deity, the worship of which was introduced among the Philistines through Chaldea. The most famous of the temples of Dagon were at Gaza (Judg. 16:23-30) and Ashdod (1 Sam. 5:1-7).

person:damaris_972.name: Damaris
person:damaris_972.title: Damaris
person:damaris_972.summary: A heifer, an Athenian woman converted to Christianity under the preaching of Paul (Acts 17:34). Some have supposed that she may have been the wife of Dionysius the Areopagite.

person:dan_973.name: Dan
person:dan_973.title: Dan
person:dan_973.summary:
The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni). The blessing pronounced on him by his father was, “Dan shall judge his people” (49:16), probably in allusion to the judgeship of Samson, who was of the tribe of Dan.
The tribe of Dan had their place in the march through the wilderness on the north side of the tabernacle (Num. 2:25, 31; 10:25). It was the last of the tribes to receive a portion in the Land of Promise. Its position and extent are described in Josh. 19:40-48.
The territory of Dan extended from the west of that of Ephraim and Benjamin to the sea. It was a small territory, but was very fertile. …

person:daniel_939.name: Daniel
person:daniel_939.title: Daniel
person:daniel_939.summary: David’s second son, “born unto him in Hebron, of Abigail the Carmelitess” (1 Chr. 3:1). He is called also Chileab (2 Sam. 3:3).

person:daniel_975.name: Daniel
person:daniel_975.title: Daniel
person:daniel_975.summary: Beltis protect the king!, the Chaldee name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:7).

person:darda_977.name: Darda
person:darda_977.title: Darda
person:darda_977.summary: Pearl of wisdom, one of the four who were noted for their wisdom, but whom Solomon excelled (1 Kings 4:31).

person:darius_979.name: Darius
person:darius_979.title: Darius
person:darius_979.summary: Darius the Persian (Neh. 12:22) was probably the Darius II. (Ochus or Nothus) of profane history, the son of Artaxerxes Longimanus, who was the son and successor of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). There are some, however, who think that the king here meant was Darius III. (Codomannus), the antagonist of Alexander the Great (B.C. 336-331).

person:dathan_982.name: Dathan
person:dathan_982.title: Dathan
person:dathan_982.summary: Welled; belonging to a fountain, a son of Eliab, a Reubenite, who joined Korah (q.v.) in his conspiracy, and with his accomplices was swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1; 26:9; Deut. 11:6; Ps. 106:17).

person:daughter_of_pharaoh_988.name: Daughter of Pharaoh
person:daughter_of_pharaoh_988.title: Daughter of Pharaoh
person:daughter_of_pharaoh_988.summary: The princess who adopted the infant Moses (q.v.), Ex. 2:10. She is twice mentioned in the New Testament (Acts 7:21: Heb. 11:24). It would seem that she was alive and in some position of influence about the court when Moses was compelled to flee from Egypt, and thus for forty years he had in some way been under her influence. She was in all probability the sister of Rameses, and the daughter of Seti I. Josephus calls her Thermuthis. It is supposed by some that she was Nefert-ari, the wife as well as sister of Rameses. The mummy of this queen was among the treasures found at Deir-el-Bahari.

person:daughter_of_pharaoh_989.name: Daughter of Pharaoh
person:daughter_of_pharaoh_989.title: Daughter of Pharaoh
person:daughter_of_pharaoh_989.summary: The wife of Solomon (1 Kings 3:1). This is the first reference since the Exodus to any connection of Israel with Egypt.

person:david_994.name: David
person:david_994.title: David
person:david_994.summary:
Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded. Some think she was the Nahash of 2 Sam. 17:25. As to his personal appearance, we only know that he was red-haired, with beautiful eyes and a fair face (1 Sam. 16:12; 17:42).
His early occupation was that of tending his father’s sheep on the uplands of Judah. From what we know of his after history, doubtless he frequently beguiled his time, when thus engaged, with his shepherd’s flute, while he drank in the many lessons taught him by the varied scenes spread around him. …

person:debir_995.name: Debir
person:debir_995.title: Debir
person:debir_995.summary: The king of Eglon, one of the five Canaanitish kings who were hanged by Joshua (Josh. 10:3, 23) after the victory at Gibeon. These kings fled and took refuge in a cave at Makkedah. Here they were kept confined till Joshua returned from the pursuit of their discomfited armies, when he caused them to be brought forth, and “Joshua smote them, and slew them, and hanged them on five trees” (26).

person:deborah_997.name: Deborah
person:deborah_997.title: Deborah
person:deborah_997.summary: A prophetess, “wife” (woman?) of Lapidoth. Jabin, the king of Hazor, had for twenty years held Israel in degrading subjection. The spirit of patriotism seemed crushed out of the nation. In this emergency Deborah roused the people from their lethargy. Her fame spread far and wide. She became a “mother in Israel” (Judg. 4:6, 14; 5:7), and “the children of Israel came up to her for judgment” as she sat in her tent under the palm tree “between Ramah and Bethel.” Preparations were everywhere made by her direction for the great effort to throw off the yoke of bondage. …

person:dedan_998.name: Dedan
person:dedan_998.title: Dedan (son of Raamah)
person:dedan_998.summary: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15. They probably settled among the sons of Cush, on the north-west coast of the Persian Gulf.

person:dedan_999.name: Dedan
person:dedan_999.title: Dedan (son of Jokshan)
person:dedan_999.summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

person:delaiah_1001.name: Delaiah
person:delaiah_1001.title: Delaiah
person:delaiah_1001.summary: The head of the twenty-third division of the priestly order (1 Chr. 24:18).

person:delaiah_1002.name: Delaiah
person:delaiah_1002.title: Delaiah
person:delaiah_1002.summary: The head of one of the bands of exiles that returned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60; Neh. 7:62).

person:delaiah_1004.name: Delaiah
person:delaiah_1004.title: Delaiah
person:delaiah_1004.summary: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

person:delilah_1005.name: Delilah
person:delilah_1005.title: Delilah
person:delilah_1005.summary: Languishing, a Philistine woman who dwelt in the valley of Sorek (Judg. 16:4-20). She was bribed by the “lords of the Philistines” to obtain from Samson the secret of his strength and the means of overcoming it (Judg. 16:4-18). She tried on three occasions to obtain from him this secret in vain. On the fourth occasion she wrung it from him. She made him sleep upon her knees, and then called the man who was waiting to help her; who “cut off the seven locks of his head,” and so his “strength went from him.”

person:demas_1006.name: Demas
person:demas_1006.title: Demas
person:demas_1006.summary: A companion and fellow-labourer of Paul during his first imprisonment at Rome (Philemon 1:24; Col. 4:14). It appears, however, that the love of the world afterwards mastered him, and he deserted the apostle (2 Tim. 4:10).

person:demetrius_1007.name: Demetrius
person:demetrius_1007.title: Demetrius
person:demetrius_1007.summary: A silversmith at Ephesus, whose chief occupation was to make “silver shrines for Diana” (q.v.), Acts 19:24, i.e., models either of the temple of Diana or of the statue of the goddess. This trade brought to him and his fellow-craftsmen “no small gain,” for these shrines found a ready sale among the countless thousands who came to this temple from all parts of Asia Minor. This traffic was greatly endangered by the progress of the gospel, and hence Demetrius excited the tradesmen employed in the manufacture of these shrines, and caused so great a tumult that “the whole city was filled with confusion.”

person:diana_1008.name: Diana
person:diana_1008.title: Diana
person:diana_1008.summary: So called by the Romans; called Artemis by the Greeks, the “great” goddess worshipped among heathen nations under various modifications. Her most noted temple was that at Ephesus. It was built outside the city walls, and was one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. “First and last it was the work of 220 years; built of shining marble; 342 feet long by 164 feet broad; supported by a forest of columns, each 56 feet high; a sacred museum of masterpieces of sculpture and painting. At the centre, hidden by curtains, within a gorgeous shrine, stood the very ancient image of the goddess, on wood or ebony reputed to have fallen from the sky. …

person:diblaim_1009.name: Diblaim
person:diblaim_1009.title: Diblaim
person:diblaim_1009.summary: Doubled cakes, the mother of Gomer, who was Hosea’s wife (Hos. 1:3).

person:dinah_1012.name: Dinah
person:dinah_1012.title: Dinah
person:dinah_1012.summary: Judged; vindicated, daughter of Jacob by Leah, and sister of Simeon and Levi (Gen. 30:21). She was seduced by Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite chief, when Jacob’s camp was in the neighbourhood of Shechem. This led to the terrible revenge of Simeon and Levi in putting the Shechemites to death (Gen. 34). Jacob makes frequent reference to this deed of blood with abhorrence and regret (Gen. 34:30; 49:5-7). She is mentioned among the rest of Jacob’s family that went down into Egypt (Gen. 46:8, 15).

person:dionysius_1013.name: Dionysius
person:dionysius_1013.title: Dionysius
person:dionysius_1013.summary: The Areopagite, one of Paul’s converts at Athens (Acts 17:34).

person:dishan_1015.name: Dishan
person:dishan_1015.title: Dishan
person:dishan_1015.summary: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

person:dodanim_1018.name: Dodanim
person:dodanim_1018.title: Dodanim
person:dodanim_1018.summary: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim (q.v.). In 1 Chr. 1:7, they are called Rodanim. The LXX. and the Samaritan Version also read Rhodii, whence some have concluded that the Rhodians, the inhabitants of the island of Rhodes, are meant.

person:dodo_1021.name: Dodo
person:dodo_1021.title: Dodo
person:dodo_1021.summary: An Ahohite, father of Eleazar, who was one of David’s three heroes (2 Sam. 23:9; 1 Chr. 11:12). He was the same with Dodai mentioned in 1 Chr. 27:4.

person:dodo_1022.name: Dodo
person:dodo_1022.title: Dodo
person:dodo_1022.summary: A Bethlehemite, and father of Elhanan, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:24).

person:doeg_1023.name: Doeg
person:doeg_1023.title: Doeg
person:doeg_1023.summary: Fearful, an Edomite, the chief overseer of Saul’s flocks (1 Sam. 21:7). At the command of Saul he slew the high priest Ahimelech (q.v.) at Nob, together with all the priests to the number of eighty-five persons. (Comp. Ps. 52, title.)

person:dorcas_2810.name: Dorcas
person:dorcas_2810.title: Dorcas
person:dorcas_2810.summary: (in Greek called Dorcas), gazelle, a disciple at Joppa. She was distinguished for her alms-deeds and good works. Peter, who was sent for from Lydda on the occasion of her death, prayed over the dead body, and said, “Tabitha, arise.” And she opened her eyes and sat up; and Peter “gave her his hand, and raised her up; and calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive” (Acts 9:36-43).

person:drusilla_1024.name: Drusilla
person:drusilla_1024.title: Drusilla
person:drusilla_1024.summary: Third and youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:1-4, 20-23). Felix, the Roman procurator of Judea, induced her to leave her husband, Azizus, the king of Emesa, and become his wife. She was present with Felix when Paul reasoned of “righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come” (Acts 24:24). She and her son perished in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius, A.D. 79.

person:ebal_1026.name: Ebal
person:ebal_1026.title: Ebal (son of Shobal)
person:ebal_1026.summary: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

person:ebal_2227.name: Ebal
person:ebal_2227.title: Ebal (son of Joktan)
person:ebal_2227.summary: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

person:ebed_1027.name: Ebed
person:ebed_1027.title: Ebed
person:ebed_1027.summary: Slave, the father of Gaal, in whom the men of Shechem “put confidence” in their conspiracy against Abimelech (Judg. 9:26, 26, 30, 31).

person:eber_1030.name: Eber
person:eber_1030.title: Eber (Heber)
person:eber_1030.summary: The third post-duluvian patriach after Shem (Gen. 10:24; 11:14). He is regarded as the founder of the Hebrew race (10:21; Num. 24:24). In Luke 3:35 he is called Heber.

person:eber_1031.name: Eber
person:eber_1031.title: Eber (a Benjamite)
person:eber_1031.summary: The oldest of the three sons of Elpaal the Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:12).

person:eber_1032.name: Eber
person:eber_1032.title: Eber (Amok Family Head)
person:eber_1032.summary: The head of the priestly family of Amok in the time of Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:20).

person:ebiasaph_19.name: Ebiasaph
person:ebiasaph_19.title: Ebiasaph
person:ebiasaph_19.summary: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

person:eden_1033.name: Eden
person:eden_1033.title: Eden
person:eden_1033.summary: Son of Joah, and one of the Levites who assisted in reforming the public worship of the sanctuary in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

person:eder_1035.name: Eder
person:eder_1035.title: Eder
person:eder_1035.summary: The second of the three sons of Mushi, of the family of Merari, appointed to the Levitical office (1 Chr. 23:23; 24:30).

person:eglah_1036.name: Eglah
person:eglah_1036.title: Eglah
person:eglah_1036.summary: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3). According to a Jewish tradition she was Michal.

person:eglon_1037.name: Eglon
person:eglon_1037.title: Eglon
person:eglon_1037.summary: Chieftain or king of one of the Moabite tribes (Judg. 3:12-14). Having entered into an alliance with Ammon and Amalek, he overran the trans-Jordanic region, and then crossing the Jordan, seized on Jericho, the “city of palm trees,” which had been by this time rebuilt, but not as a fortress. He made this city his capital, and kept Israel in subjection for eighteen years. The people at length “cried unto the Lord” in their distress, and he “raised them up a deliverer” in Ehud (q.v.), the son of Gera, a Benjamite.

person:ehud_1039.name: Ehud
person:ehud_1039.title: Ehud
person:ehud_1039.summary: The son of Gera, of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 3:15). After the death of Othniel the people again fell into idolatry, and Eglon, the king of Moab, uniting his bands with those of the Ammonites and the Amalekites, crossed the Jordan and took the city of Jericho, and for eighteen years held that whole district in subjection, exacting from it an annual tribute. At length Ehud, by a stratagem, put Eglon to death with a two-edged dagger a cubit long, and routed the Moabites at the fords of the Jordan, putting 10,000 of them to death. Thenceforward the land, at least Benjamin, enjoyed rest “for fourscore years” (Judg. 3:12-30). …

person:ehud_1040.name: Ehud
person:ehud_1040.title: Ehud
person:ehud_1040.summary: A descendant of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10), his great-grandson.

person:elah_1043.name: Elah
person:elah_1043.title: Elah
person:elah_1043.summary: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

person:elah_1045.name: Elah
person:elah_1045.title: Elah
person:elah_1045.summary: The son and successor of Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He was killed while drunk by Zimri, one of the captains of his chariots, and was the last king of the line of Baasha. Thus was fullfilled the prophecy of Jehu (6, 7, 11-14).

person:elah_1046.name: Elah
person:elah_1046.title: Elah
person:elah_1046.summary: The father of Hoshea, the last king of Israel (2 Kings 15:30; 17:1).

person:elah_1047.name: Elah
person:elah_1047.title: Elah
person:elah_1047.summary: The second of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

person:elam_1049.name: Elam
person:elam_1049.title: Elam (son of Shem)
person:elam_1049.summary:
Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles. The name Elam is an Assyrian word meaning “high.”
“The inhabitants of Elam, or ‘the Highlands,’ to the east of Babylon, were called Elamites. They were divided into several branches, speaking different dialects of the same agglutinative language. …

person:elasah_1056.name: Elasah
person:elasah_1056.title: Elasah
person:elasah_1056.summary: The son of Shaphan, one of the two who were sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and also took charge of Jeremiah’s letter to the captives in Babylon (Jer. 29:3).

person:eldad_1058.name: Eldad
person:eldad_1058.title: Eldad
person:eldad_1058.summary: Whom God has loved, one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed (Num. 11:26, 27) to administer justice among the people. He, with Medad, prophesied in the camp instead of going with the rest to the tabernacle, as Moses had commanded. This incident was announced to Moses by Joshua, who thought their conduct in this respect irregular. Moses replied, “Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets” (Num. 11:24-30; comp. Mark 9:38; Luke 9:49).

person:eleasah_1060.name: Eleasah
person:eleasah_1060.title: Eleasah
person:eleasah_1060.summary: One of the descendants of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:39, “Eleasah”).

person:eleasah_1061.name: Eleasah
person:eleasah_1061.title: Eleasah
person:eleasah_1061.summary: A descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43).

person:eleazar_1062.name: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1062.title: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1062.summary: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32). On Mount Hor he was clothed with the sacred vestments, which Moses took from off his brother Aaron and put upon him as successor to his father in the high priest’s office, which he held for more than twenty years (Num. 20:25-29). He took part with Moses in numbering the people (26:3, 4), and assisted at the inauguration of Joshua. He assisted in the distribution of the land after the conquest (Josh. 14:1). …

person:eleazar_1063.name: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1063.title: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1063.summary: An inhabitant of Kirjath-jearim who was “sanctified” to take charge of the ark, although not allowed to touch it, while it remained in the house of his father Abinadab (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; comp. Num. 3:31; 4:15).

person:eleazar_1064.name: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1064.title: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1064.summary: The son of Dodo the Ahohite, of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the three most eminent of David’s thirty-seven heroes (1 Chr. 11:12) who broke through the Philistine host and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:9, 16).

person:eleazar_1065.name: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1065.title: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1065.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21, 22).

person:eleazar_1066.name: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1066.title: Eleazar
person:eleazar_1066.summary: A son of Phinehas associated with the priests in taking charge of the sacred vessels brought back to Jerusalem after the Exile (Ezra 8:33).

person:elhanan_1070.name: Elhanan
person:elhanan_1070.title: Elhanan
person:elhanan_1070.summary: A warrior of the time of David famed for his exploits. In the Authorized Version (2 Sam. 21:19) it is recorded that “Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath.” The Revised Version here rightly omits the words “the brother of.” They were introduced in the Authorized Version to bring this passage into agreement with 1 Chr. 20:5, where it is said that he “slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath.” Goliath the Gittite was killed by David (1 Sam. 17). The exploit of Elhanan took place late in David’s reign.

person:elhanan_1071.name: Elhanan
person:elhanan_1071.title: Elhanan
person:elhanan_1071.summary: The son of Dodo, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:24).

person:eli_1072.name: Eli
person:eli_1072.title: Eli
person:eli_1072.summary:
Ascent, the high priest when the ark was at Shiloh (1 Sam. 1:3, 9). He was the first of the line of Ithamar, Aaron’s fourth son (1 Chr. 24:3; comp. 2 Sam. 8:17), who held that office. The office remained in his family till the time of Abiathar (1 Kings 2:26, 27), whom Solomon deposed, and appointed Zadok, of the family of Eleazar, in his stead (35). He acted also as a civil judge in Israel after the death of Samson (1 Sam. 4:18), and judged Israel for forty years.
His sons Hophni and Phinehas grossly misconducted themselves, to the great disgust of the people (1 Sam. 2:27-36). They were licentious reprobates. …

person:eliab_1073.name: Eliab
person:eliab_1073.title: Eliab
person:eliab_1073.summary: A son of Helon, and chief of the tribe of Zebulun at the time of the census in the wilderness (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

person:eliab_1074.name: Eliab
person:eliab_1074.title: Eliab
person:eliab_1074.summary: A Reubenite, son of Pallu (Num. 16:1, 12; 26:8, 9; Deut. 11:6).

person:eliab_1076.name: Eliab
person:eliab_1076.title: Eliab
person:eliab_1076.summary: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:9).

person:eliada_1078.name: Eliada
person:eliada_1078.title: Eliada
person:eliada_1078.summary: One of David’s sons born after his establishment in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 5:16).

person:eliada_1079.name: Eliada
person:eliada_1079.title: Eliada
person:eliada_1079.summary: A mighty man of war, a Benjamite (2 Chr. 17:17).

person:eliadah_1080.name: Eliadah
person:eliadah_1080.title: Eliadah
person:eliadah_1080.summary: An Aramite of Zobah, captain of a marauding band that troubled Solomon (1 Kings 11:23).

person:eliakim_1084.name: Eliakim
person:eliakim_1084.title: Eliakim
person:eliakim_1084.summary: The son of Hilkiah, who was sent to receive the message of the invading Assyrians and report it to Isaiah (2 Kings 18:18; 19:2; Isa. 36:3; 37:2). In his office as governor of the palace of Hezekiah he succeeded Shebna (Isa. 22:15-25). He was a good man (Isa. 22:20; 2 Kings 18:37), and had a splendid and honourable career.

person:eliakim_1087.name: Eliakim
person:eliakim_1087.title: Eliakim
person:eliakim_1087.summary: The son of Abiud, of the posterity of Zerubbabel (Matt. 1:13).

person:eliakim_1088.name: Eliakim
person:eliakim_1088.title: Eliakim
person:eliakim_1088.summary: The son of Melea (Luke 3:30), and probably grandson of Nathan.

person:eliam_1089.name: Eliam
person:eliam_1089.title: Eliam
person:eliam_1089.summary: The father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:3). In 1 Chr. 3:5 his name is Ammiel.

person:eliam_1090.name: Eliam
person:eliam_1090.title: Eliam
person:eliam_1090.summary: This name also occurs as that of a Gilonite, the son of Ahithophel, and one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:34). perhaps these two were the same person.

person:eliashib_1094.name: Eliashib
person:eliashib_1094.title: Eliashib
person:eliashib_1094.summary: A priest, head of one of the courses of the priests of the time of David (1 Chr. 24:12).

person:eliashib_1100.name: Eliashib
person:eliashib_1100.title: Eliashib
person:eliashib_1100.summary: A high priest in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (Neh. 12:22, 23). He rebuilt the eastern city wall (3:1), his own mansion being in that quarter, on the ridge Ophel (3:20, 21). His indulgence of Tobiah the Ammonite provoked the indignation of Nehemiah (13:4, 7).

person:eliathah_1102.name: Eliathah
person:eliathah_1102.title: Eliathah
person:eliathah_1102.summary: To whom God will come, one of the foureen sons of the Levite Heman, and musician of the temple in the time of David (1 Chr. 25:4).

person:elidad_1103.name: Elidad
person:elidad_1103.title: Elidad
person:elidad_1103.summary: Whom God has loved, son of Chislon, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin; one of those who were appointed to divide the Promised Land among the tribes (Num. 34:21).

person:eliel_1104.name: Eliel
person:eliel_1104.title: Eliel
person:eliel_1104.summary: A chief of Manasseh, on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

person:eliel_1109.name: Eliel
person:eliel_1109.title: Eliel
person:eliel_1109.summary: A Gadite who joined David in the hold at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:11).

person:eliel_1111.name: Eliel
person:eliel_1111.title: Eliel
person:eliel_1111.summary: One of the overseers of the offerings in the reign of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:13).

person:eliezer_1113.name: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1113.title: Eliezer (Abraham's Steward)
person:eliezer_1113.summary: “Of Damascus,” the “steward” (R.V., “possessor”) of Abraham’s house (Gen. 15:2, 3). It was probably he who headed the embassy sent by Abraham to the old home of his family in Padan-aram to seek a wife for his son Isaac. The account of this embassy is given at length in Gen. 24.

person:eliezer_1114.name: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1114.title: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1114.summary: One of the two sons of Moses, born during his sojourn in Midian (Ex. 18:4; 1 Chr. 23:15, 17). He remained with his mother and brother Gershom with Jethro when Moses returned to Egypt. (Ex. 18:4). They were restored to Moses when Jethro heard of his departure out of Egypt.

person:eliezer_1115.name: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1115.title: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1115.summary: The son of Becher, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

person:eliezer_1116.name: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1116.title: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1116.summary: One of the priests who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

person:eliezer_1117.name: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1117.title: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1117.summary: Son of Zichri, and chief of the Reubenites under David (1 Chr. 27:16).

person:eliezer_1118.name: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1118.title: Eliezer
person:eliezer_1118.summary: A prophet in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 20:37). Others of this name are mentioned Luke 3:29; Ezra 8:16; 10:18, 23, 31.

person:elihu_1126.name: Elihu
person:elihu_1126.title: Elihu
person:elihu_1126.summary: The son of Tohu, and grandfather of Elkanah (1 Sam. 1:1). He is called also Eliel (1 Chr. 6:34) and Eliab (6:27).

person:elihu_1127.name: Elihu
person:elihu_1127.title: Elihu
person:elihu_1127.summary: One of the captains of thousands of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

person:elihu_1128.name: Elihu
person:elihu_1128.title: Elihu
person:elihu_1128.summary: One of the family of Obed-edom, who were appointed porters of the temple under David (1 Chr. 26:7).

person:elihu_1130.name: Elihu
person:elihu_1130.title: Elihu
person:elihu_1130.summary: “The son of Barachel, a Buzite” (Job 32:2), one of Job’s friends. When the debate between Job and his friends is brought to a close, Elihu for the first time makes his appearance, and delivers his opinion on the points at issue (Job 32-37).

person:elijah_1131.name: Elijah
person:elijah_1131.title: Elijah
person:elijah_1131.summary:
“The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab. There is mention made of a town called Thisbe, south of Kadesh, but it is impossible to say whether this was the place referred to in the name given to the prophet.
Having delivered his message to Ahab, he retired at the command of God to a hiding-place by the brook Cherith, beyond Jordan, where he was fed by ravens. When the brook dried up God sent him to the widow of Zarephath, a city of Zidon, from whose scanty store he was supported for the space of two years. …

person:elika_1133.name: Elika
person:elika_1133.title: Elika
person:elika_1133.summary: God is his rejector, one of David’s thirty-seven distinguished heros (2 Sam. 23:25).

person:elimelech_1134.name: Elimelech
person:elimelech_1134.title: Elimelech
person:elimelech_1134.summary: God his king, a man of the tribe of Judah, of the family of the Hezronites, and kinsman of Boaz, who dwelt in Bethlehem in the days of the judges. In consequence of a great dearth he, with his wife Naomi and his two sons, went to dwell in the land of Moab. There he and his sons died (Ruth 1:2, 3; 2:1, 3; 4:3, 9). Naomi afterwards returned to Palestine with her daughter Ruth.

person:eliphalet_1143.name: Eliphalet
person:eliphalet_1143.title: Eliphalet
person:eliphalet_1143.summary: God his deliverance, one of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16); called also Eliphelet (1 Chr. 3:8).

person:eliphaz_1144.name: Eliphaz
person:eliphaz_1144.title: Eliphaz
person:eliphaz_1144.summary: The son of Esau by his wife Adah, and father of several Edomitish tribes (Gen. 36:4, 10, 11, 16).

person:elipheleh_1146.name: Elipheleh
person:elipheleh_1146.title: Elipheleh
person:elipheleh_1146.summary: God will distinguish him, one of the porters appointed to play “on the Sheminith” on the occasion of the bringing up of the ark to the city of David (1 Chr. 15:18, 21).

person:eliphelet_1147.name: Eliphelet
person:eliphelet_1147.title: Eliphelet
person:eliphelet_1147.summary: One of David’s distinguished warriors (2 Sam. 23:34); called also Eliphal in 1 Chr. 11:35.

person:eliphelet_1149.name: Eliphelet
person:eliphelet_1149.title: Eliphelet
person:eliphelet_1149.summary: A descendant of king Saul through Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:39).

person:elisabeth_1152.name: Elisabeth
person:elisabeth_1152.title: Elisabeth
person:elisabeth_1152.summary: God her oath, the mother of John the Baptist (Luke 1:5). She was a descendant of Aaron. She and her husband Zacharias (q.v.) “were both righteous before God” (Luke 1:5, 13). Mary’s visit to Elisabeth is described in 1:39-63.

person:elisha_1153.name: Elisha
person:elisha_1153.title: Elisha
person:elisha_1153.summary: God his salvation, the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah, who became the attendant and disciple of Elijah (1 Kings 19:16-19). His name first occurs in the command given to Elijah to anoint him as his successor (1 Kings 19:16). This was the only one of the three commands then given to Elijah which he accomplished. On his way from Sinai to Damascus he found Elisha at his native place engaged in the labours of the field, ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen. He went over to him, threw over his shoulders his rough mantle, and at once adopted him as a son, and invested him with the prophetical office (comp. Luke 9:61, 62). …

person:elishah_1154.name: Elishah
person:elishah_1154.title: Elishah
person:elishah_1154.summary: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis. This may be meant by “the isles of Elishah” (Ezek. 27:7).

person:elishama_1155.name: Elishama
person:elishama_1155.title: Elishama
person:elishama_1155.summary: A prince of Benjamin, grandfather of Joshua (Num. 1:10; 1 Chr. 7:26).

person:elishama_1159.name: Elishama
person:elishama_1159.title: Elishama
person:elishama_1159.summary: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the people the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:elishaphat_1161.name: Elishaphat
person:elishaphat_1161.title: Elishaphat
person:elishaphat_1161.summary: Whom God has judged, one of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in the league to overthrow the usurpation of Athaliah (2 Chr. 23:1).

person:elisheba_1162.name: Elisheba
person:elisheba_1162.title: Elisheba
person:elisheba_1162.summary: God is her oath, the daughter of Amminadab and the wife of Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

person:elishua_1163.name: Elishua
person:elishua_1163.title: Elishua
person:elishua_1163.summary: God his salvation, a son of David, 2 Sam. 5:15 = Elishama, 1 Chr. 3:6.

person:elkanah_1167.name: Elkanah
person:elkanah_1167.title: Elkanah
person:elkanah_1167.summary: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

person:elkanah_1168.name: Elkanah
person:elkanah_1168.title: Elkanah
person:elkanah_1168.summary: Another Levite of the line of Heman the singer, although he does not seem to have performed any of the usual Levitical offices. He was father of Samuel the prophet (1 Chr. 6:27, 34). He was “an Ephrathite” (1 Sam. 1:1, 4, 8), but lived at Ramah, a man of wealth and high position. He had two wives, Hannah, who was the mother of Samuel, and Peninnah.

person:elon_1182.name: Elon
person:elon_1182.title: Elon
person:elon_1182.summary: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

person:elon_1183.name: Elon
person:elon_1183.title: Elon
person:elon_1183.summary: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

person:elon_1184.name: Elon
person:elon_1184.title: Elon
person:elon_1184.summary: The eleventh of the Hebrew judges. He held office for ten years (Judg. 12:11, 12). He is called the Zebulonite.

person:elymas_403.name: Elymas
person:elymas_403.title: Elymas
person:elymas_403.summary: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus. He was miraculously struck with blindness (Acts 13:11).

person:enoch_1191.name: Enoch
person:enoch_1191.title: Enoch (son of Cain)
person:enoch_1191.summary: The eldest son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), who built a city east of Eden in the land of Nod, and called it “after the name of his son Enoch.” This is the first “city” mentioned in Scripture.

person:enoch_1192.name: Enoch
person:enoch_1192.title: Enoch (father of Methuselah)
person:enoch_1192.summary: The son of Jared, and father of Methuselah (Gen. 5:21; Luke 3:37). His father was one hundred and sixty-two years old when he was born. After the birth of Methuselah, Enoch “walked with God three hundred years” (Gen. 5:22-24), when he was translated without tasting death. His whole life on earth was three hundred and sixty-five years. He was the “seventh from Adam” (Jude 1:14), as distinguished from the son of Cain, the third from Adam. He is spoken of in the catalogue of Old Testament worthies in the Epistle to the Hebrews (11:5). When he was translated, only Adam, so far as recorded, had as yet died a natural death, and Noah was not yet born. …

person:enos_1193.name: Enos
person:enos_1193.title: Enos
person:enos_1193.summary: Man the son of Seth, and grandson of Adam (Gen. 5:6-11; Luke 3:38). He lived nine hundred and five years. In his time “men began to call upon the name of the Lord” (Gen. 4:26), meaning either (1) then began men to call themselves by the name of the Lord (marg.) i.e., to distinguish themselves thereby from idolaters; or (2) then men in some public and earnest way began to call upon the Lord, indicating a time of spiritual revival.

person:epaenetus_1194.name: Epaenetus
person:epaenetus_1194.title: Epaenetus
person:epaenetus_1194.summary: Commendable, a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutation (Rom. 16:5). He is spoken of as “the first fruits of Achaia” (R.V., “of Asia”, i.e., of proconsular Asia, which is probably the correct reading). As being the first convert in that region, he was peculiarly dear to the apostle. He calls him his “well beloved.”

person:epaphras_1195.name: Epaphras
person:epaphras_1195.title: Epaphras
person:epaphras_1195.summary: Lovely, spoken of by Paul (Col. 1:7; 4:12) as “his dear fellow-servant,” and “a faithful minister of Christ.” He was thus evidently with him at Rome when he wrote to the Colossians. He was a distinguished disciple, and probably the founder of the Colossian church. He is also mentioned in the Epistle to Philemon (1:23), where he is called by Paul his “fellow-prisoner.”

person:ephah_1199.name: Ephah
person:ephah_1199.title: Ephah
person:ephah_1199.summary:
1 Chr. 2:47, a descendant of Judah.
Ephah, a word of Egyptian origin, meaning measure; a grain measure containing “three seahs or ten omers,” and equivalent to the bath for liquids (Ex. 16:36; 1 Sam. 17:17; Zech. 5:6). The double ephah in Prov. 20:10 (marg., “an ephah and an ephah”), Deut. 25:14, means two ephahs, the one false and the other just.

person:epher_1201.name: Epher
person:epher_1201.title: Epher
person:epher_1201.summary: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

person:epher_1203.name: Epher
person:epher_1203.title: Epher
person:epher_1203.summary: The head of one of the families of trans-Jordanic Manasseh who were carried captive by Tiglath-pileser (1 Chr. 5:24).

person:ephraim_1206.name: Ephraim
person:ephraim_1206.title: Ephraim
person:ephraim_1206.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20). The first incident recorded regarding him is his being placed, along with his brother Manasseh, before their grandfather, Jacob, that he might bless them (48:10; comp. 27:1). The intention of Joseph was that the right hand of the aged patriarch should be placed on the head of the elder of the two; but Jacob set Ephraim the younger before his brother, “guiding his hands wittingly.” Before Joseph’s death, Ephraim’s family had reached the third generation (Gen. 50:23).

person:ephratah_1207.name: Ephratah
person:ephratah_1207.title: Ephratah
person:ephratah_1207.summary: The second wife of Caleb, the son of Hezron, mother of Hur, and grandmother of Caleb, who was one of those that were sent to spy the land (1 Chr. 2:19, 50).

person:ephron_1208.name: Ephron
person:ephron_1208.title: Ephron
person:ephron_1208.summary: The son of Zohar a Hittite, the owner of the field and cave of Machpelah (q.v.), which Abraham bought for 400 shekels of silver (Gen. 23:8-17; 25:9; 49:29, 30).

person:erastus_1213.name: Erastus
person:erastus_1213.title: Erastus
person:erastus_1213.summary: A companion of Paul at Ephesus, who was sent by him along with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22). Corinth was his usual place of abode (2 Tim. 4:20); but probably he may have been the same as the preceding.

person:esau_1216.name: Esau
person:esau_1216.title: Esau (Edom)
person:esau_1216.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31). The circumstances connected with his birth foreshadowed the enmity which afterwards subsisted between the twin brothers and the nations they founded (25:22, 23, 26). In process of time Jacob, following his natural bent, became a shepherd; while Esau, a “son of the desert,” devoted himself to the perilous and toilsome life of a huntsman. …

person:eshcol_1218.name: Eshcol
person:eshcol_1218.title: Eshcol
person:eshcol_1218.summary: A young Amoritish chief who joined Abraham in the recovery of Lot from the hands of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

person:esther_1343.name: Esther
person:esther_1343.title: Esther
person:esther_1343.summary: The queen of Ahasuerus, and heroine of the book that bears her name. She was a Jewess named Hadas’sah (the myrtle), but when she entered the royal harem she received the name by which she henceforth became known (Esther 2:7). It is a Syro-Arabian modification of the Persian word satarah, which means a star. She was the daughter of Abihail, a Benjamite. Her family did not avail themselves of the permission granted by Cyrus to the exiles to return to Jerusalem; and she resided with her cousin Mordecai, who held some office in the household of the Persian king at “Shushan in the palace.” Ahasuerus having divorced Vashti, chose Esther to be his wife. …

person:ethan_1222.name: Ethan
person:ethan_1222.title: Ethan
person:ethan_1222.summary: “The Ezrahite,” distinguished for his wisdom (1 Kings 4:31). He is named as the author of the 89th Psalm. He was of the tribe of Levi.

person:ethan_1622.name: Ethan
person:ethan_1622.title: Ethan
person:ethan_1622.summary: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 6:21), probably the same as Ethan (42).

person:ethbaal_1225.name: Ethbaal
person:ethbaal_1225.title: Ethbaal
person:ethbaal_1225.summary: With Baal, a king of Sidon (B.C. 940-908), father of Jezebel, who was the wife of Ahab (1 Kings 16:31). He is said to have been also a priest of Astarte, whose worship was closely allied to that of Baal, and this may account for his daughter’s zeal in promoting idolatry in Israel. This marriage of Ahab was most fatal to both Israel and Judah. Dido, the founder of Carthage, was his granddaughter.

person:euodias_1229.name: Euodias
person:euodias_1229.title: Euodias
person:euodias_1229.summary: A good journey, a female member of the church at Philippi. She was one who laboured much with Paul in the gospel. He exhorts her to be of one mind with Syntyche (Phil. 4:2). From this it seems they had been at variance with each other.

person:eutychus_1230.name: Eutychus
person:eutychus_1230.title: Eutychus
person:eutychus_1230.summary: Fortunate, (Acts 20:9-12), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.” The lattice-work of the window being open to admit the air, the lad fell out and down to the court below. Paul restored him to life again. (Comp. 1 Kings 17:21; 2 Kings 4:34.)

person:eve_1231.name: Eve
person:eve_1231.title: Eve
person:eve_1231.summary: Life; living, the name given by Adam to his wife (Gen. 3:20; 4:1). The account of her creation is given in Gen. 2:21, 22. The Creator, by declaring that it was not good for man to be alone, and by creating for him a suitable companion, gave sanction to monogamy. The commentator Matthew Henry says: “This companion was taken from his side to signify that she was to be dear unto him as his own flesh. …

person:evil-merodach_1233.name: Evil-merodach
person:evil-merodach_1233.title: Evil-merodach
person:evil-merodach_1233.summary: Merodach’s man, the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:27; Jer. 52:31, 34). He seems to have reigned but two years (B.C. 562-560). Influenced probably by Daniel, he showed kindness to Jehoiachin, who had been a prisoner in Babylon for thirty-seven years. He released him, and “spoke kindly to him.” He was murdered by Nergal-sharezer=Neriglissar, his brother-in-law, who succeeded him (Jer. 39:3, 13).

person:ezekiel_1237.name: Ezekiel
person:ezekiel_1237.title: Ezekiel
person:ezekiel_1237.summary: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest (Ezek. 1:3). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.” He was probably carried away captive with Jehoiachin (1:2; 2 Kings 24:14-16) about B.C. 597. His prophetic call came to him “in the fifth year of Jehoiachin’s captivity” (B.C. 594). He had a house in the place of his exile, where he lost his wife, in the ninth year of his exile, by some sudden and unforeseen stroke (Ezek. 8:1; 24:18). He held a prominent place among the exiles, and was frequently consulted by the elders (8:1; 11:25; 14:1; 20:1). His ministry extended over twenty-three years (29:17), B.C. …

person:ezer_1238.name: Ezer
person:ezer_1238.title: Ezer
person:ezer_1238.summary: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

person:ezra_1245.name: Ezra
person:ezra_1245.title: Ezra
person:ezra_1245.summary:
The “scribe” who led the second body of exiles that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem B.C. 459, and author of the book of Scripture which bears his name. He was the son, or perhaps grandson, of Seraiah (2 Kings 25:18-21), and a lineal descendant of Phinehas, the son of Aaron (Ezra 7:1-5). All we know of his personal history is contained in the last four chapters of his book, and in Neh. 8 and 12:26.
In the seventh year of the reign of Artaxerxes Longimanus (see DARIUS), he obtained leave to go up to Jerusalem and to take with him a company of Israelites (Ezra 8). …

person:ezra_1246.name: Ezra
person:ezra_1246.title: Ezra
person:ezra_1246.summary: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel (Neh. 12:1).

person:ezri_1247.name: Ezri
person:ezri_1247.title: Ezri
person:ezri_1247.summary: Help of Jehovah, the son of Chelub. He superintended, under David, those who “did the work of the field for tillage” (1 Chr. 27:26).

person:felix_1257.name: Felix
person:felix_1257.title: Felix
person:felix_1257.summary:
Happy, the Roman procurator of Judea before whom Paul “reasoned” (Acts 24:25). He appears to have expected a bribe from Paul, and therefore had several interviews with him. The “worthy deeds” referred to in 24:2 was his clearing the country of banditti and impostors.
At the end of a two years’ term, Porcius Festus was appointed in the room of Felix (A.D. 60), who proceeded to Rome, and was there accused of cruelty and malversation of office by the Jews of Caesarea. The accusation was rendered nugatory by the influence of his brother Pallas with Nero. (See Josephus, Ant. xx. …

person:fortunatus_1258.name: Fortunatus
person:fortunatus_1258.title: Fortunatus
person:fortunatus_1258.summary: Fortunate, a disciple of Corinth who visited Paul at Ephesus, and returned with Stephanas and Achaicus, the bearers of the apostle’s first letter to the Corinthians (1 Cor. 16:17).

person:gaal_1259.name: Gaal
person:gaal_1259.title: Gaal
person:gaal_1259.summary: Loathing, the son of Ebed, in whom the Shechemites “placed their confidence” when they became discontented with Abimelech. He headed the revolution, and led out the men of Shechem against Abimelech; but was defeated, and fled to his own home (Judg. 9:26-46). We hear no more of him after this battle.

person:gabriel_1261.name: Gabriel
person:gabriel_1261.title: Gabriel
person:gabriel_1261.summary:
Champion of God, used as a proper name to designate the angel who was sent to Daniel (8:16) to explain the vision of the ram and the he-goat, and to communicate the prediction of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:21-27).
He announced also the birth of John the Baptist (Luke 1:11), and of the Messiah (26). He describes himself in the words, “I am Gabriel, who stand in the presence of God” (1:19).

person:gad_1262.name: Gad
person:gad_1262.title: Gad
person:gad_1262.summary:
Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18). In the Authorized Version of 30:11 the words, “A troop cometh: and she called,” etc., should rather be rendered, “In fortune [R.V., ‘Fortunate’]: and she called,” etc., or “Fortune cometh,” etc.
The tribe of Gad during the march through the wilderness had their place with Simeon and Reuben on the south side of the tabernacle (Num. 2:14). The tribes of Reuben and Gad continued all through their history to follow the pastoral pursuits of the patriarchs (Num. …

person:gad_1263.name: Gad
person:gad_1263.title: Gad
person:gad_1263.summary: A prophet who joined David in the “hold,” and at whose advice he quitted it for the forest of Hareth (1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr. 29:25; 1 Sam. 22:5). Many years after we find mention made of him in connection with the punishment inflicted for numbering the people (2 Sam. 24:11-19; 1 Chr. 21:9-19). He wrote a book called the “Acts of David” (1 Chr. 29:29), and assisted in the arrangements for the musical services of the “house of God” (2 Chr. 29:25). He bore the title of “the king’s seer” (2 Sam. 24:11, 13; 1 Chr. 21:9).

person:gaddi_1264.name: Gaddi
person:gaddi_1264.title: Gaddi
person:gaddi_1264.summary: Fortunate, the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve “spies” sent by Moses to spy the land (Num. 13:11).

person:gaddiel_1265.name: Gaddiel
person:gaddiel_1265.title: Gaddiel
person:gaddiel_1265.summary: Fortune (i.e., sent) of God, the representative of the tribe of Zebulum among the twelve spies (Num. 13:10).

person:gahar_1268.name: Gahar
person:gahar_1268.title: Gahar
person:gahar_1268.summary: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47).

person:gaius_1269.name: Gaius
person:gaius_1269.title: Gaius (of Macedonia)
person:gaius_1269.summary: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).
