During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into the theatre. Some have identified this Gaius with No. (2).

person:gaius_1270.name: Gaius
person:gaius_1270.title: Gaius (of Derbe)
person:gaius_1270.summary: A man of Derbe who accompanied Paul into Asia on his last journey to Jerusalem

person:gaius_1271.name: Gaius
person:gaius_1271.title: Gaius
person:gaius_1271.summary: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into the theatre. Some have identified this Gaius with No. (2).

person:gaius_1272.name: Gaius
person:gaius_1272.title: Gaius
person:gaius_1272.summary: A Christain of Asia Minor to whom John addressed his third epistle (3 John 1:1).

person:gallio_1275.name: Gallio
person:gallio_1275.title: Gallio
person:gallio_1275.summary: The elder brother of Seneca the philosopher, who was tutor and for some time minister of the emperor Nero. He was “deputy”, i.e., proconsul, as in Revised Version, of Achaia, under the emperor Claudius, when Paul visited Corinth (Acts 18:12). The word used here by Luke in describing the rank of Gallio shows his accuracy. Achaia was a senatorial province under Claudius, and the governor of such a province was called a “proconsul.” He is spoken of by his contemporaries as “sweet Gallio,” and is described as a most popular and affectionate man. …

person:gamaliel_1276.name: Gamaliel
person:gamaliel_1276.title: Gamaliel
person:gamaliel_1276.summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai (Num. 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59).

person:gamaliel_1277.name: Gamaliel
person:gamaliel_1277.title: Gamaliel
person:gamaliel_1277.summary:
The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees. He was noted for his learning, and was president of the Sanhedrim during the regins of Tiberius, Caligula, and Claudius, and died, it is said, about eighteen years before the destruction of Jerusalem.
When the apostles were brought before the council, charged with preaching the resurrection of Jesus, as a zealous Pharisee Gamaliel councelled moderation and calmness. …

person:gamul_1278.name: Gamul
person:gamul_1278.title: Gamul
person:gamul_1278.summary: Weaned the leader of one of the priestly courses (1 Chr. 24:17).

person:gareb_1279.name: Gareb
person:gareb_1279.title: Gareb
person:gareb_1279.summary: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:38), an Ithrite.

person:geber_1286.name: Geber
person:geber_1286.title: Geber
person:geber_1286.summary: A valiant man, (1 Kings 4:19), one of Solomon’s purveyors, having jurisdiction over a part of Gilead, comprising all the kingdom of Sihon and part of the kingdom of Og (Deut. 2; 31).

person:gedaliah_1287.name: Gedaliah
person:gedaliah_1287.title: Gedaliah
person:gedaliah_1287.summary: The son of Ahikam, and grandson of Shaphan, secretary of king Josiah (Jer. 26:24). After the destruction of Jerusalem (see ZEDEKIAH), Nebuchadnezzar left him to govern the country as tributary to him (2 Kings 25:22; Jer. 40:5; 52:16). Ishmael, however, at the head of a party of the royal family, “Jewish irreconcilables”, rose against him, and slew him and “all the Jews that were with him” (Jer. 41:2, 3) at Mizpah about three months after the destruction of Jerusalem. He and his band also plundered the town of Mizpah, and carried off many captives. He was, however, overtaken by Johanan and routed. He fled with such of his followers as escaped to the Ammonites (41:15). …

person:gedaliah_1290.name: Gedaliah
person:gedaliah_1290.title: Gedaliah
person:gedaliah_1290.summary: One of the Jewish nobles who conspired against Jeremiah (Jer. 38:1).

person:gehazi_1293.name: Gehazi
person:gehazi_1293.title: Gehazi
person:gehazi_1293.summary:
Valley of vision, Elisha’s trusted servant (2 Kings 4:31; 5:25; 8:4, 5). He appears in connection with the history of the Shunammite (2 Kings 4:14, 31) and of Naaman the Syrian. On this latter occasion he was guilty of duplicity and dishonesty of conduct, causing Elisha to denounce his crime with righteous sternness, and pass on him the terrible doom that the leprosy of Naaman would cleave to him and his for ever (5:20-27).
He afterwards appeared before king Joram, to whom he recounted the great deeds of his master (2 Kings 8:1-6).

person:gemariah_1295.name: Gemariah
person:gemariah_1295.title: Gemariah
person:gemariah_1295.summary: The son of Hilkiah, who accompanied Shaphan with the tribute-money from Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and was the bearer at the same time of a letter from Jeremiah to the Jewish captives at Babylon (Jer. 29:3, 4).

person:gemariah_1296.name: Gemariah
person:gemariah_1296.title: Gemariah
person:gemariah_1296.summary: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:10; 2 Kings 22:12). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer. 36:11-20), which filled him with terror. He joined with others in entreating the king not to destroy the roll of the prophecies which Baruch had read (21-25).

person:genubath_1297.name: Genubath
person:genubath_1297.title: Genubath
person:genubath_1297.summary: Theft, the son of Hadad, of the Edomitish royal family. He was brought up in Pharaoh’s household. His mother was a sister of Tahpenes, the king of Egypt’s wife, mentioned in 1 Kings 11:20.

person:gera_1298.name: Gera
person:gera_1298.title: Gera
person:gera_1298.summary: The father of Ehud the judge (Judg. 3:15).

person:gera_1299.name: Gera
person:gera_1299.title: Gera
person:gera_1299.summary: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David (2 Sam. 16:5; 19:16, 18).

person:gershom_1302.name: Gershom
person:gershom_1302.title: Gershom
person:gershom_1302.summary: The elder of the two sons of Moses born to him in Midian (Ex. 2:22; 18:3). On his way to Egypt with his family, in obedience to the command of the Lord, Moses was attacked by a sudden and dangerous illness (4:24-26), which Zipporah his wife believed to have been sent because he had neglected to circumcise his son. She accordingly took a “sharp stone” and circumcised her son Gershom, saying, “Surely a bloody husband art thou to me”, i.e., by the blood of her child she had, as it were, purchased her husband, had won him back again.

person:gershom_1303.name: Gershom
person:gershom_1303.title: Gershom
person:gershom_1303.summary: The son of Manasseh (Judg. 18:30), in R.V. “of Moses.”

person:gershom_1304.name: Gershom
person:gershom_1304.title: Gershom
person:gershom_1304.summary: A descendant of Phinehas who returned with Ezra from Babylon (Ezra 8:2).

person:gershon_1305.name: Gershon
person:gershon_1305.title: Gershon
person:gershon_1305.summary:
'=Ger’shom expulsion, the eldest of Levi’s three sons (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).
In the wilderness the sons of Gershon had charge of the fabrics of the tabernacle when it was moved from place to place, the curtains, veils, tent-hangings (Num. 3: 21-26). Thirteen Levitical cities fell to the lot of the Gershonites (Josh. 21:27-33).

person:geshem_1307.name: Geshem
person:geshem_1307.title: Geshem
person:geshem_1307.summary: Or Gashmu, firmness, probably chief of the Arabs south of Palestine, one of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon (Neh. 2:19; 6:1, 2). He united with Sanballat and Tobiah in opposing the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.

person:gideon_1314.name: Gideon
person:gideon_1314.title: Gideon
person:gideon_1314.summary: Called also Jerubbaal (Judg. 6:29, 32), was the first of the judges whose history is circumstantially narrated (Judg. 6-8). His calling is the commencement of the second period in the history of the judges. After the victory gained by Deborah and Barak over Jabin, Israel once more sank into idolatry, and the Midianites (q.v.) and Amalekites, with other “children of the east,” crossed the Jordan each year for seven successive years for the purpose of plundering and desolating the land. Gideon received a direct call from God to undertake the task of delivering the land from these warlike invaders. He was of the family of Abiezer (Josh. 17:2; 1 Chr. …

person:girgasite_1322.name: Girgasite
person:girgasite_1322.title: Girgasite
person:girgasite_1322.summary: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1). They were a branch of the great family of the Hivites. Of their geographical position nothing is certainly known. Probably they lived somewhere in the central part of Western Palestine.

person:god_1324.name: God
person:god_1324.title: God
person:god_1324.summary: (A.S. and Dutch God; Dan. Gud; Ger. Gott), the name of the Divine Being. It is the rendering (1) of the Hebrew ’El, from a word meaning to be strong; (2) of ’Eloah_, plural _’Elohim. The singular form, Eloah, is used only in poetry. The plural form is more commonly used in all parts of the Bible, The Hebrew word Jehovah (q.v.), the only other word generally employed to denote the Supreme Being, is uniformly rendered in the Authorized Version by “LORD,” printed in small capitals. The existence of God is taken for granted in the Bible. There is nowhere any argument to prove it. He who disbelieves this truth is spoken of as one devoid of understanding (Ps. 14:1).

person:gog_1325.name: Gog
person:gog_1325.title: Gog
person:gog_1325.summary: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:4), the father of Shimei.

person:goliath_1327.name: Goliath
person:goliath_1327.title: Goliath
person:goliath_1327.summary: A famous giant of Gath, who for forty days openly defied the armies of Israel, but was at length slain by David with a stone from a sling (1 Sam. 17:4). He was probably descended from the Rephaim who found refuge among the Philistines after they were dispersed by the Ammonites (Deut. 2:20, 21). His height was “six cubits and a span,” which, taking the cubit at 21 inches, is equal to 10 1/2 feet. David cut off his head (1 Sam. 17:51) and brought it to Jerusalem, while he hung the armour which he took from him in his tent. His sword was preserved at Nob as a religious trophy (21:9). David’s victory over Goliath was the turning point in his life. …

person:gomer_1328.name: Gomer
person:gomer_1328.title: Gomer (son of Japheth)
person:gomer_1328.summary: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe. He is generally regarded as the ancestor of the Celtae and the Cimmerii, who in early times settled to the north of the Black Sea, and gave their name to the Crimea, the ancient Chersonesus Taurica. Traces of their presence are found in the names Cimmerian Bosphorus, Cimmerian Isthmus, etc. In the seventh century B.C. they were driven out of their original seat by the Scythians, and overran western Asia Minor, whence they were afterwards expelled. …

person:hadad_1338.name: Hadad
person:hadad_1338.title: Hadad
person:hadad_1338.summary: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

person:hadad_1339.name: Hadad
person:hadad_1339.title: Hadad
person:hadad_1339.summary:
One of “the king’s seed in Edom.” He fled into Egypt, where he married the sister of Pharaoh’s wife (1 Kings 11:14-22). He became one of Solomon’s adversaries.
Hadad, sharp, (a different name in Hebrew from the preceding), one of the sons of Ishmael (1 Chr. 1:30). Called also Hadar (Gen. 25:15).

person:hadad_1342.name: Hadad
person:hadad_1342.title: Hadad
person:hadad_1342.summary:
One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul. Called also Hadad (1 Chr. 1:50, 51).
It is probable that in these cases Hadar may be an error simply of transcription for Hadad.

person:hadar_1341.name: Hadar
person:hadar_1341.title: Hadar
person:hadar_1341.summary: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

person:hadarezer_1340.name: Hadarezer
person:hadarezer_1340.title: Hadarezer
person:hadarezer_1340.summary: Hadad is help; called also Hadarezer, Adod is his help, the king of Zobah. Hanun, the king of the Ammonites, hired among others the army of Hadadezer to assist him in his war against David. Joab, who was sent against this confederate host, found them in double battle array, the Ammonities toward their capital of Rabbah, and the Syrian mercenaries near Medeba. In the battle which was fought the Syrians were scattered, and the Ammonites in alarm fled into their capital. After this Hadadezer went north “to recover his border” (2 Sam. 8:3, A.V.); but rather, as the Revised Version renders, “to recover his dominion”, i.e., to recruit his forces. …

person:hadlai_1344.name: Hadlai
person:hadlai_1344.title: Hadlai
person:hadlai_1344.summary: Resting, an Ephraimite; the father of Amasa, mentioned in 2 Chr. 28:12.

person:hadoram_1345.name: Hadoram
person:hadoram_1345.title: Hadoram
person:hadoram_1345.summary: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

person:hagar_1348.name: Hagar
person:hagar_1348.title: Hagar
person:hagar_1348.summary: Flight, or, according to others, stranger, an Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid (Gen. 16:1; 21:9, 10), whom she gave to Abraham (q.v.) as a secondary wife (16:2). When she was about to become a mother she fled from the cruelty of her mistress, intending apparently to return to her relatives in Egypt, through the desert of Shur, which lay between. Wearied and worn she had reached the place she distinguished by the name of Beer-lahai-roi (“the well of the visible God”), where the angel of the Lord appeared to her. …

person:haggai_1349.name: Haggai
person:haggai_1349.title: Haggai
person:haggai_1349.summary: Festive, one of the twelve so-called minor prophets. He was the first of the three (Zechariah, his contemporary, and Malachi, who was about one hundred years later, being the other two) whose ministry belonged to the period of Jewish history which began after the return from captivity in Babylon. Scarcely anything is known of his personal history. He may have been one of the captives taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar. He began his ministry about sixteen years after the Return. The work of rebuilding the temple had been put a stop to through the intrigues of the Samaritans. …

person:haggith_1353.name: Haggith
person:haggith_1353.title: Haggith
person:haggith_1353.summary: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

person:hakkoz_1355.name: Hakkoz
person:hakkoz_1355.title: Hakkoz
person:hakkoz_1355.summary: The thorn, the head of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:10).

person:ham_1359.name: Ham
person:ham_1359.title: Ham
person:ham_1359.summary:
Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24). The curse pronounced by Noah against Ham, properly against Canaan his fourth son, was accomplished when the Jews subsequently exterminated the Canaanites.
One of the most important facts recorded in Gen. 10 is the foundation of the earliest monarchy in Babylonia by Nimrod the grandson of Ham (6, 8, 10). The primitive Babylonian empire was thus Hamitic, and of a cognate race with the primitive inhabitants of Arabia and of Ethiopia.
The race of Ham were the most energetic of all the descendants of Noah in the early times of the post-diluvian world.

person:haman_1360.name: Haman
person:haman_1360.title: Haman
person:haman_1360.summary: (of Persian origin), magnificent, the name of the vizier (i.e., the prime minister) of the Persian king Ahasuerus (Esther 3:1, etc.). He is called an “Agagite,” which seems to denote that he was descended from the royal family of the Amalekites, the bitterest enemies of the Jews, as Agag was one of the titles of the Amalekite kings. He or his parents were brought to Persia as captives taken in war. He was hanged on the gallows which he had erected for Mordecai the Jew (Esther 7:10).

person:hammedatha_1362.name: Hammedatha
person:hammedatha_1362.title: Hammedatha
person:hammedatha_1362.summary: Father of Haman, designated usually “the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, 10; 8:5).

person:hammelech_1363.name: Hammelech
person:hammelech_1363.title: Hammelech
person:hammelech_1363.summary: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son. Probably, however, it is to be taken as a proper name.

person:hammoleketh_1364.name: Hammoleketh
person:hammoleketh_1364.title: Hammoleketh
person:hammoleketh_1364.summary: The queen, the daughter of Machir and sister of Gilead (1 Chr. 7:17, 18). Abiezer was one of her three children.

person:hamor_1365.name: Hamor
person:hamor_1365.title: Hamor
person:hamor_1365.summary: He-ass, a Hivite from whom Jacob purchased the plot of ground in which Joseph was afterwards buried (Gen. 33:19). He is called “Emmor” in Acts 7:16. His son Shechem founded the city of that name which Simeon and Levi destroyed because of his crime in the matter of Dinah, Jacob’s daughter (Gen. 34:20). Hamor and Shechem were also slain (ver. 26).

person:hamul_1367.name: Hamul
person:hamul_1367.title: Hamul
person:hamul_1367.summary: Spared, one of the sons of Pharez, son of Judah (1 Chr. 2:5). His descendants are called Hamulites (Num. 26:21).

person:hamutal_1368.name: Hamutal
person:hamutal_1368.title: Hamutal
person:hamutal_1368.summary: Kinsman of the dew, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of king Josiah, and mother of king Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31), also of king Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:18).

person:hanameel_1369.name: Hanameel
person:hanameel_1369.title: Hanameel
person:hanameel_1369.summary: Whom God has graciously given, the cousin of Jeremiah, to whom he sold the field he possessed in Anathoth, before the siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 32:6-12).

person:hanan_1374.name: Hanan
person:hanan_1374.title: Hanan
person:hanan_1374.summary: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra (Neh. 8:7).

person:hanan_1375.name: Hanan
person:hanan_1375.title: Hanan
person:hanan_1375.summary: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:22).

person:hanani_1379.name: Hanani
person:hanani_1379.title: Hanani
person:hanani_1379.summary: A prophet who was sent to rebuke king Asa for entering into a league with Benhadad I., king of Syria, against Judah (2 Chr. 16:1-10). He was probably the father of the prophet Jehu (1 Kings 16:7).

person:hanani_1380.name: Hanani
person:hanani_1380.title: Hanani
person:hanani_1380.summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 25).

person:hanani_1382.name: Hanani
person:hanani_1382.title: Hanani
person:hanani_1382.summary: Probably a brother of Nehemiah (Neh. 1:2; 7:2), who reported to him the melancholy condition of Jerusalem. Nehemiah afterwards appointed him to have charge of the city gates.

person:hananiah_1385.name: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1385.title: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1385.summary: A chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:24).

person:hananiah_1386.name: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1386.title: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1386.summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 23).

person:hananiah_1387.name: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1387.title: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1387.summary: One of Uzziah’s military officers (2 Chr. 26:11).

person:hananiah_1391.name: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1391.title: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1391.summary: The “ruler of the palace; he was a faithful man, and feared God above many” (Neh. 7:2).

person:hananiah_1397.name: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1397.title: Hananiah
person:hananiah_1397.summary: Grandfather of the captain who arrested Jeremiah (Jer. 37:13).

person:haniel_1399.name: Haniel
person:haniel_1399.title: Haniel
person:haniel_1399.summary: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:39).

person:hannah_1400.name: Hannah
person:hannah_1400.title: Hannah
person:hannah_1400.summary: Favour, grace, one of the wives of Elkanah the Levite, and the mother of Samuel (1 Sam. 1; 2). Her home was at Ramathaim-zophim, whence she was wont every year to go to Shiloh, where the tabernacle had been pitched by Joshua, to attend the offering of sacrifices there according to the law (Ex. 23:15; 34:18; Deut. 16:16), probably at the feast of the Passover (comp. Ex. 13:10). On occasion of one of these “yearly” visits, being grieved by reason of Peninnah’s conduct toward her, she went forth alone, and kneeling before the Lord at the sanctuary she prayed inaudibly. …

person:hanniel_1401.name: Hanniel
person:hanniel_1401.title: Hanniel
person:hanniel_1401.summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 34:23).

person:hanun_1404.name: Hanun
person:hanun_1404.title: Hanun
person:hanun_1404.summary: The son and successor of Nahash, king of Moab. David’s messengers, sent on an embassy of condolence to him to Rabbah Ammon, his capital, were so grossly insulted that he proclaimed war against Hanun. David’s army, under the command of Joab, forthwith crossed the Jordan, and gained a complete victory over the Moabites and their allies (2 Sam. 10:1-14) at Medeba (q.v.).

person:haran_1407.name: Haran
person:haran_1407.title: Haran (brother of Abraham)
person:haran_1407.summary: Heb. haran; i.e., “mountaineer.” The eldest son of Terah, brother of Abraham and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah. He died before his father (Gen. 11:27), in Ur of the Chaldees.

person:haran_1408.name: Haran
person:haran_1408.title: Haran (son of Caleb)
person:haran_1408.summary: The son of Caleb of Judah (1 Chr. 2:46) by his concubine Ephah.

person:harbona_1410.name: Harbona
person:harbona_1410.title: Harbona
person:harbona_1410.summary: (a Persian word meaning “ass-driver”), one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains of king Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10; 7:9).

person:harhaiah_1413.name: Harhaiah
person:harhaiah_1413.title: Harhaiah
person:harhaiah_1413.summary: Zeal of Jehovah, (Neh. 3:8) “of the goldsmiths,” one whose son helped to repair the wall of Jerusalem.

person:harim_1416.name: Harim
person:harim_1416.title: Harim
person:harim_1416.summary: The head of the second course of priests (1 Chr. 24:8).

person:harnepher_1420.name: Harnepher
person:harnepher_1420.title: Harnepher
person:harnepher_1420.summary: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:36).

person:harsha_1422.name: Harsha
person:harsha_1422.title: Harsha
person:harsha_1422.summary: Worker or enchanter, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52; Neh. 7:54).

person:harum_1423.name: Harum
person:harum_1423.title: Harum
person:harum_1423.summary: Elevated, (1 Chr. 4:8), a descendant of Judah.

person:haruz_1425.name: Haruz
person:haruz_1425.title: Haruz
person:haruz_1425.summary: Eager, the father of Meshullemeth, the wife of king Manasseh (2 Kings 21:19) and mother of king Amon.

person:hasadiah_1426.name: Hasadiah
person:hasadiah_1426.title: Hasadiah
person:hasadiah_1426.summary: Favoured by Jehovah, one of the sons of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:20), of the royal line of David.

person:hasenuah_1427.name: Hasenuah
person:hasenuah_1427.title: Hasenuah
person:hasenuah_1427.summary: Bristling or hated, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 9:7).

person:hashabiah_1433.name: Hashabiah
person:hashabiah_1433.title: Hashabiah
person:hashabiah_1433.summary: One of the chief Levites (2 Chr. 35:9).

person:hashabiah_1434.name: Hashabiah
person:hashabiah_1434.title: Hashabiah
person:hashabiah_1434.summary: One of the chief priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:24).

person:hashabniah_1440.name: Hashabniah
person:hashabniah_1440.title: Hashabniah
person:hashabniah_1440.summary: One of the Levites whom Ezra appointed to interpret the law to the people (Neh. 9:5).

person:hashbadana_1441.name: Hashbadana
person:hashbadana_1441.title: Hashbadana
person:hashbadana_1441.summary: Consideration in judging, stood at Ezra’s left hand when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

person:hashubah_1445.name: Hashubah
person:hashubah_1445.title: Hashubah
person:hashubah_1445.summary: Ibid., a descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:20).

person:hashum_1447.name: Hashum
person:hashum_1447.title: Hashum
person:hashum_1447.summary: Stood on Ezra’s left hand while he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

person:hasrah_1414.name: Hasrah
person:hasrah_1414.title: Hasrah
person:hasrah_1414.summary: Poverty, “keeper of the wardrobe,” i.e., of the sacerdotal vestments (2 Chr. 34:22); called Harhas 2 Kings 22:14. He was husband of the prophetess Huldah.

person:hasshub_1450.name: Hasshub
person:hasshub_1450.title: Hasshub
person:hasshub_1450.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

person:hasupha_1451.name: Hasupha
person:hasupha_1451.title: Hasupha
person:hasupha_1451.summary: Uncovered, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

person:hatach_1452.name: Hatach
person:hatach_1452.title: Hatach
person:hatach_1452.summary: Verity, one of the eunuchs or chamberlains in the palace of Ahasuerus (Esther 4:5, 6, 9, 10).

person:hatita_1455.name: Hatita
person:hatita_1455.title: Hatita
person:hatita_1455.summary: Exploration, one of the temple porters or janitors (Ezra 2:42). He returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.

person:hattush_1460.name: Hattush
person:hattush_1460.title: Hattush
person:hattush_1460.summary: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

person:havilah_1461.name: Havilah
person:havilah_1461.title: Havilah (son of Cush)
person:havilah_1461.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

person:hazael_1463.name: Hazael
person:hazael_1463.title: Hazael
person:hazael_1463.summary: Whom God beholds, an officer of Ben-hadad II., king of Syria, who ultimately came to the throne, according to the word of the Lord to Elijah (1 Kings 19:15), after he had put the king to death (2 Kings 8:15). His interview with Elisha is mentioned in 2 Kings 8. The Assyrians soon after his accession to the throne came against him and defeated him with very great loss; and three years afterwards again invaded Syria, but on this occasion Hazael submitted to them. He then turned his arms against Israel, and ravaged “all the land of Gilead,” etc. (2 Kings 10:33), which he held in a degree of subjection to him (13:3-7, 22). …

person:hazarmaveth_1465.name: Hazarmaveth
person:hazarmaveth_1465.title: Hazarmaveth
person:hazarmaveth_1465.summary: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20). It is probably the modern province of Hadramaut, situated on the Indian Ocean east of the modern Yemen.

person:hazo_1468.name: Hazo
person:hazo_1468.title: Hazo
person:hazo_1468.summary: Vision, one of the sons of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

person:heber_1469.name: Heber
person:heber_1469.title: Heber
person:heber_1469.summary: Son of Beriah and grandson of Asher (Gen. 46:17; 1 Chr. 7:31, 32).

person:heber_1470.name: Heber
person:heber_1470.title: Heber
person:heber_1470.summary: The Kenite (Judg. 4:11, 17; 5:24), a descendant of Hobab. His wife Jael received Sisera (q.v.) into her tent and then killed him.

person:heber_1472.name: Heber
person:heber_1472.title: Heber
person:heber_1472.summary: One of the seven heads of the families of the Gadites (1 Chr. 5:13).

person:hebron_1475.name: Hebron
person:hebron_1475.title: Hebron
person:hebron_1475.summary: The third son of Kohath the Levite (Ex. 6:18; 1 Chr. 6:2, 18).

person:hegai_1477.name: Hegai
person:hegai_1477.title: Hegai
person:hegai_1477.summary: Eunuch, had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:8).

person:helah_1478.name: Helah
person:helah_1478.title: Helah
person:helah_1478.summary: Rust, (1 Chr. 4:5, 7), one of the wives of Ashur.

person:heleb_1480.name: Heleb
person:heleb_1480.title: Heleb
person:heleb_1480.summary: Fatness, one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:29).

person:helem_1479.name: Helem
person:helem_1479.title: Helem
person:helem_1479.summary: Zech. 6:10, one who returned from Babylon.

person:heli_1484.name: Heli
person:heli_1484.title: Heli
person:heli_1484.summary: Elevation, father of Joseph in the line of our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:23).

person:helkai_1485.name: Helkai
person:helkai_1485.title: Helkai
person:helkai_1485.summary: Smooth-tongued, one of the chief priests in the time of Joiakim (Neh. 12:15).

person:helon_1486.name: Helon
person:helon_1486.title: Helon
person:helon_1486.summary: Strong, father of Eliab, who was “captain of the children of Zebulun” (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

person:heman_1488.name: Heman
person:heman_1488.title: Heman
person:heman_1488.summary: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

person:heman_1489.name: Heman
person:heman_1489.title: Heman
person:heman_1489.summary: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

person:heman_1490.name: Heman
person:heman_1490.title: Heman
person:heman_1490.summary: Grandson of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:33; 15:17), to whom the 88th Psalm probably was inscribed. He was one of the “seers” named in 2 Chr. 29:14, 30, and took a leading part in the administration of the sacred services.

person:henadad_1493.name: Henadad
person:henadad_1493.title: Henadad
person:henadad_1493.summary: Favour of Hadad, the name of a Levite after the Captivity (Ezra 3:9).

person:hepher_1497.name: Hepher
person:hepher_1497.title: Hepher
person:hepher_1497.summary: The second son of Asher (1 Chr. 4:6).

person:hermogenes_1503.name: Hermogenes
person:hermogenes_1503.title: Hermogenes
person:hermogenes_1503.summary: Mercury-born, at one time Paul’s fellow-labourer in Asia Minor, who, however, afterwards abandoned him, along with one Phygellus, probably on account of the perils by which they were beset (2 Tim. 1:15).

person:herod_1505.name: Herod Antipas
person:herod_1505.title: Herod Antipas
person:herod_1505.summary: Herod’s son by Malthace (Matt. 14:1; Luke 3:1, 19; 9:7; Acts 13:1).

person:herod_1506.name: Herod Agrippa I
person:herod_1506.title: Herod Agrippa I
person:herod_1506.summary: Son of Aristobulus and Bernice, and grandson of Herod the Great. He was made tetrarch of the provinces formerly held by Lysanias II., and ultimately possessed the entire kingdom of his grandfather, Herod the Great, with the title of king. He put the apostle James the elder to death, and cast Peter into prison (Luke 3:1; Acts 12:1-19). On the second day of a festival held in honour of the emperor Claudius, he appeared in the great theatre of Caesarea. “The king came in clothed in magnificent robes, of which silver was the costly brilliant material. …

person:herodias_1507.name: Herodias
person:herodias_1507.title: Herodias
person:herodias_1507.summary: (Matt. 14:3-11; Mark 6:17-28; Luke 3:19), the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice. While residing at Rome with her husband Herod Philip I. and her daughter, Herod Antipas fell in with her during one of his journeys to that city. She consented to leave her husband and become his wife. Some time after, Herod met John the Baptist, who boldly declared the marriage to be unlawful. For this he was “cast into prison,” in the castle probably of Machaerus (q.v.), and was there subsequently beheaded.

person:herodion_1508.name: Herodion
person:herodion_1508.title: Herodion
person:herodion_1508.summary: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes and calls his “kinsman” (Rom. 16:11).

person:heth_1510.name: Heth
person:heth_1510.title: Heth
person:heth_1510.summary: Dread, a descendant of Canaan, and the ancestor of the Hittites (Gen. 10:18; Deut. 7:1), who dwelt in the vicinity of Hebron (Gen. 23:3, 7). The Hittites were a Hamitic race. They are called “the sons of Heth” (Gen. 23:3, 5, 7, 10, 16, 18, 20).

person:hezekiah_1512.name: Hezekiah
person:hezekiah_1512.title: Hezekiah
person:hezekiah_1512.summary: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697). The history of this king is contained in 2 Kings 18:20, Isa. 36-39, and 2 Chr. 29-32. He is spoken of as a great and good king. In public life he followed the example of his great-granfather Uzziah. He set himself to abolish idolatry from his kingdom, and among other things which he did for this end, he destroyed the “brazen serpent,” which had been removed to Jerusalem, and had become an object of idolatrous worship (Num. 21:9). A great reformation was wrought in the kingdom of Judah in his day (2 Kings 18:4; 2 Chr. …

person:hezion_1515.name: Hezion
person:hezion_1515.title: Hezion
person:hezion_1515.summary: Vision, the father of Tabrimon, and grandfather of Ben-hadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

person:hezir_1516.name: Hezir
person:hezir_1516.title: Hezir
person:hezir_1516.summary: The head of the seventeenth course of the priests (1 Chr. 24:15).

person:hezir_1517.name: Hezir
person:hezir_1517.title: Hezir
person:hezir_1517.summary: Neh. 10:20, one who sealed Nehemiah’s covenant.

person:hezrai_1518.name: Hezrai
person:hezrai_1518.title: Hezrai
person:hezrai_1518.summary: A Carmelite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:37).

person:hezron_1519.name: Hezron
person:hezron_1519.title: Hezron
person:hezron_1519.summary: One of the sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9; Ex. 6:14).

person:hezron_1520.name: Hezron
person:hezron_1520.title: Hezron
person:hezron_1520.summary: The older of the two sons of Pharez (Gen. 46:12).

person:hiel_1522.name: Hiel
person:hiel_1522.title: Hiel
person:hiel_1522.summary: Life of (i.e., from) God, a native of Bethel, who built (i.e., fortified) Jericho some seven hundred years after its destruction by the Israelites. There fell on him for such an act the imprecation of Joshua (6:26). He laid the foundation in his first-born, and set up the gates in his youngest son (1 Kings 16:34), i.e., during the progress of the work all his children died.

person:hilkiah_1524.name: Hilkiah
person:hilkiah_1524.title: Hilkiah
person:hilkiah_1524.summary: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem. While this was in progress, he discovered in some hidden corner of the building a book called the “book of the law” (2 Kings 22:8) and the “book of the covenant” (23:2). Some have supposed that this “book” was nothing else than the original autograph copy of the Pentateuch written by Moses (Deut. 31:9-26). This remarkable discovery occurred in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign (B.C. …

person:hillel_1530.name: Hillel
person:hillel_1530.title: Hillel
person:hillel_1530.summary: Praising, a Pirathonite, father of the judge Abdon (Judg. 12:13, 15).

person:hiram_1532.name: Hiram
person:hiram_1532.title: Hiram
person:hiram_1532.summary: Also “Huram” and “Horam,” king of Tyre. He entered into an alliance with David, and assisted him in building his palace by sending him able workmen, and also cedar-trees and fir-trees from Lebanon (2 Sam. 5:11; 1 Chr. 14:1). After the death of David he entered into a similar alliance with Solomon, and assisted him greatly in building the temple (1 Kings 5:1; 9:11; 2 Chr. 2:3). He also took part in Solomon’s traffic to the Eastern Seas (1 Kings 9:27; 10:11; 2 Chr. 8:18; 9:10).

person:hiram_1533.name: Hiram
person:hiram_1533.title: Hiram
person:hiram_1533.summary: The “master workman” whom Hiram sent to Solomon. He was the son of a widow of Dan, and of a Tyrian father. In 2 Chr. 2:13 “Huram my father” should be Huram Abi, the word “Abi” (rendered here “my father”) being regarded as a proper name, or it may perhaps be a title of distinction given to Huram, and equivalent to “master.” (Comp. 1 Kings 7:14; 2 Chr. 4:16.) He cast the magnificent brazen works for Solomon’s temple in clay-beds in the valley of Jordan, between Succoth and Zarthan.

person:hivite_1534.name: Hivite
person:hivite_1534.title: Hivite
person:hivite_1534.summary:
One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. The name is interpreted as “midlanders” or “villagers” (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15). They were probably a branch of the Hittites. At the time of Jacob’s return to Canaan, Hamor the Hivite was the “prince of the land” (Gen. 24:2-28).
They are next mentioned during the Conquest (Josh. 9:7; 11:19). They principally inhabited the northern confines of Western Palestine (Josh. 11:3; Judg. 3:3). A remnant of them still existed in the time of Solomon (1 Kings 9:20).

person:hobab_1537.name: Hobab
person:hobab_1537.title: Hobab
person:hobab_1537.summary: Beloved, the Kenite, has been usually identified with Jethro (q.v.), Ex. 18:5, 27; comp. Num. 10:29, 30. In Judg. 4:11, the word rendered “father-in-law” means properly any male relative by marriage (comp. Gen. 19:14, “son-in-law,” A.V.), and should be rendered “brother-in-law,” as in the R.V. His descendants followed Israel to Canaan (Num. 10:29), and at first pitched their tents near Jericho, but afterwards settled in the south in the borders of Arad (Judg. 1:8-11, 16).

person:hodijah_1545.name: Hodijah
person:hodijah_1545.title: Hodijah
person:hodijah_1545.summary: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law (Neh. 8:7; 9:5).

person:hodijah_1547.name: Hodijah
person:hodijah_1547.title: Hodijah
person:hodijah_1547.summary: Neh. 10:18, a Levite who sealed the covenant.

person:hoglah_1548.name: Hoglah
person:hoglah_1548.title: Hoglah
person:hoglah_1548.summary: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses (Num. 26:33; 27:1; 36:11).

person:hoham_1549.name: Hoham
person:hoham_1549.title: Hoham
person:hoham_1549.summary: Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon. He and his allies were defeated (Josh. 10:3, 5, 16-27).

person:holy_spirit_7400.name: Holy Spirit
person:holy_spirit_7400.title: Holy Spirit
person:holy_spirit_7400.summary:
The third Person of the adorable Trinity.
His personality is proved (1) from the fact that the attributes of personality, as intelligence and volition, are ascribed to him (John 14:17, 26; 15:26; 1 Cor. 2:10, 11; 12:11). He reproves, helps, glorifies, intercedes (John 16:7-13; Rom. 8:26). (2) He executes the offices peculiar only to a person. The very nature of these offices involves personal distinction (Luke 12:12; Acts 5:32; 15:28; 16:6; 28:25; 1 Cor. 2:13; Heb. 2:4; 3:7; 2 Pet. 1:21).
His divinity is established (1) from the fact that the names of God are ascribed to him (Ex. 17:7; Ps. 95:7; comp. Heb. 3:7-11); and (2) that divine attributes are also ascribed to him, omnipresence (Ps. …

person:hophni_1550.name: Hophni
person:hophni_1550.title: Hophni
person:hophni_1550.summary: Pugilist or client, one of the two sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:34), who, because he was “very old,” resigned to them the active duties of his office. By their scandalous conduct they brought down a curse on their father’s house (2:22, 12-27, 27-36; 3:11-14). For their wickedness they were called “sons of Belial,” i.e., worthless men (2:12). They both perished in the disastrous battle with the Philistines at Aphek (4:11).

person:hosah_1554.name: Hosah
person:hosah_1554.title: Hosah
person:hosah_1554.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 16:38).

person:hosea_1555.name: Hosea
person:hosea_1555.title: Hosea
person:hosea_1555.summary: Salvation, the son of Beeri, and author of the book of prophecies bearing his name. He belonged to the kingdom of Israel. “His Israelitish origin is attested by the peculiar, rough, Aramaizing diction, pointing to the northern part of Palestine; by the intimate acquaintance he evinces with the localities of Ephraim (5:1; 6:8, 9; 12:12; 14:6, etc.); by passages like 1:2, where the kingdom is styled ‘the land’, and 7:5, where the Israelitish king is designated as ‘our’ king.” The period of his ministry (extending to some sixty years) is indicated in the superscription (Hos. 1:1, 2). He is the only prophet of Israel who has left any written prophecy.

person:hoshea_1559.name: Hoshea
person:hoshea_1559.title: Hoshea
person:hoshea_1559.summary: The last king of Israel. He conspired against and slew his predecessor, Pekah (Isa. 7:16), but did not ascend the throne till after an interregnum of warfare of eight years (2 Kings 17:1, 2). Soon after this he submitted to Shalmaneser, the Assyrian king, who a second time invaded the land to punish Hoshea, because of his withholding tribute which he had promised to pay. A second revolt brought back the Assyrian king Sargon, who besieged Samaria, and carried the ten tribes away beyond the Euphrates, B.C. 720 (2 Kings 17:5, 6; 18:9-12). No more is heard of Hoshea. He disappeared like “foam upon the water” (Hos. 10:7; 13:11).

person:hoshea_1560.name: Hoshea
person:hoshea_1560.title: Hoshea
person:hoshea_1560.summary: 1 Chr. 27:20. The ruler of Ephraim in David’s time.

person:hotham_1562.name: Hotham
person:hotham_1562.title: Hotham
person:hotham_1562.summary: A stroke, great-grandson of Asher (1 Chr. 7:35).

person:hul_1566.name: Hul
person:hul_1566.title: Hul
person:hul_1566.summary: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

person:huldah_1567.name: Huldah
person:huldah_1567.title: Huldah
person:huldah_1567.summary: Weasel, a prophetess; the wife of Shallum. She was consulted regarding the “book of the law” discovered by the high priest Hilkiah (2 Kings 22:14-20; 2 Chr. 34:22-28). She resided in that part of Jerusalem called the Mishneh (A.V., “the college;” R.V., “the second quarter”), supposed by some to be the suburb between the inner and the outer wall, the second or lower city, Akra. Miriam (Ex. 15:20) and Deborah (Judg. 4:4) are the only others who bear the title of “prophetess,” for the word in Isa. 8:3 means only the prophet’s wife.

person:hur_1571.name: Hur
person:hur_1571.title: Hur
person:hur_1571.summary: The husband of Miriam, Moses’ sister (Ex. 17:10-12). He was associated with Aaron in charge of the people when Moses was absent on Sinai (Ex. 24:14). He was probably of the tribe of Judah, and grandfather of Bezaleel (Ex. 31:2; 35:30; 1 Chr. 2:19).

person:hur_1572.name: Hur
person:hur_1572.title: Hur
person:hur_1572.summary: One of the five princes of Midian who were defeated and slain by the Israelites under the command of Phinehas (Num. 31:8).

person:hurai_1521.name: Hurai
person:hurai_1521.title: Hurai
person:hurai_1521.summary: Linen-worker, one of David’s heroes, a native of the valley of Mount Gaash (1 Chr. 11:32).

person:huram_1569.name: Huram
person:huram_1569.title: Huram
person:huram_1569.summary: Generally “Huram,” one of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:5).

person:hushai_1577.name: Hushai
person:hushai_1577.title: Hushai
person:hushai_1577.summary: Quick, “the Archite,” “the king’s friend” (1 Chr. 27:33). When David fled from Jerusalem, on account of the rebellion of Absalom, and had reached the summit of Olivet, he there met Hushai, whom he sent back to Jerusalem for the purpose of counteracting the influence of Ahithophel, who had joined the ranks of Absalom (2 Sam. 15:32, 37; 16:16-18). It was by his advice that Absalom refrained from immediately pursuing after David. By this delay the cause of Absalom was ruined, for it gave David time to muster his forces.

person:ibhar_1584.name: Ibhar
person:ibhar_1584.title: Ibhar
person:ibhar_1584.summary: Chosen, one of David’s sons (1 Chr. 3:6; 2 Sam. 5:15).

person:ibzan_1588.name: Ibzan
person:ibzan_1588.title: Ibzan
person:ibzan_1588.summary: Illustrious, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:8-10). He ruled seven years.

person:iddo_1591.name: Iddo
person:iddo_1591.title: Iddo
person:iddo_1591.summary: Timely. The father of Ahinadab, who was one of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:14).

person:iddo_1593.name: Iddo
person:iddo_1593.title: Iddo
person:iddo_1593.summary: Lovely. The son of Zechariah (1 Chr. 27:21), the ruler of Manasseh in David’s time.

person:iddo_1594.name: Iddo
person:iddo_1594.title: Iddo
person:iddo_1594.summary: Lovely. A prophet of Judah who wrote the history of Rehoboam and Abijah (2 Chr. 12:15). He has been identified with Oded (2 Chr. 15:1).

person:igal_1598.name: Igal
person:igal_1598.title: Igal
person:igal_1598.summary: Num. 13:7, one of the spies of the tribe of Issachar.

person:igal_1599.name: Igal
person:igal_1599.title: Igal
person:igal_1599.summary: Son of Nathan of Zobah, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:36).

person:ilai_2982.name: Ilai
person:ilai_2982.title: Ilai
person:ilai_2982.summary: An Ahohite, one of David’s chief warriors (1 Chr. 11:29); called also Zalmon (2 Sam. 23:28).

person:imla_597.name: Imla
person:imla_597.title: Imla
person:imla_597.summary: Replenisher, the father of Micaiah the prophet (2 Chr. 18:7, 8).

person:immer_599.name: Immer
person:immer_599.title: Immer
person:immer_599.summary: The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:14).

person:iphedeiah_606.name: Iphedeiah
person:iphedeiah_606.title: Iphedeiah
person:iphedeiah_606.summary: Set free by Jehovah, a chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:25).

person:ira_608.name: Ira
person:ira_608.title: Ira
person:ira_608.summary: A Jairite and priest, a royal chaplain (2 Sam. 20:26) or confidential adviser (comp. 2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Chr. 18:17).

person:ira_609.name: Ira
person:ira_609.title: Ira
person:ira_609.summary: A Tekoite, one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

person:ira_610.name: Ira
person:ira_610.title: Ira
person:ira_610.summary: An Ithrite, also one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:38).

person:irad_611.name: Irad
person:irad_611.title: Irad
person:irad_611.summary: Runner; wild ass, one of the antediluvian patriarchs, the father of Mehujael (Gen. 4:18), and grandson of Cain.

person:iram_612.name: Iram
person:iram_612.title: Iram
person:iram_612.summary: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

person:isaac_616.name: Isaac
person:isaac_616.title: Isaac
person:isaac_616.summary:
The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3). He was circumcised when eight days old (4-7); and when he was probably two years old a great feast was held in connection with his being weaned.
The next memorable event in his life is that connected with the command of God given to Abraham to offer him up as a sacrifice on a mountain in the land of Moriah (Gen. 22). When he was forty years of age Rebekah was chosen for his wife (Gen. 24). …

person:isaiah_617.name: Isaiah
person:isaiah_617.title: Isaiah
person:isaiah_617.summary:
The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1). He had two sons, who bore symbolical names.
He exercised the functions of his office during the reigns of Uzziah (or Azariah), Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah (1:1). Uzziah reigned fifty-two years (B.C. 810-759), and Isaiah must have begun his career a few years before Uzziah’s death, probably B.C. 762. He lived till the fourteenth year of Hezekiah, and in all likelihood outlived that monarch (who died B.C. …

person:iscah_618.name: Iscah
person:iscah_618.title: Iscah
person:iscah_618.summary: Spy, the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot (Gen. 11:29, 31).

person:ish-bosheth_622.name: Ish-bosheth
person:ish-bosheth_622.title: Ish-bosheth
person:ish-bosheth_622.summary: Man of shame or humiliation, the youngest of Saul’s four sons, and the only one who survived him (2 Sam. 2-4). His name was originally Eshbaal (1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39). He was about forty years of age when his father and three brothers fell at the battle of Gilboa. Through the influence of Abner, Saul’s cousin, he was acknowledged as successor to the throne of Saul, and ruled over all Israel, except the tribe of Judah (over whom David was king), for two years, having Mahanaim, on the east of Jordan, as his capital (2 Sam. 2:9). After a troubled and uncertain reign he was murdered by his guard, who stabbed him while he was asleep on his couch at mid-day (2 Sam. …

person:ishbak_620.name: Ishbak
person:ishbak_620.title: Ishbak
person:ishbak_620.summary: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

person:ishbi-benob_621.name: Ishbi-benob
person:ishbi-benob_621.title: Ishbi-benob
person:ishbi-benob_621.summary: My seat at Nob, one of the Rephaim, whose spear was three hundred shekels in weight. He was slain by Abishai (2 Sam. 21:16, 17).

person:ishmael_630.name: Ishmael
person:ishmael_630.title: Ishmael (Son of Hagar)
person:ishmael_630.summary: Abraham’s eldest son, by Hagar the concubine (Gen. 16:15; 17:23). He was born at Mamre, when Abraham was eighty-six years of age, eleven years after his arrival in Canaan (16:3; 21:5). At the age of thirteen he was circumcised (17:25). He grew up a true child of the desert, wild and wayward. On the occasion of the weaning of Isaac his rude and wayward spirit broke out in expressions of insult and mockery (21:9, 10); and Sarah, discovering this, said to Abraham, “Expel this slave and her son.” Influenced by a divine admonition, Abraham dismissed Hagar and her son with no more than a skin of water and some bread. …

person:ishmael_631.name: Ishmael
person:ishmael_631.title: Ishmael
person:ishmael_631.summary: The son of Nethaniah, “of the seed royal” (Jer. 40:8, 15). He plotted against Gedaliah, and treacherously put him and others to death. He carried off many captives, “and departed to go over to the Ammonites.”

person:ishmaiah_636.name: Ishmaiah
person:ishmaiah_636.title: Ishmaiah
person:ishmaiah_636.summary: Son of Obadiah, and viceroy of Zebulun under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:19).

person:ismaiah_643.name: Ismaiah
person:ismaiah_643.title: Ismaiah
person:ismaiah_643.summary: A Gibeonite who joined David at Ziklag, “a hero among the thirty and over the thirty” (1 Chr. 12:4).

person:israel_682.name: Israel
person:israel_682.title: Jacob (Israel)
person:israel_682.summary:
One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old. Like his father, he was of a quiet and gentle disposition, and when he grew up followed the life of a shepherd, while his brother Esau became an enterprising hunter. His dealing with Esau, however, showed much mean selfishness and cunning (Gen. 25:29-34).
When Isaac was about 160 years of age, Jacob and his mother conspired to deceive the aged patriarch (Gen. 27), with the view of procuring the transfer of the birthright to himself. …

person:issachar_645.name: Issachar
person:issachar_645.title: Issachar
person:issachar_645.summary:
Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2). He had four sons at the going down into Egypt (46:13; Num. 26:23, 25).
Issachar, Tribe of, during the journey through the wilderness, along with Judah and Zebulun (Num. 2:5), marched on the east of the tabernacle. This tribe contained 54,400 fighting men when the census was taken at Sinai. After the entrance into the Promised Land, this tribe was one of the six which stood on Gerizim during the ceremony of the blessing and cursing (Deut. 27:12). The allotment of Issachar is described in Josh. 19:17-23. …

person:ithamar_649.name: Ithamar
person:ithamar_649.title: Ithamar
person:ithamar_649.summary: Palm isle, the fourth and youngest son of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:3). He was consecrated to the priesthood along with his brothers (Ex. 6:23); and after the death of Nadab and Abihu, he and Eleazar alone discharged the functions of that office (Lev. 10:6, 12; Num. 3:4). He and his family occupied the position of common priest till the high priesthood passed into his family in the person of Eli (1 Kings 2:27), the reasons for which are not recorded.

person:ittai_656.name: Ittai
person:ittai_656.title: Ittai
person:ittai_656.summary: A native of Gath, a Philistine, who had apparently the command of the six hundred heroes who formed David’s band during his wanderings (2 Sam. 15:19-22; comp. 1 Sam. 23:13; 27:2; 30:9, 10). He is afterwards with David at Mahanaim, holding in the army equal rank with Joab and Abishai (2 Sam. 18:2, 5, 12). He then passes from view.

person:ittai_657.name: Ittai
person:ittai_657.title: Ittai
person:ittai_657.summary: A Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29).

person:izhar_658.name: Izhar
person:izhar_658.title: Izhar
person:izhar_658.summary: Oil, one of the sons of Kohath, and grandson of Levi (Ex. 6:18, 21; Num. 16:1).

person:jaakobah_660.name: Jaakobah
person:jaakobah_660.title: Jaakobah
person:jaakobah_660.summary: Heel-catcher, a form of the name Jacob, one of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

person:jaala_661.name: Jaala
person:jaala_661.title: Jaala
person:jaala_661.summary: A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

person:jaalam_662.name: Jaalam
person:jaalam_662.title: Jaalam
person:jaalam_662.summary: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

person:jaanai_663.name: Jaanai
person:jaanai_663.title: Jaanai
person:jaanai_663.summary: Mourner, one of the chief Gadites (1 Chr. 5:12).

person:jaasiel_666.name: Jaasiel
person:jaasiel_666.title: Jaasiel
person:jaasiel_666.summary: Made by God, one of David’s body-guard, the son of Abner (1 Chr. 27:21), called Jasiel in 1 Chr. 11:47.

person:jaazaniah_668.name: Jaazaniah
person:jaazaniah_668.title: Jaazaniah
person:jaazaniah_668.summary: The son of Jeremiah, and one of the chief Rechabites (Jer. 35:3).

person:jaaziah_671.name: Jaaziah
person:jaaziah_671.title: Jaaziah
person:jaaziah_671.summary: Comforted by Jehovah, a descendant of Merari the Levite (1 Chr. 24:26, 27).

person:jaaziel_672.name: Jaaziel
person:jaaziel_672.title: Jaaziel
person:jaaziel_672.summary: Comforted by God, a Levitical musician (1 Chr. 15:18).

person:jabal_673.name: Jabal
person:jabal_673.title: Jabal
person:jabal_673.summary: A stream, a descendant of Cain, and brother of Jubal; “the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle” (Gen. 4:20). This description indicates that he led a wandering life.

person:jabesh_674.name: Jabesh
person:jabesh_674.title: Jabesh
person:jabesh_674.summary: The father of Shallum (2 Kings 15:10, 13, 14), who usurped the throne of Israel on the death of Zachariah.

person:jabez_675.name: Jabez
person:jabez_675.title: Jabez
person:jabez_675.summary: A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10).

person:jabin_676.name: Jabin
person:jabin_676.title: Jabin
person:jabin_676.summary: A king of Hazor, at the time of the entrance of Israel into Canaan (Josh. 11:1-14), whose overthrow and that of the northern chief with whom he had entered into a confederacy against Joshua was the crowning act in the conquest of the land (11:21-23; comp. 14:6-15). This great battle, fought at Lake Merom, was the last of Joshua’s battles of which we have any record. Here for the first time the Israelites encountered the iron chariots and horses of the Canaanites.

person:jabin_677.name: Jabin
person:jabin_677.title: Jabin (king of Hazor)
person:jabin_677.summary: Another king of Hazor, called “the king of Canaan,” who overpowered the Israelites of the north one hundred and sixty years after Joshua’s death, and for twenty years held them in painful subjection. The whole population were paralyzed with fear, and gave way to hopeless despondency (Judg. 5:6-11), till Deborah and Barak aroused the national spirit, and gathering together ten thousand men, gained a great and decisive victory over Jabin in the plain of Esdraelon (Judg. 4:10-16; comp. Ps. 83:9). This was the first great victory Israel had gained since the days of Joshua. They never needed to fight another battle with the Canaanites (Judg. 5:31).

person:jachan_678.name: Jachan
person:jachan_678.title: Jachan
person:jachan_678.summary: Mourner, one of the chief Gadite “brothers” in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

person:jachin_679.name: Jachin
person:jachin_679.title: Jachin
person:jachin_679.summary: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

person:jachin_680.name: Jachin
person:jachin_680.title: Jachin
person:jachin_680.summary: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

person:jachin_681.name: Jachin
person:jachin_681.title: Jachin
person:jachin_681.summary: The head of one of the courses (the twenty-first) of priests (1 Chr. 24:17).

person:jaddua_686.name: Jaddua
person:jaddua_686.title: Jaddua
person:jaddua_686.summary: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:21).

person:jaddua_687.name: Jaddua
person:jaddua_687.title: Jaddua
person:jaddua_687.summary: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

person:jadon_688.name: Jadon
person:jadon_688.title: Jadon
person:jadon_688.summary: Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).

person:jael_689.name: Jael
person:jael_689.title: Jael
person:jael_689.summary: Mountain-goat, the wife of Heber the Kenite (Judg. 4:17-22). When the Canaanites were defeated by Barak, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, fled and sought refuge with the friendly tribe of Heber, beneath the oaks of Zaanaim. As he drew near, Jael invited him to enter her tent. He did so, and as he lay wearied on the floor he fell into a deep sleep. She then took in her left hand one of the great wooden pins (“nail”) which fastened down the cords of the tent, and in her right hand the mallet, or “hammer,” used for driving it into the ground, and stealthily approaching her sleeping guest, with one well-directed blow drove the nail through his temples into the earth (Judg. 5:27). …

person:jahath_692.name: Jahath
person:jahath_692.title: Jahath
person:jahath_692.summary: A son of Shimei, and grandson of Gershom (1 Chr. 23:10).

person:jahath_693.name: Jahath
person:jahath_693.title: Jahath
person:jahath_693.summary: One of the sons of Shelomoth, of the family of Kohath (1 Chr. 24:22).

person:jahath_694.name: Jahath
person:jahath_694.title: Jahath
person:jahath_694.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the overseers of the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

person:jahaziel_697.name: Jahaziel
person:jahaziel_697.title: Jahaziel
person:jahaziel_697.summary: A priest who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:6).

person:jahaziel_698.name: Jahaziel
person:jahaziel_698.title: Jahaziel
person:jahaziel_698.summary: The third son of Hebron (1 Chr. 23:19).

person:jahaziel_699.name: Jahaziel
person:jahaziel_699.title: Jahaziel
person:jahaziel_699.summary: The son of Zechariah, a Levite of the family of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14-17). He encouraged Jehoshaphat against the Moabites and Ammonites.

person:jahdai_701.name: Jahdai
person:jahdai_701.title: Jahdai
person:jahdai_701.summary: Grasper, a descendant of Caleb, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:47).

person:jahzeel_706.name: Jahzeel
person:jahzeel_706.title: Jahzeel
person:jahzeel_706.summary: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

person:jahzerah_707.name: Jahzerah
person:jahzerah_707.title: Jahzerah
person:jahzerah_707.summary: Returner, the son of Meshullam, and father of Adiel (1 Chr. 9:12).

person:jair_664.name: Jair
person:jair_664.title: Jair
person:jair_664.summary: The father of Elhanan, who slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath (1 Chr. 20:5).

person:jair_710.name: Jair
person:jair_710.title: Jair
person:jair_710.summary: A Benjamite, the father of Mordecai, Esther’s uncle (Esther 2:5).

person:jairus_711.name: Jairus
person:jairus_711.title: Jairus
person:jairus_711.summary: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41). Entering into the chamber of death, accompanied by Peter and James and John and the father and mother of the maiden, he went forward to the bed whereon the corpse lay, and said, Talitha cumi, i.e., “Maid, arise,” and immediately the spirit of the maiden came to her again, and she arose straightway; and “at once to strengthen that life which had come back to her, and to prove that she was indeed no ghost, but had returned to the realities of a mortal existence, he commanded to give her something to eat” (Mark 5:43).

person:jakeh_712.name: Jakeh
person:jakeh_712.title: Jakeh
person:jakeh_712.summary: Pious, the father of Agur (Prov. 30:1). Nothing is known of him.

person:jakim_714.name: Jakim
person:jakim_714.title: Jakim
person:jakim_714.summary: Chief of the twelfth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:12).

person:jalon_715.name: Jalon
person:jalon_715.title: Jalon
person:jalon_715.summary: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

person:jambres_716.name: Jambres
person:jambres_716.title: Jambres
person:jambres_716.summary: One of those who opposed Moses in Egypt (2 Tim. 3:8).

person:james_717.name: James
person:james_717.title: James (Son of Zebedee)
person:james_717.summary: The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56). With John and Peter he was present at the transfiguration (Matt. 17:1; Mark 9:2), at the raising of Jairus’s daughter (Mark 5:37-43), and in the garden with our Lord (14:33). Because, probably, of their boldness and energy, he and John were called Boanerges, i.e., “sons of thunder.” He was the first martyr among the apostles, having been beheaded by King Herod Agrippa (Acts 12:1, 2), A.D. 44. (Comp. Matt. 4:21; 20:20-23).

person:james_718.name: James
person:james_718.title: James (Son of Alphaeus)
person:james_718.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature. He is mentioned along with the other apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15). He had a separate interview with our Lord after his resurrection (1 Cor. 15:7), and is mentioned as one of the apostles of the circumcision (Acts 1:13). He appears to have occupied the position of head of the Church at Jerusalem, where he presided at the council held to consider the case of the Gentiles (Acts 12:17; 15:13-29: 21:18-24). This James was the author of the epistle which bears his name.

person:james_719.name: James
person:james_719.title: James (Brother of Jesus)
person:james_719.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature. He is mentioned along with the other apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15). He had a separate interview with our Lord after his resurrection (1 Cor. 15:7), and is mentioned as one of the apostles of the circumcision (Acts 1:13). He appears to have occupied the position of head of the Church at Jerusalem, where he presided at the council held to consider the case of the Gentiles (Acts 12:17; 15:13-29: 21:18-24). This James was the author of the epistle which bears his name.

person:jannes_725.name: Jannes
person:jannes_725.title: Jannes
person:jannes_725.summary: One of the Egyptians who “withstood Moses” (2 Tim. 3:8).

person:japheth_726.name: Japheth
person:japheth_726.title: Japheth
person:japheth_726.summary:
Wide spreading: “God shall enlarge Japheth” (Heb. Yaphat Elohim le-Yephet, Gen. 9:27. Some, however, derive the name from yaphah, “to be beautiful;” hence white), one of the sons of Noah, mentioned last in order (Gen. 5:32; 6:10; 7:13), perhaps first by birth (10:21; comp. 9:24). He and his wife were two of the eight saved in the ark (1 Pet. 3:20). He was the progenitor of many tribes inhabiting the east of Europe and the north of Asia (Gen. 10:2-5). An act of filial piety (9:20-27) was the occasion of Noah’s prophecy of the extension of his posterity.
After the Flood the earth was re-peopled by the descendants of Noah, “the sons of Japheth” (Gen. …

person:japhia_727.name: Japhia
person:japhia_727.title: Japhia
person:japhia_727.summary: The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Josh. 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Josh. 10:33).

person:japhia_728.name: Japhia
person:japhia_728.title: Japhia
person:japhia_728.summary: One of the sons of David (2 Sam. 5:15), born in Jerusalem.

person:jared_730.name: Jared
person:jared_730.title: Jared
person:jared_730.summary: The fourth antediluvian patriarch in descent from Seth (Gen. 5:15-20; Luke 3:37), the father of Enoch; called Jered in 1 Chr. 1:2.

person:jarib_733.name: Jarib
person:jarib_733.title: Jarib
person:jarib_733.summary: One of the chiefs sent by Ezra to bring up the priests to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16).

person:jashen_736.name: Jashen
person:jashen_736.title: Jashen
person:jashen_736.summary: Sleeping, called also Hashem (1 Chr. 11:34); a person, several of whose sons were in David’s body-guard (2 Sam. 23:32).

person:jasher_737.name: Jasher
person:jasher_737.title: Jasher
person:jasher_737.summary: Upright. “The Book of Jasher,” rendered in the LXX. “the Book of the Upright One,” by the Vulgate “the Book of Just Ones,” was probably a kind of national sacred song-book, a collection of songs in praise of the heroes of Israel, a “book of golden deeds,” a national anthology. We have only two specimens from the book, (1) the words of Joshua which he spake to the Lord at the crisis of the battle of Beth-horon (Josh. 10:12, 13); and (2) “the Song of the Bow,” that beautiful and touching mournful elegy which David composed on the occasion of the death of Saul and Jonathan (2 Sam. 1:18-27).

person:jashobeam_738.name: Jashobeam
person:jashobeam_738.title: Jashobeam
person:jashobeam_738.summary: Dweller among the people; or to whom the people turn, the Hachmonite (1 Chr. 11:11), one of David’s chief heroes who joined him at Ziklag (12:6). He was the first of the three who broke through the host of the Philistines to fetch water to David from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:13-17). He is also called Adino the Eznite (8).

person:jashub_1638.name: Jashub
person:jashub_1638.title: Jashub
person:jashub_1638.summary: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

person:jason_742.name: Jason
person:jason_742.title: Jason
person:jason_742.summary: He that will cure, the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica. The Jews assaulted his house in order to seize Paul, but failing to find him, they dragged Jason before the ruler of the city (Acts 17:5-9). He was apparently one of the kinsmen of Paul (Rom. 16:21), and accompanied him from Thessalonica to Corinth.

person:javan_744.name: Javan
person:javan_744.title: Javan
person:javan_744.summary: The fourth “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew. Alexander the Great is called the “king of Javan” (rendered “Grecia,” Dan. 8:21; 10:20; comp. 11:2; Zech. 9:13). This word was universally used by the nations of the East as the generic name of the Greek race.

person:jebusite_748.name: Jebusite
person:jebusite_748.title: Jebusite
person:jebusite_748.summary: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.). At the time of the arrival of the Israelites in Palestine they were ruled by Adonizedek (Josh. 10:1, 23). They were defeated by Joshua, and their king was slain; but they were not entirely driven out of Jebus till the time of David, who made it the capital of his kingdom instead of Hebron. The site on which the temple was afterwards built belonged to Araunah, a Jebusite, from whom it was purchased by David, who refused to accept it as a free gift (2 Sam. 24:16-25; 1 Chr. 21:24, 25).

person:jecoliah_750.name: Jecoliah
person:jecoliah_750.title: Jecoliah
person:jecoliah_750.summary: Able through Jehovah, the wife of King Amaziah, and mother of King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:3).

person:jedaiah_751.name: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_751.title: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_751.summary: Invoker of Jehovah. The son of Shimri, a chief Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).

person:jedaiah_752.name: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_752.title: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_752.summary: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

person:jedaiah_753.name: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_753.title: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_753.summary: Knowing Jehovah. The chief of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:7).

person:jedaiah_754.name: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_754.title: Jedaiah
person:jedaiah_754.summary: One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10).

person:jediael_757.name: Jediael
person:jediael_757.title: Jediael
person:jediael_757.summary: One of the sons of Benjamin, whose descendants numbered 17,200 warriors (1 Chr. 7:6, 10, 11).

person:jediael_758.name: Jediael
person:jediael_758.title: Jediael
person:jediael_758.summary: A Shimrite, one of David’s bodyguard (1 Chr. 11:45). Probably same as in 12:20.

person:jediael_760.name: Jediael
person:jediael_760.title: Jediael
person:jediael_760.summary: A Korhite of the family of Ebiasaph, and one of the gate-keepers to the temple (1 Chr. 26:2).

person:jeduthun_1224.name: Jeduthun
person:jeduthun_1224.title: Jeduthun (Ethan)
person:jeduthun_1224.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the leaders of the temple music (1 Chr. 6:44; 15:17, 19). He was probably the same as Jeduthun. He is supposed by some to be the same also as (1).

person:jehalelel_765.name: Jehalelel
person:jehalelel_765.title: Jehalelel
person:jehalelel_765.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (2 Chr. 29:12).

person:jehdeiah_766.name: Jehdeiah
person:jehdeiah_766.title: Jehdeiah
person:jehdeiah_766.summary: One of the Levitical attendants at the temple, a descendant of Shubael (1 Chr. 24:20).

person:jehdeiah_767.name: Jehdeiah
person:jehdeiah_767.title: Jehdeiah
person:jehdeiah_767.summary: A Meronothite, herdsman of the asses under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:30).

person:jehiel_770.name: Jehiel
person:jehiel_770.title: Jehiel
person:jehiel_770.summary: One of the Levites “of the second degree,” appointed to conduct the music on the occasion of the ark’s being removed to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

person:jehiel_772.name: Jehiel
person:jehiel_772.title: Jehiel
person:jehiel_772.summary: A Hachmonite, a tutor in the family of David toward the close of his reign (1 Chr. 27:32).

person:jehiel_773.name: Jehiel
person:jehiel_773.title: Jehiel
person:jehiel_773.summary: The second of Jehoshaphat’s six sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

person:jehiel_774.name: Jehiel
person:jehiel_774.title: Jehiel
person:jehiel_774.summary: One of the Levites of the family of Heman who assisted Hezekiah in his work of reformation (2 Chr. 29:14).

person:jehiel_776.name: Jehiel
person:jehiel_776.title: Jehiel
person:jehiel_776.summary: A “prince” and “ruler of the house of God” who contributed liberally to the renewal of the temple sacrifices under Josiah (2 Chr. 35:8).

person:jehizkiah_781.name: Jehizkiah
person:jehizkiah_781.title: Jehizkiah
person:jehizkiah_781.summary: Jehovah strengthens, one of the chiefs of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12).

person:jehoaddan_783.name: Jehoaddan
person:jehoaddan_783.title: Jehoaddan
person:jehoaddan_783.summary: Jehovah his ornament, the wife of King Jehoash, and mother of King Amaziah (2 Kings 14:2).

person:jehoahaz_784.name: Jehoahaz
person:jehoahaz_784.title: Jehoahaz
person:jehoahaz_784.summary: The son and successor of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 10:35). He reigned seventeen years, and followed the evil ways of the house of Jeroboam. The Syrians, under Hazael and Benhadad, prevailed over him, but were at length driven out of the land by his son Jehoash (13:1-9, 25).

person:jehoahaz_2516.name: Jehoahaz
person:jehoahaz_2516.title: Jehoahaz
person:jehoahaz_2516.summary: A son of king Josiah (1 Chr. 3:15; Jer. 22:11), who was elected to succeed his father on the throne, although he was two years younger than his brother Eliakim. He assumed the crown under the name of Jehoahaz (q.v.). He did not imitate the example of his father (2 Kings 23:32), but was “a young lion, and it learned to catch the prey; it devoured men” (Ezek. 19:3). His policy was anti-Egyptian therefore. Necho, at that time at Riblah, sent an army against Jerusalem, which at once yielded, and Jehoahaz was carried captive to the Egyptian camp, Eliakim being appointed king in his stead. He remained a captive in Egypt till his death, and was the first king of Judah that died in exile.

person:jehohanan_785.name: Jehohanan
person:jehohanan_785.title: Jehohanan
person:jehohanan_785.summary: A Korhite, the head of one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:3).

person:jehoiachin_791.name: Jehoiachin
person:jehoiachin_791.title: Jehoiachin
person:jehoiachin_791.summary: Succeeded his father Jehoiakin (B.C. 599) when only eight years of age, and reigned for one hundred days (2 Chr. 36:9). He is also called Jeconiah (Jer. 24:1; 27:20, etc.), and Coniah (22:24; 37:1). He was succeeded by his uncle, Mattaniah = Zedekiah (q.v.). He was the last direct heir to the Jewish crown. He was carried captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, along with the flower of the nobility, all the leading men in Jerusalem, and a great body of the general population, some thirteen thousand in all (2 Kings 24:12-16; Jer. 52:28). After an imprisonment of thirty-seven years (Jer. …

person:jehoiada_792.name: Jehoiada
person:jehoiada_792.title: Jehoiada
person:jehoiada_792.summary: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

person:jehoiada_793.name: Jehoiada
person:jehoiada_793.title: Jehoiada
person:jehoiada_793.summary:
The high priest at the time of Athaliah’s usurpation of the throne of Judah. He married Jehosheba, or Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram (2 Chr. 22:11), and took an active part along with his wife in the preservation and training of Jehoash when Athaliah slew all the royal family of Judah.
The plans he adopted in replacing Jehoash on the throne of his ancestors are described in 2 Kings 11:2; 12:2; 2 Chr. 22:11; 23:24. He was among the foremost of the benefactors of the kingdom, and at his death was buried in the city of David among the kings of Judah (2 Chr. 24:15, 16). He is said to have been one hundred and thirty years old.

person:jehoiakim_1085.name: Jehoiakim
person:jehoiakim_1085.title: Jehoiakim
person:jehoiakim_1085.summary:
He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C. 610-599). His original name was Eliakim (q.v.).
On the death of his father his younger brother Jehoahaz (=Shallum, Jer. 22:11), who favoured the Chaldeans against the Egyptians, was made king by the people; but the king of Egypt, Pharaoh-necho, invaded the land and deposed Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:33, 34; Jer. 22:10-12), setting Eliakim on the throne in his stead, and changing his name to Jehoiakim.
After this the king of Egypt took no part in Jewish politics, having been defeated by the Chaldeans at Carchemish (2 Kings 24:7; Jer. 46:2). …

person:jehoiarib_798.name: Jehoiarib
person:jehoiarib_798.title: Jehoiarib
person:jehoiarib_798.summary: Jehovah defends, a priest at Jerusalem, head of one of the sacerdotal courses (1 Chr. 9:10; 24:7). His “course” went up from Babylon after the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42).

person:jehonathan_800.name: Jehonathan
person:jehonathan_800.title: Jehonathan
person:jehonathan_800.summary: One of the stewards of David’s store-houses (1 Chr. 27:25).

person:jehonathan_801.name: Jehonathan
person:jehonathan_801.title: Jehonathan
person:jehonathan_801.summary: A Levite who taught the law to the people of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:jehoram_803.name: Jehoram
person:jehoram_803.title: Jehoram
person:jehoram_803.summary: The eldest son and successor of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned eight years (B.C. 892-885) alone as king of Judah, having been previously for some years associated with his father (2 Chr. 21:5, 20; 2 Kings 8:16). His wife was Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel. His daughter Jehosheba was married to the high priest Jehoiada. He sank into gross idolatry, and brought upon himself and his kingdom the anger of Jehovah. The Edomites revolted from under his yoke, and the Philistines and the Arabians and Cushites invaded the land, and carried away great spoil, along with Jehoram’s wives and all his children, except Ahaziah. …

person:jehoram_805.name: Jehoram
person:jehoram_805.title: Jehoram
person:jehoram_805.summary: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to instructruct the people in Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:jehoshabeath_811.name: Jehoshabeath
person:jehoshabeath_811.title: Jehoshabeath
person:jehoshabeath_811.summary: Jehovah-swearing, the daughter of Jehoram, the king of Israel. She is called Jehoshabeath in 2 Chr. 22:11. She was the only princess of the royal house who was married to a high priest, Jehoiada (2 Chr. 22:11).

person:jehoshaphat_806.name: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_806.title: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_806.summary: Son of Ahilud, “recorder” or annalist under David and Solomon (2 Sam. 8:16), a state officer of high rank, chancellor or vizier of the kingdom.

person:jehoshaphat_808.name: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_808.title: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_808.summary:
The son and successor of Asa, king of Judah. After fortifying his kingdom against Israel (2 Chr. 17:1, 2), he set himself to cleanse the land of idolatry (1 Kings 22:43). In the third year of his reign he sent out priests and Levites over the land to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7-9). He enjoyed a great measure of peace and prosperity, the blessing of God resting on the people “in their basket and their store.”
The great mistake of his reign was his entering into an alliance with Ahab, the king of Israel, which involved him in much disgrace, and brought disaster on his kingdom (1 Kings 22:1-33). Escaping from the bloody battle of Ramoth-gilead, the prophet Jehu (2 Chr. …

person:jehoshaphat_809.name: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_809.title: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_809.summary: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2, 14).

person:jehoshaphat_810.name: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_810.title: Jehoshaphat
person:jehoshaphat_810.summary: One of the priests who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

person:jehozabad_812.name: Jehozabad
person:jehozabad_812.title: Jehozabad
person:jehozabad_812.summary: The son of Shomer, one of the two conspirators who put king Jehoash to death in Millo in Jerusalem (2 Kings 12:21).

person:jehozabad_813.name: Jehozabad
person:jehozabad_813.title: Jehozabad
person:jehozabad_813.summary: The son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), one of the Levite porters.

person:jehu_816.name: Jehu
person:jehu_816.title: Jehu
