person:jehu_816.summary: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah (1 Kings 16:1, 7; 2 Chr. 19:2; 20:34), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

person:jehu_817.name: Jehu
person:jehu_817.title: Jehu
person:jehu_817.summary: King of Israel, the son of Jehoshaphat (2 Kings 9:2), and grandson of Nimshi. The story of his exaltation to the throne is deeply interesting. During the progress of a war against the Syrians, who were becoming more and more troublesome to Israel, in a battle at Ramoth-gilead Jehoram, the king of Israel, had been wounded; and leaving his army there, had returned to Jezreel, whither his ally, Ahaziah, king of Judah, had also gone on a visit of sympathy with him (2 Kings 8:28, 29). …

person:jehu_818.name: Jehu
person:jehu_818.title: Jehu
person:jehu_818.summary: The son of Obed, and father of Azariah (1 Chr. 2:38).

person:jehu_820.name: Jehu
person:jehu_820.title: Jehu
person:jehu_820.summary: One of the Benjamite slingers that joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

person:jehudi_823.name: Jehudi
person:jehudi_823.title: Jehudi
person:jehudi_823.summary: A Jew, son of Nethaniah. He was sent by the princes to invite Baruch to read Jeremiah’s roll to them (Jer. 36:14, 21).

person:jeiel_827.name: Jeiel
person:jeiel_827.title: Jeiel
person:jeiel_827.summary: One of the Levites who took part in praising God on the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:5).

person:jeiel_830.name: Jeiel
person:jeiel_830.title: Jeiel

person:jephthah_839.name: Jephthah
person:jephthah_839.title: Jephthah
person:jephthah_839.summary: Whom God sets free, or the breaker through, a “mighty man of valour” who delivered Israel from the oppression of the Ammonites (Judg. 11:1-33), and judged Israel six years (12:7). He has been described as “a wild, daring, Gilead mountaineer, a sort of warrior Elijah.” After forty-five years of comparative quiet Israel again apostatized, and in “process of time the children of Ammon made war against Israel” (11:5). In their distress the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob, to which he had fled when driven out wrongfully by his brothers from his father’s inheritance (2), and the people made him their head and captain. …

person:jephunneh_840.name: Jephunneh
person:jephunneh_840.title: Jephunneh
person:jephunneh_840.summary: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

person:jephunneh_841.name: Jephunneh
person:jephunneh_841.title: Jephunneh

person:jeremiah_851.summary: A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:10).

person:jeremiah_853.name: Jeremiah
person:jeremiah_853.title: Jeremiah
person:jeremiah_853.summary: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah (q.v.), a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628). He left his native place, and went to reside in Jerusalem, where he greatly assisted Josiah in his work of reformation (2 Kings 23:1-25). The death of this pious king was bewailed by the prophet as a national calamity (2 Chr. …

person:jerimoth_864.name: Jerimoth

person:jerimoth_866.summary: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

person:jerimoth_867.name: Jerimoth
person:jerimoth_867.title: Jerimoth
person:jerimoth_867.summary: A Levitical musician under Heman his father (1 Chr. 25:4).

person:jerimoth_870.name: Jerimoth
person:jerimoth_870.title: Jerimoth
person:jerimoth_870.summary: A Levite, one of the overseers of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13) in the reign of Hezekiah.

person:jeroboam_872.name: Jeroboam
person:jeroboam_872.title: Jeroboam
person:jeroboam_872.summary: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945). He was the son of a widow of Zereda, and while still young was promoted by Solomon to be chief superintendent of the “burnden”, i.e., of the bands of forced labourers. Influenced by the words of the prophet Ahijah, he began to form conspiracies with the view of becoming king of the ten tribes; but these having been discovered, he fled to Egypt (1 Kings 11:29-40), where he remained for a length of time under the protection of Shishak I. On the death of Solomon, the ten tribes, having revolted, sent to invite him to become their king. …

person:jeroboam_873.name: Jeroboam
person:jeroboam_873.title: Jeroboam
person:jeroboam_873.summary: Jeroboam II., the son and successor of Jehoash, and the fourteenth king of Israel, over which he ruled for forty-one years, B.C. 825-784 (2 Kings 14:23). He followed the example of the first Jeroboam in keeping up the worship of the golden calves (2 Kings 14:24). His reign was contemporary with those of Amaziah (2 Kings 14:23) and Uzziah (15:1), kings of Judah. He was victorious over the Syrians (13:4; 14:26, 27), and extended Israel to its former limits, from “the entering of Hamath to the sea of the plain” (14:25; Amos 6:14). His reign of forty-one years was the most prosperous that Israel had ever known as yet. …

person:jeroham_874.name: Jeroham

person:jeroham_874.summary: Father of Elkanah, and grandfather of the prophet Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1).

person:jeroham_877.name: Jeroham

person:jeroham_877.summary: 1 Chr. 9:12; a priest, perhaps the same as in Neh. 11:12.

person:jeroham_880.name: Jeroham
person:jeroham_880.title: Jeroham
person:jeroham_880.summary: 2 Chr. 23:1; one whose son assisted in placing Joash on the throne.

person:jerubbesheth_881.title: Jerubbesheth
person:jerubbesheth_881.summary: Contender with the shame; i.e., idol, a surname also of Gideon (2 Sam. 11:21).

person:jerushah_882.name: Jerushah
person:jerushah_882.title: Jerushah
person:jerushah_882.summary: Possession, or possessed; i.e., “by a husband”, the wife of Uzziah, and mother of king Jotham (2 Kings 15:33).

person:jesaiah_883.title: Jesaiah
person:jesaiah_883.summary: One of the three sons of Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

person:jeshaiah_647.name: Jeshaiah
person:jeshaiah_647.title: Jeshaiah
person:jeshaiah_647.summary: A Kohathite Levite, the father of Joram, of the family of Eliezer (1 Chr. 26:25); called also Isshiah (24:21).

person:jeshaiah_885.name: Jeshaiah
person:jeshaiah_885.title: Jeshaiah
person:jeshaiah_885.summary: One of the sons of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 15).

person:jesharelah_334.name: Jesharelah
person:jesharelah_334.title: Jesharelah
person:jesharelah_334.summary: Upright towards God, the head of the seventh division of Levitical musicians (1 Chr. 25:14).

person:jeshebeab_888.name: Jeshebeab
person:jeshebeab_888.title: Jeshebeab
person:jeshebeab_888.summary: Seat of his father, the head of the fourteenth division of priests (1 Chr. 24:13).

person:jesher_889.name: Jesher
person:jesher_889.title: Jesher
person:jesher_889.summary: Uprightness, the first of the three sons of Caleb by Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

person:jeshua_892.name: Jeshua
person:jeshua_892.title: Jeshua
person:jeshua_892.summary: A Levite appointed by Hezekiah to distribute offerings in the priestly cities (2 Chr. 31:15).

person:jeshua_899.name: Jeshua
person:jeshua_899.title: Jeshua
person:jeshua_899.summary: Head of the ninth priestly order (Ezra 2:36); called also Jeshuah (1 Chr. 24:11).

person:jesse_903.name: Jesse
person:jesse_903.title: Jesse
person:jesse_903.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12). The phrase “stem of Jesse” is used for the family of David (Isa. 11:1), and “root of Jesse” for the Messiah (Isa. 11:10; Rev. 5:5). Jesse was a man apparently of wealth and position at Bethlehem (1 Sam. 17:17, 18, 20; Ps. 78:71). The last reference to him is of David’s procuring for him an asylum with the king of Moab (1 Sam. 22:3).

person:jesus_904.name: Jesus
person:jesus_904.title: Jesus
person:jesus_904.summary:
A Jewish Christian surnamed Justus (Col. 4:11).
Je’sus, the proper, as Christ is the official, name of our Lord. To distinguish him from others so called, he is spoken of as “Jesus of Nazareth” (John 18:7), and “Jesus the son of Joseph” (John 6:42).
This is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, which was originally Hoshea (Num. 13:8, 16), but changed by Moses into Jehoshua (Num. 13:16; 1 Chr. 7:27), or Joshua. After the Exile it assumed the form Jeshua, whence the Greek form Jesus. It was given to our Lord to denote the object of his mission, to save (Matt. …

person:jesus_905.name: Jesus
person:jesus_905.title: Jesus Christ
person:jesus_905.summary:
Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah” (q.v.), the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament. It denotes that he was anointed or consecrated to his great redemptive work as Prophet, Priest, and King of his people. He is Jesus the Christ (Acts 17:3; 18:5; Matt. 22:42), the Anointed One. He is thus spoken of by Isaiah (61:1), and by Daniel (9:24-26), who styles him “Messiah the Prince.”
The Messiah is the same person as “the seed of the woman” (Gen. 3:15), “the seed of Abraham” (Gen. 22:18), the “Prophet like unto Moses” (Deut. 18:15), “the priest after the order of Melchizedek” (Ps. …

person:jether_906.name: Jether
person:jether_906.title: Jether
person:jether_906.summary: The oldest of Gideon’s seventy sons (Judg. 8:20).

person:jether_907.name: Jether
person:jether_907.title: Jether
person:jether_907.summary: The father of Amasa, David’s general (1 Kings 2:5, 32); called Ithra (2 Sam. 17:25).

person:jetheth_910.name: Jetheth
person:jetheth_910.title: Jetheth
person:jetheth_910.summary: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

person:jethro_2431.name: Jethro
person:jethro_2431.title: Jethro
person:jethro_2431.summary: “The priest of Midian,” Moses’ father-in-law (Ex. 2:18)=Raguel (Num. 10:29). If he be identified with Jethro (q.v.), then this may be regarded as his proper name, and Jether or Jethro (i.e., “excellency”) as his official title.

person:jetur_911.name: Jetur
person:jetur_911.title: Jetur
person:jetur_911.summary: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

person:jeuel_912.name: Jeuel
person:jeuel_912.title: Jeuel
person:jeuel_912.summary: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah (1 Chr. 9:6).

person:jeush_913.name: Jeush
person:jeush_913.title: Jeush
person:jeush_913.summary: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

person:jeush_1601.title: Jeush
person:jeush_1601.summary: A son of Bilhan, grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10).

person:jeush_1602.name: Jeush
person:jeush_1602.title: Jeush
person:jeush_1602.summary: A Levite, one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chr. 23:10, 11).

person:jeush_1603.name: Jeush
person:jeush_1603.title: Jeush
person:jeush_1603.summary: One of the three sons of Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:19).

person:jezaniah_667.name: Jezaniah
person:jezaniah_667.title: Jezaniah
person:jezaniah_667.summary: A Maachathite (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8; 42:1). He is also called Azariah (Jer. 43:2).

person:jezebel_1605.name: Jezebel
person:jezebel_1605.title: Jezebel
person:jezebel_1605.summary: Chaste, the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Zidonians, and the wife of Ahab, the king of Israel (1 Kings 16:31). This was the “first time that a king of Israel had allied himself by marriage with a heathen princess; and the alliance was in this case of a peculiarly disastrous kind. Jezebel has stamped her name on history as the representative of all that is designing, crafty, malicious, revengeful, and cruel. She is the first great instigator of persecution against the saints of God. Guided by no principle, restrained by no fear of either God or man, passionate in her attachment to her heathen worship, she spared no pains to maintain idolatry around her in all its splendour. …

person:jeziel_1608.name: Jeziel
person:jeziel_1608.title: Jeziel
person:jeziel_1608.summary: Assembled by God, a son of Azmaveth. He was one of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

person:joab_1617.name: Joab
person:joab_1617.title: Joab
person:joab_1617.summary: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15). His father’s name is nowhere mentioned, although his sepulchre at Bethlehem is mentioned (2 Sam. 2:32). His two brothers were Abishai and Asahel, the swift of foot, who was killed by Abner (2 Sam. 2:13-32), whom Joab afterwards treacherously murdered (3:22-27). He afterwards led the assault at the storming of the fortress on Mount Zion, and for this service was raised to the rank of “prince of the king’s army” (2 Sam. 5:6-10; 1 Chr. 27:34). …

person:joah_1621.name: Joah
person:joah_1621.title: Joah
person:joah_1621.summary: The son of Asaph, and “recorder” (q.v.) or chronicler to King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

person:joah_1623.name: Joah
person:joah_1623.title: Joah
person:joah_1623.summary: One of the sons of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), a Korhite porter.

person:joah_1626.name: Joah
person:joah_1626.title: Joah
person:joah_1626.summary: Son of Joahaz, and “recorder” (q.v.) or keeper of the state archives under King Josiah (2 Chr. 34:8).

person:joahaz_1627.name: Joahaz
person:joahaz_1627.title: Joahaz
person:joahaz_1627.summary: (2 Chr. 34:8), a contracted form of Jehoahaz (q.v.).

person:joanna_1628.name: Joanna
person:joanna_1628.title: Joanna
person:joanna_1628.summary: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ (Luke 3:27); the same as Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:19).

person:joanna_1629.name: Joanna
person:joanna_1629.title: Joanna
person:joanna_1629.summary: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3). She was one of the women who ministered to our Lord, and to whom he appeared after his resurrection (Luke 8:3; 24:10).

person:joash_1630.name: Joash
person:joash_1630.title: Joash
person:joash_1630.summary: A contracted form of Jehoash, the father of Gideon (Judg. 6:11, 29; 8:13, 29, 32).

person:joash_1631.name: Joash
person:joash_1631.title: Joash
person:joash_1631.summary: One of King Ahab’s sons (1 Kings 22:26).

person:joash_1632.name: Joash
person:joash_1632.title: Joash
person:joash_1632.summary: The son of King Ahaziah. While yet an infant, he was saved from the general massacre of the family by his aunt Jehosheba, and was apparently the only surviving descendant of Solomon (2 Chr. 21:4, 17). His uncle, the high priest Jehoiada, brought him forth to public notice when he was eight years of age, and crowned and anointed him king of Judah with the usual ceremonies. Athaliah was taken by surprise when she heard the shout of the people, “Long live the king;” and when she appeared in the temple, Jehoiada commanded her to be led forth to death (2 Kings 11:13-20). …

person:joash_1633.name: Joash
person:joash_1633.title: Joash
person:joash_1633.summary: The son and successor of Jehoahaz, king of Israel (2 Kings 14:1; comp. 12:1; 13:10). When he ascended the throne the kingdom was suffering from the invasion of the Syrians. Hazael “was cutting Israel short.” He tolerated the worship of the golden calves, yet seems to have manifested a character of sincere devotion to the God of his fathers. He held the prophet Elisha in honour, and wept by his bedside when he was dying, addressing him in the words Elisha himself had used when Elijah was carried up into heaven: “O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof.” He was afterwards involved in war with Amaziah, the king of Judah (2 Chr. …

person:joash_1636.name: Joash
person:joash_1636.title: Joash
person:joash_1636.summary: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

person:joash_1637.name: Joash
person:joash_1637.title: Joash
person:joash_1637.summary: One who had charge of the royal stores of oil under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:28).

person:job_1639.name: Job
person:job_1639.title: Job
person:job_1639.summary: Persecuted, an Arabian patriarch who resided in the land of Uz (q.v.). While living in the midst of great prosperity, he was suddenly overwhelmed by a series of sore trials that fell upon him. Amid all his sufferings he maintained his integrity. Once more God visited him with the rich tokens of his goodness and even greater prosperity than he had enjoyed before. He survived the period of trial for one hundred and forty years, and died in a good old age, an example to succeeding generations of integrity (Ezek. 14:14, 20) and of submissive patience under the sorest calamities (James 5:11). His history, so far as it is known, is recorded in his book.

person:jobab_1640.name: Jobab
person:jobab_1640.title: Jobab (son of Joktan)
person:jobab_1640.summary: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

person:jobab_1642.name: Jobab
person:jobab_1642.title: Jobab
person:jobab_1642.summary: A Canaanitish king (Josh. 11:1) who joined the confederacy against Joshua.

person:jochebed_1645.name: Jochebed
person:jochebed_1645.title: Jochebed
person:jochebed_1645.summary: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses (Num. 26:59). She is spoken of as the sister of Kohath, Amram’s father (Ex. 6:20; comp. 16, 18; 2:1-10).

person:joel_1647.name: Joel
person:joel_1647.title: Joel
person:joel_1647.summary: The oldest of Samuel’s two sons appointed by him as judges in Beersheba (1 Sam. 8:2).

person:joel_1653.name: Joel
person:joel_1653.title: Joel
person:joel_1653.summary: One of David’s famous warriors (1 Chr. 11:38).

person:joel_1654.name: Joel
person:joel_1654.title: Joel
person:joel_1654.summary: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 15:7, 11).

person:joel_1660.name: Joel
person:joel_1660.title: Joel
person:joel_1660.summary: The second of the twelve minor prophets. He was the son of Pethuel. His personal history is only known from his book.

person:joelah_1661.name: Joelah
person:joelah_1661.title: Joelah
person:joelah_1661.summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:7).

person:joezer_1662.name: Joezer
person:joezer_1662.title: Joezer
person:joezer_1662.summary: Jehovah is his help, one of the Korhites who became part of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 12:6).

person:johanan_1666.name: Johanan
person:johanan_1666.title: Johanan
person:johanan_1666.summary: Son of Careah, one of the Jewish chiefs who rallied round Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had made governor in Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8). He warned Gedaliah of the plans of Ishmael against him, a warning which was unheeded (Jer. 40:13, 16). He afterwards pursued the murderer of the governor, and rescued the captives (41:8, 13, 15, 16). He and his associates subsequently fled to Tahpanhes in Egypt (43:2, 4, 5), taking Jeremiah with them. “The flight of Gedaliah’s community to Egypt extinguished the last remaining spark of life in the Jewish state. The work of the ten centuries since Joshua crossed the Jordan had been undone.”

person:johanan_1667.name: Johanan
person:johanan_1667.title: Johanan
person:johanan_1667.summary: The oldest of King Josiah’s sons (1 Chr. 3:15).

person:johanan_1671.name: Johanan
person:johanan_1671.title: Johanan
person:johanan_1671.summary: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the desert of Judah (1 Chr. 12:12).

person:john_1676.name: John
person:john_1676.title: John the Baptist
person:john_1676.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent. His father, Zacharias, was a priest of the course of Abia (1 Chr. 24:10), and his mother, Elisabeth, was of the daughters of Aaron (Luke 1:5). The mission of John was the subject of prophecy (Matt. 3:3; Isa. 40:3; Mal. 3:1). His birth, which took place six months before that of Jesus, was foretold by an angel. Zacharias, deprived of the power of speech as a token of God’s truth and a reproof of his own incredulity with reference to the birth of his son, had the power of speech restored to him on the occasion of his circumcision (Luke 1:64). …

person:john_1677.name: John
person:john_1677.title: John the Apostle
person:john_1677.summary: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida. His father was apparently a man of some wealth (comp. Mark 1:20; Luke 5:3; John 19:27). He was doubtless trained in all that constituted the ordinary education of Jewish youth. When he grew up he followed the occupation of a fisherman on the Lake of Galilee. When John the Baptist began his ministry in the wilderness of Judea, John, with many others, gathered round him, and was deeply influenced by his teaching. …

person:john_1678.name: John
person:john_1678.title: John (Relative of the High Priest)
person:john_1678.summary: One who, with Annas and Caiaphas, sat in judgment on the apostles Peter and John (Acts 4:6). He was of the kindred of the high priest; otherwise unknown.

person:joiakim_1681.name: Joiakim
person:joiakim_1681.title: Joiakim
person:joiakim_1681.summary: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua (Neh. 12:10, 12, 26).

person:joiarib_797.name: Joiarib
person:joiarib_797.title: Joiarib
person:joiarib_797.summary: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

person:joiarib_1682.name: Joiarib
person:joiarib_1682.title: Joiarib
person:joiarib_1682.summary: Ezra 8:16, a “man of understanding” whom Ezra sent to “bring ministers for the house of God.”

person:jokim_1684.name: Jokim
person:jokim_1684.title: Jokim
person:jokim_1684.summary: Whom Jehovah has set up, one of the descendants of Shelah (1 Chr. 4:22).

person:jokshan_1685.name: Jokshan
person:jokshan_1685.title: Jokshan
person:jokshan_1685.summary: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).

person:joktan_1686.name: Joktan
person:joktan_1686.title: Joktan
person:joktan_1686.summary: Little, the second of the two sons of Eber (Gen. 10:25; 1 Chr. 1:19). There is an Arab tradition that Joktan (Arab. Kahtan) was the progenitor of all the purest tribes of Central and Southern Arabia.

person:jonadab_799.name: Jonadab
person:jonadab_799.title: Jonadab
person:jonadab_799.summary: A son of Rechab, the founder of a tribe who bound themselves by a vow to abstain from wine (Jer. 35:6-19). There were different settlements of Rechabites (Judg. 1:16; 4:11; 1 Chr. 2:55). His interview and alliance with Jehu are mentioned in 2 Kings 10:15-23. He went with Jehu in his chariot to Samaria.

person:jonadab_1688.name: Jonadab
person:jonadab_1688.title: Jonadab
person:jonadab_1688.summary: Son of Shammah, and David’s nephew, and also one of his chief warriors (2 Sam. 21:21). He slew a giant in Gath.

person:jonah_1689.name: Jonah
person:jonah_1689.title: Jonah
person:jonah_1689.summary: A dove, the son of Amittai of Gath-hepher. He was a prophet of Israel, and predicted the restoration of the ancient boundaries (2 Kings 14:25-27) of the kingdom. He exercised his ministry very early in the reign of Jeroboam II., and thus was contemporary with Hosea and Amos; or possibly he preceded them, and consequently may have been the very oldest of all the prophets whose writings we possess. His personal history is mainly to be gathered from the book which bears his name. It is chiefly interesting from the two-fold character in which he appears, (1) as a missionary to heathen Nineveh, and (2) as a type of the “Son of man.”

person:jonas_1687.name: Jonas
person:jonas_1687.title: Jonas
person:jonas_1687.summary: The father of the apostles Peter (John 21:15-17) and Andrew; but the reading should be (also in 1:42), as in the Revised Version, “John,” instead of Jonas.

person:jonathan_1691.name: Jonathan
person:jonathan_1691.title: Jonathan
person:jonathan_1691.summary: A Levite descended from Gershom (Judg. 18:30). His history is recorded in 17:7-13 and 18:30. The Rabbins changed this name into Manasseh “to screen the memory of the great lawgiver from the stain of having so unworthy an apostate among his near descendants.” He became priest of the idol image at Dan, and this office continued in his family till the Captivity.

person:jonathan_1692.name: Jonathan
person:jonathan_1692.title: Jonathan
person:jonathan_1692.summary: The eldest son of king Saul, and the bosom friend of David. He is first mentioned when he was about thirty years of age, some time after his father’s accession to the throne (1 Sam. 13:2). Like his father, he was a man of great strength and activity (2 Sam. 1:23), and excelled in archery and slinging (1 Chr. 12:2;2 Sam. 1:22). The affection that evidently subsisted between him and his father was interrupted by the growth of Saul’s insanity. At length, “in fierce anger,” he left his father’s presence and cast in his lot with the cause of David (1 Sam. 20:34). …

person:jonathan_1693.name: Jonathan
person:jonathan_1693.title: Jonathan
person:jonathan_1693.summary: Son of the high priest Abiathar, and one who adhered to David at the time of Absalom’s rebellion (2 Sam. 15:27, 36). He is the last descendant of Eli of whom there is any record.

person:joram_804.name: Joram
person:joram_804.title: Joram
person:joram_804.summary: The son of Ahab and Jezebel, and successor to his brother Ahaziah on the throne of Israel. He reigned twelve years, B.C. 896-884 (2 Kings 1:17; 3:1). His first work was to reduce to subjection the Moabites, who had asserted their independence in the reign of his brother. Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, assisted Jehoram in this effort. He was further helped by his ally the king of Edom. Elisha went forth with the confederated army (2 Kings 3:1-19), and at the solicitation of Jehoshaphat encouraged the army with the assurance from the Lord of a speedy victory. The Moabites under Mesha their king were utterly routed and their cities destroyed. At Kir-haraseth Mesha made a final stand. …

person:joram_1705.name: Joram
person:joram_1705.title: Joram
person:joram_1705.summary: The son of Tou, king of Hamath, sent by his father to congratulate David on his victory over Hadarezer, king of Syria (1 Chr. 18:10; called Joram 2 Sam. 8:10).

person:josabad_1708.name: Josabad
person:josabad_1708.title: Josabad
person:josabad_1708.summary: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

person:josedech_815.name: Josedech
person:josedech_815.title: Josedech
person:josedech_815.summary: Jehovah-justified, the son of the high priest Seraiah at the time of the Babylonian exile (1 Chr. 6:14, 15). He was carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar, and probably died in Babylon. He was the father of Jeshua, or Joshua, who returned with Zerubbabel.

person:joseph_1710.name: Joseph
person:joseph_1710.title: Joseph (son of Jacob)
person:joseph_1710.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.” “The Lord shall add [Heb. yoseph] to me another son” (Gen. 30:24). He was a child of probably six years of age when his father returned from Haran to Canaan and took up his residence in the old patriarchal town of Hebron. “Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age,” and he “made him a long garment with sleeves” (Gen. 37:3, R.V. marg.), i.e., a garment long and full, such as was worn by the children of nobles. This seems to be the correct rendering of the words. …

person:joseph_1712.name: Joseph
person:joseph_1712.title: Joseph (son of Asaph)
person:joseph_1712.summary: One of the sons of Asaph, head of the first division of sacred musicians (1 Chr. 25:2, 9).

person:joseph_1715.name: Joseph
person:joseph_1715.title: Joseph (Mary's Husband)
person:joseph_1715.summary: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.” He was by trade a carpenter (Matt. 13:55). He is last mentioned in connection with the journey to Jerusalem, when Jesus was twelve years old. It is probable that he died before Jesus entered on his public ministry. This is concluded from the fact that Mary only was present at the marriage feast in Cana of Galilee. His name does not appear in connection with the scenes of the crucifixion along with that of Mary (q.v.), John 19:25.

person:joseph_1716.name: Joseph
person:joseph_1716.title: Joseph (of Arimathea)
person:joseph_1716.summary: A native of Arimathea, probably the Ramah of the Old Testament (1 Sam. 1:19), a man of wealth, and a member of the Sanhedrim (Matt. 27:57; Luke 23:50), an “honourable counsellor, who waited for the kingdom of God.” As soon as he heard the tidings of Christ’s death, he “went in boldly” (lit. “having summoned courage, he went”) “unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.” Pilate having ascertained from the centurion that the death had really taken place, granted Joseph’s request, who immediately, having purchased fine linen (Mark 15:46), proceeded to Golgotha to take the body down from the cross. …

person:joseph_1718.name: Joseph
person:joseph_1718.title: Joseph (son of Judah)
person:joseph_1718.summary: The son of Judah, and father of Semei (Luke 3:26). Other two of the same name in the ancestry of Christ are also mentioned (3:24, 30).

person:joshua_893.name: Joshua
person:joshua_893.title: Joshua
person:joshua_893.summary: The son of Jozadak, and high priest of the Jews under Zerubbabel (Neh. 7:7; 12:1, 7, 10, 26); called Joshua (Hag. 1:1, 12; 2:2, 4; Zech. 3:1, 3, 6, 8, 9).

person:joshua_1727.name: Joshua
person:joshua_1727.title: Joshua
person:joshua_1727.summary:
Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel. He is called Jehoshua in Num. 13:16 (A.V.), and Jesus in Acts 7:45 and Heb. 4:8 (R.V., Joshua).
He was born in Egypt, and was probably of the age of Caleb, with whom he is generally associated. He shared in all the events of the Exodus, and held the place of commander of the host of the Israelites at their great battle against the Amalekites in Rephidim (Ex. 17:8-16). He became Moses’ minister or servant, and accompanied him part of the way when he ascended Mount Sinai to receive the two tables (Ex. 32:17). …

person:josiah_1730.name: Josiah
person:josiah_1730.title: Josiah
person:josiah_1730.summary: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chr. 34:1). His history is contained in 2 Kings 22, 23. He stands foremost among all the kings of the line of David for unswerving loyalty to Jehovah (23:25). He “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in all the way of David his father.” He ascended the throne at the early age of eight years, and it appears that not till eight years afterwards did he begin “to seek after the God of David his father.” At that age he devoted himself to God. …

person:josiah_1731.name: Josiah
person:josiah_1731.title: Josiah
person:josiah_1731.summary: Common in later times among the Jews in Palestine (Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34). It is noticeable that this familiar bird is only mentioned in these passages in connection with our Lord’s lamentation over the impenitence of Jerusalem.

person:jotham_1734.name: Jotham
person:jotham_1734.title: Jotham
person:jotham_1734.summary: The youngest of Gideon’s seventy sons. He escaped when the rest were put to death by the order of Abimelech (Judg. 9:5). When “the citizens of Shechem and the whole house of Millo” were gathered together “by the plain of the pillar” (i.e., the stone set up by Joshua, 24:26; comp. Gen. 35:4) “that was in Shechem, to make Abimelech king,” from one of the heights of Mount Gerizim he protested against their doing so in the earliest parable, that of the bramble-king. His words then spoken were prophetic. There came a recoil in the feelings of the people toward Abimelech, and then a terrible revenge, in which many were slain and the city of Shechem was destroyed by Abimelech (Judg. 9:45). …

person:jotham_1735.name: Jotham
person:jotham_1735.title: Jotham
person:jotham_1735.summary: The son and successor of Uzziah on the throne of Judah. As during his last years Uzziah was excluded from public life on account of his leprosy, his son, then twenty-five years of age, administered for seven years the affairs of the kingdom in his father’s stead (2 Chr. 26:21, 23; 27:1). After his father’s death he became sole monarch, and reigned for sixteen years (B.C. 759-743). He ruled in the fear of God, and his reign was prosperous. He was contemporary with the prophets Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, by whose ministrations he profited. He was buried in the sepulchre of the kings, greatly lamented by the people (2 Kings 15:38; 2 Chr. 27:7-9).

person:jubal_1748.name: Jubal
person:jubal_1748.title: Jubal
person:jubal_1748.summary: Jubilee, music, Lamech’s second son by Adah, of the line of Cain. He was the inventor of “the harp” (Heb. kinnor, properly “lyre”) and “the organ” (Heb. ‘ugab, properly “mouth-organ” or Pan’s pipe), Gen. 4:21.

person:jucal_822.name: Jucal
person:jucal_822.title: Jucal
person:jucal_822.summary: Able, the son of Shelemiah. He is also called Jucal (Jer. 38:1). He was one of the two persons whom Zedekiah sent to request the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the kingdom (Jer. 37:3) during the time of its final siege by Nebuchadnezzar. He was accompanied by Zephaniah (q.v.).

person:juda_1750.name: Juda
person:juda_1750.title: Juda
person:juda_1750.summary: The father of Simeon in Christ’s maternal ancestry (Luke 3:30).

person:judah_1751.name: Judah
person:judah_1751.title: Judah (patriarch)
person:judah_1751.summary:
Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah. The name originated in Leah’s words of praise to the Lord on account of his birth: “Now will I praise [Heb. odeh] Jehovah, and she called his name Yehudah” (Gen. 29:35).
It was Judah that interposed in behalf of Joseph, so that his life was spared (Gen. 37:26, 27). He took a lead in the affairs of the family, and “prevailed above his brethren” (Gen. 43:3-10; 44:14, 16-34; 46:28; 1 Chr. 5:2).
Soon after the sale of Joseph to the Ishmaelites, Judah went to reside at Adullam, where he married a woman of Canaan. …

person:judas_1758.name: Judas
person:judas_1758.title: Judas (Jew of Damascus)
person:judas_1758.summary: A Jew of Damascus (Acts 9:11), to whose house Ananias was sent. The street called “Straight” in which it was situated is identified with the modern “street of bazaars,” where is still pointed out the so-called “house of Judas.”

person:judas_1759.name: Judas
person:judas_1759.title: Judas Barsabas
person:judas_1759.summary: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council (Acts 15:22, 27, 32). He was a “prophet” and a “chief man among the brethren.”

person:judas_1760.name: Judas
person:judas_1760.title: Judas Iscariot
person:judas_1760.summary: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels. The evil of his nature probably gradually unfolded itself till “Satan entered into him” (John 13:27), and he betrayed our Lord (18:3). Afterwards he owned his sin with “an exceeding bitter cry,” and cast the money he had received as the wages of his iniquity down on the floor of the sanctuary, and “departed and went and hanged himself” (Matt. 27:5). He perished in his guilt, and “went unto his own place” (Acts 1:25). …

person:jude_1756.name: Jude
person:jude_1756.title: Jude
person:jude_1756.summary: '= Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas (Jude 1:1; Matt. 13:55; John 14:22; Acts 1:13), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18); and (2) Judas Iscariot (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:19). He who is called “the brother of James” (Luke 6:16), may be the same with the Judas surnamed Lebbaeus. The only thing recorded regarding him is in John 14:22.

person:julia_1762.name: Julia
person:julia_1762.title: Julia
person:julia_1762.summary: A Christian woman at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutations (Rom. 16:15), supposed to be the wife of Philologus.

person:julius_1763.name: Julius
person:julius_1763.title: Julius
person:julius_1763.summary: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome (Acts 27:1, 3, 43). He entreated Paul “courteously,” showing in many ways a friendly regard for him.

person:junia_1764.name: Junia
person:junia_1764.title: Junia
person:junia_1764.summary: (Rom. 16:7), a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sends salutations along with Andronicus.

person:justus_1766.name: Justus
person:justus_1766.title: Justus
person:justus_1766.summary: A Jewish proselyte at Corinth, in whose house, next door to the synagogue, Paul held meetings and preached after he left the synagogue (Acts 18:7).

person:kadmiel_1767.name: Kadmiel
person:kadmiel_1767.title: Kadmiel
person:kadmiel_1767.summary: Before God; i.e., his servant, one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 9:4; 10:9; 12:8).

person:kareah_919.name: Kareah
person:kareah_919.title: Kareah
person:kareah_919.summary: Bald, the father of Johanan and Jonathan, who for a time were loyal to Gedaliah, the Babylonian governor of Jerusalem (Jer. 40:8, 13, 15, 16).

person:kedar_1769.name: Kedar
person:kedar_1769.title: Kedar
person:kedar_1769.summary:
Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:13).
It is the name for the nomadic tribes of Arabs, the Bedouins generally (Isa. 21:16; 42:11; 60:7; Jer. 2:10; Ezek. 27:21), who dwelt in the north-west of Arabia. They lived in black hair-tents (Cant. 1:5). To “dwell in the tents of Kedar” was to be cut off from the worship of the true God (Ps. 120:5). The Kedarites suffered at the hands of Nebuchadnezzar (Jer. 49:28, 29).

person:kedemah_1770.name: Kedemah
person:kedemah_1770.title: Kedemah
person:kedemah_1770.summary: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

person:kelita_1772.name: Kelita
person:kelita_1772.title: Kelita
person:kelita_1772.summary: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:7; 10:10).

person:kemuel_1774.name: Kemuel
person:kemuel_1774.title: Kemuel
person:kemuel_1774.summary: Son of Shiphtan, appointed on behalf of the tribe of Ephraim to partition the land of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

person:kenaz_1778.name: Kenaz
person:kenaz_1778.title: Kenaz
person:kenaz_1778.summary: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel (Josh. 15:17), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David (1 Chr. 27:15). Some think that Othniel (Judg. 1:13), and not Kenaz, was Caleb’s brother.

person:keren-happuch_1780.name: Keren-happuch
person:keren-happuch_1780.title: Keren-happuch
person:keren-happuch_1780.summary: Horn of the face-paint = cosmetic-box, the name of Job’s third daughter (Job. 42:14), born after prosperity had returned to him.

person:keturah_1782.name: Keturah
person:keturah_1782.title: Keturah
person:keturah_1782.summary: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death (Gen. 25:1-6), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country. Her nationality is unknown. She is styled “Abraham’s concubine” (1 Chr. 1:32). Through the offshoots of the Keturah line Abraham became the “father of many nations.”

person:kish_1784.name: Kish
person:kish_1784.title: Kish
person:kish_1784.summary: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul (1 Sam. 9:1, 3; 10:11, 21; 14:51; 2 Sam. 21:14). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah. Called Cis, Acts 13:21 (R.V., Kish).

person:kish_1785.name: Kish
person:kish_1785.title: Kish
person:kish_1785.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21; 24:29).

person:kish_1786.name: Kish
person:kish_1786.title: Kish
person:kish_1786.summary: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

person:kohath_1790.name: Kohath
person:kohath_1790.title: Kohath
person:kohath_1790.summary: Assembly, the second son of Levi, and father of Amram (Gen. 46:11). He came down to Egypt with Jacob, and lived to the age of one hundred and thirty-three years (Ex. 6:18).

person:korah_1793.name: Korah
person:korah_1793.title: Korah
person:korah_1793.summary: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

person:korah_1795.name: Korah
person:korah_1795.title: Korah (Levite)
person:korah_1795.summary: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 6:21). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution. The old priesthood of the heads of families passed away. This gave rise to murmurings and discontent, while the Israelites were encamped at Kadesh for the first time, which came to a head in a rebellion against Moses and Aaron, headed by Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Two hundred and fifty princes, “men of renown” i.e., well-known men from among the other tribes, joined this conspiracy. …

person:kore_1797.name: Kore
person:kore_1797.title: Kore
person:kore_1797.summary: A Levite and temple-warder of the Korahites, the son of Asaph. He was father of Shallum and Meshelemiah, temple-porters (1 Chr. 9:19; 26:1).

person:kore_1798.name: Kore
person:kore_1798.title: Kore
person:kore_1798.summary: A Levitical porter at the east gate of the temple (2 Chr. 31:14).

person:laadan_1823.name: Laadan
person:laadan_1823.title: Laadan
person:laadan_1823.summary: White, one of the two sons of Gershon, the son of Levi (Ex. 6:17; Num. 3:18, 21).

person:laban_1803.name: Laban
person:laban_1803.title: Laban
person:laban_1803.summary: The son of Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. He lived at Haran in Mesopotamia. His sister Rebekah was Isaac’s wife (Gen. 24). Jacob, one of the sons of this marriage, fled to the house of Laban, whose daughters Leah and Rachel (ch. 29) he eventually married.

person:lamech_1808.name: Lamech
person:lamech_1808.title: Lamech (descendant of Cain)
person:lamech_1808.summary: The fifth in descent from Cain. He was the first to violate the primeval ordinance of marriage (Gen. 4:18-24). His address to his two wives, Adah and Zillah (4:23, 24), is the only extant example of antediluvian poetry. It has been called “Lamech’s sword-song.” He was “rude and ruffianly,” fearing neither God nor man. With him the curtain falls on the race of Cain. We know nothing of his descendants.

person:lamech_1809.name: Lamech
person:lamech_1809.title: Lamech (father of Noah)
person:lamech_1809.summary: The seventh in descent from Seth, being the only son of Methuselah. Noah was the oldest of his several sons (Gen. 5:25-31; Luke 3:36).

person:lapidoth_1810.name: Lapidoth
person:lapidoth_1810.title: Lapidoth
person:lapidoth_1810.summary: Torches. Deborah is called “the wife of Lapidoth” (Judg. 4:4). Some have rendered the expression “a woman of a fiery spirit,” under the supposition that Lapidoth is not a proper name, a woman of a torch-like spirit.

person:lazarus_1812.name: Lazarus
person:lazarus_1812.title: Lazarus
person:lazarus_1812.summary: The brother of Mary and Martha of Bethany. He was raised from the dead after he had lain four days in the tomb (John 11:1-44). This miracle so excited the wrath of the Jews that they sought to put both Jesus and Lazarus to death.

person:leah_1813.name: Leah
person:leah_1813.title: Leah
person:leah_1813.summary: Weary, the eldest daughter of Laban, and sister of Rachel (Gen. 29:16). Jacob took her to wife through a deceit of her father (Gen. 29:23). She was “tender-eyed” (17). She bore to Jacob six sons (32-35), also one daughter, Dinah (30:21). She accompanied Jacob into Canaan, and died there before the time of the going down into Egypt (Gen. 31), and was buried in the cave of Machpelah (49:31).

person:lebbaeus_1815.name: Lebbaeus
person:lebbaeus_1815.title: Lebbaeus Thaddaeus
person:lebbaeus_1815.summary: Breast, the name of one of the apostles (Mark 3:18), called “Lebbaeus” in Matt. 10:3, and in Luke 6:16, “Judas the brother of James;” while John (14:22), probably referring to the same person, speaks of “Judas, not Iscariot.” These different names all designate the same person, viz., Jude or Judas, the author of the epistle.

person:lemuel_1817.name: Lemuel
person:lemuel_1817.title: Lemuel
person:lemuel_1817.summary: Dedicated to God, a king whom his mother instructed (Prov. 31:1-9). Nothing is certainly known concerning him. The rabbis identified him with Solomon.

person:leummim_1819.name: Leummim
person:leummim_1819.title: Leummim
person:leummim_1819.summary: Peoples; nations, the last mentioned of the three sons of Dedan, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:3).

person:levi_1820.name: Levi
person:levi_1820.title: Levi (patriarch)
person:levi_1820.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.” He is mentioned as taking a prominent part in avenging his sister Dinah (Gen. 34:25-31). He and his three sons went down with Jacob (46:11) into Egypt, where he died at the age of one hundred and thirty-seven years (Ex. 6:16).

person:levi_1822.name: Levi
person:levi_1822.title: Levi
person:levi_1822.summary: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ (Luke 3:29).

person:lo-ammi_1827.name: Lo-ammi
person:lo-ammi_1827.title: Lo-ammi
person:lo-ammi_1827.summary: Not my people, a symbolical name given by God’s command to Hosea’s second son in token of Jehovah’s rejection of his people (Hos. 1:9, 10), his treatment of them as a foreign people. This Hebrew word is rendered by “not my people” in ver. 10; 2:23.

person:lo-ruhamah_1829.name: Lo-ruhamah
person:lo-ruhamah_1829.title: Lo-ruhamah
person:lo-ruhamah_1829.summary: Not pitied, the name of the prophet Hosea’s first daughter, a type of Jehovah’s temporary rejection of his people (Hos. 1:6; 2:23).

person:lois_1828.name: Lois
person:lois_1828.title: Lois
person:lois_1828.summary: The maternal grandmother of Timothy. She is commended by Paul for her faith (2 Tim. 1:5).

person:lot_1830.name: Lot
person:lot_1830.title: Lot
person:lot_1830.summary: (Heb. goral, a “pebble”), a small stone used in casting lots (Num. 33:54; Jonah 1:7). The lot was always resorted to by the Hebrews with strictest reference to the interposition of God, and as a method of ascertaining the divine will (Prov. 16:33), and in serious cases of doubt (Esther 3:7). Thus the lot was used at the division of the land of Canaan among the serveral tribes (Num. 26:55; 34:13), at the detection of Achan (Josh. 7:14, 18), the election of Saul to be king (1 Sam. 10:20, 21), the distribution of the priestly offices of the temple service (1 Chr. 24:3, 5, 19; Luke 1:9), and over the two goats at the feast of Atonement (Lev. 16:8). …

person:lotan_1831.name: Lotan
person:lotan_1831.title: Lotan
person:lotan_1831.summary: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

person:lucifer_1832.name: Lucifer
person:lucifer_1832.title: Lucifer
person:lucifer_1832.summary: Brilliant star, a title given to the king of Babylon (Isa. 14:12) to denote his glory.

person:lucius_1833.name: Lucius
person:lucius_1833.title: Lucius
person:lucius_1833.summary: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch (Acts 13:1), and Paul’s kinsman (Rom. 16:21). His name is Latin, but his birthplace seems to indicate that he was one of the Jews of Cyrene, in North Africa.

person:lud_1834.name: Lud
person:lud_1834.title: Lud
person:lud_1834.summary: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

person:ludim_1835.name: Ludim
person:ludim_1835.title: Ludim
person:ludim_1835.summary: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11). They are associated (Jer. 46:9) with African nations as mercenaries of the king of Egypt.

person:luke_1836.name: Luke
person:luke_1836.title: Luke
person:luke_1836.summary: The evangelist, was a Gentile. The date and circumstances of his conversion are unknown. According to his own statement (Luke 1:2), he was not an “eye-witness and minister of the word from the beginning.” It is probable that he was a physician in Troas, and was there converted by Paul, to whom he attached himself. He accompanied him to Philippi, but did not there share his imprisonment, nor did he accompany him further after his release in his missionary journey at this time (Acts 17:1). On Paul’s third visit to Philippi (20:5, 6) we again meet with Luke, who probably had spent all the intervening time in that city, a period of seven or eight years. …

person:lydia_1837.name: Lydia
person:lydia_1837.title: Lydia
person:lydia_1837.summary: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13). She thus became the first in Europe who embraced Christianity. She was a person apparently of considerable wealth, for she could afford to give a home to Paul and his companions.

person:lysanias_1838.name: Lysanias
person:lysanias_1838.title: Lysanias
person:lysanias_1838.summary: Tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

person:maacah_1839.name: Maacah
person:maacah_1839.title: Maacah
person:maacah_1839.summary: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur. She became one of David’s wives, and was the mother of Absalom (2 Sam. 3:3).

person:maachah_1841.name: Maachah
person:maachah_1841.title: Maachah
person:maachah_1841.summary: The daughter of Abishalom (called Absalom, 2 Chr. 11:20-22), the third wife of Rehoboam, and mother of Abijam (1 Kings 15:2). She is called “Michaiah the daughter of Uriel,” who was the husband of Absalom’s daughter Tamar (2 Chr. 13:2). Her son Abijah or Abijam was heir to the throne.

person:maachah_1845.name: Maachah
person:maachah_1845.title: Maachah
person:maachah_1845.summary: The father of Hanan, who was one of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 11:43).

person:maachah_1934.name: Maachah
person:maachah_1934.title: Maachah
person:maachah_1934.summary: The father of Achish, the king of Gath (1 Kings 2:39), called also Maoch (1 Sam. 27:2).

person:maaseiah_1849.name: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1849.title: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1849.summary: One of the Levites whom David appointed as porter for the ark (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

person:maaseiah_1850.name: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1850.title: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1850.summary: One of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in restoring king Jehoash to the throne (2 Chr. 23:1).

person:maaseiah_1853.name: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1853.title: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1853.summary: One who was sent by king Josiah to repair the temple (2 Chr. 34:8). He was governor (Heb. sar, rendered elsewhere in the Authorized Version “prince,” “chief captain,” chief ruler”) of Jerusalem.

person:maaseiah_1866.name: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1866.title: Maaseiah
person:maaseiah_1866.summary: The father of the priest Zephaniah (Jer. 21:1; 37:3).

person:maasiai_1870.name: Maasiai
person:maasiai_1870.title: Maasiai
person:maasiai_1870.summary: Work of Jehovah, one of the priests resident at Jerusalem at the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:12).

person:maath_1871.name: Maath
person:maath_1871.title: Maath
person:maath_1871.summary: Small, a person named in our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:26).

person:maaziah_1873.name: Maaziah
person:maaziah_1873.title: Maaziah
person:maaziah_1873.summary: The head of the twenty-fourth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:18) in David’s reign.

person:machir_1877.name: Machir
person:machir_1877.title: Machir
person:machir_1877.summary: Manasseh’s oldest son (Josh. 17:1), or probably his only son (see 1 Chr. 7:14, 15; comp. Num. 26:29-33; Josh. 13:31). His descendants are referred to under the name of Machirites, being the offspring of Gilead (Num. 26:29). They settled in land taken from the Amorites (Num. 32:39, 40; Deut. 3:15) by a special enactment (Num. 36:1-3; Josh. 17:3, 4). He is once mentioned as the representative of the tribe of Manasseh east of Jordan (Judg. 5:14).

person:machir_1878.name: Machir
person:machir_1878.title: Machir
person:machir_1878.summary: A descendant of the preceding, residing at Lo-debar, where he maintained Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth till he was taken under the care of David (2 Sam. 9:4), and where he afterwards gave shelter to David himself when he was a fugitive (17:27).

person:madai_1880.name: Madai
person:madai_1880.title: Madai
person:madai_1880.summary: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

person:magog_1882.name: Magog
person:magog_1882.title: Magog
person:magog_1882.summary: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth. They are described as skilled horsemen, and expert in the use of the bow. The Latin father Jerome says that this word denotes “Scythian nations, fierce and innumerable, who live beyond the Caucasus and the Lake Maeotis, and near the Caspian Sea, and spread out even onward to India.” Perhaps the name “represents the Assyrian Mat Gugi, or ‘country of Gugu,’ the Gyges of the Greeks” (Sayce’s Races, etc.).

person:mahalaleel_1885.name: Mahalaleel
person:mahalaleel_1885.title: Mahalaleel (line of Seth)
person:mahalaleel_1885.summary: The son of Cainan, of the line of Seth (Gen. 5:12-17); called Maleleel (Luke 3:37).

person:mahalath_1888.name: Mahalath
person:mahalath_1888.title: Mahalath
person:mahalath_1888.summary: The daughter of Jerimoth, who was one of David’s sons. She was one of Rehoboam’s wives (2 Chr. 11:18).

person:mahath_150.name: Mahath
person:mahath_150.title: Mahath
person:mahath_150.summary: A Kohathite Levite, father of Elkanah (1 Chr. 6:35).

person:mahath_1891.name: Mahath
person:mahath_1891.title: Mahath
person:mahath_1891.summary: Another Kohathite Levite, of the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

person:mahazioth_1893.name: Mahazioth
person:mahazioth_1893.title: Mahazioth
person:mahazioth_1893.summary: Visions, a Kohathite Levite, chief of the twenty-third course of musicians (1 Chr. 25:4, 30).

person:maher-shalal-hash-baz_1894.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
person:maher-shalal-hash-baz_1894.title: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
person:maher-shalal-hash-baz_1894.summary: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, (Isa. 8:1-3; comp. Zeph. 1:14), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him (Isa. 8:1, 3), as denoting the sudden attack on Damascus and Syria by the Assyrian army.

person:mahlah_1895.name: Mahlah
person:mahlah_1895.title: Mahlah
person:mahlah_1895.summary: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad (Num. 27:1-11) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

person:mahlon_1897.name: Mahlon
person:mahlon_1897.title: Mahlon
person:mahlon_1897.summary: Sickly, the elder of Elimelech the Bethlehemite’s two sons by Naomi. He married Ruth and died childless (Ruth 1:2, 5; 4:9, 10), in the land of Moab.

person:mahol_1898.name: Mahol
person:mahol_1898.title: Mahol
person:mahol_1898.summary: Dance, the father of four sons (1 Kings 4:31) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

person:malachi_1899.name: Malachi
person:malachi_1899.title: Malachi
person:malachi_1899.summary:
Messenger or angel, the last of the minor prophets, and the writer of the last book of the Old Testament canon (Mal. 4:4, 5, 6). Nothing is known of him beyond what is contained in his book of prophecies. Some have supposed that the name is simply a title descriptive of his character as a messenger of Jehovah, and not a proper name. There is reason, however, to conclude that Malachi was the ordinary name of the prophet.
He was contemporary with Nehemiah (comp. Mal. 2:8 with Neh. 13:15; Mal. 2:10-16 with Neh. 13:23). …

person:malcham_1900.name: Malcham
person:malcham_1900.title: Malcham
person:malcham_1900.summary: (2 Sam. 12:30, Heb., R.V., “their king;” Jer. 49:1, 3, R.V.; Zeph. 1:5), the national idol of the Ammonites. When Rabbah was taken by David, the crown of this idol was among the spoils. The weight is said to have been “a talent of gold” (above 100 lbs.). The expression probably denotes its value rather than its weight. It was adorned with precious stones.

person:malchi-shua_1990.name: Malchi-shua
person:malchi-shua_1990.title: Malchi-shua
person:malchi-shua_1990.summary: King of help, one of the four sons of Saul (1 Chr. 8:33). He perished along with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2).

person:malchiah_1906.name: Malchiah
person:malchiah_1906.title: Malchiah
person:malchiah_1906.summary: A priest who stood by Ezra when he “read in the book of the law of God” (Neh. 8:4).

person:malchijah_1910.name: Malchijah
person:malchijah_1910.title: Malchijah
person:malchijah_1910.summary: The head of the fifth division of the priests in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:9).

person:malchijah_1914.name: Malchijah
person:malchijah_1914.title: Malchijah
person:malchijah_1914.summary: One of the priests appointed as musicians to celebrate the completion of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

person:malchus_1916.name: Malchus
person:malchus_1916.title: Malchus
person:malchus_1916.summary: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane (John 18:10). But our Lord cured it with a touch (Matt. 26:51; Mark 14:47; Luke 22:51). This was the last miracle of bodily cure wrought by our Lord. It is not mentioned by John.

person:mallothi_1917.name: Mallothi
person:mallothi_1917.title: Mallothi
person:mallothi_1917.summary: My fulness, a Kohathite Levite, one of the sons of Heman the Levite (1 Chr. 25:4), and chief of the nineteenth division of the temple musicians (26).

person:malluch_1918.name: Malluch
person:malluch_1918.title: Malluch
person:malluch_1918.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:44).

person:malluch_1921.name: Malluch
person:malluch_1921.title: Malluch
person:malluch_1921.summary: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

person:mamre_1923.name: Mamre
person:mamre_1923.title: Mamre
person:mamre_1923.summary: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham (Gen. 14:13, 24).

person:manaen_1926.name: Manaen
person:manaen_1926.title: Manaen
person:manaen_1926.summary: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch. Nothing else is known of him beyond what is stated in Acts 13:1, where he is spoken of as having been brought up with (Gr. syntrophos; rendered in R.V. “foster brother” of) Herod, i.e., Herod Antipas, the tetrach, who, with his brother Archelaus, was educated at Rome.

person:manasseh_1928.name: Manasseh
person:manasseh_1928.title: Manasseh (son of Joseph)
person:manasseh_1928.summary:
The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1). There is an account of his marriage to a Syrian (1 Chr. 7:14); and the only thing afterwards recorded of him is, that his grandchildren were “brought up upon Joseph’s knees” (Gen. 50:23; R.V., “born upon Joseph’s knees”) i.e., were from their birth adopted by Joseph as his own children.
The tribe of Manasseh was associated with that of Ephraim and Benjamin during the wanderings in the wilderness. They encamped on the west side of the tabernacle. According to the census taken at Sinai, this tribe then numbered 32,200 (Num. 1:10, 35; 2:20, 21). …

person:manasseh_1930.name: Manasseh
person:manasseh_1930.title: Manasseh (son of Hezekiah)
person:manasseh_1930.summary:
The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1). There is an account of his marriage to a Syrian (1 Chr. 7:14); and the only thing afterwards recorded of him is, that his grandchildren were “brought up upon Joseph’s knees” (Gen. 50:23; R.V., “born upon Joseph’s knees”) i.e., were from their birth adopted by Joseph as his own children.
The tribe of Manasseh was associated with that of Ephraim and Benjamin during the wanderings in the wilderness. They encamped on the west side of the tabernacle. According to the census taken at Sinai, this tribe then numbered 32,200 (Num. 1:10, 35; 2:20, 21). …

person:manoah_1933.name: Manoah
person:manoah_1933.title: Manoah
person:manoah_1933.summary: Rest, a Danite, the father of Samson (Judg. 13:1-22, and 14:2-4).

person:mark_1679.name: John
person:mark_1679.title: John Mark
person:mark_1679.summary:
The evangelist; “John whose surname was Mark” (Acts 12:12, 25). Mark (Marcus, Col. 4:10, etc.) was his Roman name, which gradually came to supersede his Jewish name John. He is called John in Acts 13:5, 13, and Mark in 15:39, 2 Tim. 4:11, etc.
He was the son of Mary, a woman apparently of some means and influence, and was probably born in Jerusalem, where his mother resided (Acts 12:12). Of his father we know nothing. He was cousin of Barnabas (Col. 4:10). It was in his mother’s house that Peter found “many gathered together praying” when he was released from prison; and it is probable that it was here that he was converted by Peter, who calls him his “son” (1 Pet. 5:13). …

person:martha_1937.name: Martha
person:martha_1937.title: Martha
person:martha_1937.summary: Bitterness, the sister of Lazarus and Mary, and probably the eldest of the family, who all resided at Bethany (Luke 10:38, 40, 41; John 11:1-39). From the residence being called “her house,” some have supposed that she was a widow, and that her brother and sister lodged with her. She seems to have been of an anxious, bustling spirit, anxious to be helpful in providing the best things for the Master’s use, in contrast to the quiet earnestness of Mary, who was more concerned to avail herself of the opportunity of sitting at his feet and learning of him. …

person:mary_1938.name: Mary
person:mary_1938.title: Mary (Mother of Jesus)
person:mary_1938.summary:
The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14). Little is known of her personal history. Her genealogy is given in Luke 3. She was of the tribe of Judah and the lineage of David (Ps. 132:11; Luke 1:32). She was connected by marriage with Elisabeth, who was of the lineage of Aaron (Luke 1:36).
While she resided at Nazareth with her parents, before she became the wife of Joseph, the angel Gabriel announced to her that she was to be the mother of the promised Messiah (Luke 1:35). After this she went to visit her cousin Elisabeth, who was living with her husband Zacharias (probably at Juttah, Josh. …

person:mary_1939.name: Mary
person:mary_1939.title: Mary (sister of Lazarus)
person:mary_1939.summary: Mary the sister of Lazarus is brought to our notice in connection with the visits of our Lord to Bethany. She is contrasted with her sister Martha, who was “cumbered about many things” while Jesus was their guest, while Mary had chosen “the good part.” Her character also appears in connection with the death of her brother (John 11:20, 31, 33). On the occasion of our Lord’s last visit to Bethany, Mary brought “a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus” as he reclined at table in the house of one Simon, who had been a leper (Matt. 26:6; Mark 14:3; John 12:2, 3). This was an evidence of her overflowing love to the Lord. …

person:mary_1941.name: Mary
person:mary_1941.title: Mary (Mother of John Mark)
person:mary_1941.summary: Mary the mother of John Mark was one of the earliest of our Lord’s disciples. She was the sister of Barnabas (Col. 4:10), and joined with him in disposing of their land and giving the proceeds of the sale into the treasury of the Church (Acts 4:37; 12:12). Her house in Jerusalem was the common meeting-place for the disciples there.

person:mary_1942.name: Mary
person:mary_1942.title: Mary (of Rome)
person:mary_1942.summary: A Christian at Rome who treated Paul with special kindness (Rom. 16:6).

person:mary_1943.name: Mary
person:mary_1943.title: Mary Magdalene
person:mary_1943.summary: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.). A mistaken notion has prevailed that this Mary was a woman of bad character, that she was the woman who is emphatically called “a sinner” (Luke 7:36-50).

person:mash_1944.name: Mash
person:mash_1944.title: Mash
person:mash_1944.summary: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia. Some have supposed that they were the inhabitants of Mount Masius, the present Karja Baghlar, which forms part of the chain of Taurus.

person:massa_1945.name: Massa
person:massa_1945.title: Massa
person:massa_1945.summary: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

person:mattan_1948.name: Mattan
person:mattan_1948.title: Mattan
person:mattan_1948.summary: A priest of Baal, slain before his altar during the reformation under Jehoiada (2 Kings 11:18).

person:mattaniah_1952.name: Mattaniah
person:mattaniah_1952.title: Mattaniah
person:mattaniah_1952.summary: A Levite, son of Heman, the chief of the ninth class of temple singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 16).

person:mattaniah_1954.name: Mattaniah
person:mattaniah_1954.title: Mattaniah
person:mattaniah_1954.summary: A Levite who assisted in purifying the temple at the reformation under Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

person:mattathias_1963.name: Mattathias
person:mattathias_1963.title: Mattathias
person:mattathias_1963.summary: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:25).

person:mattathias_1964.name: Mattathias
person:mattathias_1964.title: Mattathias
person:mattathias_1964.summary: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy (Luke 3:26).

person:matthan_1968.name: Matthan
person:matthan_1968.title: Matthan
person:matthan_1968.summary: The son of Eleazar, and father of Jacob, who was the father of Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary (Matt. 1:15).

person:matthat_1969.name: Matthat
person:matthat_1969.title: Matthat
person:matthat_1969.summary: The son of Levi, and father of Heli (Luke 3:24).

person:matthew_1971.name: Matthew
person:matthew_1971.title: Matthew
person:matthew_1971.summary: Gift of God, a common Jewish name after the Exile. He was the son of Alphaeus, and was a publican or tax-gatherer at Capernaum. On one occasion Jesus, coming up from the side of the lake, passed the custom-house where Matthew was seated, and said to him, “Follow me.” Matthew arose and followed him, and became his disciple (Matt. 9:9). Formerly the name by which he was known was Levi (Mark 2:14; Luke 5:27); he now changed it, possibly in grateful memory of his call, to Matthew. The same day on which Jesus called him he made a “great feast” (Luke 5:29), a farewell feast, to which he invited Jesus and his disciples, and probably also many of old associates. …

person:mattithiah_1973.name: Mattithiah
person:mattithiah_1973.title: Mattithiah
person:mattithiah_1973.summary: The eldest son of Shallum, of the family of Korah (1 Chr. 9:31).

person:mattithiah_1974.name: Mattithiah
person:mattithiah_1974.title: Mattithiah
person:mattithiah_1974.summary: One of the sons of Jeduthun (1 Chr. 25:3, 21).

person:mattithiah_1976.name: Mattithiah
person:mattithiah_1976.title: Mattithiah
person:mattithiah_1976.summary: One who stood by Ezra while reading the law (Neh. 8:4).

person:medan_1978.name: Medan
person:medan_1978.title: Medan
person:medan_1978.summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

person:mehetabeel_1979.name: Mehetabeel
person:mehetabeel_1979.title: Mehetabeel
person:mehetabeel_1979.summary: Whose benefactor is God, the father of Delaiah, and grandfather of Shemaiah, who joined Sanballat against Nehemiah (Neh. 6:10).

person:mehetabel_1980.name: Mehetabel
person:mehetabel_1980.title: Mehetabel
person:mehetabel_1980.summary: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

person:mehujael_1983.name: Mehujael
person:mehujael_1983.title: Mehujael
person:mehujael_1983.summary: Smitten by God, the son of Irad, and father of Methusael (Gen. 4:18).

person:mehuman_1984.name: Mehuman
person:mehuman_1984.title: Mehuman
person:mehuman_1984.summary: Faithful, one of the eunchs whom Ahasuerus (Xerxes) commanded to bring in Vashti (Esther 1:10).

person:mehunim_1985.name: Mehunim
person:mehunim_1985.title: Mehunim
person:mehunim_1985.summary:
Habitations, (2 Chr. 26:7; R.V. “Meunim,” Vulg. Ammonitae), a people against whom Uzziah waged a successful war. This word is in Hebrew the plural of Ma’on, and thus denotes the Maonites who inhabited the country on the eastern side of the Wady el-Arabah. They are again mentioned in 1 Chr. 4:41 (R.V.), in the reign of King Hezekiah, as a Hamite people, settled in the eastern end of the valley of Gedor, in the wilderness south of Palestine. In this passage the Authorized Version has “habitation,” erroneously following the translation of Luther.
They are mentioned in the list of those from whom the Nethinim were made up (Ezra 2:50; Neh. 7:52).

person:melchi_1988.name: Melchi
person:melchi_1988.title: Melchi
person:melchi_1988.summary: The son of Addi, and father of Neri (Luke 3:28).

person:melchisedec_1991.name: Melchisedec
person:melchisedec_1991.title: Melchisedec
person:melchisedec_1991.summary: King of righteousness, the king of Salem (q.v.). All we know of him is recorded in Gen. 14:18-20. He is subsequently mentioned only once in the Old Testament, in Ps. 110:4. The typical significance of his history is set forth in detail in the Epistle to the Hebrews, ch. 7. …

person:melea_1992.name: Melea
person:melea_1992.title: Melea
person:melea_1992.summary: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

person:melech_1993.name: Melech
person:melech_1993.title: Melech
person:melech_1993.summary: King, the second of Micah’s four sons (1 Chr. 8:35), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

person:melzar_1994.name: Melzar
person:melzar_1994.title: Melzar
person:melzar_1994.summary: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court (Dan. 1:11, 16) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

person:memucan_1995.name: Memucan
person:memucan_1995.title: Memucan
person:memucan_1995.summary: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced (Esther 1:14, 16, 21).

person:menahem_1996.name: Menahem
person:menahem_1996.title: Menahem
person:menahem_1996.summary: Conforting, the son of Gadi, and successor of Shallum, king of Israel, whom he slew. After a reign of about ten years (B.C. 771-760) he died, leaving the throne to his son Pekahiah. His reign was one of cruelty and oppression (2 Kings 15:14-22). During his reign, Pul (q.v.), king of Assyria, came with a powerful force against Israel, but was induced to retire by a gift from Menahem of 1,000 talents of silver.

person:mephibosheth_1999.name: Mephibosheth
person:mephibosheth_1999.title: Mephibosheth
person:mephibosheth_1999.summary:
The son of Jonathan, and grandson of Saul (2 Sam. 4:4). He was but five years old when his father and grandfather fell on Mount Gilboa. The child’s nurse hearing of this calamity, fled with him from Gibeah, the royal residence, and stumbling in her haste, the child was thrown to the ground and maimed in both his feet, and ever after was unable to walk (19:26). He was carried to the land of Gilead, where he found a refuge in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, at Lo-debar, by whom he was brought up.
Some years after this, when David had subdued all the adversaries of Israel, he began to think of the family of Jonathan, and discovered that Mephibosheth was residing in the house of Machir. …

person:mephibosheth_2000.name: Mephibosheth
person:mephibosheth_2000.title: Mephibosheth
person:mephibosheth_2000.summary: The name of Saul’s son by the concubine Rizpah (q.v.), the daughter of Aiah. He and his brother Armoni were with five others “hanged on a hill before the Lord” by the Gibeonites, and their bodies exposed in the sun for five months (2 Sam. 21:8-10).

person:merab_2001.name: Merab
person:merab_2001.title: Merab
person:merab_2001.summary: Increase, the eldest of Saul’s two daughters (1 Sam. 14:49). She was betrothed to David after his victory over Goliath, but does not seem to have entered heartily into this arrangement (18:2, 17, 19). She was at length, however, married to Adriel of Abel-Meholah, a town in the Jordan valley, about 10 miles south of Bethshean, with whom the house of Saul maintained alliance. She had five sons, who were all put to death by the Gibeonites on the hill of Gibeah (2 Sam. 21:8).

person:meraiah_2002.name: Meraiah
person:meraiah_2002.title: Meraiah
person:meraiah_2002.summary: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim (Neh. 12:12).

person:meraioth_2003.name: Meraioth
person:meraioth_2003.title: Meraioth
person:meraioth_2003.summary: Father of Amariah, a high priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:6, 7, 52).

person:merari_2004.name: Merari
person:merari_2004.title: Merari
person:merari_2004.summary: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16). He became the head of one of the great divisions of the Levites (Ex. 6:19).

person:mered_2005.name: Mered
person:mered_2005.title: Mered
person:mered_2005.summary: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

person:meremoth_2006.name: Meremoth
person:meremoth_2006.title: Meremoth
person:meremoth_2006.summary: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3), to whom were sent the sacred vessels (Ezra 8:33) belonging to the temple. He took part in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

person:merodach-baladan_483.name: Merodach-baladan
person:merodach-baladan_483.title: Merodach-baladan
person:merodach-baladan_483.summary: Merodach has given a son, (Isa. 39:1), “the hereditary chief of the Chaldeans, a small tribe at that time settled in the marshes at the mouth of the Euphrates, but in consequence of his conquest of Babylon afterwards, they became the dominant caste in Babylonia itself.” One bearing this name sent ambassadors to Hezekiah (B.C. 721). He is also called Berodach-baladan (2 Kings 20:12; 2 Chr. 20:31).

person:mesha_2009.name: Mesha
person:mesha_2009.title: Mesha
person:mesha_2009.summary: Heb. id, a king of Moab, the son of Chemosh-Gad, a man of great wealth in flocks and herds (2 Kings 3:4). After the death of Ahab at Ramoth-Gilead, Mesha shook off the yoke of Israel; but on the ascension of Jehoram to the throne of Israel, that king sought the help of Jehoshaphat in an attempt to reduce the Moabites again to their former condition. The united armies of the two kings came unexpectedly on the army of the Moabites, and gained over them an easy victory. The whole land was devastated by the conquering armies, and Mesha sought refuge in his last stronghold, Kir-harasheth (q.v.). …

person:mesha_2010.name: Mesha
person:mesha_2010.title: Mesha
person:mesha_2010.summary: Heb. meysh’a, “deliverance,” the eldest son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:42), and brother of Jerahmeel.

person:meshach_2092.name: Meshach
person:meshach_2092.title: Meshach
person:meshach_2092.summary: One of the three Hebrew youths who were trained with Daniel in Babylon (Dan. 1:11, 19), and promoted to the rank of Magi. He and his companions were afterwards cast into the burning fiery furnace for refusing to worship the idol the king had set up, from which they were miraculously delivered (3:13-30). His Chaldean name was Meshach (q.v.).

person:meshech_2012.name: Meshech
person:meshech_2012.title: Meshech
person:meshech_2012.summary: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the founder of a tribe (1 Chr. 1:5; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2, 3). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas. In Ps. 120:5 the name occurs as simply a synonym for foreigners or barbarians. “During the ascendency of the Babylonians and Persians in Western Asia, the Moschi were subdued; but it seems probable that a large number of them crossed the Caucasus range and spread over the northern steppes, mingling with the Scythians. …

person:meshelemiah_2013.name: Meshelemiah
person:meshelemiah_2013.title: Meshelemiah
person:meshelemiah_2013.summary: Friendship of Jehovah, a Levite of the family of the Korhites, called also Shelemiah (1 Chr. 9:21; 26:1, 2, 9, 14). He was a temple gate-keeper in the time of David.

person:meshillemith_2017.name: Meshillemith
person:meshillemith_2017.title: Meshillemith
person:meshillemith_2017.summary: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

person:meshullam_2020.name: Meshullam
person:meshullam_2020.title: Meshullam
person:meshullam_2020.summary: Grandfather of Shaphan, “the scribe,” in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:3).

person:meshullam_2022.name: Meshullam
person:meshullam_2022.title: Meshullam
person:meshullam_2022.summary: One of the chief Gadites in Bashan in the time of Jotham (1 Chr. 5:13).

person:meshullam_2033.name: Meshullam
person:meshullam_2033.title: Meshullam
person:meshullam_2033.summary: One of the principal Israelites who supported Ezra when expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:4).

person:meshullemeth_2040.name: Meshullemeth
person:meshullemeth_2040.title: Meshullemeth
person:meshullemeth_2040.summary: Friend, the wife of Manasseh, and the mother of Amon (2 Kings 21:19), Kings of Judah.

person:methusael_2041.name: Methusael
person:methusael_2041.title: Methusael
person:methusael_2041.summary: Champion of El; man of God, a descendant of Cain (Gen. 4:18), so called, perhaps, to denote that even among the descendants of Cain God had not left himself without a witness.

person:methuselah_2042.name: Methuselah
person:methuselah_2042.title: Methuselah
person:methuselah_2042.summary: Man of the dart, the son of Enoch, and grandfather of Noah. He was the oldest man of whom we have any record, dying at the age of nine hundred and sixty-nine years, in the year of the Flood (Gen. 5:21-27; 1 Chr. 1:3).

person:mezahab_2043.name: Mezahab
person:mezahab_2043.title: Mezahab
person:mezahab_2043.summary: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

person:mibhar_2045.name: Mibhar
person:mibhar_2045.title: Mibhar
