person:mibhar_2045.summary: Choice, a Hagarene, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:38); called also Bani the Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

person:mibsam_2046.name: Mibsam
person:mibsam_2046.title: Mibsam
person:mibsam_2046.summary: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

person:mibzar_2048.name: Mibzar
person:mibzar_2048.title: Mibzar
person:mibzar_2048.summary: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

person:micah_2049.name: Micah
person:micah_2049.title: Micah
person:micah_2049.summary: A man of Mount Ephraim, whose history so far is introduced in Judg. 17, apparently for the purpose of leading to an account of the settlement of the tribe of Dan in Northern Palestine, and for the purpose also of illustrating the lawlessness of the times in which he lived (Judg. 18; 19:1-29; 21:25).

person:micah_2050.name: Micah
person:micah_2050.title: Micah
person:micah_2050.summary: A descendant of Joel the Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:5).

person:micah_2053.name: Micah
person:micah_2053.title: Micah
person:micah_2053.summary: “The Morasthite,” so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15). Very little is known of the circumstances of his life (comp. Jer. 26:18, 19).

person:micaiah_2054.name: Micaiah
person:micaiah_2054.title: Micaiah
person:micaiah_2054.summary: Who is like Jehovah?, the son of Imlah, a faithful prophet of Samaria (1 Kings 22:8-28). Three years after the great battle with Ben-hadad (20:29-34), Ahab proposed to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, that they should go up against Ramoth-Gilead to do battle again with Ben-hadad. Jehoshaphat agreed, but suggested that inquiry should be first made “at the word of Jehovah.” Ahab’s prophets approved of the expedition; but Jehoshaphat, still dissatisfied, asked if there was no other prophet besides the four hundred that had appeared, and was informed of this Micaiah. …

person:micha_2051.name: Micha
person:micha_2051.title: Micha
person:micha_2051.summary: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

person:michael_2058.name: Michael
person:michael_2058.title: Michael
person:michael_2058.summary: The father of Sethur, the spy selected to represent Asher (Num. 13:13).

person:michael_2059.name: Michael
person:michael_2059.title: Michael
person:michael_2059.summary: A chief Gadite in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

person:michael_2062.name: Michael
person:michael_2062.title: Michael
person:michael_2062.summary: 1 Chr. 7:3, a chief of the tribe of Issachar.

person:michael_2064.name: Michael
person:michael_2064.title: Michael
person:michael_2064.summary: A Manassite, “a captain of thousands” who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

person:michael_2066.name: Michael
person:michael_2066.title: Michael
person:michael_2066.summary: One of the sons of king Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 21:2, 4). He was murdered by his brother Jehoram.

person:michael_2068.name: Michael
person:michael_2068.title: Michael
person:michael_2068.summary: The title given to one of the chief angels (Dan. 10:13, 21; 12:1). He had special charge of Israel as a nation. He disputed with Satan (Jude 1:9) about the body of Moses. He is also represented as warning against “that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world” (Rev. 12:7-9).

person:michah_2052.name: Michah
person:michah_2052.title: Michah
person:michah_2052.summary: The first in rank of the priests of the family of Kohathites (1 Chr. 23:20).

person:michaiah_2070.name: Michaiah
person:michaiah_2070.title: Michaiah
person:michaiah_2070.summary: One of those sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

person:michaiah_2072.name: Michaiah
person:michaiah_2072.title: Michaiah
person:michaiah_2072.summary: The son of Gemariah. He reported to the king’s officers Jeremiah’s prediction, which he had heard Baruch read (Jer. 36:11, 13) from his father Gemariah’s chamber in the temple.

person:michal_2073.name: Michal
person:michal_2073.title: Michal
person:michal_2073.summary: Rivulet, or who as God?, the younger of Saul’s two daughters by his wife Ahinoam (1 Sam. 14:49, 50). “Attracted by the graces of his person and the gallantry of his conduct, she fell in love with David and became his wife” (18:20-28). She showed her affection for him by promoting his escape to Naioth when Saul sought his life (1 Sam. 19:12-17. Comp. Ps. 59. See TERAPHIM). After this she did not see David for many years. Meanwhile she was given in marriage to another man, Phalti or Phaltiel of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44), but David afterwards formally reclaimed her as his lawful wife (2 Sam. 3:13-16). The relation between her and David soon after this was altered. …

person:michri_2074.name: Michri
person:michri_2074.title: Michri
person:michri_2074.summary: Prize of Jehovah, a Benjamite, the father of Uzzi (1 Chr. 9:8).

person:midian_2075.name: Midian
person:midian_2075.title: Midian
person:midian_2075.summary: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

person:mikloth_2079.name: Mikloth
person:mikloth_2079.title: Mikloth
person:mikloth_2079.summary: An officer under Dodai, in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:4).

person:milalai_2081.name: Milalai
person:milalai_2081.title: Milalai
person:milalai_2081.summary: Eloquent, a Levitical musician (Neh. 12:36) who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

person:miniamin_2077.name: Miniamin
person:miniamin_2077.title: Miniamin
person:miniamin_2077.summary: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

person:miriam_2087.name: Miriam
person:miriam_2087.title: Miriam
person:miriam_2087.summary: The sister of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 2:4-10; 1 Chr. 6:3). Her name is prominent in the history of the Exodus. She is called “the prophetess” (Ex. 15:20). She took the lead in the song of triumph after the passage of the Red Sea. She died at Kadesh during the second encampment at that place, toward the close of the wanderings in the wilderness, and was buried there (Num. 20:1).

person:miriam_2088.name: Miriam
person:miriam_2088.title: Miriam
person:miriam_2088.summary: 1 Chr. 4:17, one of the descendants of Judah.

person:mishael_2090.name: Mishael
person:mishael_2090.title: Mishael
person:mishael_2090.summary: A Levite; the eldest of the three sons of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

person:misham_2093.name: Misham
person:misham_2093.title: Misham
person:misham_2093.summary: Their cleansing or their beholding, a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chr. 8:12).

person:mishma_2094.name: Mishma
person:mishma_2094.title: Mishma
person:mishma_2094.summary: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

person:mishmannah_2096.name: Mishmannah
person:mishmannah_2096.title: Mishmannah
person:mishmannah_2096.summary: Fatness, one of the Gadite heroes who gathered to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:10).

person:mispereth_2099.name: Mispereth
person:mispereth_2099.title: Mispereth
person:mispereth_2099.summary: Number, one of the Jews who accompanied Zerubbabel from Babylon (Ezra 2:2); called also Mispereth (Neh. 7:7).

person:mizraim_2100.name: Mizraim
person:mizraim_2100.title: Mizraim
person:mizraim_2100.summary: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11). It was the name generally given by the Hebrews to the land of Egypt (q.v.), and may denote the two Egypts, the Upper and the Lower. The modern Arabic name for Egypt is Muzr.

person:mnason_2102.name: Mnason
person:mnason_2102.title: Mnason
person:mnason_2102.summary: Reminding, or remembrancer, a Christian of Jerusalem with whom Paul lodged (Acts 21:16). He was apparently a native of Cyprus, like Barnabas (11:19, 20), and was well known to the Christians of Caesarea (4:36). He was an “old disciple” (R.V., “early disciple”), i.e., he had become a Christian in the beginning of the formation of the Church in Jerusalem.

person:moab_2103.name: Moab
person:moab_2103.title: Moab
person:moab_2103.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

person:molech_2104.name: Molech
person:molech_2104.title: Molech
person:molech_2104.summary: King, the name of the national god of the Ammonites, to whom children were sacrificed by fire. He was the consuming and destroying and also at the same time the purifying fire. In Amos 5:26, “your Moloch” of the Authorized Version is “your king” in the Revised Version (comp. Acts 7:43). Solomon (1 Kings 11:7) erected a high place for this idol on the Mount of Olives, and from that time till the days of Josiah his worship continued (2 Kings 23:10, 13). In the days of Jehoahaz it was partially restored, but after the Captivity wholly disappeared. He is also called Molech (Lev. 18:21; 20:2-5, etc.), Milcom (1 Kings 11:5, 33, etc.), and Malcham (Zeph. 1:5). …

person:mordecai_2107.name: Mordecai
person:mordecai_2107.title: Mordecai
person:mordecai_2107.summary:
The son of Jair, of the tribe of Benjamin. It has been alleged that he was carried into captivity with Jeconiah, and hence that he must have been at least one hundred and twenty-nine years old in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). But the words of Esther do not necessarily lead to this conclusion. It was probably Kish of whom it is said (ver. 6) that he “had been carried away with the captivity.”
He resided at Susa, the metropolis of Persia. He adopted his cousin Hadassah (Esther), an orphan child, whom he tenderly brought up as his own daughter. …

person:moses_2108.name: Moses
person:moses_2108.title: Moses
person:moses_2108.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt. This immigration took place probably about 350 years before the birth of Moses. Some centuries before Joseph, Egypt had been conquered by a pastoral Semitic race from Asia, the Hyksos, who brought into cruel subjection the native Egyptians, who were an African race. Jacob and his retinue were accustomed to a shepherd’s life, and on their arrival in Egypt were received with favour by the king, who assigned them the “best of the land”, the land of Goshen, to dwell in. …

person:mother_of_the_wife_of_simon_2111.name: Mother of the Wife of Simon
person:mother_of_the_wife_of_simon_2111.title: Mother of the Wife of Simon

person:moza_2113.name: Moza
person:moza_2113.title: Moza
person:moza_2113.summary: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:46).

person:moza_2114.name: Moza
person:moza_2114.title: Moza
person:moza_2114.summary: The son of Zimri, of the posterity of Saul (1 Chr. 8:36, 37; 9:42, 43).

person:mushi_2116.name: Mushi
person:mushi_2116.title: Mushi
person:mushi_2116.summary: Receding, the second of the two sons of Merari (Ex. 6:19; Num. 3:20). His sons were called Mushites (Num. 3:33; 26:58).

person:naam_2117.name: Naam
person:naam_2117.title: Naam
person:naam_2117.summary: Pleasantness, one of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

person:naamah_2118.name: Naamah
person:naamah_2118.title: Naamah (line of Cain)
person:naamah_2118.summary: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah (Gen. 4: 22).

person:naamah_2119.name: Naamah
person:naamah_2119.title: Naamah
person:naamah_2119.summary: The daughter of the king of Ammon, one of the wives of Solomon, the only one who appears to have borne him a son, viz., Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:21, 31).

person:naaman_2122.name: Naaman
person:naaman_2122.title: Naaman
person:naaman_2122.summary: Pleasantness, a Syrian, the commander of the armies of Benhadad II. in the time of Joram, king of Israel. He was afflicted with leprosy; and when the little Hebrew slave-girl that waited on his wife told her of a prophet in Samaria who could cure her master, he obtained a letter from Benhadad and proceeded with it to Joram. The king of Israel suspected in this some evil design against him, and rent his clothes. Elisha the prophet hearing of this, sent for Naaman, and the strange interview which took place is recorded in 2 Kings 5. The narrative contains all that is known of the Syrian commander. …

person:naarah_2124.name: Naarah
person:naarah_2124.title: Naarah
person:naarah_2124.summary: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:5, 6).

person:naarai_2125.name: Naarai
person:naarai_2125.title: Naarai
person:naarai_2125.summary: Youthful, a military chief in David’s army (1 Chr. 11:37), called also Paarai (2 Sam. 23:35).

person:nabal_2126.name: Nabal
person:nabal_2126.title: Nabal
person:nabal_2126.summary: Foolish, a descendant of Caleb who dwelt at Maon (1 Sam. 25), the modern Main, 7 miles south-east of Hebron. He was “very great, and he had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats...but the man was churlish and evil in his doings.” During his wanderings David came into that district, and hearing that Nabal was about to shear his sheep, he sent ten of his young men to ask “whatsoever cometh unto thy hand for thy servants.” Nabal insultingly resented the demand, saying, “Who is David, and who is the son of Jesse?” (1 Sam. 25:10, 11). …

person:naboth_2127.name: Naboth
person:naboth_2127.title: Naboth
person:naboth_2127.summary: Fruits, “the Jezreelite,” was the owner of a portion of ground on the eastern slope of the hill of Jezreel (2 Kings 9:25, 26). This small “plat of ground” seems to have been all he possessed. It was a vineyard, and lay “hard by the palace of Ahab” (1 Kings 21:1, 2), who greatly coveted it. Naboth, however, refused on any terms to part with it to the king. He had inherited it from his fathers, and no Israelite could lawfully sell his property (Lev. 25:23). Jezebel, Ahab’s wife, was grievously offended at Naboth’s refusal to part with his vineyard. By a crafty and cruel plot she compassed his death. His sons also shared his fate (2 Kings 9:26; 1 Kings 21:19). …

person:nadab_2128.name: Nadab
person:nadab_2128.title: Nadab
person:nadab_2128.summary: The eldest of Aaron’s four sons (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2). He with his brothers and their father were consecrated as priests of Jehovah (Ex. 28:1). He afterwards perished with Abihu for the sin of offering strange fire on the altar of burnt-offering (Lev. 10:1, 2; Num. 3:4; 26:60).

person:nadab_2129.name: Nadab
person:nadab_2129.title: Nadab
person:nadab_2129.summary: The son and successor of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 14:20). While engaged with all Israel in laying siege to Gibbethon, a town of southern Dan (Josh. 19:44), a conspiracy broke out in his army, and he was slain by Baasha (1 Kings 15:25-28), after a reign of two years (B.C. 955-953). The assassination of Nadab was followed by that of his whole house, and thus this great Ephraimite family became extinct (1 Kings 15:29).

person:nadab_2130.name: Nadab
person:nadab_2130.title: Nadab
person:nadab_2130.summary: One of the sons of Shammai in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 30).

person:naharai_2135.name: Naharai
person:naharai_2135.title: Naharai
person:naharai_2135.summary: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab (1 Chr. 11:39).

person:nahash_2136.name: Nahash
person:nahash_2136.title: Nahash
person:nahash_2136.summary: King of the Ammonites in the time of Saul. The inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead having been exposed to great danger from Nahash, sent messengers to Gibeah to inform Saul of their extremity. He promptly responded to the call, and gathering together an army he marched against Nahash. “And it came to pass that they which remained were scattered, so that two of them [the Ammonites] were not left together” (1 Sam. 11:1-11).

person:nahash_2138.name: Nahash
person:nahash_2138.title: Nahash
person:nahash_2138.summary: The father of Amasa, who was commander-in-chief of Abasolom’s army (2 Sam. 17:25). Jesse’s wife had apparently been first married to this man, to whom she bore Abigail and Zeruiah, who were thus David’s sisters, but only on the mother’s side (1 Chr. 2:16).

person:nahath_2140.name: Nahath
person:nahath_2140.title: Nahath
person:nahath_2140.summary: A Levite, one of the overseers of the sacred offerings of the temple (2 Chr. 31:13).

person:nahath_2146.name: Nahath
person:nahath_2146.title: Nahath
person:nahath_2146.summary: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

person:nahbi_2141.name: Nahbi
person:nahbi_2141.title: Nahbi
person:nahbi_2141.summary: Hidden, one of the twelve spies sent out to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:14).

person:nahor_2142.name: Nahor
person:nahor_2142.title: Nahor (father of Terah)
person:nahor_2142.summary: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham (Gen. 11:22-25; Luke 3:34).

person:nahor_2143.name: Nahor
person:nahor_2143.title: Nahor (brother of Abraham)
person:nahor_2143.summary: A son of Terah, and elder brother of Abraham (Gen. 11:26, 27; Josh. 24:2, R.V.). He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran, and remained in the land of his nativity on the east of the river Euphrates at Haran (Gen. 11:27-32). A correspondence was maintained between the family of Abraham in Canaan and the relatives in the old ancestral home at Haran till the time of Jacob. When Jacob fled from Haran all intercourse between the two branches of the family came to an end (Gen. 31:55). His grand-daughter Rebekah became Isaac’s wife (24:67).

person:nahshon_2144.name: Nahshon
person:nahshon_2144.title: Nahshon
person:nahshon_2144.summary: Sorcerer, the son of Aminadab, and prince of the children of Judah at the time of the first numbering of the tribes in the wilderness (Ex. 6:23). His sister Elisheba was the wife of Aaron. He died in the wilderness (Num. 26:64, 65). His name occurs in the Greek form Naasson in the genealogy of Christ (Matt, 1:4; Luke 3:32).

person:naomi_2147.name: Naomi
person:naomi_2147.title: Naomi
person:naomi_2147.summary: Bitter; sad, a symbolical name which Naomi gave to herself because of her misfortunes (Ruth 1:20).

person:naphtali_2149.name: Naphtali
person:naphtali_2149.title: Naphtali
person:naphtali_2149.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24). Little is known of him as an individual.

person:naphtuhim_2150.name: Naphtuhim
person:naphtuhim_2150.title: Naphtuhim
person:naphtuhim_2150.summary: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan. This city was the royal residence, it is said, of Queen Candace (Acts 8:27). Here there are extensive and splendid ruins.

person:narcissus_2151.name: Narcissus
person:narcissus_2151.title: Narcissus
person:narcissus_2151.summary: Daffodil, a Roman whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:11). He is supposed to have been the private secretary of the emperor Claudius. This is, however, quite uncertain.

person:nathan_2152.name: Nathan
person:nathan_2152.title: Nathan
person:nathan_2152.summary: A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

person:nathan_2153.name: Nathan
person:nathan_2153.title: Nathan
person:nathan_2153.summary: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14). He was charged with the education of Solomon (12:25), at whose inauguration to the throne he took a prominent part (1 Kings 1:8, 10, 11, 22-45). His two sons, Zabad (1 Chr. 2:36) and Azariah (1 Kings 4:5) occupied places of honour at the king’s court. He last appears in assisting David in reorganizing the public worship (2 Chr. 29:25). He seems to have written a life of David, and also a life of Solomon (1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr. …

person:nathan_2155.name: Nathan
person:nathan_2155.title: Nathan
person:nathan_2155.summary: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14). He was charged with the education of Solomon (12:25), at whose inauguration to the throne he took a prominent part (1 Kings 1:8, 10, 11, 22-45). His two sons, Zabad (1 Chr. 2:36) and Azariah (1 Kings 4:5) occupied places of honour at the king’s court. He last appears in assisting David in reorganizing the public worship (2 Chr. 29:25). He seems to have written a life of David, and also a life of Solomon (1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr. …

person:nathanael_2158.name: Nathanael
person:nathanael_2158.title: Nathanael
person:nathanael_2158.summary: Given or gift of God, one of our Lord’s disciples, “of Cana in Galilee” (John 21:2). He was “an Israelite indeed, in whom was no guile” (1:47, 48). His name occurs only in the Gospel of John, who in his list of the disciples never mentions Bartholomew, with whom he has consequently been identified. He was one of those to whom the Lord showed himself alive after his resurrection, at the Sea of Tiberias.

person:nebajoth_2164.name: Nebajoth
person:nebajoth_2164.title: Nebajoth
person:nebajoth_2164.summary: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16). He had a sister, Mahalath, who was one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 28:9; 36:3).

person:nebat_2165.name: Nebat
person:nebat_2165.title: Nebat
person:nebat_2165.summary: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

person:nebuchadnezzar_2167.name: Nebuchadnezzar
person:nebuchadnezzar_2167.title: Nebuchadnezzar
person:nebuchadnezzar_2167.summary:
In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.” He was the son and successor of Nabopolassar, who delivered Babylon from its dependence on Assyria and laid Nineveh in ruins. He was the greatest and most powerful of all the Babylonian kings. He married the daughter of Cyaxares, and thus the Median and Babylonian dynasties were united.
Necho II., the king of Egypt, gained a victory over the Assyrians at Carchemish. This secured to Egypt the possession of the Syrian provinces of Assyria, including Palestine. …

person:nebushasban_2168.name: Nebushasban
person:nebushasban_2168.title: Nebushasban
person:nebushasban_2168.summary: Adorer of Nebo, or Nebo saves me, the “Rabsaris,” or chief chamberlain, of the court of Babylon. He was one of those whom the king sent to release Jeremiah from prison in Jerusalem (Jer. 39:13).

person:nebuzar-adan_2169.name: Nebuzar-adan
person:nebuzar-adan_2169.title: Nebuzar-adan
person:nebuzar-adan_2169.summary: “the captain of the guard,” in rank next to the king, who appears prominent in directing affairs at the capture of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8-20; Jer. 39:11; 40:2-5). He showed kindness toward Jeremiah, as commanded by Nebuchadnezzar (40:1). Five years after this he again came to Jerusalem and carried captive seven hundred and forty-five more Jews.

person:nedabiah_2170.name: Nedabiah
person:nedabiah_2170.title: Nedabiah
person:nedabiah_2170.summary: Moved of Jehovah, one of the sons of Jeconiah (1 Chr. 3:18).

person:nehemiah_2172.name: Nehemiah
person:nehemiah_2172.title: Nehemiah
person:nehemiah_2172.summary: The son of Hachaliah (Neh. 1:1), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem (Neh. 2:3). He was one of the “Jews of the dispersion,” and in his youth was appointed to the important office of royal cup-bearer at the palace of Shushan. The king, Artaxerxes Longimanus, seems to have been on terms of friendly familiarity with his attendant. Through his brother Hanani, and perhaps from other sources (Neh. 1:2; 2:3), he heard of the mournful and desolate condition of the Holy City, and was filled with sadness of heart. For many days he fasted and mourned and prayed for the place of his fathers’ sepulchres. …

person:nehushta_2174.name: Nehushta
person:nehushta_2174.title: Nehushta
person:nehushta_2174.summary: Copper, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, and the wife of Jehoiakin (2 Kings 24:8), king of Judah.

person:nemuel_2177.name: Nemuel
person:nemuel_2177.title: Nemuel
person:nemuel_2177.summary: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 26:9).

person:ner_2181.name: Ner
person:ner_2181.title: Ner
person:ner_2181.summary: Light, the father of Kish (1 Chr. 8:33). 1 Sam. 14:51 should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.” And hence this Kish and Ner were brothers, and Saul and Abner were first cousins (comp. 1 Chr. 9:36).

person:nergal-sharezer_2183.name: Nergal-sharezer
person:nergal-sharezer_2183.title: Nergal-sharezer
person:nergal-sharezer_2183.summary: Another of the “princes,” who bore the title of “Rabmag.” He was one of those who were sent to release Jeremiah from prison (Jer. 39:13) by “the captain of the guard.” He was a Babylonian grandee of high rank. From profane history and the inscriptions, we are led to conclude that he was the Neriglissar who murdered Evil-merodach, the son of Nebuchadnezzar, and succeeded him on the throne of Babylon (B.C. 559-556). He was married to a daughter of Nebuchadnezzar. The ruins of a palace, the only one on the right bank of the Euphrates, bear inscriptions denoting that it was built by this king. …

person:nethaneel_2188.name: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2188.title: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2188.summary: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus (Num. 1:8; 2:5).

person:nethaneel_2190.name: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2190.title: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2190.summary: A priest who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

person:nethaneel_2192.name: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2192.title: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2192.summary: A temple porter, of the family of the Korhites (1 Chr. 26:4).

person:nethaneel_2193.name: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2193.title: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2193.summary: One of the “princes” appointed by Jehoshaphat to teach the law through the cities of Judah (2 Chr. 17:7).

person:nethaneel_2194.name: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2194.title: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2194.summary: A chief Levite in the time of Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

person:nethaneel_2197.name: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2197.title: Nethaneel
person:nethaneel_2197.summary: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:36).

person:nethaniah_2200.name: Nethaniah
person:nethaniah_2200.title: Nethaniah
person:nethaniah_2200.summary: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:nicanor_2203.name: Nicanor
person:nicanor_2203.title: Nicanor
person:nicanor_2203.summary: Conqueror, one of the seven deacons appointed in the apostolic Church (Acts 6:1-6). Nothing further is known of him.

person:nicodemus_2204.name: Nicodemus
person:nicodemus_2204.title: Nicodemus
person:nicodemus_2204.summary: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.” He is next met with in the Sanhedrin (7:50-52), where he protested against the course they were taking in plotting against Christ. Once more he is mentioned as taking part in the preparation for the anointing and burial of the body of Christ (John 19:39). We hear nothing more of him. There can be little doubt that he became a true disciple.

person:nicolas_2205.name: Nicolas
person:nicolas_2205.title: Nicolas
person:nicolas_2205.summary: The victory of the people, a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5).

person:nimrod_2206.name: Nimrod
person:nimrod_2206.title: Nimrod
person:nimrod_2206.summary: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10). The “land of Nimrod” (Micah 5:6) is a designation of Assyria or of Shinar, which is a part of it.

person:nimshi_2207.name: Nimshi
person:nimshi_2207.title: Nimshi
person:nimshi_2207.summary: Saved. Jehu was “the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi” (2 Kings 9:2; comp. 1 Kings 19:16).

person:noadiah_2208.name: Noadiah
person:noadiah_2208.title: Noadiah
person:noadiah_2208.summary: A Levite who returned from Babylon (Ezra 8:33).

person:noadiah_2209.name: Noadiah
person:noadiah_2209.title: Noadiah
person:noadiah_2209.summary: A false prophetess who assisted Tobiah and Sanballat against the Jews (Neh. 6:14). Being bribed by them, she tried to stir up discontent among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and so to embarrass Nehemiah in his great work of rebuilding the ruined walls of the city.

person:noah_2210.name: Noah
person:noah_2210.title: Noah
person:noah_2210.summary:
Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second great progenitor of the human family.
The words of his father Lamech at his birth (Gen. 5:29) have been regarded as in a sense prophetical, designating Noah as a type of Him who is the true “rest and comfort” of men under the burden of life (Matt. 11:28).
He lived five hundred years, and then there were born unto him three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth (Gen. 5:32). …

person:noah_2211.name: Noah
person:noah_2211.title: Noah (daughter of Zelophehad)
person:noah_2211.summary:
Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second great progenitor of the human family.
The words of his father Lamech at his birth (Gen. 5:29) have been regarded as in a sense prophetical, designating Noah as a type of Him who is the true “rest and comfort” of men under the burden of life (Matt. 11:28).
He lived five hundred years, and then there were born unto him three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth (Gen. 5:32). …

person:nogah_2213.name: Nogah
person:nogah_2213.title: Nogah
person:nogah_2213.summary: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem (1 Chr. 3:7).

person:nun_2214.name: Nun
person:nun_2214.title: Nun
person:nun_2214.summary: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

person:obadiah_2215.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2215.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2215.summary: An Israelite who was chief in the household of King Ahab (1 Kings 18:3). Amid great spiritual degeneracy he maintained his fidelity to God, and interposed to protect The Lord’s prophets, an hundred of whom he hid at great personal risk in a cave (4, 13). Ahab seems to have held Obadiah in great honour, although he had no sympathy with his piety (5, 6, 7). The last notice of him is his bringing back tidings to Ahab that Elijah, whom he had so long sought for, was at hand (9-16). “Go,” said Elijah to him, when he met him in the way, “go tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here.”

person:obadiah_2217.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2217.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2217.summary: A chief of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:3).

person:obadiah_2219.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2219.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2219.summary: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

person:obadiah_2220.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2220.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2220.summary: A Gadite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:9).

person:obadiah_2221.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2221.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2221.summary: A prince of Zebulun in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:19).

person:obadiah_2222.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2222.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2222.summary: One of the princes sent by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

person:obadiah_2223.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2223.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2223.summary: A Levite who superintended the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

person:obadiah_2224.name: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2224.title: Obadiah
person:obadiah_2224.summary: One who accompanied Ezra on the return from Babylon (Ezra 8:9).

person:obed_2228.name: Obed
person:obed_2228.title: Obed
person:obed_2228.summary: A son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:21, 22), and the grandfather of David (Matt. 1:5).

person:obil_2234.name: Obil
person:obil_2234.title: Obil
person:obil_2234.summary: A keeper of camels, an Ishmaelite who was “over the camels” in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:30).

person:oded_2237.name: Oded
person:oded_2237.title: Oded
person:oded_2237.summary: A prophet in the time of Ahaz and Pekah (2 Chr. 28:9-15).

person:og_2238.name: Og
person:og_2238.title: Og
person:og_2238.summary: Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons (Deut. 1:4), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 21:32-35; Deut. 3:1-13). His bedstead (or rather sarcophagus) was of iron (or ironstone), 9 cubits in length and 4 cubits in breadth. His overthrow was afterwards celebrated in song (Ps. 135:11; 136:20).

person:ohad_2239.name: Ohad
person:ohad_2239.title: Ohad
person:ohad_2239.summary: United, or power, the third son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10).

person:ohel_2240.name: Ohel
person:ohel_2240.title: Ohel
person:ohel_2240.summary: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:20).

person:olympas_2241.name: Olympas
person:olympas_2241.title: Olympas
person:olympas_2241.summary: A Roman Christian whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:15).

person:omar_2242.name: Omar
person:omar_2242.title: Omar
person:omar_2242.summary: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

person:omri_2243.name: Omri
person:omri_2243.title: Omri
person:omri_2243.summary: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah (1 Kings 16:15-27), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931). For four years there was continued opposition to his reign, Tibni, another claimant to the throne, leading the opposing party; but at the close of that period all his rivals were defeated, and he became king of Israel, “Tibni died and Omri reigned” (B.C. 927). By his vigour and power he gained great eminence and consolidated the kingdom. He fixed his dynasty on the throne so firmly that it continued during four succeeding reigns. Tirza was for six years the seat of his government. …

person:onan_2250.name: Onan
person:onan_2250.title: Onan
person:onan_2250.summary: Strong, the second son of Judah (Gen. 38:4-10; comp. Deut. 25:5; Matt. 22:24). He died before the going down of Jacob and his family into Egypt.

person:onesimus_2251.name: Onesimus
person:onesimus_2251.title: Onesimus
person:onesimus_2251.summary:
Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name. In it he beseeches Philemon to receive his slave as a “faithful and beloved brother.” Paul offers to pay to Philemon anything his slave had taken, and to bear the wrong he had done him. He was accompanied on his return by Tychicus, the bearer of the Epistle to the Colossians (Philemon 1:16, 18).
The story of this fugitive Colossian slave is a remarkable evidence of the freedom of access to the prisoner which was granted to all, and “a beautiful illustration both of the character of St. …

person:onesiphorus_2252.name: Onesiphorus
person:onesiphorus_2252.title: Onesiphorus
person:onesiphorus_2252.summary: Bringing profit, an Ephesian Christian who showed great kindness to Paul at Rome. He served him in many things, and had oft refreshed him. Paul expresses a warm interest in him and his household (2 Tim. 1:16-18; 4:19).

person:ophir_2253.name: Ophir
person:ophir_2253.title: Ophir
person:ophir_2253.summary: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

person:oreb_2255.name: Oreb
person:oreb_2255.title: Oreb
person:oreb_2255.summary: Raven, a prince of Midian, who, being defeated by Gideon and put to straits, was slain along with Zeeb (Judg. 7:20-25). Many of the Midianites perished along with him (Ps. 83:9; Isa. 10:26).

person:oren_2256.name: Oren
person:oren_2256.title: Oren
person:oren_2256.summary: Ash or pine, the son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

person:ornan_289.name: Ornan
person:ornan_289.title: Ornan
person:ornan_289.summary: Agile; also called Ornan 1 Chr. 21:15, a Jebusite who dwelt in Jerusalem before it was taken by the Israelites. The destroying angel, sent to punish David for his vanity in taking a census of the people, was stayed in his work of destruction near a threshing-floor belonging to Araunah which was situated on Mount Moriah. Araunah offered it to David as a free gift, together with the oxen and the threshing instruments; but the king insisted on purchasing it at its full price (2 Sam. 24:24; 1 Chr. 21:24, 25), for, according to the law of sacrifices, he could not offer to God what cost him nothing. On the same place Solomon afterwards erected the temple (2 Sam. 24:16; 2 Chr. 3:1).

person:orpah_2257.name: Orpah
person:orpah_2257.title: Orpah
person:orpah_2257.summary: Forelock or fawn, a Moabitess, the wife of Chilion (Ruth 1:4; 4:10). On the death of her husband she accompanied Naomi, her mother-in-law, part of the way to Bethlehem, and then returned to Moab.

person:othni_2258.name: Othni
person:othni_2258.title: Othni
person:othni_2258.summary: A lion of Jehovah, a son of Shemaiah, and one of the temple porters in the time of David (1 Chr. 26:7). He was a “mighty man of valour.”

person:othniel_2259.name: Othniel
person:othniel_2259.title: Othniel
person:othniel_2259.summary: Lion of God, the first of the judges. His wife Achsah was the daughter of Caleb (Josh. 15:16, 17; Judg. 1:13). He gained her hand as a reward for his bravery in leading a successful expedition against Debir (q.v.). Some thirty years after the death of Joshua, the Israelites fell under the subjection of Chushan-rishathaim (q.v.), the king of Mesopotamia. He oppressed them for full eight years, when they “cried” unto Jehovah, and Othniel was raised up to be their deliverer. He was the younger brother of Caleb (Judg. 3:8, 9-11). He is the only judge mentioned connected with the tribe of Judah. Under him the land had rest forty years.

person:ozem_2260.name: Ozem
person:ozem_2260.title: Ozem
person:ozem_2260.summary: One of David’s brothers; the sixth son of Jesse (1 Chr. 2:15).

person:ozni_1235.name: Ozni
person:ozni_1235.title: Ozni
person:ozni_1235.summary: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

person:paarai_2262.name: Paarai
person:paarai_2262.title: Paarai
person:paarai_2262.summary: Opening of the Lord, “the Arbite,” one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:35); called also Naarai, 1 Chr. 11:37.

person:pagiel_2264.name: Pagiel
person:pagiel_2264.title: Pagiel
person:pagiel_2264.summary: God allots, a prince of the tribe of Asher (Num. 1:13), in the wilderness.

person:pahath-moab_2265.name: Pahath-moab
person:pahath-moab_2265.title: Pahath-moab
person:pahath-moab_2265.summary: Governor of Moab, a person whose descendants returned from the Captivity and assisted in rebuilding Jerusalem (Ezra 2:6; 8:4; 10:30).

person:pallu_2325.name: Pallu
person:pallu_2325.title: Pallu
person:pallu_2325.summary: Separated, the second son of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:3); called Phallu, Gen. 46:9. He was the father of the Phalluites (Ex. 6:14; Num. 26:5, 8).

person:palti_2269.name: Palti
person:palti_2269.title: Palti
person:palti_2269.summary: Deliverance from the Lord, one of the spies representing the tribe of Benjamin (Num. 13:9).

person:paltiel_2270.name: Paltiel
person:paltiel_2270.title: Paltiel
person:paltiel_2270.summary: Deliverance of God, the prince of Issachar who assisted “to divide the land by inheritance” (Num. 34:26).

person:parmashta_2271.name: Parmashta
person:parmashta_2271.title: Parmashta
person:parmashta_2271.summary: Strong-fisted, a son of Haman, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:9).

person:parshandatha_2277.name: Parshandatha
person:parshandatha_2277.title: Parshandatha
person:parshandatha_2277.summary: An interpreter of the law, the eldest of Haman’s sons, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:7).

person:paruah_2278.name: Paruah
person:paruah_2278.title: Paruah
person:paruah_2278.summary: Flourishing, the father of Jehoshaphat, appointed to provide monthly supplies for Solomon from the tribe of Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

person:pasach_2279.name: Pasach
person:pasach_2279.title: Pasach
person:pasach_2279.summary: Clearing, one of the sons of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:33).

person:patrobas_2289.name: Patrobas
person:patrobas_2289.title: Patrobas
person:patrobas_2289.summary: A Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

person:paul_2479.name: Paul
person:paul_2479.title: Paul
person:paul_2479.summary: '=Saul (q.v.) was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name. He was a native of Tarsus, the capital of Cilicia, a Roman province in the south-east of Asia Minor. That city stood on the banks of the river Cydnus, which was navigable thus far; hence it became a centre of extensive commercial traffic with many countries along the shores of the Mediterranean, as well as with the countries of central Asia Minor. …

person:pedahel_2290.name: Pedahel
person:pedahel_2290.title: Pedahel
person:pedahel_2290.summary: Redeemed of God, the son of Ammihud, a prince of Naphtali (Num. 34:28).

person:pedahzur_2291.name: Pedahzur
person:pedahzur_2291.title: Pedahzur
person:pedahzur_2291.summary: Rock of redemption, the father of Gamaliel and prince of Manasseh at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:20).

person:pedaiah_2292.name: Pedaiah
person:pedaiah_2292.title: Pedaiah
person:pedaiah_2292.summary: The father of Zebudah, who was the wife of Josiah and mother of king Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

person:pedaiah_2294.name: Pedaiah
person:pedaiah_2294.title: Pedaiah
person:pedaiah_2294.summary: . The father of Joel, ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr. 27:20).

person:pekah_2299.name: Pekah
person:pekah_2299.title: Pekah
person:pekah_2299.summary: Open-eyed, the son of Remaliah a captain in the army of Pekahiah, king of Israel, whom he slew, with the aid of a band of Gileadites, and succeeded (B.C. 758) on the throne (2 Kings 15:25). Seventeen years after this he entered into an alliance with Rezin, king of Syria, and took part with him in besieging Jerusalem (2 Kings 15:37; 16:5). But Tiglath-pilser, who was in alliance with Ahaz, king of Judah, came up against Pekah, and carried away captive many of the inhabitants of his kingdom (2 Kings 15:29). This was the beginning of the “Captivity.” Soon after this Pekah was put to death by Hoshea, the son of Elah, who usurped the throne (2 Kings 15:30; 16:1-9. Comp. Isa. 7:16; 8:4; 9:12). …

person:pekahiah_2300.name: Pekahiah
person:pekahiah_2300.title: Pekahiah
person:pekahiah_2300.summary: The Lord opened his eyes, the son and successor of Menahem on the throne of Israel. He was murdered in the royal palace of Samaria by Pekah, one of the captains of his army (2 Kings 15:23-26), after a reign of two years (B.C. 761-759). He “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

person:pelaiah_2302.name: Pelaiah
person:pelaiah_2302.title: Pelaiah
person:pelaiah_2302.summary: A Levite who expounded the law (Neh. 8:7).

person:pelatiah_2304.name: Pelatiah
person:pelatiah_2304.title: Pelatiah
person:pelatiah_2304.summary: A son of Hananiah and grandson of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:21).

person:pelatiah_2307.name: Pelatiah
person:pelatiah_2307.title: Pelatiah
person:pelatiah_2307.summary: One of the twenty-five princes of the people against whom Ezekiel prophesied on account of their wicked counsel (Ezek. 11:1-13).

person:peleg_2308.name: Peleg
person:peleg_2308.title: Peleg
person:peleg_2308.summary: Division, one of the sons of Eber; so called because “in his days was the earth divided” (Gen. 10:25). Possibly he may have lived at the time of the dispersion from Babel. But more probably the reference is to the dispersion of the two races which sprang from Eber, the one spreading towards Mesopotamia and Syria, and the other southward into Arabia.

person:pelet_2310.name: Pelet
person:pelet_2310.title: Pelet
person:pelet_2310.summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

person:peleth_2311.name: Peleth
person:peleth_2311.title: Peleth
person:peleth_2311.summary: A Reubenite whose son was one of the conspirators against Moses and Aaron (Num. 16:1).

person:peleth_2312.name: Peleth
person:peleth_2312.title: Peleth
person:peleth_2312.summary: One of the sons of Jonathan (1 Chr. 2:33).

person:perida_2318.name: Perida
person:perida_2318.title: Perida
person:perida_2318.summary: One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:55); called also Perida (Neh. 7:57).

person:persis_2317.name: Persis
person:persis_2317.title: Persis
person:persis_2317.summary: A female Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:12). She is spoken of as “beloved,” and as having “laboured much in the Lord.”

person:peter_2745.name: Simon
person:peter_2745.title: Simon Peter
person:peter_2745.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture. He had a younger brother called Andrew, who first brought him to Jesus (John 1:40-42). His native town was Bethsaida, on the western coast of the Sea of Galilee, to which also Philip belonged. Here he was brought up by the shores of the Sea of Galilee, and was trained to the occupation of a fisher. His father had probably died while he was still young, and he and his brother were brought up under the care of Zebedee and his wife Salome (Matt. 27:56; Mark 15:40; 16:1). …

person:pethahiah_2319.name: Pethahiah
person:pethahiah_2319.title: Pethahiah
person:pethahiah_2319.summary: The chief of one of the priestly courses (the nineteenth) in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:16).

person:pethahiah_2322.name: Pethahiah
person:pethahiah_2322.title: Pethahiah
person:pethahiah_2322.summary: A descendant of Judah who had some office at the court of Persia (Neh. 11:24).

person:pethuel_2323.name: Pethuel
person:pethuel_2323.title: Pethuel
person:pethuel_2323.summary: Vision of God, the father of Joel the prophet (Joel 1:1).

person:peulthai_2324.name: Peulthai
person:peulthai_2324.title: Peulthai
person:peulthai_2324.summary: Wages of the Lord, one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite porter (1 Chr. 26:5).

person:phaltiel_2326.name: Phaltiel
person:phaltiel_2326.title: Phaltiel
person:phaltiel_2326.summary: Deliverance of the Lord, the son of Laish of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44)= Phaltiel (2 Sam. 3:15). Michal, David’s wife, was given to him.

person:phanuel_2327.name: Phanuel
person:phanuel_2327.title: Phanuel
person:phanuel_2327.summary: Face of God, father of the prophetess Anna (q.v.), Luke 2:36.

person:pharaoh_2328.name: Pharaoh
person:pharaoh_2328.title: Pharaoh (during Abraham's Journey)
person:pharaoh_2328.summary: The Pharaoh who was on the throne when Abram went down into Egypt (Gen. 12:10-20) was probably one of the Hyksos, or “shepherd kings.” The Egyptians called the nomad tribes of Syria Shasu, “plunderers,” their king or chief Hyk, and hence the name of those invaders who conquered the native kings and established a strong government, with Zoan or Tanis as their capital. They were of Semitic origin, and of kindred blood accordingly with Abram. They were probably driven forward by the pressure of the Hittites. The name they bear on the monuments is “Mentiu.”

person:pharaoh_2329.name: Pharaoh
person:pharaoh_2329.title: Pharaoh (of Joseph)
person:pharaoh_2329.summary: The Pharaoh of Joseph’s days (Gen. 41) was probably Apopi, or Apopis, the last of the Hyksos kings. To the old native Egyptians, who were an African race, shepherds were “an abomination;” but to the Hyksos kings these Asiatic shepherds who now appeared with Jacob at their head were congenial, and being akin to their own race, had a warm welcome (Gen. 47:5, 6). Some argue that Joseph came to Egypt in the reign of Thothmes III., long after the expulsion of the Hyksos, and that his influence is to be seen in the rise and progress of the religious revolution in the direction of monotheism which characterized the middle of the Eighteenth Dynasty. …

person:pharaoh_2330.name: Pharaoh
person:pharaoh_2330.title: Pharaoh
person:pharaoh_2330.summary:
The “new king who knew not Joseph” (Ex. 1:8-22) has been generally supposed to have been Aahmes I., or Amosis, as he is called by Josephus. Recent discoveries, however, have led to the conclusion that Seti was the “new king.”
For about seventy years the Hebrews in Egypt were under the powerful protection of Joseph. After his death their condition was probably very slowly and gradually changed. The invaders, the Hyksos, who for some five centuries had been masters of Egypt, were driven out, and the old dynasty restored. The Israelites now began to be looked down upon. They began to be afflicted and tyrannized over. …

person:pharaoh_2331.name: Pharaoh
person:pharaoh_2331.title: Pharaoh (of the Exodus)
person:pharaoh_2331.summary: The Pharaoh of the Exodus was probably Menephtah I., the fourteenth and eldest surviving son of Rameses II. He resided at Zoan, where he had the various interviews with Moses and Aaron recorded in the book of Exodus. His mummy was not among those found at Deir el-Bahari. It is still a question, however, whether Seti II. or his father Menephtah was the Pharaoh of the Exodus. Some think the balance of evidence to be in favour of the former, whose reign it is known began peacefully, but came to a sudden and disastrous end. …

person:pharaoh_2333.name: Pharaoh
person:pharaoh_2333.title: Pharaoh
person:pharaoh_2333.summary: Pharaoh, in whom Hezekiah put his trust in his war against Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:21).

person:pharez_2338.name: Pharez
person:pharez_2338.title: Pharez
person:pharez_2338.summary: '=Pharez, (q.v.), breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3). Four hundred and sixty-eight of his “sons” came back from captivity with Zerubbabel, who himself was one of them (1 Chr. 9:4; Neh. 11:6).

person:phebe_2340.name: Phebe
person:phebe_2340.title: Phebe
person:phebe_2340.summary: A “deaconess of the church at Cenchrea,” the port of Corinth. She was probably the bearer of Paul’s epistle to the Romans. Paul commended her to the Christians at Rome; “for she hath been,” says he, “a succourer of many, and of myself also” (Rom. 16:1, 2).

person:phichol_2341.name: Phichol
person:phichol_2341.title: Phichol
person:phichol_2341.summary: Great, the chief captain of the army of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar. He entered into an alliance with Abraham with reference to a certain well which, from this circumstance, was called Beersheba (q.v.), “the well of the oath” (Gen. 21:22, 32; 26:26).

person:philemon_2342.name: Philemon
person:philemon_2342.title: Philemon
person:philemon_2342.summary: An inhabitant of Colosse, and apparently a person of some note among the citizens (Col. 4:9; Philemon 1:2). He was brought to a knowledge of the gospel through the instrumentality of Paul (19), and held a prominent place in the Christian community for his piety and beneficence (4-7). He is called in the epistle a “fellow-labourer,” and therefore probably held some office in the church at Colosse; at all events, the title denotes that he took part in the work of spreading a knowledge of the gospel.

person:philetus_2343.name: Philetus
person:philetus_2343.title: Philetus
person:philetus_2343.summary: Amiable, with Hymenaeus, at Ephesus, said that the “resurrection was past already” (2 Tim. 2:17, 18). This was a Gnostic heresy held by the Nicolaitanes.

person:philip_2344.name: Philip
person:philip_2344.title: Phillip the Apostle
person:philip_2344.summary: One of the twelve apostles; a native of Bethsaida, “the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). He readily responded to the call of Jesus when first addressed to him (43), and forthwith brought Nathanael also to Jesus (45, 46). He seems to have held a prominent place among the apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; John 6:5-7; 12:21, 22; 14:8, 9; Acts 1:13). Of his later life nothing is certainly known. He is said to have preached in Phrygia, and to have met his death at Hierapolis.

person:philip_2345.name: Philip
person:philip_2345.title: Philip
person:philip_2345.summary: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome. (See HEROD PHILIP I.)

person:philip_2347.name: Philip
person:philip_2347.title: Phillip the Evangelist
person:philip_2347.summary: One of the “seven” (Acts 6:5), called also “the evangelist” (21:8, 9). He was one of those who were “scattered abroad” by the persecution that arose on the death of Stephen. He went first to Samaria, where he laboured as an evangelist with much success (8:5-13). While he was there he received a divine command to proceed toward the south, along the road leading from Jerusalem to Gaza. These towns were connected by two roads. …

person:phinehas_2349.name: Phinehas
person:phinehas_2349.title: Phinehas (Levite)
person:phinehas_2349.summary: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25). While yet a youth he distinguished himself at Shittim by his zeal against the immorality into which the Moabites had tempted the people (Num. 25:1-9), and thus “stayed the plague” that had broken out among the people, and by which twenty-four thousand of them perished. For his faithfulness on that occasion he received the divine approbation (10-13). He afterwards commanded the army that went out against the Midianites (31:6-8). …

person:phinehas_2350.name: Phinehas
person:phinehas_2350.title: Phinehas
person:phinehas_2350.summary: One of the sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:12). He and his brother Hophni were guilty of great crimes, for which destruction came on the house of Eli (31). He died in battle with the Philistines (1 Sam. 4:4, 11); and his wife, on hearing of his death, gave birth to a son, whom she called “Ichabod,” and then she died (19-22).

person:phlegon_2352.name: Phlegon
person:phlegon_2352.title: Phlegon
person:phlegon_2352.summary: Burning, a Roman Christian to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

person:phut_2354.name: Phut
person:phut_2354.title: Phut
person:phut_2354.summary: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

person:phygellus_2356.name: Phygellus
person:phygellus_2356.title: Phygellus
person:phygellus_2356.summary: Fugitive, a Christian of Asia, who “turned away” from Paul during his second imprisonment at Rome (2 Tim. 1:15). Nothing more is known of him.

person:pilate_2365.name: Pontius
person:pilate_2365.title: Pontius Pilate
person:pilate_2365.summary: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one. He was the sixth in the order of the Roman procurators of Judea (A.D. 26-36). His headquarters were at Caesarea, but he frequently went up to Jerusalem. His reign extended over the period of the ministry of John the Baptist and of Jesus Christ, in connection with whose trial his name comes into prominent notice. …

person:portius_2367.name: Portius
person:portius_2367.title: Portius Festus
person:portius_2367.summary: The successor of Felix (A.D. 60) as procurator of Judea (Acts 24:27). A few weeks after he had entered on his office the case of Paul, then a prisoner at Caesarea, was reported to him. The “next day,” after he had gone down to Caesarea, he heard Paul defend himself in the presence of Herod Agrippa II. and his sister Bernice, and not finding in him anything worthy of death or of bonds, would have set him free had he not appealed unto Caesar (Acts 25:11, 12). In consequence of this appeal Paul was sent to Rome. Festus, after being in office less than two years, died in Judea.

person:potiphar_2368.name: Potiphar
person:potiphar_2368.title: Potiphar
person:potiphar_2368.summary: Dedicated to Ra; i.e., to the sun-god, the Egyptian to whom the Ishmaelites sold Joseph (Gen. 39:1). He was “captain of the guard”, i.e., chief, probably, of the state police, who, while they formed part of the Egyptian army, were also largely employed in civil duties (37:36; marg., “chief of the executioners”). Joseph, though a foreigner, gradually gained his confidence, and became overseer over all his possessions. Believing the false accusation which his profligate wife brought against Joseph, Potiphar cast him into prison, where he remained for some years.

person:priscilla_2370.name: Priscilla
person:priscilla_2370.title: Priscilla
person:priscilla_2370.summary: The wife of Aquila (Acts 18:2), who is never mentioned without her. Her name sometimes takes the precedence of his (Rom. 16:3; 2 Tim. 4:19). She took part with Aquila (q.v.) in insturcting Apollos (Acts 18:26).

person:puah_2372.name: Puah
person:puah_2372.title: Puah
person:puah_2372.summary: One of the two midwives who feared God, and refused to kill the Hebrew male children at their birth (Ex. 1:15-21).

person:publius_2374.name: Publius
person:publius_2374.title: Publius
person:publius_2374.summary: “the chief man of the island” of Malta (Acts 28:7), who courteously entertained Paul and his shipwrecked companions for three days, till they found a more permanent place of residence; for they remained on the island for three months, till the stormy season had passed. The word here rendered “chief man” (protos) is supposed by some to be properly a Maltese term, the official title of the governor.

person:pudens_2375.name: Pudens
person:pudens_2375.title: Pudens
person:pudens_2375.summary: Bashful, a Christian at Rome, who sent his greetings to Timothy (2 Tim. 4:21).

person:quartus_2378.name: Quartus
person:quartus_2378.title: Quartus
person:quartus_2378.summary: Fourth, a Corinthian Christian who sent by Paul his salutations to friends at Rome (Rom. 16:23).

person:raamah_2380.name: Raamah
person:raamah_2380.title: Raamah
person:raamah_2380.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

person:rabsaris_2382.name: Rabsaris
person:rabsaris_2382.title: Rabsaris
person:rabsaris_2382.summary: Chief of the Heads, one of the three officers whom Sennacherib sent from Lachish with a threatening message to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Jer. 39:3, 13).

person:rabshakeh_2384.name: Rabshakeh
person:rabshakeh_2384.title: Rabshakeh
person:rabshakeh_2384.summary: Chief of the princes, the name given to the chief cup-bearer or the vizier of the Assyrian court; one of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah. See the speech he delivered, in the Hebrew language, in the hearing of all the people, as he stood near the wall on the north side of the city (2 Kings 18:17-37). He and the other envoys returned to their master and reported that Hezekiah and his people were obdurate, and would not submit.

person:rachab_2385.name: Rachab
person:rachab_2385.title: Rachab
person:rachab_2385.summary: '=Rahab, a name found in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:5).

person:rachel_2386.name: Rachel
person:rachel_2386.title: Rachel
person:rachel_2386.summary: Ewe, “the daughter”, “the somewhat petulant, peevish, and self-willed though beautiful younger daughter” of Laban, and one of Jacob’s wives (Gen. 29:6, 28). He served Laban fourteen years for her, so deep was Jacob’s affection for her. She was the mother of Joseph (Gen. 30:22-24). Afterwards, on Jacob’s departure from Mesopotamia, she took with her her father’s teraphim (31:34, 35). As they journeyed on from Bethel, Rachel died in giving birth to Benjamin (35:18, 19), and was buried “in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem. And Jacob set a pillar upon her grave”. Her sepulchre is still regarded with great veneration by the Jews. …

person:rahab_2388.name: Rahab
person:rahab_2388.title: Rahab
person:rahab_2388.summary:
Insolence; pride, a poetical name applied to Egypt in Ps. 87:4; 89:10; Isa. 51:9, as “the proud one.”
Rahab, (Heb. Rahab; i.e., “broad,” “large”). When the Hebrews were encamped at Shittim, in the “Arabah” or Jordan valley opposite Jericho, ready to cross the river, Joshua, as a final preparation, sent out two spies to “spy the land.” After five days they returned, having swum across the river, which at this season, the month Abib, overflowed its banks from the melting of the snow on Lebanon. The spies reported how it had fared with them (Josh. 2:1-7). …

person:raham_2389.name: Raham
person:raham_2389.title: Raham
person:raham_2389.summary: Merciful, one of the descendants of Caleb, the son of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:44).

person:ram_2391.name: Ram
person:ram_2391.title: Ram
person:ram_2391.summary: The son of Hezron, and one of the ancestors of the royal line (Ruth 4:19). The margin of 1 Chr. 2:9, also Matt. 1:3, 4 and Luke 3:33, have “Aram.”

person:ram_2392.name: Ram
person:ram_2392.title: Ram
person:ram_2392.summary: One of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25, 27).

person:ram_2393.name: Ram
person:ram_2393.title: Ram
person:ram_2393.summary: A person mentioned in Job 32:2 as founder of a clan to which Elihu belonged. The same as Aram of Gen. 22:21.

person:rapha_2447.name: Rapha
person:rapha_2447.title: Rapha
person:rapha_2447.summary: A Benjamite, the son of Binea (1 Chr. 8:2, 37), a descendant of Saul.

person:raphu_2397.name: Raphu
person:raphu_2397.title: Raphu
person:raphu_2397.summary: Healed, a Benjamite, whose son Palti was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:9).

person:reba_2400.name: Reba
person:reba_2400.title: Reba
person:reba_2400.summary: Fourth, one of the Midianite chiefs slain by the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 31:8; Josh. 13:21).

person:rebekah_2401.name: Rebekah
person:rebekah_2401.title: Rebekah
person:rebekah_2401.summary: A noose, the daughter of Bethuel, and the wife of Isaac (Gen. 22:23; 24:67). The circumstances under which Abraham’s “steward” found her at the “city of Nahor,” in Padan-aram, are narrated in Gen. 24-27. “She can hardly be regarded as an amiable woman. When we first see her she is ready to leave her father’s house for ever at an hour’s notice; and her future life showed not only a full share of her brother Laban’s duplicity, but the grave fault of partiality in her relations to her children, and a strong will, which soon controlled the gentler nature of her husband.” The time and circumstances of her death are not recorded, but it is said that she was buried in the cave of Machpelah (Gen. …

person:rechab_2402.name: Rechab
person:rechab_2402.title: Rechab
person:rechab_2402.summary: One of Ishbosheth’s “captains of bands” or leaders of predatory troops (2 Sam. 4:2).

person:rechab_2403.name: Rechab
person:rechab_2403.title: Rechab
person:rechab_2403.summary: The father of Jehonadab, who was the father of the Rechabites (2 Kings 10:15, 23; Jer. 35:6-19).

person:reelaiah_2406.name: Reelaiah
person:reelaiah_2406.title: Reelaiah
person:reelaiah_2406.summary: Thunder of the Lord, one of the princes who returned from the Exile (Neh. 7:7); called also Reelaiah (Ezra 2:2).

person:regem-melech_2408.name: Regem-melech
person:regem-melech_2408.title: Regem-melech
person:regem-melech_2408.summary: Friend of the king, one of the two messengers sent by the exiled Jews to Jerusalem in the time of Darius (Zech. 7:2) to make inquiries at the temple.

person:rehabiah_2409.name: Rehabiah
person:rehabiah_2409.title: Rehabiah
person:rehabiah_2409.summary: Enlargement of the Lord, the son of Eliezer, and grandson of Moses (1 Chr. 23:17; 24:21).

person:rehob_2410.name: Rehob
person:rehob_2410.title: Rehob
person:rehob_2410.summary: The father of Hadadezer, king of Tobah (2 Sam. 8:3, 12).

person:rehoboam_2412.name: Rehoboam
person:rehoboam_2412.title: Rehoboam
person:rehoboam_2412.summary: He enlarges the people, the successor of Solomon on the throne, and apparently his only son. He was the son of Naamah “the Ammonitess,” some well-known Ammonitish princess (1 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 12:13). He was forty-one years old when he ascended the throne, and he reigned seventeen years (B.C. 975-958). Although he was acknowledged at once as the rightful heir to the throne, yet there was a strongly-felt desire to modify the character of the government. The burden of taxation to which they had been subjected during Solomon’s reign was very oppressive, and therefore the people assembled at Shechem and demanded from the king an alleviation of their burdens. …

person:rehum_2413.name: Rehum
person:rehum_2413.title: Rehum
person:rehum_2413.summary: One of “the children of the province” who returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:2); the same as “Nehum” (Neh. 7:7).

person:rehum_2414.name: Rehum
person:rehum_2414.title: Rehum
person:rehum_2414.summary: The “chancellor” of Artaxerxes, who sought to stir him up against the Jews (Ezra 4:8-24) and prevent the rebuilding of the walls and the temple of Jerusalem.

person:rei_2417.name: Rei
person:rei_2417.title: Rei
person:rei_2417.summary: Friendly, one who maintained true allegiance to king David (1 Kings 1:8) when Adonijah rebelled.

person:rekem_2418.name: Rekem
person:rekem_2418.title: Rekem
person:rekem_2418.summary: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites destroyed (Num. 31:8).

person:rekem_2419.name: Rekem
person:rekem_2419.title: Rekem
person:rekem_2419.summary: One of the sons of Hebron (1 Chr. 2:43, 44).

person:remaliah_2420.name: Remaliah
person:remaliah_2420.title: Remaliah
person:remaliah_2420.summary: Adorned by the Lord, the father of Pekah, who conspired successfully against Pekahiah (2 Kings 15:25, 27, 30, 32, 37; Isa. 7:1, 4, 5, 9; 8:6).

person:rephael_2421.name: Rephael
person:rephael_2421.title: Rephael
person:rephael_2421.summary: Healed of God, one of Shemaiah’s sons. He and his brethren, on account of their “strength for service,” formed one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:7, 8).

person:reuben_2429.name: Reuben
person:reuben_2429.title: Reuben
person:reuben_2429.summary: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4). He showed kindness to Joseph, and was the means of saving his life when his other brothers would have put him to death (37:21, 22). It was he also who pledged his life and the life of his sons when Jacob was unwilling to let Benjamin go down into Egypt. After Jacob and his family went down into Egypt (46:8) no further mention is made of Reuben beyond what is recorded in ch. 49:3, 4.

person:reuel_2430.name: Reuel
person:reuel_2430.title: Reuel
person:reuel_2430.summary: A son of Esau and Bashemath (Gen. 36:4, 10; 1 Chr. 1:35).

person:rezin_2435.name: Rezin
person:rezin_2435.title: Rezin
person:rezin_2435.summary: Firm; a prince, a king of Syria, who joined Pekah (q.v.) in an invasion of the kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 15:37; 16:5-9; Isa. 7:1-8). Ahaz induced Tiglath-pileser III. to attack Damascus, and this caused Rezin to withdraw for the purpose of defending his own kingdom. Damascus was taken, and Rezin was slain in battle by the Assyrian king, and his people carried into captivity, B.C. 732 (2 Kings 16:9).

person:rezon_2437.name: Rezon
person:rezon_2437.title: Rezon
person:rezon_2437.summary: Prince, son of Eliadah. Abandoning the service of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, on the occasion of his being defeated by David, he became the “captain over a band” of marauders, and took Damascus, and became king of Syria (1 Kings 11:23-25; 2 Sam. 8:3-8). For centuries after this the Syrians were the foes of Israel. He “became an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon.”

person:rhesa_2438.name: Rhesa
person:rhesa_2438.title: Rhesa
person:rhesa_2438.summary: Affection, son of Zorobabel, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:27).

person:rhoda_2439.name: Rhoda
person:rhoda_2439.title: Rhoda
person:rhoda_2439.summary: A rose, the damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark. She came to hearken when Peter knocked at the door of the gate (Acts 12:12-15).

person:rimmon_2441.name: Rimmon
person:rimmon_2441.title: Rimmon
person:rimmon_2441.summary: A man of Beeroth (2 Sam. 4:2), one of the four Gibeonite cities. (See Josh. 9:17.)

person:riphath_2443.name: Riphath
person:riphath_2443.title: Riphath
person:riphath_2443.summary: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

person:rizpah_2444.name: Rizpah
person:rizpah_2444.title: Rizpah
person:rizpah_2444.summary:
Coal; hot stone, the daughter of Aiah, and one of Saul’s concubines. She was the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth (2 Sam. 3:7; 21:8, 10, 11).
It happened that a grievous famine, which lasted for three years, fell upon the land during the earlier half of David’s reign at Jerusalem. This calamity was sent “for Saul and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.” David inquired of the Gibeonites what satisfaction they demanded, and was answered that nothing would compensate for the wrong Saul had done to them but the death of seven of Saul’s sons. …

person:romamti-ezer_2446.name: Romamti-ezer
person:romamti-ezer_2446.title: Romamti-ezer
person:romamti-ezer_2446.summary: Elevation of help, one of the sons of Heman, “the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn.” He was head of the “four-and-twentieth” course of singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 31).

person:ruth_2450.name: Ruth
person:ruth_2450.title: Ruth
person:ruth_2450.summary: A friend, a Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, whose father, Elimelech, had settled in the land of Moab. On the death of Elimelech and Mahlon, Naomi came with Ruth, her daughter-in-law, who refused to leave her, to Bethlehem, the old home from which Elimelech had migrated. There she had a rich relative, Boaz, to whom Ruth was eventually married. She became the mother of Obed, the grandfather of David. Thus Ruth, a Gentile, is among the maternal progenitors of our Lord (Matt. 1:5). …

person:sabtah_2451.name: Sabtah
person:sabtah_2451.title: Sabtah
person:sabtah_2451.summary: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

person:sacar_2453.name: Sacar
person:sacar_2453.title: Sacar
person:sacar_2453.summary: A son of Obed-edom the Gittite, and a temple porter (1 Chr. 26:4).

person:sadoc_2454.name: Sadoc
person:sadoc_2454.title: Sadoc
person:sadoc_2454.summary: Just, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:14).

person:salah_2455.name: Salah
person:salah_2455.title: Salah
person:salah_2455.summary: A shoot, a descendant of Arphaxed (Luke 3:35, 36); called also Shelah (1 Chr. 1:18, 24).

person:salathiel_2457.name: Salathiel
person:salathiel_2457.title: Salathiel
person:salathiel_2457.summary: Whom I asked of God, the son of Jeconiah (Matt. 1:12; 1 Chr. 3:17); also called the son of Neri (Luke 3:27). The probable explanation of the apparent discrepancy is that he was the son of Neri, the descendant of Nathan, and thus heir to the throne of David on the death of Jeconiah (comp. Jer. 22:30).

person:salmon_2463.name: Salmon
person:salmon_2463.title: Salmon
person:salmon_2463.summary: Shady; or Zalmon (q.v.), a hill covered with dark forests, south of Shechem, from which Abimelech and his men gathered wood to burn that city (Judg. 9:48). In Ps. 68:14 the change from war to peace is likened to snow on the dark mountain, as some interpret the expression. Others suppose the words here mean that the bones of the slain left unburied covered the land, so that it seemed to be white as if covered with snow. The reference, however, of the psalm is probably to Josh. 11 and 12. The scattering of the kings and their followers is fitly likened unto the snow-flakes rapidly falling on the dark Salmon. It is the modern Jebel Suleiman.

person:salome_2464.name: Salome
person:salome_2464.title: Salome
person:salome_2464.summary: The wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John (Mat. 27:56), and probably the sister of Mary, the mother of our Lord (John 19:25). She sought for her sons places of honour in Christ’s kingdom (Matt. 20:20, 21; comp. 19:28). She witnessed the crucifixion (Mark 15:40), and was present with the other women at the sepulchre (Matt. 27:56).

person:samgar-nebo_2466.name: Samgar-nebo
person:samgar-nebo_2466.title: Samgar-nebo
person:samgar-nebo_2466.summary: Be gracious, O Nebo! or a cup-bearer of Nebo, probably the title of Nergal-sharezer, one of the princes of Babylon (Jer. 39:3).

person:samson_2468.name: Samson
person:samson_2468.title: Samson
person:samson_2468.summary: Of the sun, the son of Manoah, born at Zorah. The narrative of his life is given in Judg. 13-16. He was a “Nazarite unto God” from his birth, the first Nazarite mentioned in Scripture (Judg. 13:3-5; comp. Num. 6:1-21). The first recorded event of his life was his marriage with a Philistine woman of Timnath (Judg. 14:1-5). Such a marriage was not forbidden by the law of Moses, as the Philistines did not form one of the seven doomed Canaanite nations (Ex. 34:11-16; Deut. 7:1-4). It was, however, an ill-assorted and unblessed marriage. His wife was soon taken from him and given “to his companion” (Judg. 14:20). …

person:samuel_2469.name: Samuel
person:samuel_2469.title: Samuel
person:samuel_2469.summary: Heard of God. The peculiar circumstances connected with his birth are recorded in 1 Sam. 1:20. Hannah, one of the two wives of Elkanah, who came up to Shiloh to worship before the Lord, earnestly prayed to God that she might become the mother of a son. Her prayer was graciously granted; and after the child was weaned she brought him to Shiloh nd consecrated him to the Lord as a perpetual Nazarite (1:23-2:11). Here his bodily wants and training were attended to by the women who served in the tabernacle, while Eli cared for his religious culture. Thus, probably, twelve years of his life passed away. “The child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the Lord, and also with men” (2:26; comp. …

person:sanballat_2470.name: Sanballat
person:sanballat_2470.title: Sanballat
person:sanballat_2470.summary: Held some place of authority in Samaria when Nehemiah went up to Jerusalem to rebuild its ruined walls. He vainly attempted to hinder this work (Neh. 2:10, 19; 4:1-12; 6). His daughter became the wife of one of the sons of Joiada, a son of the high priest, much to the grief of Nehemiah (13:28).

person:sapphira_2472.name: Sapphira
person:sapphira_2472.title: Sapphira
person:sapphira_2472.summary: Beautiful, the wife of Ananias (q.v.). She was a partner in his guilt and also in his punishment (Acts 5:1-11).

person:sarah_2473.name: Sarah
person:sarah_2473.title: Sarah
person:sarah_2473.summary:
Princess, the wife and at the same time the half-sister of Abraham (Gen. 11:29; 20:12). This name was given to her at the time that it was announced to Abraham that she should be the mother of the promised child. Her story is from her marriage identified with that of the patriarch till the time of her death. Her death, at the age of one hundred and twenty-seven years (the only instance in Scripture where the age of a woman is recorded), was the occasion of Abraham’s purchasing the cave of Machpelah as a family burying-place.
In the allegory of Gal. 4:22-31 she is the type of the “Jerusalem which is above.” She is also mentioned as Sara in Heb. …

person:satan_2476.name: Satan
person:satan_2476.title: Satan
person:satan_2476.summary:
Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7). In the New Testament it is used as interchangeable with Diabolos, or the devil, and is so used more than thirty times.
He is also called “the dragon,” “the old serpent” (Rev. 12:9; 20:2); “the prince of this world” (John 12:31; 14:30); “the prince of the power of the air” (Eph. 2:2); “the god of this world” (2 Cor. 4:4); “the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience” (Eph. 2:2). The distinct personality of Satan and his activity among men are thus obviously recognized. He tempted our Lord in the wilderness (Matt. 4:1-11). …

person:saul_2478.name: Saul
person:saul_2478.title: Saul
person:saul_2478.summary: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10. His father’s she-asses had strayed, and Saul was sent with a servant to seek for them. Leaving his home at Gibeah (10:5, “the hill of God,” A.V.; lit., as in R.V. marg., “Gibeah of God”), Saul and his servant went toward the north-west over Mount Ephraim, and then turning north-east they came to “the land of Shalisha,” and thence eastward to the land of Shalim, and at length came to the district of Zuph, near Samuel’s home at Ramah (9:5-10). …

person:sceva_2480.name: Sceva
person:sceva_2480.title: Sceva
person:sceva_2480.summary: An implement, a Jew, chief of the priests at Ephesus (Acts 19:13-16); i.e., the head of one of the twenty-four courses of the house of Levi. He had seven sons, who “took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus,” in imitation of Paul. They tried their method of exorcism on a fierce demoniac, and failed. His answer to them was to this effect (19:15): “The Jesus whom you invoke is One whose authority I acknowledge; and the Paul whom you name I recognize to be a servant or messenger of God; but what sort of men are ye who have been empowered to act as you do by neither?” (Lindsay on the Acts of the Apostles.)

person:seba_2481.name: Seba
person:seba_2481.title: Seba
person:seba_2481.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

person:secundus_2482.name: Secundus
person:secundus_2482.title: Secundus
person:secundus_2482.summary: Second, a Christian of Thessalonica who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4).

person:segub_2483.name: Segub
person:segub_2483.title: Segub
person:segub_2483.summary: The youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite. His death is recorded in 1 Kings 16:34 (comp. Josh. 6:26).

person:seir_2485.name: Seir
person:seir_2485.title: Seir
person:seir_2485.summary: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

person:semei_2488.name: Semei
person:semei_2488.title: Semei
person:semei_2488.summary: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

person:sennacherib_2489.name: Sennacherib
person:sennacherib_2489.title: Sennacherib
