person:sennacherib_2489.summary: Sin (the god) sends many brothers, son of Sargon, whom he succeeded on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 705), in the 23rd year of Hezekiah. “Like the Persian Xerxes, he was weak and vainglorious, cowardly under reverse, and cruel and boastful in success.” He first set himself to break up the powerful combination of princes who were in league against him. Among these was Hezekiah, who had entered into an alliance with Egypt against Assyria. He accordingly led a very powerful army of at least 200,000 men into Judea, and devastated the land on every side, taking and destroying many cities (2 Kings 18:13-16; comp. Isa. 22, 24, 29, and 2 Chr. 32:1-8). …

person:seorim_2491.name: Seorim
person:seorim_2491.title: Seorim
person:seorim_2491.summary: Barley, the chief of the forth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:8).

person:serah_2492.name: Serah
person:serah_2492.title: Serah
person:serah_2492.summary: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

person:seraiah_2498.name: Seraiah
person:seraiah_2498.title: Seraiah
person:seraiah_2498.summary: A priest of the days of Jehoiakim (Neh. 12:1, 12).

person:seraiah_2500.name: Seraiah
person:seraiah_2500.title: Seraiah
person:seraiah_2500.summary: The son of Neriah. When Zedekiah made a journey to Babylon to do homage to Nebuchadnezzar, Seraiah had charge of the royal gifts to be presented on that occasion. Jeremiah took advantage of the occasion, and sent with Seraiah a word of cheer to the exiles in Babylon, and an announcement of the doom in store for that guilty city. The roll containing this message (Jer. 50:1-8) Seraiah was to read to the exiles, and then, after fixing a stone to it, was to throw it into the Euphrates, uttering, as it sank, the prayer recorded in Jer. 51:59-64. Babylon was at this time in the height of its glory, the greatest and most powerful monarchy in the world. …

person:sered_2501.name: Sered
person:sered_2501.title: Sered
person:sered_2501.summary: Fear, one of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

person:sergius_2502.name: Sergius
person:sergius_2502.title: Sergius Paulus
person:sergius_2502.summary:
A “prudent man” (R.V., “man of understanding”), the deputy (R.V., “proconsul”) of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-13). He became a convert to Christianity under Paul, who visited this island on his first mission to the heathen.
A remarkable memorial of this proconsul was recently (1887) discovered at Rome. On a boundary stone of Claudius his name is found, among others, as having been appointed (A.D. 47) one of the curators of the banks and the channel of the river Tiber. After serving his three years as proconsul at Cyprus, he returned to Rome, where he held the office referred to. As he is not saluted in Paul’s letter to the Romans, he probably died before it was written.

person:serug_2503.name: Serug
person:serug_2503.title: Serug
person:serug_2503.summary: Branch, the father of Nahor (Gen. 11:20-23); called Saruch in Luke 3:35.

person:seth_2504.name: Seth
person:seth_2504.title: Seth
person:seth_2504.summary: Appointed; a substitute, the third son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4:25; 5:3). His mother gave him this name, “for God,” said she, “hath appointed me [i.e., compensated me with] another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.”

person:sethur_2505.name: Sethur
person:sethur_2505.title: Sethur
person:sethur_2505.summary: Hidden, one of the spies sent to search the Promised Land. He was of the tribe of Asher (Num. 13:13).

person:shaashgaz_2508.name: Shaashgaz
person:shaashgaz_2508.title: Shaashgaz
person:shaashgaz_2508.summary: Servant of the beautiful, a chief eunuch in the second house of the harem of king Ahasuerus (Esther 2:14).

person:shadrach_1398.name: Shadrach
person:shadrach_1398.title: Shadrach
person:shadrach_1398.summary: Aku’s command, the Chaldean name given to Hananiah, one of the Hebrew youths whom Nebuchadnezzar carried captive to Babylon (Dan. 1:6, 7; 3:12-30). He and his two companions refused to bow down before the image which Nebuchadnezzar had set up on the plains of Dura. Their conduct filled the king with the greatest fury, and he commanded them to be cast into the burning fiery furnace. Here, amid the fiery flames, they were miraculously preserved from harm. Over them the fire had no power, “neither was a hair of their head singed, neither had the smell of fire passed on them.” Thus Nebuchadnezzar learned the greatness of the God of Israel.

person:shallum_2514.name: Shallum
person:shallum_2514.title: Shallum
person:shallum_2514.summary: The son of Jabesh, otherwise unknown. He “conspired against Zachariah, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead” (2 Kings 15:10). He reigned only “a month of days in Samaria” (15:13, marg.). Menahem rose up against Shallum and put him to death (2 Kings 15:14, 15, 17), and became king in his stead.

person:shallum_2515.name: Shallum
person:shallum_2515.title: Shallum
person:shallum_2515.summary: Keeper of the temple vestments in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:14).

person:shallum_2517.name: Shallum
person:shallum_2517.title: Shallum
person:shallum_2517.summary: One of the posterity of Judah (1 Chr. 2:40, 41).

person:shallum_2520.name: Shallum
person:shallum_2520.title: Shallum
person:shallum_2520.summary: A keeper of the gate in the reign of David (1 Chr. 9:17).

person:shallum_2525.name: Shallum
person:shallum_2525.title: Shallum
person:shallum_2525.summary: The uncle of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 32:7).

person:shalmaneser_2529.name: Shalmaneser
person:shalmaneser_2529.title: Shalmaneser
person:shalmaneser_2529.summary: An Assyrian king (Hos. 10:14), identified with Shalmaneser II. (Sayce) or IV. (Lenormant), the successor of Pul on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 728). He made war against Hoshea, the king of Israel, whom he subdued and compelled to pay an annual tribute. Hoshea, however, soon after rebelled against his Assyrian conquerer. Shalmaneser again marched against Samaria, which, after a siege of three years, was taken (2 Kings 17:3-5; 18:9) by Sargon (q.v.). A revolution meantime had broken out in Assyria, and Shalmaneser was deposed. Sargon usurped the vacant throne. Schrader thinks that this is probably the name of a king of Moab mentioned on an inscription of Tiglath-pileser as Salamanu.

person:shamer_2725.name: Shamer
person:shamer_2725.title: Shamer
person:shamer_2725.summary: A man of Asher (1 Chr. 7:32); called also Shamer (34).

person:shamgar_2534.name: Shamgar
person:shamgar_2534.title: Shamgar
person:shamgar_2534.summary: The Philistines from the maritime plain had made incursions into the Hebrew upland for the purposes of plunder, when one of this name, the son of Anath, otherwise unknown, headed a rising for the purpose of freeing the land from this oppression. He repelled the invasion, slaying 600 men with an “ox goad” (q.v.). The goad was a formidable sharpointed instrument, sometimes ten feet long. He was probably contemporary for a time with Deborah and Barak (Judg. 3:31; 5:6).

person:shamir_2536.name: Shamir
person:shamir_2536.title: Shamir
person:shamir_2536.summary: One of the sons of Michah (1 Chr. 24:24).

person:shammah_2539.name: Shammah
person:shammah_2539.title: Shammah
person:shammah_2539.summary: One of David’s three mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11, 12).

person:shammah_2540.name: Shammah
person:shammah_2540.title: Shammah
person:shammah_2540.summary: One of David’s mighties (2 Sam. 23:25); called also Shammoth (1 Chr. 11:27) and Shamhuth (27:8).

person:shammah_2700.name: Shammah
person:shammah_2700.title: Shammah
person:shammah_2700.summary: One of the sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:9). He is also called Shimeah (2 Sam. 13:3) and Shimma (1 Chr. 2:13).

person:shammua_2545.name: Shammua
person:shammua_2545.title: Shammua
person:shammua_2545.summary: One of the spies sent out by Moses to search the land (Num. 13:4). He represented the tribe of Reuben.

person:shammua_2547.name: Shammua
person:shammua_2547.title: Shammua
person:shammua_2547.summary: One of David’s sons by Bathsheba (1 Chr. 3:5); called also Shammua (14:4).

person:shaphan_2550.name: Shaphan
person:shaphan_2550.title: Shaphan
person:shaphan_2550.summary: A coney, a scribe or secretary of king Josiah (2 Kings 22:3-7). He consulted Huldah concerning the newly-discovered copy of the law which was delivered to him by Hilkiah the priest (8-14). His grandson Gedaliah was governor of Judea (25:22).

person:shaphat_2552.name: Shaphat
person:shaphat_2552.title: Shaphat
person:shaphat_2552.summary: One of the spies. He represented the tribe of Simeon (Num. 13:5).

person:shaphat_2556.name: Shaphat
person:shaphat_2556.title: Shaphat
person:shaphat_2556.summary: One of David’s chief herdsmen (1 Chr. 27:29).

person:sharar_2558.title: Sharar

person:sharezer_2559.name: Sharezer
person:sharezer_2559.title: Sharezer
person:sharezer_2559.summary: (god) protect the king!, a son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria. He and his brother Adrammelech murdered their father, and then fled into the land of Armenia (2 Kings 19:37).

person:shaul_2477.name: Shaul
person:shaul_2477.title: Shaul
person:shaul_2477.summary: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

person:shavsha_2493.summary: (“Seraiah,” 2 Sam. 8:17; “Shisha,” 1 Kings 4:3), one of David’s secretaries (1 Chr. 18:16).

person:shealtiel_2456.name: Shealtiel
person:shealtiel_2456.title: Shealtiel
person:shealtiel_2456.summary: Asked for of God, father of Zerubbabel (Ezra 3:2, 8; Neh. 12:1).

person:sheba_2567.name: Sheba
person:sheba_2567.title: Sheba (son of Raamah)
person:sheba_2567.summary: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

person:sheba_2568.name: Sheba
person:sheba_2568.title: Sheba (son of Joktan)
person:sheba_2568.summary: Heb. id. A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:28), probably the founder of the Sabeans.

person:sheba_2569.name: Sheba
person:sheba_2569.title: Sheba
person:sheba_2569.summary: Heb. id. A son of Jokshan, who was a son of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:3).

person:sheba_2570.name: Sheba
person:sheba_2570.title: Sheba
person:sheba_2570.summary: Heb. id. A “son of Bichri,” of the family of Becher, the son of Benjamin, and thus of the stem from which Saul was descended (2 Sam. 20:1-22). When David was returning to Jerusalem after the defeat of Absalom, a strife arose between the ten tribes and the tribe of Judah, because the latter took the lead in bringing back the king. Sheba took advantage of this state of things, and raised the standard of revolt, proclaiming, “We have no part in David.” With his followers he proceeded northward. David seeing it necessary to check this revolt, ordered Abishai to take the gibborim, “mighty men,” and the body-guard and such troops as he could gather, and pursue Sheba. …

person:shebaniah_2572.name: Shebaniah
person:shebaniah_2572.title: Shebaniah
person:shebaniah_2572.summary: A Levite appointed to blow the trumpet before the ark of God (1 Chr. 15:24).

person:shebaniah_2574.name: Shebaniah
person:shebaniah_2574.title: Shebaniah
person:shebaniah_2574.summary: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

person:shebna_2577.name: Shebna
person:shebna_2577.title: Shebna
person:shebna_2577.summary: Tender youth, “treasurer” over the house in the reign of Hezekiah, i.e., comptroller or governor of the palace. On account of his pride he was ejected from his office, and Eliakim was promoted to it (Isa. 22:15-25). He appears to have been the leader of the party who favoured an alliance with Egypt against Assyria. It is conjectured that “Shebna the scribe,” who was one of those whom the king sent to confer with the Assyrian ambassador (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37; 19:2; Isa. 36:3, 11, 22; 37:2), was a different person.

person:shecaniah_2581.name: Shecaniah
person:shecaniah_2581.title: Shecaniah
person:shecaniah_2581.summary: A priest to whom the tenth lot came forth when David divided the priests (1 Chr. 24:11).

person:shecaniah_2582.name: Shecaniah
person:shecaniah_2582.title: Shecaniah
person:shecaniah_2582.summary:
One of the priests who were set “to give to their brethren by courses” of the daily portion (2 Chr. 31:15).
Shechani’ah, id.

person:shechaniah_2583.name: Shechaniah
person:shechaniah_2583.title: Shechaniah
person:shechaniah_2583.summary: A priest whose sons are mentioned in 1 Chr. 3:21, 22.

person:shechaniah_2586.name: Shechaniah
person:shechaniah_2586.title: Shechaniah
person:shechaniah_2586.summary: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

person:shechem_2588.name: Shechem
person:shechem_2588.title: Shechem
person:shechem_2588.summary: The son of Hamor the Hivite (Gen. 33:19; 34).

person:shelemiah_2600.name: Shelemiah
person:shelemiah_2600.title: Shelemiah
person:shelemiah_2600.summary: Father of one of those who accused Jeremiah to Zedekiah (Jer. 37:3; 38:1).

person:shelemiah_2601.name: Shelemiah
person:shelemiah_2601.title: Shelemiah
person:shelemiah_2601.summary: Father of a captain of the ward (Jer. 37:13).

person:shem_2613.name: Shem
person:shem_2613.title: Shem
person:shem_2613.summary: A name; renown, the first mentioned of the sons of Noah (Gen. 5:32; 6:10). He was probably the eldest of Noah’s sons. The words “brother of Japheth the elder” in Gen. 10:21 are more correctly rendered “the elder brother of Japheth,” as in the Revised Version. Shem’s name is generally mentioned first in the list of Noah’s sons. He and his wife were saved in the ark (7:13). Noah foretold his preeminence over Canaan (9:23-27). He died at the age of six hundred years, having been for many years contemporary with Abraham, according to the usual chronology. The Israelitish nation sprang from him (Gen. 11:10-26; 1 Chr. 1:24-27).

person:shema_2617.name: Shema
person:shema_2617.title: Shema
person:shema_2617.summary: One who stood by Ezra when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

person:shemaah_2618.name: Shemaah
person:shemaah_2618.title: Shemaah
person:shemaah_2618.summary: Rumour, a Benjamite whose sons “came to David to Ziklag” (1 Chr. 12:3).

person:shemaiah_2619.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2619.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2619.summary: A prophet in the reign of Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:22-24).

person:shemaiah_2625.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2625.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2625.summary: A Levite in the time of David, who with 200 of his brethren took part in the bringing up of the ark from Obed-edom to Hebron (1 Chr. 15:8).

person:shemaiah_2627.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2627.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2627.summary: The eldest son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4-8).

person:shemaiah_2628.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2628.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2628.summary: One of the Levites whom Jehoshaphat appointed to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:shemaiah_2630.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2630.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2630.summary: A Levite appointed to “distribute the oblations of the Lord” (2 Chr. 31:15).

person:shemaiah_2637.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2637.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2637.summary: A false prophet who hindered the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Neh. 6:10).

person:shemaiah_2642.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2642.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2642.summary: The father of Urijah the prophet (Jer. 26:20).

person:shemaiah_2643.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2643.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2643.summary: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah (Jer. 29:24-32).

person:shemaiah_2644.name: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2644.title: Shemaiah
person:shemaiah_2644.summary: The father of a prince in the reign of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

person:shemariah_2645.name: Shemariah
person:shemariah_2645.title: Shemariah
person:shemariah_2645.summary: One who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

person:shemeber_2648.name: Shemeber
person:shemeber_2648.title: Shemeber
person:shemeber_2648.summary: Soaring on high, the king of Zeboiim, who joined with the other kings in casting off the yoke of Chedorlaomer. After having been reconquered by him, he was rescued by Abraham (Gen. 14:2).

person:shemiramoth_2651.name: Shemiramoth
person:shemiramoth_2651.title: Shemiramoth
person:shemiramoth_2651.summary: A Levite in David’s time (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

person:shemiramoth_2652.name: Shemiramoth
person:shemiramoth_2652.title: Shemiramoth
person:shemiramoth_2652.summary: A Levite in the reign of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:shemuel_2653.name: Shemuel
person:shemuel_2653.title: Shemuel
person:shemuel_2653.summary: The son of Ammihud. He represented Simeon in the division of the land (Num. 34:20).

person:shemuel_2654.name: Shemuel
person:shemuel_2654.title: Shemuel
person:shemuel_2654.summary: A prince of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2).

person:shephatiah_2658.name: Shephatiah
person:shephatiah_2658.title: Shephatiah
person:shephatiah_2658.summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

person:shephatiah_2659.name: Shephatiah
person:shephatiah_2659.title: Shephatiah
person:shephatiah_2659.summary: A Simeonite prince in David’s time (1 Chr. 27:16).

person:shephatiah_2664.name: Shephatiah
person:shephatiah_2664.title: Shephatiah
person:shephatiah_2664.summary: One of the princes who urged the putting of Jeremiah to death (Jer. 38:1-4).

person:sheresh_2669.name: Sheresh
person:sheresh_2669.title: Sheresh
person:sheresh_2669.summary: Root, a descendant of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:16).

person:sherezer_2670.name: Sherezer
person:sherezer_2670.title: Sherezer
person:sherezer_2670.summary: One of the messengers whom the children of the Captivity sent to Jerusalem “to pray for them before the Lord” (Zech. 7:2).

person:shethar_2673.name: Shethar
person:shethar_2673.title: Shethar
person:shethar_2673.summary: A star, a prince at the court of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:14).

person:shethar-boznai_2674.name: Shethar-boznai
person:shethar-boznai_2674.title: Shethar-boznai
person:shethar-boznai_2674.summary: Star of splendour, a Persian officer who vainly attempted to hinder the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:3, 6; 6:6, 13).

person:shimea_2680.name: Shimea
person:shimea_2680.title: Shimea
person:shimea_2680.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:30).

person:shimea_2681.name: Shimea
person:shimea_2681.title: Shimea
person:shimea_2681.summary: Another Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:39).

person:shimeah_2682.name: Shimeah
person:shimeah_2682.title: Shimeah
person:shimeah_2682.summary: A Benjamite, a descendant of Gibeon (1 Chr. 8:32); called also Shimeam (9:38).

person:shimei_691.name: Shimei
person:shimei_691.title: Shimei
person:shimei_691.summary: A Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:42).

person:shimei_2684.name: Shimei
person:shimei_2684.title: Shimei
person:shimei_2684.summary: A Benjamite of the house of Saul, who stoned and cursed David when he reached Bahurim in his flight from Jerusalem on the occasion of the rebellion of Absalom (2 Sam. 16:5-13). After the defeat of Absalom he “came cringing to the king, humbly suing for pardon, bringing with him a thousand of his Benjamite tribesmen, and representing that he was heartily sorry for his crime, and had hurried the first of all the house of Israel to offer homage to the king” (19:16-23). David forgave him; but on his death-bed he gave Solomon special instructions regarding Shimei, of whose fidelity he seems to have been in doubt (1 Kings 2:8, 9). …

person:shimei_2685.name: Shimei
person:shimei_2685.title: Shimei
person:shimei_2685.summary: One of David’s mighty men who refused to acknowledge Adonijah as David’s successor (1 Kings 1:8). He is probably the same person who is called elsewhere (4:18) “the son of Elah.”

person:shimei_2686.name: Shimei
person:shimei_2686.title: Shimei
person:shimei_2686.summary: A son of Pedaiah, the brother of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19).

person:shimei_2690.name: Shimei
person:shimei_2690.title: Shimei
person:shimei_2690.summary: A Ramathite who was “over the vineyards” of David (1 Chr. 27:27).

person:shimei_2691.name: Shimei
person:shimei_2691.title: Shimei
person:shimei_2691.summary: One of the sons of Heman, who assisted in the purification of the temple (2 Chr. 29:14).

person:shimri_2704.name: Shimri
person:shimri_2704.title: Shimri
person:shimri_2704.summary: The father of one of the “valiant men” of David’s armies (1 Chr. 11:45).

person:shimri_2705.name: Shimri
person:shimri_2705.title: Shimri
person:shimri_2705.summary: Assisted at the purification of the temple in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

person:shimrith_2724.name: Shimrith
person:shimrith_2724.title: Shimrith
person:shimrith_2724.summary: The mother of Jehozabad, who murdered Joash (2 Kings 12:21); called also Shimrith, a Moabitess (2 Chr. 24:26).

person:shimron_2706.name: Shimron
person:shimron_2706.title: Shimron
person:shimron_2706.summary: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

person:shimshai_2707.name: Shimshai
person:shimshai_2707.title: Shimshai
person:shimshai_2707.summary: The shining one, or sunny, the secretary of Rehum the chancellor, who took part in opposing the rebuilding of the temple after the Captivity (Ezra 4:8, 9, 17-23).

person:shinab_2708.name: Shinab
person:shinab_2708.title: Shinab
person:shinab_2708.summary: Cooling, the king of Adamah, in the valley of Siddim, who with his confederates was conquered by Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

person:shiphrah_2710.name: Shiphrah
person:shiphrah_2710.title: Shiphrah
person:shiphrah_2710.summary: Beauty, one of the Egyptian midwives (Ex. 1:15).

person:shiphtan_2711.name: Shiphtan
person:shiphtan_2711.title: Shiphtan
person:shiphtan_2711.summary: Judicial, an Ephraimite prince at the time of the division of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

person:shishak_2712.name: Shishak
person:shishak_2712.title: Shishak
person:shishak_2712.summary: '=Sheshonk I., king of Egypt. His reign was one of great national success, and a record of his wars and conquests adorns the portico of what are called the “Bubastite kings” at Karnak, the ancient Thebes. Among these conquests is a record of that of Judea. In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign Shishak came up against the kingdom of Judah with a powerful army. He took the fenced cities and came to Jerusalem. He pillaged the treasures of the temple and of the royal palace, and carried away the shields of gold which Solomon had made (1 Kings 11:40; 14:25; 2 Chr. 12:2). This expedition of the Egyptian king was undertaken at the instigation of Jeroboam for the purpose of humbling Judah. …

person:shobab_2715.name: Shobab
person:shobab_2715.title: Shobab
person:shobab_2715.summary: One of David’s sons by Bathseheba (2 Sam. 5:14).

person:shobab_2716.name: Shobab
person:shobab_2716.title: Shobab
person:shobab_2716.summary: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18), the son of Hezron.

person:shobach_2717.name: Shobach
person:shobach_2717.title: Shobach
person:shobach_2717.summary: Poured out, the “captain of the host of Hadarezer” when he mustered his vassals and tributaries from beyond “the river Euphrates” (2 Sam. 10:15-18); called also Shophach (1 Chr. 19:16).

person:shobal_2719.name: Shobal
person:shobal_2719.title: Shobal
person:shobal_2719.summary: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

person:shobal_2720.name: Shobal
person:shobal_2720.title: Shobal
person:shobal_2720.summary: One of the sons of Caleb, and a descendant of Hur (1 Chr. 2:50, 52; 4:1, 2).

person:shobi_2722.name: Shobi
person:shobi_2722.title: Shobi
person:shobi_2722.summary: Captor, son of Nahash of Rabbah, the Ammonite. He showed kindness to David when he fled from Jerusalem to Mahanaim (2 Sam. 17:27).

person:shua_2726.name: Shua
person:shua_2726.title: Shua
person:shua_2726.summary: A daughter of Heber the Asherite (1 Chr. 7:32).

person:shuah_2727.name: Shuah
person:shuah_2727.title: Shuah
person:shuah_2727.summary: One of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2; Chr. 1:32).

person:shuah_2728.name: Shuah
person:shuah_2728.title: Shuah
person:shuah_2728.summary: A Canaanite whose daughter was married to Judah (1 Chr. 2:3).

person:shubael_2579.name: Shubael
person:shubael_2579.title: Shubael
person:shubael_2579.summary: One of the descendants of Gershom, who had charge of the temple treasures in the time of David (1 Chr. 23:16; 26:24).

person:shubael_2580.name: Shubael
person:shubael_2580.title: Shubael
person:shubael_2580.summary: One of the sons of Heman; one of those whose duty it was to “lift up the horn” in the temple service (1 Chr. 25:4, 5); called also Shubael (ver. 20).

person:sibbechai_2737.name: Sibbechai
person:sibbechai_2737.title: Sibbechai
person:sibbechai_2737.summary: The Lord sustains, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:29), general of the eighth division of the army (27:11). He slew the giant Saph in the battle of Gob (2 Sam. 21:18; R.V., “Sibbechai”). Called also Mebunnai (23:27).

person:sihon_2739.name: Sihon
person:sihon_2739.title: Sihon
person:sihon_2739.summary:
Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them. The Israelites went forth against him to battle, and gained a complete victory. The Amorites were defeated; Sihon, his sons, and all his people were smitten with the sword, his walled towns were captured, and the entire country of the Amorites was taken possession of by the Israelites (Num. 21:21-30; Deut. 2:24-37).
The country from the Jabbok to Hermon was at this time ruled by Og, the last of the Rephaim. …

person:silas_2740.name: Silas
person:silas_2740.title: Silas
person:silas_2740.summary: Wood, a prominent member of the church at Jerusalem; also called Silvanus. He and Judas, surnamed Barsabas, were chosen by the church there to accompany Paul and Barnabas on their return to Antioch from the council of the apostles and elders (Acts 15:22), as bearers of the decree adopted by the council. He assisted Paul there in his evangelistic labours, and was also chosen by him to be his companion on his second missionary tour (Acts 16:19-24). He is referred to in the epistles under the name of Silvanus (2 Cor. 1:19; 1 Thess. 1:1; 2 Thess. 1:1; 1 Pet. 5:12). There is no record of the time or place of his death.

person:simeon_2741.name: Simeon
person:simeon_2741.title: Simeon
person:simeon_2741.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26). He was detained by Joseph in Egypt as a hostage (42:24). His father, when dying, pronounced a malediction against him (49:5-7). The words in the Authorized Version (49:6), “they digged down a wall,” ought to be, as correctly rendered in the Revised Version, “they houghed an ox.”

person:simeon_2743.name: Simeon
person:simeon_2743.title: Simeon
person:simeon_2743.summary: One of the ancestors of Joseph (Luke 3:30).

person:simeon_2744.name: Simeon
person:simeon_2744.title: Simeon
person:simeon_2744.summary: Surnamed Niger, i.e., “black,” perhaps from his dark complexion, a teacher of some distinction in the church of Antioch (Acts 13:1-3). It has been supposed that this was the Simon of Cyrene who bore Christ’s cross. Note the number of nationalities represented in the church at Antioch.

person:simon_2746.name: Simon
person:simon_2746.title: Simon Zelotes
person:simon_2746.summary: One of the twelve apostles, called the Canaanite (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:18). This word “Canaanite” does not mean a native of Canaan, but is derived from the Syriac word Kanean or Kaneniah, which was the name of a Jewish sect. The Revised Version has “Cananaean;” marg., “or Zealot” He is also called “Zelotes” (Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13; R.V., “the Zealot”), because previous to his call to the apostleship he had been a member of the fanatical sect of the Zealots. There is no record regarding him.

person:simon_2747.name: Simon
person:simon_2747.title: Simon
person:simon_2747.summary: One of the brothers of our Lord (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).

person:simon_2748.name: Simon
person:simon_2748.title: Simon
person:simon_2748.summary: A leper of Bethany, in whose house Mary anointed our Lord’s head with ointment “as he sat at meat” (Matt. 26:6-13; Mark 14:3-9).

person:simon_2749.name: Simon
person:simon_2749.title: Simon
person:simon_2749.summary: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number. They had a synagogue in Jerusalem for such of their number as went thither to the annual feasts. Simon was seized by the soldiers as the procession wended its way to the place of crucifixion as he was passing by, and the heavy cross which Christ from failing strength could no longer bear was laid on his shoulders. Perhaps they seized him because he showed sympathy with Jesus. He was the “father of Alexander and Rufus” (Matt. 27:32). …

person:simon_2752.name: Simon
person:simon_2752.title: Simon the Sorcerer
person:simon_2752.summary: A sorcerer of great repute for his magical arts among the Samaritans (Acts 8:9-11). He afterwards became a professed convert to the faith under the preaching of Philip the deacon and evangelist (12, 13). His profession was, however, soon found to be hollow. His conduct called forth from Peter a stern rebuke (8:18-23). From this moment he disappears from the Church’s history. The term “Simony,” as denoting the purchase for money of spiritual offices, is derived from him.

person:simon_2753.name: Simon
person:simon_2753.title: Simon the Tanner
person:simon_2753.summary: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

person:simri_2754.name: Simri
person:simri_2754.title: Simri
person:simri_2754.summary: Watchman, a Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 26:10).

person:sinite_2755.name: Sinite
person:sinite_2755.title: Sinite
person:sinite_2755.summary: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

person:sippai_2471.name: Sippai
person:sippai_2471.title: Sippai
person:sippai_2471.summary: Extension, the son of the giant whom Sibbechai slew (2 Sam. 21:18); called also Sippai (1 Chr. 20:4).

person:sisera_2757.name: Sisera
person:sisera_2757.title: Sisera (army captain)
person:sisera_2757.summary: The captain of Jabin’s army (Judg. 4:2), which was routed and destroyed by the army of Barak on the plain of Esdraelon. After all was lost he fled to the settlement of Heber the Kenite in the plain of Zaanaim. Jael, Heber’s wife, received him into her tent with apparent hospitality, and “gave him butter” (i.e., lebben, or curdled milk) “in a lordly dish.” Having drunk the refreshing beverage, he lay down, and soon sank into the sleep of the weary. …

person:sisera_2758.name: Sisera
person:sisera_2758.title: Sisera
person:sisera_2758.summary: The ancestor of some of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

person:so_2760.name: So
person:so_2760.title: So
person:so_2760.summary: (Nubian, Sabako), an Ethiopian king who brought Egypt under his sway. He was bribed by Hoshea to help him against the Assyrian monarch Shalmaneser (2 Kings 17:4). This was a return to the policy that had been successful in the reign of Jeroboam I.

person:solomon_2762.name: Solomon
person:solomon_2762.title: Solomon
person:solomon_2762.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1). He succeeded his father on the throne in early manhood, probably about sixteen or eighteen years of age. Nathan, to whom his education was intrusted, called him Jedidiah, i.e., “beloved of the Lord” (2 Sam. 12:24, 25). He was the first king of Israel “born in the purple.” His father chose him as his successor, passing over the claims of his elder sons: “Assuredly Solomon my son shall reign after me.” His history is recorded in 1 Kings 1-11 and 2 Chr. 1-9. …

person:sopater_2770.name: Sopater
person:sopater_2770.title: Sopater
person:sopater_2770.summary: The father who saves, probably the same as Sosipater, a kinsman of Paul (Rom. 16:21), a Christian of the city of Berea who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4-6).

person:sosthenes_2772.name: Sosthenes
person:sosthenes_2772.title: Sosthenes
person:sosthenes_2772.summary: Safe in strength, the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, who was seized and beaten by the mob in the presence of Gallio, the Roman governor, when he refused to proceed against Paul at the instigation of the Jews (Acts 18:12-17). The motives of this assault against Sosthenes are not recorded, nor is it mentioned whether it was made by Greeks or Romans. Some identify him, but without sufficient grounds, with one whom Paul calls “Sosthenes our brother,” a convert to the faith (1 Cor. 1:1).

person:stachys_2774.name: Stachys
person:stachys_2774.title: Stachys
person:stachys_2774.summary: Spike; an ear of corn, a convert at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:9).

person:stephanas_2801.name: Stephanas
person:stephanas_2801.title: Stephanas
person:stephanas_2801.summary: Crown, a member of the church at Corinth, whose family were among those the apostle had baptized (1 Cor. 1:16; 16:15, 17). He has been supposed by some to have been the “jailer of Philippi” (comp. Acts 16:33). The First Epistle to the Corinthians was written from Philippi some six years after the jailer’s conversion, and he was with the apostle there at that time.

person:stephen_2802.name: Stephen
person:stephen_2802.title: Stephen
person:stephen_2802.summary:
One of the seven deacons, who became a preacher of the gospel. He was the first Christian martyr. His personal character and history are recorded in Acts 6. “He fell asleep” with a prayer for his persecutors on his lips (7:60). Devout men carried him to his grave (8:2).
It was at the feet of the young Pharisee, Saul of Tarsus, that those who stoned him laid their clothes (comp. Deut. 17:5-7) before they began their cruel work. …

person:susanna_2804.name: Susanna
person:susanna_2804.title: Susanna
person:susanna_2804.summary: Lily, with other pious women, ministered to Jesus (Luke 8:3).

person:susi_2805.name: Susi
person:susi_2805.title: Susi
person:susi_2805.summary: The father of Gaddi, who was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:11).

person:syntyche_2806.name: Syntyche
person:syntyche_2806.title: Syntyche
person:syntyche_2806.summary: Fortunate; affable, a female member of the church at Philippi, whom Paul beseeches to be of one mind with Euodias (Phil. 4:2, 3).

person:tabbaoth_2807.name: Tabbaoth
person:tabbaoth_2807.title: Tabbaoth
person:tabbaoth_2807.summary: Impressions; rings, “the children of,” returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:43).

person:tabeal_2808.name: Tabeal
person:tabeal_2808.title: Tabeal
person:tabeal_2808.summary: Goodness of God, the father of one whom the kings of Syria and Samaria in vain attempted to place on the throne of Ahaz (Isa. 7:6).

person:tabeel_2809.name: Tabeel
person:tabeel_2809.title: Tabeel
person:tabeel_2809.summary: A Persian governor of Samaria, who joined others in the attempt to prevent the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:7).

person:tabrimon_2811.name: Tabrimon
person:tabrimon_2811.title: Tabrimon
person:tabrimon_2811.summary: Good is Rimmon, the father of Benhadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

person:tahpenes_2817.name: Tahpenes
person:tahpenes_2817.title: Tahpenes
person:tahpenes_2817.summary: The wife of Pharaoh, who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11:19, 20).

person:talmai_2818.name: Talmai
person:talmai_2818.title: Talmai
person:talmai_2818.summary: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

person:talmai_2819.name: Talmai
person:talmai_2819.title: Talmai
person:talmai_2819.summary: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37). His daughter, Maachah, was one of David’s wives, and the mother of Absalom (1 Chr. 3:2).

person:tamar_2821.name: Tamar
person:tamar_2821.title: Tamar
person:tamar_2821.summary: The daughter-in-law of Judah, to whose eldest son, Er, she was married (Gen. 38:6). After her husband’s death, she was married to Onan, his brother (8), and on his death, Judah promised to her that his third son, Shelah, would become her husband. This promise was not fulfilled, and hence Tamar’s revenge and Judah’s great guilt (38:12-30).

person:tamar_2822.name: Tamar
person:tamar_2822.title: Tamar
person:tamar_2822.summary: A daughter of David (2 Sam. 13:1-32; 1 Chr. 3:9), whom Amnon shamefully outraged and afterwards “hated exceedingly,” thereby illustrating the law of human nature noticed even by the heathen, “Proprium humani ingenii est odisse quem laeseris”, i.e., “It is the property of human nature to hate one whom you have injured.”

person:tanhumeth_2824.name: Tanhumeth
person:tanhumeth_2824.title: Tanhumeth
person:tanhumeth_2824.summary: Consolation, a Netophathite; one of the captains who supported Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8).

person:tarshish_2828.name: Tarshish
person:tarshish_2828.title: Tarshish (son of Javan)
person:tarshish_2828.summary: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

person:tartan_2830.name: Tartan
person:tartan_2830.title: Tartan
person:tartan_2830.summary: One of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17).

person:tatnai_2831.name: Tatnai
person:tatnai_2831.title: Tatnai
person:tatnai_2831.summary: Gift, a Persian governor (Heb. pehah, i.e., “satrap;” modern “pasha”) “on this side the river”, i.e., of the whole tract on the west of the Euphrates. This Hebrew title pehah is given to governors of provinces generally. It is given to Nehemiah (5:14) and to Zerubbabel (Hag. 1:1). It is sometimes translated “captain” (1 Kings 20:24; Dan. 3:2, 3), sometimes also “deputy” (Esther 8:9; 9:3). With others, Tatnai opposed the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:6); but at the command of Darius, he assisted the Jews (6:1-13).

person:temeni_2840.name: Temeni
person:temeni_2840.title: Temeni
person:temeni_2840.summary: One of the sons of Ashur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chr. 4:6).

person:terah_2841.name: Terah
person:terah_2841.title: Terah
person:terah_2841.summary: The wanderer; loiterer, for some unknown reason emigrated with his family from his native mountains in the north to the plains of Mesopotamia. He had three sons, Haran, Nahor, and Abraham, and one daughter, Sarah. He settled in “Ur of the Chaldees,” where his son Haran died, leaving behind him his son Lot. Nahor settled at Haran, a place on the way to Ur. Terah afterwards migrated with Abraham (probably his youngest son) and Lot (his grandson), together with their families, from Ur, intending to go with them to Canaan; but he tarried at Haran, where he spent the remainder of his days, and died at the age of two hundred and five years (Gen. 11:24-32; Josh. 24:2). …

person:teresh_2842.name: Teresh
person:teresh_2842.title: Teresh
person:teresh_2842.summary: Severe, a eunuch or chamberlain in the palace of Ahasuerus, who conspired with another to murder him. The plot was detected by Mordecai, and the conspirators were put to death (Esther 2:21; 6:2).

person:tertullus_2844.name: Tertullus
person:tertullus_2844.title: Tertullus
person:tertullus_2844.summary: A modification of “Tertius;” a Roman advocate, whom the Jews employed to state their case against Paul in the presence of Felix (Acts 24:1-9). The charges he adduced against the apostle were, “First, that he created disturbances among the Romans throughout the empire, an offence against the Roman government (crimen majestatis). Secondly, that he was a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes; disturbed the Jews in the exercise of their religion, guaranteed by the state; introduced new gods, a thing prohibited by the Romans. And thirdly, that he attempted to profane the temple, a crime which the Jews were permitted to punish.”

person:thahash_2845.name: Thahash
person:thahash_2845.title: Thahash
person:thahash_2845.summary: A badger, a son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother (Gen. 22:24).

person:the_giant_in_gath_2848.name: the giant in Gath
person:the_giant_in_gath_2848.title: the giant in Gath
person:the_giant_in_gath_2848.summary: Heb. ‘Anakim (Deut. 2:10, 11, 21; Josh. 11:21, 22; 14:12, 15; called “sons of Anak,” Num. 13:33; “children of Anak,” 13:22; Josh. 15:14), a nomad race of giants descended from Arba (Josh. 14:15), the father of Anak, that dwelt in the south of Palestine near Hebron (Gen. 23:2; Josh. 15:13). They were a Cushite tribe of the same race as the Philistines and the Egyptian shepherd kings. David on several occasions encountered them (2 Sam. 21:15-22). From this race sprung Goliath (1 Sam. 17:4).

person:theophilus_2849.name: Theophilus
person:theophilus_2849.title: Theophilus
person:theophilus_2849.summary: Lover of God, a Christian, probably a Roman, to whom Luke dedicated both his Gospel (Luke 1:3) and the Acts of the Apostles (1:1). Nothing beyond this is known of him. From the fact that Luke applies to him the title “most excellent”, the same title Paul uses in addressing Felix (Acts 23:26; 24:3) and Festus (26:25), it has been concluded that Theophilus was a person of rank, perhaps a Roman officer.

person:theudas_2850.name: Theudas
person:theudas_2850.title: Theudas
person:theudas_2850.summary: Thanksgiving, referred to by Gamaliel in his speech before the council at Jerusalem (Acts 5:36). He headed an insurrection against the Roman authority. Beyond this nothing is known of him.

person:thomas_2851.name: Thomas
person:thomas_2851.title: Thomas
person:thomas_2851.summary: Twin, one of the twelve (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18, etc.). He was also called Didymus (John 11:16; 20:24), which is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew name. All we know regarding him is recorded in the fourth Gospel (John 11:15, 16; 14:4, 5; 20:24, 25, 26-29). From the circumstance that in the lists of the apostles he is always mentioned along with Matthew, who was the son of Alphaeus (Mark 3:18), and that these two are always followed by James, who was also the son of Alphaeus, it has been supposed that these three, Matthew, Thomas, and James, were brothers.

person:tiberius_2852.name: Tiberius
person:tiberius_2852.title: Tiberius
person:tiberius_2852.summary: I.e., as known in Roman history, Tiberius Claudius Nero, only mentioned in Luke 3:1. He was the stepson of Augustus, whom he succeeded on the throne, A.D. 14. He was noted for his vicious and infamous life. In the fifteenth year of his reign John the Baptist entered on his public ministry, and under him also our Lord taught and suffered. He died A.D. 37. He is frequently referred to simply as “Caesar” (Matt. 22:17, 21; Mark 12:14, 16, 17; Luke 20:22, 24, 25; 23:2; John 19:12, 15).

person:tibni_2853.name: Tibni
person:tibni_2853.title: Tibni
person:tibni_2853.summary: Building of Jehovah, the son of Ginath, a man of some position, whom a considerable number of the people chose as monarch. For the period of four years he contended for the throne with Omri (1 Kings 16:21, 22), who at length gained the mastery, and became sole monarch of Israel.

person:tidal_2854.name: Tidal
person:tidal_2854.title: Tidal
person:tidal_2854.summary: (in the LXX. called “Thorgal”), styled the “king of nations” (Gen. 14:1-9). Mentioned as Tudkhula on Arioch’s brick (see facing page 139). Goyyim, translated “nations,” is the country called Gutium, east of Tigris and north of Elam.

person:tilgath-pilneser_2376.name: Tilgath-pilneser
person:tilgath-pilneser_2376.title: Tilgath-pilneser
person:tilgath-pilneser_2376.summary: An Assyrian king. It has been a question whether he was identical with Tiglath-pileser III. (q.v.), or was his predecessor. The weight of evidence is certainly in favour of their identity. Pul was the throne-name he bore in Babylonia as king of Babylon, and Tiglath-pileser the throne-name he bore as king of Assyria. He was the founder of what is called the second Assyrian empire. He consolidated and organized his conquests on a large scale. He subdued Northern Syria and Hamath, and the kings of Syria rendered him homage and paid him tribute. His ambition was to found in Western Asia a kingdom which should embrace the whole civilized world, having Nineveh as its centre. …

person:timaeus_2858.name: Timaeus
person:timaeus_2858.title: Timaeus
person:timaeus_2858.summary: Defiled, the father of blind Bartimaeus (Mark 10:46).

person:timon_2862.name: Timon
person:timon_2862.title: Timon
person:timon_2862.summary: Honouring, one of the seven deacons at Jerusalem (Acts 6:5). Nothing further is known of him.

person:timotheus_2863.name: Timotheus
person:timotheus_2863.title: Timotheus
person:timotheus_2863.summary: Honouring God, a young disciple who was Paul’s companion in many of his journeyings. His mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, are mentioned as eminent for their piety (2 Tim. 1:5). We know nothing of his father but that he was a Greek (Acts 16:1). He is first brought into notice at the time of Paul’s second visit to Lystra (16:2), where he probably resided, and where it seems he was converted during Paul’s first visit to that place (1 Tim. 1:2; 2 Tim. 3:11). The apostle having formed a high opinion of his “own son in the faith,” arranged that he should become his companion (Acts 16:3), and took and circumcised him, so that he might conciliate the Jews. …

person:tiras_2864.name: Tiras
person:tiras_2864.title: Tiras
person:tiras_2864.summary: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

person:tirhakah_2865.name: Tirhakah
person:tirhakah_2865.title: Tirhakah
person:tirhakah_2865.summary: The last king of Egypt of the Ethiopian (the fifteenth) dynasty. He was the brother-in-law of So (q.v.). He probably ascended the throne about B.C. 692, having been previously king of Ethiopia (2 Kings 19:9; Isa. 37:9), which with Egypt now formed one nation. He was a great warrior, and but little is known of him. The Assyrian armies under Esarhaddon, and again under Assur-bani-pal, invaded Egypt and defeated Tirhakah, who afterwards retired into Ethiopia, where he died, after reigning twenty-six years.

person:tirzah_2868.name: Tirzah
person:tirzah_2868.title: Tirzah
person:tirzah_2868.summary: The youngest of Zelophehad’s five daughters (Num. 26:33; Josh. 17:3).

person:titus_2869.name: Titus
person:titus_2869.title: Titus
person:titus_2869.summary: Honourable, was with Paul and Barnabas at Antioch, and accompanied them to the council at Jerusalem (Gal. 2:1-3; Acts 15:2), although his name nowhere occurs in the Acts of the Apostles. He appears to have been a Gentile, and to have been chiefly engaged in ministering to Gentiles; for Paul sternly refused to have him circumcised, inasmuch as in his case the cause of gospel liberty was at stake. We find him, at a later period, with Paul and Timothy at Ephesus, whence he was sent by Paul to Corinth for the purpose of getting the contributions of the church there in behalf of the poor saints at Jerusalem sent forward (2 Cor. 8:6; 12:18). …

person:tobadonijah_2870.name: Tobadonijah
person:tobadonijah_2870.title: Tobadonijah
person:tobadonijah_2870.summary: Good is Jehovah, my Lord, a Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people of Judah in the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:tobiah_2872.name: Tobiah
person:tobiah_2872.title: Tobiah
person:tobiah_2872.summary: Pleasing to Jehovah, the “servant,” the “Ammonite,” who joined with those who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Exile (Neh. 2:10). He was a man of great influence, which he exerted in opposition to the Jews, and “sent letters” to Nehemiah “to put him in fear” (Neh. 6:17-19). “Eliashib the priest” prepared for him during Nehemiah’s absence “a chamber in the courts of the house of God,” which on his return grieved Nehemiah sore, and therefore he “cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber” (13:7, 8).

person:tobijah_2873.name: Tobijah
person:tobijah_2873.title: Tobijah
person:tobijah_2873.summary: Id., a Levite sent out through Judah by Jehoshaphat to teach the people (2 Chr. 17:8).

person:togarmah_2875.name: Togarmah
person:togarmah_2875.title: Togarmah
person:togarmah_2875.summary: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

person:toi_2877.name: Toi
person:toi_2877.title: Toi
person:toi_2877.summary: A king of Hamath, who sent “Joram his son unto King David to salute him,” when he “heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer” (2 Sam. 8:9, 10). Called Tou (1 Chr. 18:9, 10).

person:tola_2879.name: Tola
person:tola_2879.title: Tola
person:tola_2879.summary: A judge of the tribe of Issachar who “judged” Israel twenty-three years (Judg. 10:1, 2), when he died, and was buried in Shamir. He was succeeded by Jair.

person:trophimus_2880.name: Trophimus
person:trophimus_2880.title: Trophimus
person:trophimus_2880.summary: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29). He was with Paul in Jerusalem, and the Jews, supposing that the apostle had brought him with him into the temple, raised a tumult which resulted in Paul’s imprisonment. (See TEMPLE, HEROD’S.) In writing to Timothy, the apostle says, “Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick” (2 Tim. 4:20). This must refer to some event not noticed in the Acts.

person:tubal-cain_2884.name: Tubal-cain
person:tubal-cain_2884.title: Tubal-cain
person:tubal-cain_2884.summary: The son of Lamech and Zillah, “an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron” (Gen. 4:22; R.V., “the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron”).

person:tychicus_2885.name: Tychicus
person:tychicus_2885.title: Tychicus
person:tychicus_2885.summary: Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4). He is alluded to also in Col. 4:7, Titus 3:12, and 2 Tim. 4:12 as having been with Paul at Rome, whence he sent him to Ephesus, probably for the purpose of building up and encouraging the church there.

person:tyrannus_2886.name: Tyrannus
person:tyrannus_2886.title: Tyrannus
person:tyrannus_2886.summary: Prince, a Greek rhetorician, in whose “school” at Ephesus Paul disputed daily for the space of two years with those who came to him (Acts 19:9). Some have supposed that he was a Jew, and that his “school” was a private synagogue.

person:ucal_2887.name: Ucal
person:ucal_2887.title: Ucal
person:ucal_2887.summary: The name of a person to whom Agur’s words are addressed (Prov. 30:1).

person:unni_2891.name: Unni
person:unni_2891.title: Unni
person:unni_2891.summary: A Levite whom David appointed to take part in bringing the ark up to Jerusalem from the house of Obed-edom by playing the psaltery on that occasion (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

person:unni_2892.name: Unni
person:unni_2892.title: Unni
person:unni_2892.summary: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 12:9).

person:uriah_2898.name: Uriah
person:uriah_2898.title: Uriah
person:uriah_2898.summary: A Hittite, the husband of Bathsheba, whom David first seduced, and then after Uriah’s death married. He was one of the band of David’s “mighty men.” The sad story of the curel wrongs inflicted upon him by David and of his mournful death are simply told in the sacred record (2 Sam. 11:2-12:26).

person:uriel_2900.name: Uriel
person:uriel_2900.title: Uriel
person:uriel_2900.summary: A Kohathite ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1 Chr. 6:36).

person:uriel_2901.name: Uriel
person:uriel_2901.title: Uriel
person:uriel_2901.summary: The chief of the Kohathites at the time when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:5, 11).

person:uriel_2902.name: Uriel
person:uriel_2902.title: Uriel
person:uriel_2902.summary: The father of Michaiah, one of Rehoboam’s wives, and mother of Abijah (2 Chr. 13:2).

person:urijah_2899.name: Urijah
person:urijah_2899.title: Urijah
person:urijah_2899.summary: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

person:urijah_2903.name: Urijah
person:urijah_2903.title: Urijah
person:urijah_2903.summary: A high priest in the time of Ahaz (2 Kings 16:10-16), at whose bidding he constructed an idolatrous altar like one the king had seen at Damascus, to be set up instead of the brazen altar.

person:urijah_2904.name: Urijah
person:urijah_2904.title: Urijah
person:urijah_2904.summary: One of the priests who stood at the right hand of Ezra’s pulpit when he read and expounded the law (Neh. 8:4).

person:urijah_2905.name: Urijah
person:urijah_2905.title: Urijah
person:urijah_2905.summary: A prophet of Kirjath-jearim in the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 26:20-23). He fled into Egypt from the cruelty of the king, but having been brought back he was beheaded and his body “cast into the graves of the common people.”

person:uz_2908.name: Uz
person:uz_2908.title: Uz (son of Aram)
person:uz_2908.summary: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

person:uz_2909.name: Uz
person:uz_2909.title: Uz (son of Dishan)
person:uz_2909.summary: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

person:uzal_2911.name: Uzal
person:uzal_2911.title: Uzal
person:uzal_2911.summary: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

person:uzzah_2916.name: Uzzah
person:uzzah_2916.title: Uzzah
person:uzzah_2916.summary: Strength, a son of Abinadab, in whose house the men of Kirjath-jearim placed the ark when it was brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1). He with his brother Ahio drove the cart on which the ark was placed when David sought to bring it up to Jerusalem. When the oxen stumbled, Uzzah, in direct violation of the divine law (Num. 4:15), put forth his hand to steady the ark, and was immediately smitten unto death. The place where this occurred was henceforth called Perez-uzzah (1 Chr. 13:11). David on this feared to proceed further, and placed the ark in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite (2 Sam. 6:2-11; 1 Chr. 13:6-13).

person:uzzi_2917.name: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2917.title: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2917.summary: The son of Bukki, and a descendant of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:5, 51; Ezra 7:4).

person:uzzi_2919.name: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2919.title: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2919.summary: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

person:uzzi_2920.name: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2920.title: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2920.summary: A Benjamite, a chief in the tribe (1 Chr. 9:8).

person:uzzi_2921.name: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2921.title: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2921.summary: A son of Bani. He had the oversight of the Levites after the return from captivity (Neh. 11:22).

person:uzzi_2922.name: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2922.title: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2922.summary: The head of the house of Jedaiah, one of “the chief of the priests” (Neh. 12:19).

person:uzzi_2923.name: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2923.title: Uzzi
person:uzzi_2923.summary: A priest who assisted in the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

person:uzziah_375.name: Uzziah
person:uzziah_375.title: Uzziah
person:uzziah_375.summary: One of Amaziah’s sons, whom the people made king of Judah in his father’s stead (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:1). His long reign of about fifty-two years was “the most prosperous excepting that of Jehosaphat since the time of Solomon.” He was a vigorous and able ruler, and “his name spread abroad, even to the entering in of Egypt” (2 Chr. 26:8, 14). In the earlier part of his reign, under the influence of Zechariah, he was faithful to Jehovah, and “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord” (2 Kings 15:3; 2 Chr. 26:4, 5); but toward the close of his long life “his heart was lifted up to his destruction,” and he wantonly invaded the priest’s office (2 Chr. …

person:uzziah_2926.name: Uzziah
person:uzziah_2926.title: Uzziah
person:uzziah_2926.summary: The father of Jehonathan, one of David’s overseers (1 Chr. 27:25).

person:uzziel_2929.name: Uzziel
person:uzziel_2929.title: Uzziel
person:uzziel_2929.summary: One of the sons of Kohath, and uncle of Aaron (Ex. 6:18; Lev. 10:4).

person:uzziel_2931.name: Uzziel
person:uzziel_2931.title: Uzziel
person:uzziel_2931.summary: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

person:uzziel_2932.name: Uzziel
person:uzziel_2932.title: Uzziel
person:uzziel_2932.summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4); called also Azareel (18).

person:vajezatha_2935.name: Vajezatha
person:vajezatha_2935.title: Vajezatha
person:vajezatha_2935.summary: Purity; worthy of honour, one of Haman’s sons, whom the Jews slew in the palace of Shushan (Esther 9:9).

person:vashti_2937.name: Vashti
person:vashti_2937.title: Vashti
person:vashti_2937.summary: Beautiful, the queen of Ahasuerus, who was deposed from her royal dignity because she refused to obey the king when he desired her to appear in the banqueting hall of Shushan the palace (Esther 1:10-12).

person:zabad_1746.name: Zabad
person:zabad_1746.title: Zabad
person:zabad_1746.summary: The son of Shemath. He conspired against Joash, king of Judah, and slew him (2 Chr. 24:25, 26). He is called also Jozachar (2 Kings 12:21).

person:zabad_2947.name: Zabad
person:zabad_2947.title: Zabad
person:zabad_2947.summary: One of David’s valiant men (1 Chr. 11:41), the descendant of Ahlai, of the “children of Sheshan” (2:31).

person:zabbai_2952.name: Zabbai
person:zabbai_2952.title: Zabbai
person:zabbai_2952.summary: The father of Baruch, who “earnestly repaired” part of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:20; marg., “Zaccai”).

person:zabdi_2954.name: Zabdi
person:zabdi_2954.title: Zabdi
person:zabdi_2954.summary: An ancestor of Achan (Josh. 7:1, 17, 18). He is probably the “Zimri” of 1 Chr. 2:6.

person:zabdi_2956.name: Zabdi
person:zabdi_2956.title: Zabdi
person:zabdi_2956.summary: Called “the Shiphmite,” one of David’s officers, who had charge of his vineyards (1 Chr. 27:27).

person:zabdiel_2957.name: Zabdiel
person:zabdiel_2957.title: Zabdiel
person:zabdiel_2957.summary: The father of Jashobeam, who was one of David’s officers (1 Chr. 27:2).

person:zabdiel_2958.name: Zabdiel
person:zabdiel_2958.title: Zabdiel
person:zabdiel_2958.summary: An overseer of the priests after the Captivity (Neh. 11:14).

person:zabud_2959.name: Zabud
person:zabud_2959.title: Zabud
person:zabud_2959.summary: Gift, the son of Nathan, who was “king’s friend” in the court of Solomon (1 Kings 4:5).

person:zaccai_2960.name: Zaccai
person:zaccai_2960.title: Zaccai
person:zaccai_2960.summary: Pure, one whose “sons” returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:9; Neh. 7:14).

person:zacchaeus_2961.name: Zacchaeus
person:zacchaeus_2961.title: Zacchaeus
person:zacchaeus_2961.summary: Pure, a superintendant of customs; a chief tax-gather (publicanus) at Jericho (Luke 19:1-10). “The collection of customs at Jericho, which at this time produced and exported a considerable quantity of balsam, was undoubtedly an important post, and would account for Zacchaeus being a rich man.” Being short of stature, he hastened on before the multitude who were thronging about Christ as he passed through Jericho on his way to Jerusalem, and climbed up a sycamore tree that he might be able to see him. When our Lord reached the spot he looked up to the publican among the branches, and addressing him by name, told him to make haste and come down, as he intended that day to abide at his house. …

person:zaccur_2963.name: Zaccur
person:zaccur_2963.title: Zaccur
person:zaccur_2963.summary: Father of Shammua, who was one of the spies sent out by Moses (Num. 13:4).

person:zaccur_2965.name: Zaccur
person:zaccur_2965.title: Zaccur
person:zaccur_2965.summary: A son of Asaph, and chief of one of the courses of singers as arranged by David (1 Chr. 25:2, 10).

person:zachariah_2969.name: Zachariah
person:zachariah_2969.title: Zachariah
person:zachariah_2969.summary: Son of Jeroboam II., king of Israel. On the death of his father there was an interregnum of ten years, at the end of which he succeeded to the throne, which he occupied only six months, having been put to death by Shallum, who usurped the throne. “He did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his fathers had done” (2 Kings 14:29; 15:8-12). In him the dynasty of Jehu came to an end.

person:zacharias_2971.name: Zacharias
person:zacharias_2971.title: Zacharias
person:zacharias_2971.summary: A priest of the course of Abia, the eighth of the twenty-four courses into which the priests had been originally divided by David (1 Chr. 23:1-19). Only four of these courses or “families” of the priests returned from the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39); but they were then re-distributed under the old designations. The priests served at the temple twice each year, and only for a week each time. Zacharias’s time had come for this service. During this period his home would be one of the chambers set apart for the priests on the sides of the temple ground. …

person:zacharias_3011.name: Zacharias
person:zacharias_3011.title: Zacharias
person:zacharias_3011.summary: The son or grandson of Jehoiada, the high priest in the times of Ahaziah and Joash. After the death of Jehoiada he boldly condemned both the king and the people for their rebellion against God (2 Chr. 24:20), which so stirred up their resentment against him that at the king’s commandment they stoned him with stones, and he died “in the court of the house of the Lord” (24:21). Christ alludes to this deed of murder in Matt. 23:35, Luke 11:51.

person:zacher_2972.name: Zacher
person:zacher_2972.title: Zacher
person:zacher_2972.summary: Memorial, a son of Jehiel (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:35); called Zechariah (9:37).

person:zadok_2973.name: Zadok
person:zadok_2973.title: Zadok
person:zadok_2973.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4). He is first mentioned as coming to take part with David at Hebron (1 Chr. 12:27, 28). He was probably on this account made ruler over the Aaronites (27:17). Zadok and Abiathar acted as high priests on several important occasions (1 Chr. 15:11; 2 Sam. 15:24-29, 35, 36); but when Adonijah endeavoured to secure the throne, Abiathar went with him, and therefore Solomon “thrust him out from being high priest,” and Zadok, remaining faithful to David, became high priest alone (1 Kings 2:27, 35; 1 Chr. 29:22). …

person:zadok_2974.name: Zadok
person:zadok_2974.title: Zadok
person:zadok_2974.summary: The father of Jerusha, who was wife of King Uzziah, and mother of King Jotham (2 Kings 15:33; 2 Chr. 27:1).

person:zadok_2976.name: Zadok
person:zadok_2976.title: Zadok
person:zadok_2976.summary: The sons of Baana, one of those who assisted in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

person:zadok_2979.name: Zadok
person:zadok_2979.title: Zadok
person:zadok_2979.summary: “The scribe” set over the treasuries of the temple by Nehemiah along with a priest and a Levite (Neh. 13:13).

person:zalmunna_2983.name: Zalmunna
person:zalmunna_2983.title: Zalmunna
person:zalmunna_2983.summary: One of the two kings of Midian whom the “Lord delivered” into the hands of Gideon. He was slain afterwards with Zebah (Judg. 8:5-21).

person:zattu_2986.name: Zattu
person:zattu_2986.title: Zattu
person:zattu_2986.summary: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:8; Neh. 7:13); probably the same as Zatthu.

person:zavan_2944.name: Zavan
person:zavan_2944.title: Zavan
person:zavan_2944.summary: Terror, one of the “dukes of Edom” (Gen. 36:27); called also Zavan (1 Chr. 1:42).

person:zaza_2987.name: Zaza
person:zaza_2987.title: Zaza
person:zaza_2987.summary: Plenty, a descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:33).

person:zebadiah_2991.name: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2991.title: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2991.summary: A Korhite porter of the Lord’s house (1 Chr. 26:2). Three or four others of this name are also mentioned.

person:zebadiah_2992.name: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2992.title: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2992.summary: A son of Asahel, Joab’s brother (1 Chr. 27:7).

person:zebadiah_2993.name: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2993.title: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2993.summary: A Levite who took part as one of the teachers in the system of national education instituted by Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:7, 8).

person:zebadiah_2994.name: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2994.title: Zebadiah
person:zebadiah_2994.summary: The son of Ishmael, “the ruler of the house of Judah in all the king’s matters” (2 Chr. 19:8-11).

person:zebah_2997.name: Zebah
person:zebah_2997.title: Zebah
person:zebah_2997.summary: Man-killer, or sacrifice, one of the two kings who led the vast host of the Midianites who invaded the land of Israel, and over whom Gideon gained a great and decisive victory (Judg. 8). Zebah and Zalmunna had succeeded in escaping across the Jordan with a remnant of the Midianite host, but were overtaken at Karkor, probably in the Hauran, and routed by Gideon. The kings were taken alive and brought back across the Jordan; and confessing that they had personally taken part in the slaughter of Gideon’s brothers, they were put to death (comp. 1 Sam. 12:11; Isa. 10:26; Ps. 83:11).

person:zebedee_2998.name: Zebedee
person:zebedee_2998.title: Zebedee
person:zebedee_2998.summary: A Galilean fisherman, the husband of Salome (q.v.), and the father of James and John, two of our Lord’s disciples (Matt. 4:21; 27:56; Mark 15:40). He seems to have been a man of some position in Capernaum, for he had two boats (Luke 5:4) and “hired servants” (Mark 1:20) of his own. No mention is made of him after the call of his two sons by Jesus.

person:zebudah_3000.name: Zebudah
person:zebudah_3000.title: Zebudah
person:zebudah_3000.summary: Given, the wife of Josiah and mother of Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

person:zebul_3001.name: Zebul
person:zebul_3001.title: Zebul
person:zebul_3001.summary: Habitation, the governor of Shechem under Abimelech (Judg. 9:28, 30, 36). He informed his master of the intention of the people of Shechem to transfer their allegiance to the Hivite tribe of Hamor. This led to Abimelech’s destroying the city, when he put its entire population to the sword, and sowed the ruins with salt (Judg. 9:28-45).

person:zebulun_3002.name: Zebulun
person:zebulun_3002.title: Zebulun
person:zebulun_3002.summary: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history. He had three sons (46:14).

person:zechariah_2970.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_2970.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_2970.summary: The father of Abijah, who was the mother of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:1).

person:zechariah_3003.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3003.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3003.summary: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:7).

person:zechariah_3004.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3004.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3004.summary: A Levite who assisted at the bringing up of the ark from the house of Obededom (1 Chr. 15:20-24).

person:zechariah_3008.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3008.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3008.summary: One who assisted in teaching the law to the people in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:7).

person:zechariah_3009.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3009.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3009.summary: A Levite of the sons of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14).

person:zechariah_3012.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3012.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3012.summary:
A prophet, who had “understanding in the seeing of God,” in the time of Uzziah, who was much indebted to him for his wise counsel (2 Chr. 26:5).
Besides these, there is a large number of persons mentioned in Scripture bearing this name of whom nothing is known.

person:zechariah_3015.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3015.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3015.summary: One of the “rulers of the house of God” (2 Chr. 35:8).

person:zechariah_3016.name: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3016.title: Zechariah
person:zechariah_3016.summary:
A prophet of Judah, the eleventh of the twelve minor prophets. Like Ezekiel, he was of priestly extraction. He describes himself (1:1) as “the son of Berechiah.” In Ezra 5:1 and 6:14 he is called “the son of Iddo,” who was properly his grandfather. His prophetical career began in the second year of Darius (B.C. 520), about sixteen years after the return of the first company from exile. He was contemporary with Haggai (Ezra 5:1).
His book consists of two distinct parts, (1) chapters 1 to 8, inclusive, and (2) 9 to the end. It begins with a preface (1:1-6), which recalls the nation’s past history, for the purpose of presenting a solemn warning to the present generation. …

person:zedekiah_1950.name: Zedekiah
person:zedekiah_1950.title: Zedekiah
person:zedekiah_1950.summary: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31; 24:17, 18). His original name was Mattaniah; but when Nebuchadnezzar placed him on the throne as the successor to Jehoiachin he changed his name to Zedekiah. The prophet Jeremiah was his counsellor, yet “he did evil in the sight of the Lord” (2 Kings 24:19, 20; Jer. 52:2, 3). He ascended the throne at the age of twenty-one years. …

person:zedekiah_3029.name: Zedekiah
person:zedekiah_3029.title: Zedekiah
person:zedekiah_3029.summary: The son of Chenaanah, a false prophet in the days of Ahab (1 Kings 22:11, 24; 2 Chr. 18:10, 23).

person:zedekiah_3032.name: Zedekiah
person:zedekiah_3032.title: Zedekiah
person:zedekiah_3032.summary: The son of Hananiah, a prince of Judah in the days of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

person:zeeb_3033.name: Zeeb
person:zeeb_3033.title: Zeeb
person:zeeb_3033.summary: The wolf, one of the two leaders of the great Midianite host which invaded Israel and was utterly routed by Gideon. The division of that host, which attempted to escape across the Jordan, under Oreb and Zeeb, was overtaken by the Ephraimites, who, in a great battle, completely vanquished them, their leaders being taken and slain (Judg. 7:25; Ps. 83:11; Isa. 10:26).

person:zelek_3034.name: Zelek
person:zelek_3034.title: Zelek
person:zelek_3034.summary: Cleft, an Ammonite; one of David’s valiant men (2 Sam. 23:37).

person:zelophehad_3035.name: Zelophehad
person:zelophehad_3035.title: Zelophehad
person:zelophehad_3035.summary: First-born, of the tribe of Manasseh, and of the family of Gilead; died in the wilderness. Having left no sons, his daughters, concerned lest their father’s name should be “done away from among his family,” made an appeal to Moses, who, by divine direction, appointed it as “a statute of judgment” in Israel that daughters should inherit their father’s portion when no sons were left (Num. 27:1-11). But that the possession of Zelophehad might not pass away in the year of jubilee from the tribe to which he belonged, it was ordained by Moses that his daughters should not marry any one out of their father’s tribe; and this afterwards became a general law (Num. 36).

person:zemarite_3036.name: Zemarite
person:zemarite_3036.title: Zemarite
person:zemarite_3036.summary: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range. In the Amarna tablets (B.C. 1400) Zemar, or Zumur, was one of the most important of the Phoenician cities, but it afterwards almost disappears from history.

person:zemira_3037.name: Zemira
person:zemira_3037.title: Zemira
person:zemira_3037.summary: Vine-dresser, a Benjamite; one of the sons of Becher (1 Chr. 7:8).

person:zenas_3038.name: Zenas
person:zenas_3038.title: Zenas
person:zenas_3038.summary: A disciple called “the lawyer,” whom Paul wished Titus to bring with him (Titus 3:13). Nothing more is known of him.

person:zephaniah_3039.name: Zephaniah
person:zephaniah_3039.title: Zephaniah
person:zephaniah_3039.summary: The son of Maaseiah, the “second priest” in the reign of Zedekiah, often mentioned in Jeremiah as having been sent from the king to inquire (Jer. 21:1) regarding the coming woes which he had denounced, and to entreat the prophet’s intercession that the judgment threatened might be averted (Jer. 29:25, 26, 29; 37:3; 52:24). He, along with some other captive Jews, was put to death by the king of Babylon “at Riblah in the land of Hamath” (2 Kings 25:21).

person:zephaniah_3041.name: Zephaniah
person:zephaniah_3041.title: Zephaniah
person:zephaniah_3041.summary: The father of Josiah, the priest who dwelt in Jerusalem when Darius issued the decree that the temple should be rebuilt (Zech. 6:10).

person:zerah_2984.name: Zerah
person:zerah_2984.title: Zerah
person:zerah_2984.summary: A son of Tamar (Gen. 38:30); called also Zara (Matt. 1:3).

person:zerah_3046.name: Zerah
person:zerah_3046.title: Zerah
person:zerah_3046.summary: An “Ethiopian,” probably Osorkon II., the successor of Shishak on the throne of Egypt. With an enormous army, the largest we read of in Scripture, he invaded the kingdom of Judah in the days of Asa (2 Chr. 14:9-15). He reached Zephathah, and there encountered the army of Asa. This is the only instance “in all the annals of Judah of a victorious encounter in the field with a first-class heathen power in full force.” The Egyptian host was utterly routed, and the Hebrews gathered “exceeding much spoil.” Three hundred years elapsed before another Egyptian army, that of Necho (B.C. 609), came up against Jerusalem.

person:zerah_3102.name: Zerah
person:zerah_3102.title: Zerah
person:zerah_3102.summary: One of the sons of Simeon (Gen. 46:10; Ex. 6:15).

person:zeresh_3049.name: Zeresh
person:zeresh_3049.title: Zeresh
person:zeresh_3049.summary: Star of Venus, the wife of Haman, whom she instigated to prepare a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5:10).

person:zeruah_3053.name: Zeruah
person:zeruah_3053.title: Zeruah
person:zeruah_3053.summary: Stricken, mother of Jeroboam, the first king of the ten tribes (1 Kings 11:26).

person:zerubbabel_3054.name: Zerubbabel
person:zerubbabel_3054.title: Zerubbabel
person:zerubbabel_3054.summary: The seed of Babylon, the son of Salathiel or Shealtiel (Hag. 1:1; Zorobabel, Matt. 1:12); called also the son of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:17-19), i.e., according to a frequent usage of the word “son;” the grandson or the nephew of Salathiel. He is also known by the Persian name of Sheshbazzar (Ezra 1:8, 11). In the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, he led the first band of Jews, numbering 42,360 (Ezra 2:64), exclusive of a large number of servants, who returned from captivity at the close of the seventy years. In the second year after the Return, he erected an altar and laid the foundation of the temple on the ruins of that which had been destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar (3:8-13; ch. 4-6). …

person:zeruiah_3055.name: Zeruiah
person:zeruiah_3055.title: Zeruiah
person:zeruiah_3055.summary: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chr. 2:16), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

person:ziba_3060.name: Ziba
person:ziba_3060.title: Ziba
person:ziba_3060.summary: Post; statue, “a servant of the house of Saul” (2 Sam. 9:2), who informed David that Mephibosheth, a son of Jonathan, was alive. He afterwards dealt treacherously toward Mephibosheth, whom he slanderously misrepresented to David.

person:zibiah_3064.name: Zibiah
person:zibiah_3064.title: Zibiah
person:zibiah_3064.summary: The mother of King Joash (2 Kings 12:1; 2 Chr. 24:1).

person:zichri_3067.name: Zichri
person:zichri_3067.title: Zichri
person:zichri_3067.summary: Another of the same tribe (1 Chr. 8:23).

person:zichri_3069.name: Zichri
person:zichri_3069.title: Zichri
person:zichri_3069.summary: A Levite, one of the sons of Asaph (Neh. 11:17); probably the same as Zichri (1 Chr. 9:15), and Zaccur (Neh. 12:35).

person:zidkijah_3077.name: Zidkijah
person:zidkijah_3077.title: Zidkijah
person:zidkijah_3077.summary: The Lord is righteous, one who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh. 10:1).

person:zidon_2738.name: Zidon
person:zidon_2738.title: Zidon
person:zidon_2738.summary: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19). It was the first home of the Phoenicians on the coast of Palestine, and from its extensive commercial relations became a “great” city (Josh. 11:8; 19:28). It was the mother city of Tyre. It lay within the lot of the tribe of Asher, but was never subdued (Judg. 1:31). The Zidonians long oppressed Israel (Judg. 10:12). From the time of David its glory began to wane, and Tyre, its “virgin daughter” (Isa. 23:12), rose to its place of pre-eminence. …

person:ziha_3078.name: Ziha
person:ziha_3078.title: Ziha
person:ziha_3078.summary: The name of a family of Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

person:zillah_3080.name: Zillah
person:zillah_3080.title: Zillah
person:zillah_3080.summary: Shadow, one of the wives of Lamech, of the line of Cain, and mother of Tubal-cain (Gen. 4:19, 22).

person:zilpah_3081.name: Zilpah
person:zilpah_3081.title: Zilpah
person:zilpah_3081.summary: Drooping, Leah’s handmaid, and the mother of Gad and Asher (Gen. 30:9-13).

person:zilthai_3083.name: Zilthai
person:zilthai_3083.title: Zilthai
person:zilthai_3083.summary: One of the captains of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

person:zimran_3086.name: Zimran
person:zimran_3086.title: Zimran
person:zimran_3086.summary: Vine-dressers; celebrated, one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

person:zimri_3088.name: Zimri
person:zimri_3088.title: Zimri
person:zimri_3088.summary: Murdered Elah at Tirzah, and succeeded him on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He reigned only seven days, for Omri, whom the army elected as king, laid siege to Tirzah, whereupon Zimri set fire to the palace and perished amid its ruins (11-20). Omri succeeded to the throne only after four years of fierce war with Tibni, another claimant to the throne.

person:zippor_3094.name: Zippor
person:zippor_3094.title: Zippor
person:zippor_3094.summary: A little bird, the father of Balak, king of Moab (Num. 22:2, 4).

person:zipporah_3095.name: Zipporah
person:zipporah_3095.title: Zipporah
person:zipporah_3095.summary: A female bird. Reuel’s daughter, who became the wife of Moses (Ex. 2:21). In consequence of the event recorded in Ex. 4:24-26, she and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer, when so far on the way with Moses toward Egypt, were sent back by him to her own kinsfolk, the Midianites, with whom they sojourned till Moses afterwards joined them (18:2-6).

person:zithri_3096.name: Zithri
person:zithri_3096.title: Zithri
person:zithri_3096.summary: The Lord protects, a Levite, son of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

person:zohar_3101.name: Zohar
person:zohar_3101.title: Zohar
person:zohar_3101.summary: The father of Ephron the Hittite (Gen. 23:8).

person:zoheth_3103.name: Zoheth
person:zoheth_3103.title: Zoheth
person:zoheth_3103.summary: Snatching (?), one of the sons of Ishi (1 Chr. 4:20).

person:zophah_3104.name: Zophah
person:zophah_3104.title: Zophah
person:zophah_3104.summary: Spreading out, a son of Helem (1 Chr. 7:35), a chief of Asher.

person:zophar_3105.name: Zophar
person:zophar_3105.title: Zophar
